title: Three Vital Changes The Ravens Must Make To The Run Game, Including Less Derrick Henry
full_text:
The Ravens’ run game is beyond broken.
And it’s probably unfixable. The loss of historically mobile, two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has sunk their ability to win the numbers game at the line of scrimmage and create holes and math that works in their favor; and Jackson isn’t coming back to this sinking ship. Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has become very predictable in his run concepts, with multiple execs from other teams pointing out to me that teams are keying on when the under-center and outside zone runs are coming.
And, well, the offensive line that failing general manager Eric DeCosta has concocted is the worst by far of all the suspect units he’s constructed, one that seems hellbent on getting quarterbacks maimed, and quickly-aging 32-year-old running back Derrick Henry swarmed behind the line of scrimmage. It’s so bad that one could rightfully make the case that four of the five starting spots should be shuffled so that someone perhaps less prone to crushing mistakes could get a shot.
It’s a fairly dire circumstance and the fact that no QB on this roster is going to shift that math in Doyle’s favor is damning. If he is in fact the genius he was purported to be this summer, well, now would be the perfect time to show it. More likely, Doyle will be hard-pressed to change things even on the margins, but he absolutely must lean into these three fundamental changes to his approach after henry ran 10 times for 10 yards against a middling Chargers defense Monday night and the team ran 15 times for 16 yards.
“There's to me just a combination of a lot of factors that we need to figure out how to be able to run the football,” struggling rookie head coach Jesse Minter said Monday. “There's been spurts of it, but the last few games, it's obviously not where it needs to be.
“It starts with me, starts with the coaches, goes down to the players. Unacceptable, honestly, that we're not able to. The first half, to have no yards rushing, it's embarrassing. And so, we'll keep trying to find a better way to do it."
We have a few suggestions:
Nothing lasts forever, there was always a good reason to suspect a decline at this age (all the data pointed to it ), and that Doyle was not going to be able to get the 300 carries he badly wanted from him with the effectiveness he would expect. That’s out the window now. (Henry has never run 300 times for three straight years).
With failing center Cam Jurgens now anchoring this line, under center runs are impossible and running between the tackles, period, is out. That’s Henry’s bread-and-butter, along with outside zone rushes, but teams are shooting the gap with linebackers and defensive backs and blowing that up in the backfield. Monday night – on the feels of five weeks of stagnation (at best) – should be the end of thinking this can be based around Henry with this line and personnel.
Henry: 110 – 358 – 3 TD        3.3 yards/carry           0.36 Yds Before Contact
Hill: 23 – 187 – 1                8.8 yards/carry           3.78 Yds Before Contact
Henry: 60 – 194 – 4                3.21 yards/carry         0.53 Yds Before Contact
Hill: 19 – 144 – 0                  7.60 yards/carry         4.63 Yds Before Contact
Henry: 28 – 84 – 1                  3.00 yards/carry         0.54 Yds Before Contact
Hill: 8 – 85 – 1                      10.6 yards/carry         8.63 Yds Before Contact
So, yeah, it's time for more spread formations and less I-formation and more sprint plays with speed out of the gun.
The Ravens cannot get as caught up in outside zone and trying to do something they thought would be a calling hard. They have had a new line almost every week and Doyle isn’t fooling anyone. It’s time to incorporate more power and duo blocking and see if that can unlock Henry and save the perimeter stuff for others.
And that goes way beyond just Hill.
The team seems reluctant to get fifth-round pick Adam Randall into a football game this season as he sits on Injured Reserve. But they need to see what he can do as a “Joker” in this offense who can run wide receiver routes as an inside player and also carry the football and serve as an H-back and fullback. They are desperate for some new looks and traits.
And Zay Flowers needs to get back into the flow of the run game and used like he was early in the season with Jackson. They need to think about pony packages with Hill and Flowers in the backfield and Henry and Flowers and, shoot, Henry and Randall.
Anybody see what Sean McVay did last week due to injuries, basically just leaning on 13 personnel and pony packages to destroy the Cardinals on Sunday? Get that film to Doyle.
Feel like we say this all the time, but in light of what we just noted with McVay, and given the limitations of this roster, Doyle needs to be willing to throw more manpower at the problem and get the tackle eligible involved and let Jacoby Brissett take some play-action shots out of that heavy stuff.
They should think about having a fullback be much more a part of this offense (paging Pat Ricard).If Carson Vinson replaces Ronnie Stanley at left tackle, as I would espouse, then find another swing tackle.
The Ravens have gone with six offensive linemen 31 times, which is fourth-most in the NFL, but given the depths the traditional run game has hit, that’s not enough. They average a hefty 5.4 yards/carry when they do it, which is also fourth in the NFL. Doyle is using two or more tight ends 44% of the time, which is top 10 in the NFL, but the head coach Doyle worked for last year in Chicago – Ben Johnson, a true savant – is using them over half the time and running the ball with vigor and getting plenty of people involved.
Baltimore could badly use more of that.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Had Superior Options To Jesse Minter On Recent Coaching Staffs. We Rank Them 1-5
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are facing an existential crisis.
Their front office has made it clear – after surviving the firing of potential Hall of Fame coach John Harbaugh – that it’s actually by far the biggest issue in the organization. Both through its systematic roster and contract failures under GM Eric DeCosta and through hiring a rudimentary and inexperienced coaching staff that has been thoroughly overmatched to this point. Which begs questions about the future of the coordinators if not the outright potential for Jesse Minter to be a one-and-done as his losing streak hits five games after being by the winless Chargers, his former team.
If it feels like a lot just 10 games in, well, that’s because it is. And, yeah, that hot seat should be getting a little toasty. You sell Lombardi Trophy contention and can’t beat the worst team in the NFL – by far – at home on MNF, welcome to reality. Life comes at you fast in the NFL .
It also begs massive questions about how coaches were being evaluated for years inside The Castle and how the once-proud franchise finds itself among the dregs of the NFL facing a roster crisis and a salary-cap crisis and an unprecedented contractual situation with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, having to recruit him to stick around Baltimore at a time when those in charge are lacking leadership, solutions and with little to bank on inside that locker room moving forward.
Since reaching the AFC title game in 2023, it’s been all downhill, and in reality there are at least five coaches who have been in Baltimore since then that could make the case as superior head coaching options to what Minter and this novice staff are providing right now. Personally, any of the names listed below would carry a stronger profile and pedigree to what the Ravens are getting from their current head coach – who was sold at the solution right now, in the present, for a team in Super Bowl-or-bust mode, not some lengthy rebuild.
He is the unicorn. He is the chosen one on the defensive side of the ball in the way Sean McVay is on offense and of course the Super Bowl went through those two last year. Left after two years as Ravens defensive coordinator, went 10-7 and nearly made the playoffs his first year making no big moves and running it back with Pete Carroll’s players.
Lombardi Trophy in Year Two. No way Steve Bisciotti was going to replace Harbaugh with him after giving away that Championship Game to the Chiefs … but he was The Special One. The fact that Minter hung out with him as young assistants in Baltimore means nothing, and Macdonald would never be associated with the $160M disaster that is the Ravens’ 2026 defense (which is markedly worse than the 2025 version that got Zach Orr fired ).
He might win NFL Coach Of The Year with the Browns. That young team plays with more fire and passion and will than Minter’s veteran’s ever will. Cleveland in the best fourth-quarter team in the NFL; Baltimore remain the biggest chokers in the NFL. Monken helped Jackson to his two best seasons by far and blended his passing concepts with the vestiges of the Greg Roman run game.
He has verve and he can motivate players and no one is shattering expectations more than he is with a team that might mess around and make the playoffs. Damn near pulled off a comeback road win with Shedeur Sanders at QB against a Saints team that pulled off a double-digit comeback against Minter in Baltimore.
This ain’t even close to being a discussion. Minter had a nice run as a college head coach. Jets should have hired him as HC when they hired Adam Gase. Ravens could have promoted him to the big chair in Baltimore. Already kicked Minter's ass once and De Costa-ed the Ravens in the process, overcoming a 10-point deficit in the second half.
Amazing run as a head coach with the Colts. Overcame cancer, hired a tremendous staff. Players ran through walls for him. You wanted to keep this team together and try to get over the top real quick in a few years? Coulda hired Pagano.
There would be standards and guardrails coming in. He already knew what he was up against with DeCosta and Sashi Brown in charge and could thread that needle. He understands their quirks and was part of better defenses from the past in Baltimore than Minter ever was and could have helped them discover young coordinators to take over for him.
It would have been better than this, people .
He brought the secret sauce to this coaching staff when he got together with Macdonald for that epic 2023 run. He added his flair to the Wink Martindale installed packages Macdonald was operating with and helped that defense win the triple crown for the first time in NFL history – led the NFL in sacks, takeaways and points allowed.
Former standout at Maryland, and a native Marylander, he played the game at a high level and can relate to players in a way Minter never could -  a star for Terps who got a cup of coffee with Washington in the NFL. Deep personnel background trained to scout with the Bears and extensive coaching experience and now doing a tremendous job with the Giants as their defensive coordinator.
The Ravens foolishly let him leave as DC for the Titans in 2024 – the front office viewed Zach Orr, a former Ravens player , as more one of them and Wilson was an outsider. Harbaugh thought enough of his work to hire him in NY. The Terps should hire him as their head coach and he’s going to be getting head coaching interviews soon enough.
Has far more presence and heft than Minter in terms of getting up in front of an entire 53-man roster. Has a far more diverse background too, while Minter is merely an extension of the Harbaugh brothers for the most part.
Yeah, the message was stale, and he had to go and I am not going to pretend that wasn’t the case … But imagine Bisciotti flipped the script - blew up the personnel side and kept Harbaugh with Monken and maybe a new defensive coordinator, you can’t tell me that wouldn’t be better than this.
They wouldn’t have given up 33 or more in three-straight games, while failing to score 14 in four straight in losing five straight. Not with this cupcake schedule.
They wouldn’t lead the NFL in offensive penalties and pre-snap penalties. Yeah, maybe they would still choke game away, because that was part of the brand, but this has been adject failure since Minter’s first home game in charge. Say what you want about Harbaugh’s many faults, but he had a doghouse and wasn’t afraid to shake things up, while Minter has offered nothing but empty rhetoric in that regard.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Must Make Sweeping Changes Across The Offensive Line. Immediately
full_text:
The Ravens have been swapping out offensive linemen all season and have yet to find anything but a failing five-man unit.
If they want to keep journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett – their fourth starting QB in the last four weeks – upright long enough to make it to their Week 13 bye ( a big ask at this point ), they had better be willing to get very real about the current state of affairs. Sure, they have juggled personnel based on injuries to this point, or created a spot for struggling players who they vastly overpaid for in trade (Cam Jurgens) but the reality is the men up front are getting whipped, collectively and individually.
There is no interconnectivity or cohesion, and rookie offensive playcaller Declan Doyle is now dealing with opposing defenses having strong tells on when he is running inside on under-center rushes and when he is calling outside zone for Derrick Henry and it’s creating a total mess. The coaches do not appear to have the answers.
Pass protection is bottom of the NFL (26th in pressure rate). Run blocking is nonexistent (-2 yards before contact for Henry in the first half in Monday’s capitulation to the winless Chargers and 15 rushes for 16 yards in the game).
Moving Jurgens to center in place of now-injured rookie Vega Ioane has been a catastrophe, the signing of free agent guard John Simpson has been like lighting $20M on fire and the entire interior offensive line was tossed around repeatedly by the Chargers - not a stout defensive line. Neither tackle, Ronnie Stanley or Roger Rosengarten, is holding up in pass protection.
It’s a disaster all the way around and overmatched rookie head coach Jesse Minter’s frustration is clearly growing by the week, and the decisions not to peddle Henry and Stanley for whatever they could get at the trade deadline will only look worse with the passing of time . Getting three QBs hurt in rapid succession in Buffalo a few weeks back should have promoted a front-office shakeup.
“Unacceptable, honestly,” Minter said Monday of the inept run game.
Their season is over with five straight losses, and they don’t have to worry about protecting a franchise quarterback for the remainder of the year with Lamar Jackson done for 2026 (trust). Now is the time to find out whatever they can about some of the young linemen here and to be willing to make sweeping changes to this line once more.
When asked what was wrong with the run game, Henry offered: “Everything. We're just not doing a good enough job to be efficient in the run game. Sixteen total yards is a clear explanation … I don't know. I don't have an answer. The guys who are out there (linemen) are healthy and are trying to do their jobs. We just aren't good enough."
Over the last five weeks the Ravens have run 118 times for 434 yards (3.7 yards/carry – 27th in the NFL). They are averaging 0.86 yards before contact (25th) and converting a rush on third down just 37.5% of the time despite having a Hall of Fame power back (27th). When they run under center – a core tenant of change rookie coordinator Declan Doyle was banking on – they have averaged 2.7 yards per carry since Week 6, tied for last in the NFL.
Stanley, 32, was on borrowed time since suffered career-threatening lower leg/high ankle issues years ago. The Ravens were able to keep him on the cheap when his injuries prevented him from having a robust free-agent market, but their voidable years and poor contract structure has caught up to them. Stanley is virtually certain to be gone in the spring – as explained here – and now is the time to see what Carson Vinson can do.
They need at least one new starting tackle next season and maybe two. Stanley suffered a painful toe injury early in the season, he is suffering in pass pro and has been among the most penalized players in the NFL (nine penalties in nine games, second-most in the NFL). Minter has mumbled about “accountability and telling the truth” but done nothing about the same veterans making the same mistakes over and over.
That must change, and this is a good place to start. Stanley allowed two QB hits, four hurries and five pressures Monday
They prefer Edoga, 29, to youngster Emery Jones (guess that’s yet another overhyped projectable OL from a front office that never hits). Fine. He has started at left guard for three different teams including in Atlanta, where he was with Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford - alleged to be some sort of OL savant. Okay, give him all his guys.
Would be surprised if Ioane doesn’t need more time out after repeated injuries and looking physically not right at all Monday. No reason to keep pushing it with one of the few bright spots to come out of this lost year.
Eagles GM Howie Roseman knew what he was doing when he moved Jurgens to guard and then shipped him to Baltimore. He has not been close to the same player since undergoing major back surgery a few years back, and it’s not working here. He was getting tossed around Monday to the point multiple personnel execs were texting me in game about it.
“Centers get a limited number of plays where they are actually blocking someone one-on-one,” said one personnel exec who watched Jurgens’s film. “The times that Jurgens was asked to block like that last night were really tough. The sack. Some of the pressures. They gave up more than a (second-round pick) for a bad center.”
The Ravens are stuck with roughly $16M guaranteed to Jurgens next season. Maybe he could be better at guard. The Ravens bizarrely traded for Atlanta’s Ryan Neuzil (another Ledford guy) despite getting ripped off for Jurgens already. He has held it down as a replacement level starting center for over a year now. Give him a shot.
Simpson’s contract is so brutal the Ravens have to pay him $5.5M in 2027 no matter what, and he’s been banged up. But he’s had a horrible season, 10 games is enough, and it’s time to try something else now. Of course, with Jones on the outs now, would be surprising to see him at right guard.
It would make sense, but like Neuzil above that’s far too revealing for this staff and front office. Maybe they would be okay giving Neuzil a look at right guard and sitting Simpson? Or Jurgens there if they put Neuzil at center? On Monday Simpson allowed one hit, four hurries, five pressures and was flat-out beat twice. He has been beat nine times in the last four games and been fairly disastrous all season.
He has been in steady decline since his rookie season and, early in the season, was at least an anchor they could run outside zone behind. Everything is cratering now. He’s been falling apart since edge rusher Greg Rousseau thrashed him in Buffalo and Monday he allowed seven hurries, seven pressures and five beats. That’s ugly. He’s allowed two sacks, 13 pressures and 11 beats in the last four games.
If they don’t want to see Vinson at left tackle, then maybe give him a run at right tackle. This franchise has believes that rotating tackles and guards made them look smart for years – even when they had far better and deeper lines than this – so why aren’t they trying it now?
Anything would be better than the status quo.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Top 5 Reasons Jesse Minter Could Be A One-And-Done Head Coach For Ravens
full_text:
There is no reason to presuppose that Monday night’s debacle loss to the previously-winless Chargers is the nadir for the 2026 Ravens.
With no discernable strengths in any of the three phases of football, and two months still to play including four games against the mighty AFC North, where everyone else is making a real playoff case, it can always get worse. With a bloated roster full of underachievers who should have been peddled at the deadline as part of an inevitable rebuild that really should have began with the firing of general manager Eric DeCosta along with potential Hall of Fame coach John Harbaugh, it can definitely get worse.
And if they continue on this slide – five straight losses, matching their collapse to end the 2021 season; three straight games without holding a lead – it is going to continue to beg major questions of this coaching staff across the board, and call even more into question owner Steve Bisciotti giving his entire personnel department a pass and outsourcing the coaching search to DeCosta and Sashi Brown (the entire league knew this was Jesse Minter’s job to lose, given his past ties to the Ravens).
There is every reason to believe it’s going to continue a disaster.
And there are the five primary reasons why this could absolutely be heading to a one-and-done situation for the overmatched rookie head coach … or at least why any organization that was able to look cogently at the state of affairs would be considering wholesale changes to every aspect of the organization in a way that Harbaugh's outster should have immediately triggered.
The Ravens are the worst second-half team in football and Minter immediately ramped up their preexisting fatal flaw – blowing 10-point leads in the second half to lose to bad teams. Lamar Jackson is the only thing that kept them competitive – and he isn’t throwing another pass this season and maybe never again as a Raven . The Ravens have played one of the easiest schedules in the NFL and are 2-5 in the AFC, with a bottom three strength of victory. This season is over, and Minter’s future should be in the balance.
This was sold as Super Bowl or bust, not a three-year plan.
Bisciotti broke a Cardinal rule he has always prized in the past – separation of Church And State.
Equally empowered football ops and coaching staff who reported to him. When he chose DeCosta over Harbaugh, and then let DeCosta and Brown steer almost the entirety of the head coaching search – that was always headed in a certain direction to team presidents and GMs and execs around the NFL – that power balance swung drastically.
Now the head coach and GM were not tied on equal footing, at similar points in their career. One was being called a genius who “bats .800” on transactions and the other had never been a head coach anywhere and had the most novice staff in the NFL , and instead of hiring former NFL head coaches to help him (like his buddy Mike Macdonald did in Seattle after leaving Baltimore), Minter hired his dad.
DeCosta’s personnel record, despite what the media suggest almost anytime he makes a move, is littered with failures and his inability to get Jackson’s extended, find a competent outside WR, build anything but garbage offensive lines and run a $370M payroll devoid of real playmakers in the clutch besides Jackson, is grounds for immediate termination in any serious franchise.
If that happened, any top candidate brought in from the outside might far prefer, say, Brian Flores or Steve Spagnuolo or Sean McDermott to Minter for 1000 notable reasons … And if you want to have a true regime and restart, with the GM and head coach brought in at the same time, and you wanted to truly compete for the best and the brightest, well … one and dones occur in the league all the time for just such reasons.
Minter’s biggest strength has become his biggest weakness.
They couldn’t sell him as some field general or CEO or leader of men. There was nothing in his profile to suggest any of that. He never managed the game or oversaw a full roster or had the power to hire and fire people and build a full staff. All of that was a guess.
He was hired because the Ravens sold you he was a boy wonder defensive play-caller, just like Macdonald. He was smarter and better than the prior staff and he was going to immediately elevate that entire unit. In fact he was going to do it so swiftly that they could thrive with a 29-year old who didn’t know whether to call plays from the sidelines or press box ( turns out Declan Doyle got that wrong, too) to run the offense in Lamar’s walk year.
It wouldn’t matter because Minter had the secret sauce and all the blowing of leads was over and he is a savant in the secondary and DeCosta had sunk everything into the D and threw a $60M “closer” at him – Trey Hendrickson, a colossal bust – as part of a $160M defense. And they are the biggest chokers and biggest failures of all on that side of the ball. and Minter has yet to make a cogent in-game adjustment to salvage anything. He has no playmakers, and seems unable to scheme them up .
Longtime Raiders exec Amy Trask told us last week coordinator changes must be on the table , so, um, if that’s the case, and that’s Minter’s supposed super power, why are we keeping him around to pretend to be a head coach and hope he grows into it?
His scheme as been exposed since very early on this season against awful QBs.
The second-half implosions are massive, and, when forced to start Joe Fagnano or Jacoby Brissett on short notice, and therefore need the defense to show up early so they don’t play from behind, the defense chokes immediately. The Ravens effort on defense has been called into questions by former players and former coaches from very early on, that is a brutal indicator, and Wink Martindale said so much of the quiet part out-loud on “The Daily Flock” show weeks ago, with “business decisions being made on defense” in an acceptable way.
That was after the Bengals game, The distressing trend continued in the second half of the Jaguars game, multiple personnel execs who have studied Ravens film, contend, and their lack of effort and inability to get $20M-$30M defenders to show up is disgraceful.
“There are moments in the second half throughout the season where the defense quits in the second half,” said one exec who has advance scouted the Ravens this season. “It’s not an isolated thing. It’s right there. They see it. We all see it. They badly miss the Giants (Harbaugh) and Browns (former Ravens OC Todd Monken) head coaches in that building.”
Minter’s messaging has been suspect from the onset.
He is remarkably pragmatic, seems incapable of much emotion and has been the total opposite of a motivator for this roster. If anything, they seem to have taken on his stoicism and soft rhetorical style, and the fact Minter had to beg for a leader to emerge in October spoke volumes of the warped culture he is not improving in the least.
Calling Jackson’s high-ankle sprain a “day-to-day” situation for nearly three weeks was shameful. He lacks energy and verve in his press conferences; not making eye contact and looking down at his notes. His cheap talk about benching guys and lineup changes has not been backed up. He looks like someone desperate for help, deeply over his head, lacking the voice, confidence and conviction required of the horrible situation this franchise is in.
There isn't anything close to a Bad Cop on his staff and boy does that show every time the game starts.
“He’s trying to be a Harbaugh, but it’s not working,” one longtime NFL personnel exec noted very early on in Minter’s arrival and has continued to make the point. “He has to learn to be his own man and step up in his own way. It looks like he is going through the motions and trying to say what he thinks they would say. He wasn’t ready for this. He looks lost to me.”
The same veterans committ the same penalties week after week and Doyle's offense can't get the ball snapped on time or avoid…

title: Free-Falling Ravens Franchise Hits New  Lows In Loss To Winless Chargers. 4 Key Takeaways
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers were the worst team in football, and it was not particularly close.
The basically never played with a lead in 2026, let alone keep games tight. They had no discernable strength (losers of 11 in a row), they shocked the football world by not selling off players at the deadline after an 0-8 start and their season was over before the flew to Baltimore for a Monday night game. Still, there was reason to like their chances, with Ravens overmatched and outclassed head coach Jesse Minter lacking confidence and gravitas and much of clue, and his mentally soft football team hanging by a thread.
And so it stands to reason, that right now, with the Ravens (4-6) falling immediately behind the Chargers and unable to comeback, losing, 23-20 at M&T Bank Stadium , that this failure of a franchise is among the very worst in the NFL. This defeat cements everything warped and entitled and overhyped about the Ravens “football culture” throughout Eric DeCosta’s inglorious tenure as general manager. It laid all of their self-mythologizing to bare, and further exposed how naïve and callous it was to fire head coach John Harbaugh and replace him with sycophantic replacements who simply were not ready for the job, while DeCosta amassed unchecked power in the process.
This was a football humiliation, even with starting quarterback Lamar Jackson on Injured Reserve (he’s not throwing another pass this season as we told you all along ). The Chargers, who recently went 37 straight possessions without scoring, accomplished things they have not done all season; Baltimore is now 3-10 in its last 13 home games (losers of five straight home prime time games) and 6-10 in its last 16 overall.
"Not good enough," Minter said, defaulting to his usual rhetoric about the rot starting with him. if he has a strength as an NFL head coach it has yet to become anything close to obvious.
Quarterback Jacoby Brissett was as good as anyone could have hoped for thrust into a new team midseason after going three-and-out three straight times to start the game. But Zay Flowers’ fumble with about two minutes left negated any chance at a comeback. The Ravens were thrashed yet again at the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball, and this front office has been thoroughly exposed – not selling at the trade deadline another signal of their misguided hubris, and Derrick Henry ran 10 times for 10 yards.
Here’s what you need to know:
Whichever half Minter needs his defense to show up for, they wilt and collapse and walk all over him and make him look meek.
Monday, it was the first half, with the Ravens starting their fourth different quarterback in four weeks and with there going to be a learning curve with Brissett. So instead of bow up and show up against the worst defense in the NFL, of course Minter’s failure of a unit let LA march all over the field in the first quarter.
The Chargers took a fast 7-0 lead, with Justin Herbert carving them his legs and completing big passes when they needed it. They yielded repeated 10-yard runs and quarterback Justin Herbert capped the drive with a 22-yard TD run on third and long. Baltimore showed why it’s the worst third-and-long defense in the NFL., and could not get a sack when they needed it yet again (the Trey Hendrickson signing will go down as a massive failure for a GM who specializes in them).
"We let them off the hook," Minter said of the early mistakes.
The Ravens allowed 8.0 yards/play in the first quarter to quicky fall behind by two scores. The Chargers had not scored more than 10 points in the first half all season and rolled up 17 Monday. The Chargers had not led at the half all season, but of course they did here.
The Chargers have the worst OL in the NFL, Herbert was sacked eight times in his last game and 31 on the season and went down once at the line of scrimmage in the first half, caught from behind by Mike Green. And Green got to him late, but the Ravens could not win up front and allowed 160 rushing yards in the process.
The Ravens had zero rushing yards in the first half. When they tried to run the ball under center, $17M center Cam Jurgens was absolutely obliterated and tossed around. It was pretty ugly to watch, Jurgens was getting abused and rookie guard Vega Iaone, on the injured report quite a bit this season, was getting pushed around too before leaving with injury. Right tackle Roger Rosengarten’s blatant tripping attempt was a nice touch to open the second half.
“Jurgens is terrible,” one NFL personnel exec told me during the game. “You don’t have to wait for the film. He can’s handle strength or speed … He looks awful.”
The only chance this team has to run the ball came on sprint plays out of the pistol with Justice Hill. Keeping 32-year-old RB Derrick Henry at the trade deadline is going to go down as yet another ridiculous mistake from DeCosta. He has no chance behind this line, he is cut down behind the line of scrimmage with abandon and without Lamar Jackson creating with his legs Baltimore will not move this ball on anyone on the ground.
The line is an embarrassment to the organization. It should get DeCosta fired if nothing else . Frankly, that should have happened after three QBs got hurt in about 15 snaps in Buffalo a few weeks back.
HENRY AVERAGED -2 YARDS BEFORE CONTACT IN THE FIRST HALF. YOU READ THAT RIGHT. THAT HAPPENED!
"Too many missed chances in the run game on both sides of the ball," Minter said.
Close up shop. The yards before contact have somehow gotten horribly worse every week since DeCosta got fleeced by the Eagles to take Jurgens, who was getting benched, off their hands for a second-round pick before he was benched in Philly. (He was awful on some sacks, too).
Oh, and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has gotten pretty predictable, especially with the under center runs. “You can key on the under-center running game, so obvious,” one defensive coach from another team texted me during the game.
This head coach – hired to be a functionary for a power-hungry front office – came out last Monday with his notebook filled with talking points and made hints about benching people. He kinda sorta talked tough – as much as someone who has proven to be an utter pushover for his front office and locker room this far can – and then backed it up with nothing.
No messages were sent. It was essentially the same people doing the same things. He made one change – and we told you on “The Daily Flock Show” for a week we thought it was coming. He dropped Kyle Hamilton more in coverage, and he got destroyed by it.
The Chargers kept getting receiver Tre Harris matched up on Hamilton and he killed him on crossers. And he came up with a huge 31-yard sliding catch on an out. Harris had 85 scrimmage yards in the first half and it was often at Hamilton’s expense.
The offensive line isn’t just terrible, it’s penalty filled.  Doyle, an alleged “genius” during seven-on-seven drills, has the most penalized offense in the NFL and they also lead in pre-snap infractions, and we got plenty of that from the start Monday.
Struggling left tackle Ronnie Stanley – who also needed to be moved at the deadline – bookended the first half with holding penalties in critical spots. He negated Justice Hill’s 14-yard burst from Baltimore’s endzone (John Simpson got the call but it was Stanley’s penalty) and he negated Brissett’s scramble in the two-minute drill at the end of the half. Oh, and there was a delay-of-game in that two-minute drill as well, and of course they had a false start.
In a game that was going to be this close, and with Brissett already having to overcome so much, the rash of early penalties was too much.
"it was mostly self-inflicted things," Brissett said.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Five Pivotal Ravens Matchups to Watch vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens' Week 10 primetime bout against the Los Angeles Chargers could ultimately be decided by battles between specific position groups or individual players outperforming their counterparts on the other side of the ball.
In the team's first game with journeyman veteran Jacoby Brissett under center after he was acquired from the Arizona Cardinals via trade, they're entering this matchup as only slight favorites to come out on top over the last winless team in the league.
If the Ravens prevail, they will improve to 5-5 and will still be in last place in the AFC North standings since they're the only team without a division win. Here are the five  matchups that can either make or break this game:
Coming off back-to-back quiet games in which he was held without a catch for the first time in his career and a season low in scrimmage yards among games where he received a single touch with just 23 yards last week, the two-time Pro Bowler is primed and hungry to get back on track.
In games where he's gotten competent quarterback play, Flowers has been unstoppable, and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle should get back to trying to find ways to get him isolated in single coverage on off-ball linebackers over the middle of the field. However, the primary responsibility for limiting his impact will be the Chargers' Derwin James-less defensive backfield that got toasted for five passing touchdowns and allowed a pair of wideouts to eclipse 100 receiving yards last week.
Los Angeles has a pair of Pro Bowl edge rushers in Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu, both of whom have three sacks on the season and neither of whom was able to bring down Brissettt in the season-opener when he helped the Cardinals hand them the first of their eight straight losses. The motivated duo will be going up against the Ravens' tackle tandem of two-time Pro Bowl veteran Ronnie Stanley and third-year pro Roger Rosengarten, who held them both without a sack and a combined one quarterback hit between them the last time they played against each other in Week 12 of the 2024 season.
Going up against an offensive line and pass-blocking unit that just allowed Justin Herbert to get sacked a career-high eight times last week, the second-year pro has a chance to break his tie for the team lead in sacks with injured fourth-year pro Tavius Robinson. Since four-time Pro Bowler Trey Hendrickson lines up predominantly across from the left tackle, he'll be facing off with fellow Pro Bowler Joe Alt, which means Green will get to go up against fourth-round rookie Travis Burke, who has a pass-blocking grade of 56.1 from Pro Football Focus that ranks 61st out of 71 qualifying tackles.
During his last season and a half with the Cardinals, Brissett excelled at throwing over the middle of the field and heavily targeted the tight end position as he helped turn Trey McBride into a household name around the league. While the Ravens' resident multi-time Pro Bowler, Mark Andrews, is clearly on a steep decline, he can still be a solid possession option, while rookies Matt Hibner and Josh Cuevas can emerge and be utilized as more dynamic weapons on screens and stretching the seam of the defense. They'll be going up against a Chargers' off-ball linebacker tandem of Daiyan Henley, whom they attempted to trade last week, and former Ravens special teams ace Del'Shawn Phillips.
With the Chargers downgrading leading wide receiver Ladd McConkey to out for this matchup with a back injury, their top big-play threat in the passing game left standing is the big-bodied fourth-year pro. Johnston leads the team with 20 yards per catch but only has 13 receptions in eight games, as his inconsistent hands make him a boom-or-bust big-play target whenever the ball comes his way. Wiggins possesses the speed to run stride-for-stride with any receiver in the league and is physical at the catch point, making him the ideal one-on-one matchup to line up against Johnston in this game when Herbert looks to push the ball downfield.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and reporting. He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: Four Ravens X-Factors For Clash vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will continue the 2026 regular season with a second straight home primetime game in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Chargers . Going up against a winless opponent desperate to taste victory for the first time, the difference in the game could come down to how an individual player performs when it matters most or over the course of the game by capitalizing on opportunities when presented with them.
With a win, the Ravens would improve to 5-5 and would still be last in the AFC North division standings but would stay in the hunt for a wildcard playoff berth. A loss would be inexcusable and would drop their record further below .500.
Here are four players who could wind up tilting the scales in favor of the Ravens and first-year head coach Jesse Minter.
The Ravens have a new starter under center in veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett , whom they acquired in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals ahead of the deadline. During his time in the desert over the last season and a half, he helped two-time Pro Bowl tight end Trey McBride become a household name and earn First Team All Pro honors in 2025.
Projecting the Ravens' fourth-round rookie to be the next McBride is overly optimistic, but he shares some similar traits when it comes to his ability to rack up yards after the catch and threaten the seams of defenses vertically. While Brissett might be more inclined to target veteran Mark Andrews early and often, offensive coordinator Declan Doyle should have some plays schemed up to get the ball in Hibner's hands as the first or primary read.
Coming off a much-needed mini bye in which the coaches claimed to have done a lot of self-scouting, one of the shakeups that Minter all but vowed they'd make on defense should be playing the third-year pro more moving forward, starting in this game. Tampa has seen 20-plus snaps on defense in each of the Ravens' last two games since returning from injured reserve. Between his play in coverage, run support and being in the right place at the right time to recover a fumble in Week 8, he's shown he's deserving of a regular role as part of a rotation at outside corner at the expense of four-time Pro Bowl veteran Marlon Humphrey, whose recent struggles have come in too many high-leverage moments.
The Ravens' running game hasn't been the same since they lost veteran blocking tight end Durham Smythe to injury, and their attempts to have others step up and replace him haven't yielded the desired results. However, they might have the next best thing by deploying the second-year swing tackle more often in jumbo formations as an extra blocker on the end of the line. The chunk plays his blocks helped spring were some of the few impressive highlights from their last game, especially the one that resulted in running back Justice Hill for a 65-yard touchdown. Instead of forcing the issue with traditional 12 and 13 personnel, taking off Andrews or one of the young tight ends in favor of Vinson when they want to get the ground game going will tremendously aid in the effort.
Carson Vinson 👀 pic.twitter.com/SyI6piSQEV
Under first-year offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels, the Chargers dial screens on 10.2% of their dropbacks through Week 9, which is the ninth-highest rate in the league . This could lead to a very active game for the Ravens' fourth-year off-ball linebacker, who is a heat-seeking missile when coming downhill. Simpson can snuff out screens and checkdowns for tackles for loss and minimal gains and even spy the quarterback. Los Angeles' Justin Herbert is averaging 5.6 yards per rushing attempt through eight games and could be more prone to scrambling coming off a game in which he was sacked a career-high eight times.

title: These 4 Ravens Youngsters Must Take The Leap vs Chargers Monday Night
full_text:
The Ravens cannot lose to the Chargers Monday night.
Correction: the Ravens certainly could manage to lose to a previously-winless outfit at home on Monday night, they just can’t expect anything else they do this season to matter if that happens. Given their propensity to choke away games and with just three wins in their last 12 home games and having dropped four in a row in primetime at M&T Bank Stadium, there is certainly reason for concern.
The gravity of the situation weighed on rookie head coach Jesse Minter, who continues to look overmatched, and delivered strange messaging about Lamar Jackson’s thumb surgery . And who seemed to want to embrace being more of a bad cop, but he probably just doesn’t have it in him and he’s been thoroughly runover by a veteran roster to this point, begging questions about him and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle.
Minter hinted at changes in terms of playing time and roles, and, well, after failing to acknowledge the franchise’s sweeping and overarching roster failures at the trade deadline, stripping underperforming players of their role is about all Minter can do. And that must be happening at critical position groups on both sides of the ball, and a path must be created for more youngsters to make a bigger impact.
“I'm excited for us to sort of re-establish our identity,” Minter said last week. “[With] lineup changes, I think those are all individual basis. But there's certain things that we have to have really high standards for. So, we'll see how it all shakes out."
Let’s hope is shakes out with these young players getting more of an opportunity to impact the football game, starting now.
Feels like a long time ago that he was getting as much pre-season hype as any rookie in the NFL. Oh, it was constant . Keep in mind, the third-round pick was going against one of the most pathetic secondaries in the NFL in practice – no matter how heavily failing general manager Eric DeCosta over-drafted the DBs or overpaid them. So there’s that.
And the Ravens faced some preseason defenses that weren’t doing much. But we all know DeCosta’s track record drafting receivers is abysmal, which is why he’s talked about the need to keep swinging. With Jacoby Brissett at quarterback now, the ability to push the ball deep down the seam is there and Lane has clearly always been crafted to do most of his early damage in the slot. It’s time to see if they can unlock his kid a little bit and give him something positive to take into the offseason.
Injuries to him and to the QBs have sapped that early momentum.
No one stands to gain more than him from Brissett’s arrival. He has some of the attributed Trey McBride had in Arizona and McBride rewrote the NFL history books for TEs with Brissett. He’s back from his hand injury for a few weeks now, and needs to be unleashed from the slot, too. Play action deep shots , go routes, double moves.
This offense is utterly pathetic, it lacks any lack or verve outside of Zay Flowers and this fifth-round pick has some acceleration in his game. He should he unleashed against the Chargers linebackers and a secondary that is without All Pro hybrid defender Derwin James.
The coaching staff loves to hype him, but he’s had to play second-fiddle to $60M alleged-closer Trey Hendrickson ( a bust so far no matter how the Ravens want to couch it ) but he needs to get a real chance to rush from the inside and the outside. Especially if Henrickson is going to have his right hand wrapped up like crazy.
He’s tied for first on the team with 3.5 sacks – with injured Tavius Robinson – and has shown an ability to twist in the A Gap and make things happen. The Chargers interior offensive line is the dregs of the NFL and has been for years. Can we get him unleashed a little bit here in a creative manner?
If the Ravens are going to persists on running $19.3M corner Marlon Humphrey against top outside receivers, only to get shredded, then close up shop. He should have been a slot corner years ago; he can’t win outside and there is reason to think Justin Herbert has hit rock bottom for the Chargers and can only get better from here .
Tampa needs to get a chance to show what he can do. He’s healthy, which has been a real problem, and has the length and levers and profile to fit these zone concepts maybe more than some others who have played in front of him. The Chargers do not have a pass catcher with 300 yards or two touchdowns; seems like the perfect time to make this switch and start riding this kid after hyping him up as some kind of draft steal to the local media for years.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Jacoby Brissett Will Improve  Ravens Offense In These 3 Critical Areas
full_text:
Jacoby Brissett will give the Ravens an opportunity to operate a downfield passing game in ways they never could under Snoop Huntley.
As much as people in Owings Mills have pretended that Huntley is something he’s not, the reality is the scope of Baltimore’s passing game has crumbled when he has had to step in for Lamar Jackson over the years. And there is every reason to believe Jackson is not throwing another pass this season , and maybe never again in Baltimore. And therefore any hopes they have of mustering even a pedestrian pass game rest with the ability to keep Brissett upright; and with this offensive line, that’s going to be no small task .
Having to drop into a new locker room to try to save a season with coaches and players you do not know and in a system that is fairly foreign is a lot to ask anyone. Let alone someone about to turn 34 without great mobility who was just demoted to third-string in Arizona. But that’s where Brissett and the Ravens find themselves.
Brissett will absolutely improve their ability to facilitate certain parts of this offseason, and give them a fighting chance to try to find out what youngsters like Ja’Kobi Lane  and Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas can do catching the football .
He’s a gamer, and he won’t go down without a fight.
“I've been super impressed by him,” rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said, “just being able to work with him as he's picking up our offense very quickly, and also being able to provide a little bit of stability to the situation. But really excited about him being here and helping us."
Here’s where Brissett can help the Ravens the most:
Two of the core principles Doyle wanted to emphasize here have fallen totally by the wayside. The under-center running and passing game have washed away with Jackson not finishing a football game since Week 3 and the offensive line is once again one of the worst in the NFL. And with Huntley and then undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano thrust into duty, the play action pass game has faded away, too.
Brissett will lean into that heavily, and it should become more of a staple again.
Since Week 4, the Ravens have attempted just 38 play action passes, that’s 25th in the NFL. Those passes have averaged just 5.9 yards/attempt, that’s, frankly, pathetic and ranks 28th in the NFL since Week 4. And Ravens quarterbacks have completed just 55% of their play-action passes in that span, also 28th in the NFL.
All we heard all spring and summer long was that Doyle was a “genius” because his nascent playbook was loaded with “explosive” plays. This offense is desperate for them now, and getting Zay Flowers going again.
“He's been awesome,” Brissett said Doyle. “What he's thinking as far as the play structure and then obviously how we're attacking the defense, he's very vocal about it. I think that cleans up the communication. I know what he's thinking."
Brissett threw to tight ends more than any QB in the NFL during his two years in Arizona. More even than Jackson. He did it 33% of the time and helped dynamic TE Trey McBride take his game to historic levels . He doesn’t have that guy here, but it’s hard to think that Hibner, with the ability to win with some straight-line speed and a double move won’t become a favorite target if the Ravens do the right thing.
Getting Mark Andrews off the field and out of the way is the only thing to do with his mobility a detriment. They need to get these young TEs in the slot and get them running seam routes that Brissett loves to chuck downfield. Hibner was averaging 9.0 YAC/catch with Jackson in a very limited sample.
If Doyle wants to keep running 11 personnel and then wondering why he can’t run or throw the ball in the second half of games, then maybe he’s just over his head. Lane is even a Joker TE of sorts in the seam.
Brissett is going to throw it 20 yards or more downfield about 10 percent of the time and one of every three attempts with the Cardinals went at least 15 yards downfield – on par with league averages. He has a far bigger arm than Huntley. He isn’t afraid to throw it out of his own endzone.
He will force defenses to respect that and show it early in games to keep them honest in ways we just haven’t seen since Jackson hurt his ankle in early October. He also loves throwing crossers – Brissett had a 113.5 rating on those routes in Arizona – and that’s Flowers specialty coming across the face of the defense. Brissett also excels on outs – 79% completions and 103.9 rating with the Cardinals – and Flowers has been targeted on those routes more than any other.
"We all know he can throw the ball," Flowers said. "He can spin it. But he's just been connecting with us, telling us how he feels about a route, where we should be [and] talking to 'D-Hen' about certain things coming out of the backfield. So, he's just letting his experience show."
Flowers shouldn’t be getting shutout in the boxscore anymore.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Tre'Davious White's Inevitable Return to Bills' Lineup May Be Closer Than You Think
full_text:
Tre Day is on the horizon this holiday season.
Although the actual date is not yet known, the Buffalo Bills appear close to deploying veteran cornerback Tre'Davious White for game action.
"I think he's really close to being able to help us. We had some injuries here this last game, if need be, I think he's ready to step up and play for us," said Bills' defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard on Monday following the Week 10 win over the New York Jets.
White, a 2017 first-round draft pick who has been with the Bills for nine of his 10 seasons, last appeared during the team's divisional round road loss to the Denver Broncos last January.
Garnering limited interest on the free-agent market, the 31-year-old White eventually took the opportunity to return to Orchard Park for one more crack at winning a Lombardi. He officially signed on October 19 as the Bills embarked on their Week 7 bye.
Although seemingly content with starting off as a practice squad player, one has to think White didn't come off the couch to sit back and watch others play the position he has mastered.
White's first practice was on October 28 as the Bills began preparations for a November 1 home game against the Baltimore Ravens.
Having not had the benefit of a training camp, the grizzled veteran recognizes he may need a little extra practice time to ramp up.
"This was a different kind of offseason for me. I've been sitting on the couch, drinking ginger ale and eating popcorn for a while," said White while appearing on Eric Wood's Centered On Buffalo podcastlast month. "I got so much respect for the position, I'd disrespect the position just thinking I can just come off the couch and come out there and be Tre White."
A reasonable four-week ramp up puts a potential debut around the November 26 game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.
“Anytime you kind of onboard some veteran players as the season goes on, that's part of the process is how many plays do you think you could play right now? I like where he's at," said Leonhard.
Physically speaking, White appeared to have enough tread left on his tires when he unexpectedly made 16 regular season starts for the Bills in 2025 as first-round draft pick Max Hairston began his rookie year on Injured Reserve.
"I thought he played really good football at the end of last season," said head coach Joe Brady on Wednesday. "Genetically, he's kind of a freak. A guy that can kinda roll out of bed, and maybe not do it as much for a long time, and still look like a guy that was a first-round pick for a reason."
Furthermore, White, who built a reputation for being a true student of the game early on in his Bills' tenure, has reached an experience level that makes Buffalo comfortable with deploying him when needed .
"I got the confidence that whenever that time does come, and Tre White has to be up, there's gonna be no holding the breath, because I know he's so calm, cool collected, he's ready to go," said Brady.
With Buffalo somewhat banged up in the defensive secondary following the November 15 road win, the time may come as early as this Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.
Starting boundary cornerback Christian Benford and slot cornerback Dee Alford both left the Week 10 road game due to injuries and never returned.
Benford is dealing with a groin injury , which is usually more than a day-to-day issue. Alford was ruled out against the Jets after being evaluated for a concussion .
After second-round rookie starter Davison Igbinosun and the aforementioned Hairston, the Bills have no other true outside cornerbacks on their 53-man roster. Meanwhile, nickel cornerback Jordan Hancock is the next man up behind Alford.
Simply put, Buffalo will most likely need at least one more cornerback on the Week 11 game day roster, and an obvious option in the elevate White.

title: New Bills 2027 Mock Draft Upgrades Buffalo's Offensive Line
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' general manager Brandon Beane deserves credit for the work he's done this year. While he did completely whiff on CJ Gardner-Johnson, he made up for that by adding Amani Hooker at the NFL trade deadline.
This was after adding DJ Moore in a trade with the Chicago Bears during the offseason. While Moore hasn't put up elite numbers, he's been a difference-maker when healthy and has helped the offense with several big plays.
Both those players are under contract in 2027 as well, which means Beane won't need to fill two positions that have been considered needs for several years. Instead, he can look for upgrades elsewhere, which is what NFL Draft On SI's Justin Melo has him doing in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
With their top pick, which Melo has at No. 32 overall, the Bills take Notre Dame guard Anthoine Knapp . Melo praises Knapp's hand usage and anchor, while saying he could be an upgrade over current left guard, Alec Anderson.
"The Buffalo Bills acquired safety Amani Hooker at the trade deadline. Hooker is under contract for several more seasons, crossing 'safety' off Brandon Beane's offseason to-do list,"  Melo wrote. "We turn our attention to left guard, where starter Alec Anderson can be upgraded on. Notre Dame's Anthonie Knapp protects the interior with a strong anchor and well-developed hand usage."
The 6-foot-5, 305-pound actually played left tackle for the first two seasons of his career. He played well in that role, surrendering four sacks as a freshman and just one during his sophomore campaign. This year, he moved inside to left guard and his play has vastly improved.
Knapp has given up six pressures and no sacks in 322 pass protection snaps. He's also been a weapon in the run game, earning a 74.4 in run blocking through his first 10 games of the season.
As for Anderson, he hasn't been bad by any means this season. He enters Week 11 with a PFF rating of 62.3 overall , which is 37th out of 77 qualified guards. He has, however, had issues in the pass game. Anderson has a pass-protection grade of 50.5 while allowing 14 pressures and two sacks.
Anderson has been a decent starter and the Bills would be more than comfortable turning to him again in 2027. Of course, with Anderson set for free agency, Buffalo could decide to go with a more affordable rookie and Knapp could be a major upgrade.

title: Three Rookies Giving Bills Much Needed Midseason Boost
full_text:
After slow starts to their rookie campaigns, several of the Buffalo Bills ' 2026 draft picks are beginning to make a consistent impact for the team.
As the defense continues to improve , build chemistry and gain time on task against inferior QBs, three defensive rookies have emerged as impactful players that Joe Brady and Jim Leonhard will be able to count on.
Sunday's win over the Jets solidified three defensive rookies as important starters or role players for Buffalo's defense moving forward.
Igbinosun has asserted himself as an aggressive, playmaking cornerback opposite Christian Benford. After playing a combined 57 defensive snaps through the first three weeks of the season, the second round pick has been above 80% of snaps in five of the last six games.
The uptick in playing time is for good reason, too. The Ohio State product currently leads all rookies with 11 pass breakups (including two on Sunday against the Jets), which also happens to be the third most among all players this season.
Prior to Sunday's game against the Jets, Igbinosun ranked eighth in lockdown coverage rate , right behind players like Trent McDuffie, Denzel Ward and Derek Stingley. His 84.4 impact score from Pro Football Network led all rookie DBs at the halfway point of the season.
After the pass defense suffered a rough start to the season, Igbinosun is firmly locked in place as a cornerstone of the secondary that continues to improve each week.
Echoing what I wrote about in my rookie report card at the end of October, the plan with Parker was never for him to play a majority of snaps in Year 1. The investments in Bradley Chubb and Michael Hoecht  to pair with Greg Rousseau left an uphill climb for Buffalo's first pick in 2026.
Well, Parker may be on an accelerated course. He's tallied three sacks over the last three weeks, while hovering around the 50% mark for defensive snaps played in that stretch. His eight QB pressures in that three-game span double the amount he had in the first six games of the season.
Parker is slowly emerging as a reliable edge rusher faster than anticipated. While his sack numbers should regress to the mean in the coming weeks, his consistent pressure numbers would be a welcome sign for an edge rush room desperate for more contribution opposite Rousseau.
Buffalo's fourth-round pick quietly saw his highest snap share of the season last week, 35.2% against the Jets. On 25 defensive snaps, he recorded two tackles, a fumble recovery, and allowed zero catches in coverage. He also continued his streak of not been charged with a missed tackle yet this year, a rare feat for a rookie linebacker.
The path for Elarms-Orr to start is murky. Dorian Williams continues to make impact plays, recording a sack, INT, or fumble recovery in each of the last four games. However, the coaching staff is beginning to put more on the rookie's plate, playing over a quarter of defensive snaps in four straight games.
Whether it's three linebacker sets in short yardage and goal line packages, one of Williams or Terrel Bernard needing a breather, or more of a consistent rotation between the off-ball linebackers, expect Elarms-Orr to continue finding himself around the football and making plays in the middle of the field.

title: Bills' AFC Playoff Picture Overview: Remaining No. 1 Is Top Priority vs. Dolphins
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are right where they want to be in terms of the conference standings through the NFL's season first 10 weeks.
Now, the challenge is to stay there.
The Bills (8-1) currently own the AFC's No. 1 seed as the only one-loss team amongst the conference's 16 clubs. The three other division leaders all sit at 7-2 overall.
Bills' starting left tackle Dion Dawkins, a 2017 second-round draft pick, has never experienced the No. 1 seed, and the New Jersey native is focused on changing that this year .
"That's where I want to see the Buffalo Bills," said Dawkins. "I don't want nobody's season to dictate our standings. I want to know where we are going to be by ourself. I don't want that stress of, did they win? Did they lose? I don't want that. I want it to be like we handled our business, we know exactly where we're going to be.”
The Bills will have the opportunity to take care of their own business and earn potential head-to-head tiebreakers over both the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos later this season.
As for the AFC East race, there's a real possibility that Buffalo clinches the crown, and the automatic playoff berth that comes with it, by Week 13. Naturally, it will require a head-to-head win over the New England Patriots (5-5) on December 6 along with a couple other occurrences .
Here's an overview of how the Bills fit into the AFC playoff picture with the Miami Dolphins for to visit Orchard Park for a Week 11 divisional game on November 22.

title: Bills' Calculated Move Opens Roster Spot for Mid-Season WR Addition Tyrell Shavers
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills placed seventh-round rookie guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams onto Injured Reserve on Tuesday, but there's likely more behind the move than one may initially surmise.
Reed-Adams must miss at least the next four weeks before becoming eligible to re-join the active roster.
Giving an IR designation to Reed-Adams opens up a spot on the Bills' 53-man roster, and it just so happens they could use some roster flexibility this week with wide receiver Tyrell Shavers set to come off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list .
The Bills initially listed Reed-Adams on the official injury report in Week 3 due to an elbow issue, and he's remained there since. The seventh-round rookie made his NFL debut in Week 9 against the Minnesota Vikings, seeing three snaps. He was a game day inactive for the eighth time in Week 10.
Reed-Adams has been a full participant in practice since Week 4, but it seems possible he could've experienced a setback that led the Bills to stash him on IR.
Shavers, who has been out since January, began practicing on October 28 , meaning his 21-day activation window will close this week, if Buffalo chooses to not make a move.
After signing with the Bills as an undrafted rookie in, Shavers spent back-to-back seasons on the team's practice squad.
Seeing three appearances as a game day call-up in 2024, Shavers took his first career reception 69 yards for a touchdown in the regular season finale against the New York Jets.
Making the active roster out of training camp, Shavers played in all 17 games during the 2025 regular season. He recorded a 39 percent snap share on offense, hauling in 15 of 23 targets for 245 yards and one touchdown.
“A guy like Tyrell Shavers is what you want to build your team around, like the personality, the mindset," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady as the wide receiver returned to the practice field last month. "I think he's attacked the return to play. He's been outstanding. l'm excited to let him go play football today."
With veteran Josh Palmer on IR, the 27-year-old Shavers is likely to be treated as the Bills' fourth wide receiver ahead of fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell and return specialist Greg Dortch.
Shavers left his peers in awe by playing an entire half with a torn ACL during the wildcard playoff win over the Jacksonville Jaguars last January.
"He's got one of the best stories out there," said quarterback Josh Allen. "Just how he bounced around in college, coming here, being a P squad guy, not really getting opportunities, and finally getting his opportunities, and making the most of them. Getting injured, fighting back, and now he's back out here practicing. He's one of the best teammates I've ever had."
In addition to his contributions to the wide receiver room, Shavers emerged as a core special teamer in 2025. He totaled 241 special teams reps over 17 regular season games.

title: Bills Bring Back Familiar Face at CB, Move Rookie OL to Injured Reserve
full_text:
Te'Cory Couch was a surprising standout for the Buffalo Bills during their Week 8 victory over the Baltimore Ravens .
With CJ Gardner-Johnson out due to a suspension , Couch was signed from the practice squad and proved worthy of playing snaps in the slot.
His role with the team didn't last long, unfortunately, as he was released ahead of the Bills' road game against the New York Jets. Buffalo decided to move on from Couch after Jordan Hancock came off the IR.
Thankfully, Couch was not claimed on waivers and on Tuesday, the Bills announced he was back as a member of their practice squad. To make room for Couch, Buffalo released guard Nick Broeker from the squad. They also placed rookie seventh-round pick Ar'Maj Reed-Adams on the IR.
Roster moves: - Signed DB Te’Cory Couch to the practice squad - Released G Nick Broeker from the practice squad - Placed G Ar’maj Reed-Adams on the Injured Reserve list
Adams played in just three snaps this season, all againt the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9. Leading up to Week 10, Reed-Adams was dealing with back and elbow issues, which ultimatley landing him on the reserve.
Broeker was on his fourth stint with the Bills, originally signing with them in 2023 as an undrafted free agent. He returned in 2025 and again in 2026. He was released by the Bills in September and signed by the Tennessee Titans. The Titans released him in October, and Broeker returned on Nov. 11.
Couch originally signed as an undrafted free agent in 2024 out of Miami but didn't make his debut until this season. He's played in four games, two as a practice squad elevation and two after being signed to the active roster on October 31 . In those appearances, Couch has eight tackles, five of which were against the Ravens.
He's eligible to be called up one more time and that could very well happen given the injuries Buffalo continues to have in the secondary. It also helps that Couch has earned the trust and praise of defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard.
"Te'Cory Couch had a great game," said Leonhard via Bills On SI's Ralph Ventre . "He went in there and executed really at a high level, communication and just winning some one-on-ones."
If Buffalo were to call him up a third time, they would then need to sign Couch to the active roster if they wanted to make him active in any more games.

title: Spencer Brown Goes from Doubtful to Dominant for Bills vs. Jets' Prized Rookie
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' starting right tackle Spencer Brown faced long odds to become available during a short week.
With Brown not practicing, the Bills were preparing to face a New York Jets' defensive front headlined by No. 2 overall draft pick David Bailey coming off the edge in Week 10.
Furthermore, Alec Anderson, who filled in so admirably last year when Brown was unavailable against the Pittsburgh Steelers and TJ Watt, is now the starting left guard.
Not that the Bills didn't trust sturdy swing tackle Tylan Grable, but Brown is much more equipped to deal with an elite edge rusher.
"That's why, given the opportunity, and if he felt like he can go, he was going to give us the best opportunity to go. He's played so much football for us, and I got all the trust in him to not be able to get the practice. So, like I said, Bailey is going to be a problem in this division for a long time," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady after the 31-12 road win .
After seemingly having gotten past a back flare-up that kept him sidelined in Week 8, Brown picked up a new injury in Week 9 on Monday Night Football. He tweaked his ankle blocking for a rushing attempt on Buffalo's second possession of the game in Minnesota.
Brown, who fought through the entire 23-6 win over the Vikings in Week 9, didn't sound like someone intending to miss time.
"I'm just playing football right now. It's a tough sport. That's why I play it. That's why I love to play it. I look forward to next week and getting back out there again," said Brown in the postgame locker room.
Although he failed to practice leading up to the Week 10 road game, the Bills were holding onto a glimmer of hope hence the doubtful designation on the final injury report . As it turned out, Brown's warrior mentality paid dividends.
"We were hopeful of it. Maybe that's the competitor in him. Then, we put him through a workout this morning, and he felt like he was going to be okay," said Brady. "It was obviously a surprise to me. Not him having that mindset, but I was a little surprised that he'd wake up and felt a little bit better enough to kind of roll with it."
Brown played every offensive snap until catching a breather during the final three kneel-downs. He was practically perfect in protection against Bailey, and he helped spring James Cook for a 74-yard touchdown run.
"I knew it wasn't going to be just a day off coming out here with a bum ankle, but yeah, he's a good player and I look forward to going against him again," said Brown.
According to Next Gen Stats, Brown did not allow a pressure in 13 pass rush reps against Bailey, who entered the game with 7.5 sacks, five forced fumbles and 12 quarterback hits to his credit.
"To be able to go out there and be able to just execute against him without really getting ready for anything, it's a testament to kind of who Spencer is," said Brady.

title: Ex-NFL QB Channels Inner Chris Berman With Bills-Inspired Super Bowl LXI Prediction
full_text:
For years, longtime ESPN sports commentator Chris Berman had a running schtick for his annual Super Bowl prediction at the beginning of the NFL season.
Regardless of the actual outlook, Berman—who has always appeared to have a soft spot for Western New York—would choose the Buffalo Bills and the San Francisco 49ers as his pick for the big game when appearing on shows such as Sunday NFL Countdown or Monday Night Countdown .
Eventually, though, those crystal ball visions that pictured the 49ers and Bills paired up at the end of each season seemed less and less realistic, especially during the drought years of the early 2000s.
For the current 2026 campaign, though? Well, it wouldn’t seem so outlandish . . . and one other analyst is apparently hopping on the nostalgic hype train that Berman was once the lead conductor of.
According to former NFL quarterback turned analyst Dan Orlovsky, who recently made an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Monday, the teams with the top two records in the NFL at the current moment—Buffalo (8-1) and San Francisco (8-1)—will be the two squads that represent the AFC and NFC in Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, 2027.
“In the AFC—on November 16th—I’m going to select the Buffalo Bills. And, then in the NFC I would select San Francisco,” Dan Orlovsky said on air on Monday.
"I'm going to select the Buffalo Bills and the San Francisco 49ers.. That's who I think is gonna be in the Super Bowl right now" ~ @danorlovsky7 #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/eNmtPC2RHB
“A Buffalo-San Francisco Super Bowl would be awesome.”
While some might not think the prediction from Orlovosky is all that intriguing or bold, particularly due to the standings in both conferences entering Week 11, it’s definitely an outcome that would be an overwhelmingly welcomed sight amongst Bills Mafia, who haven’t seen their beloved Bills in the NFL’s pinnacle game since the 1993-1994 season.
And, after reaching its best record since 1991—another year the team happened to also reach the Super Bowl—following last Sunday’s divisional road victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, fans certainly have plenty of reasons to be optimistic about Buffalo’s playoff chances later on this winter.
Led by former 2024 MVP quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook III, who is second in the NFL right now in total rushing yards ( 971 yds ), the Bills boast the league’s highest-scoring offense ( 31.9 PPG ) heading into the latter portions of November, which is right ahead of San Francisco ( 31.2  PPG ).
The one thing that might hold Buffalo back during its chase toward championship glory, however, is its defense, which is still only tied for 13th in the NFL right now at 22.1 points allowed per game despite having three straight matchups this month where Jim Leonhard’s previously struggling unit has given up 12 points or less to opposing offenses in each contest.
In the end, the hope is that the recent addition of veteran safety Amani Hooker prior to the trade deadline , along with an uptick in production from other specific players on that side of the ball, can help the Bills continue on their current path all the way to California in February.
Only time will tell, though.
