title: Frustrated Joe Brady Admits One of Bills' Biggest Issues is 'Embarrassing'
full_text:
Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady is clearly frustrated with one particular issue that has plagued his team all season long.
That issue is penalties, and more specifically, pre-snap penalties. In Week 10 alone, the Bills were flagged 10 times in total, with seven of those being accepted. Nine of those penalties came before the snap.
On Monday, Brady touched on that issue and is at the point where he believes it's "embarrassing."
"It's embarrassing," Brady said of the Bills' issue with penalties.
“We’ve had two weeks in a row with special teams pre-snap penalties,” Brady added. “We had defensive penalties pre-snap (against the Jets). You guys know how I feel about penalties within the scheme of the game, and we’ve got to get the play started.”
Luckily for the Bills, they've been able to overcome their many infractions, but that doesn't mean Brady isn't concerned.
“Those are the things where it’s not winning football,” Brady said. “Whether we’re able to overcome (penalties) or not doesn’t make them right. We’re making it too hard on ourselves."
The Bills' issues with penalties extend beyond just Week 10. It has been a problem all season long.
According to NFLPenalties.com , the Bills rank sixth in total flags with 88, and of those 88, 76 have been accepted, which is the seventh-highest mark. Something to keep in mind with those marks is the Bills have a handful of teams ahead of them that haven't had a bye week yet like they have.
When it comes to pre-snap penalties, the Bills rank 10th with 29, but again, five teams with more have played in 10 games to Buffalo's nine.
This is something the Bills can definitely get away with far more often than not during the regular season, but they won't be so fortunate once the playoffs roll around and the competition is tougher, so it goes without saying this must be cleaned up.
It really comes down to being more disciplined and improving both fundamentals and technique, Brady said earlier in the season .
"We've got to be more disciplined, and it's almost, it's kind of a lot of different position groups, too," said Brady. "Our fundamentals and technique have to improve."
Some have wondered if Brady's coaching style is a cause for the lack of discipline that leads to more penalties, but this is an issue Buffalo had during the Sean McDermott era , also.
The Bills ranked seventh in penalties accepted against them in 2023 and 2024, and then improved to 13th last season.
In that same span, the Bills did not have as big an issue with pre-snap flags in 2023 and 2025, totaling 37 and 32 in those seasons, but they tallied a whopping 50 in 2024.

title: NFL Week 11 Power Rankings Roundup: Bills Remain High Despite Questions
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are on quite a run as they are now 8-1 and own the No. 1 seed in the AFC . They’ve also had some help over the past few weeks due to injuries suffered by their opponents.
Buffalo knocked off the Baltimore Ravens with Joe Fagnano taking the majority of the snaps with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffering injuries. The following game was against another backup as Carson Wentz filled in for an injured Kyler Murray when the Bills took on the Minnesota Vikings.
In Week 10 against the New York Jets , they saw a good bit of Cade Klubnik, with Geno Smith getting knocked out of the game . Buffalo can’t help who its opponents are, but the level of play they’ve faced has some questioning their viability. That said, they still stand atop most Week 11 NFL power rankings.
Connor Orr saw enough to move the Bills up one spot and praised Josh Allen for the way he keeps scoring touchdowns at a high rate.
"I thought New York City sports talk radio had an interesting response to the idea that if Josh Allen got hit like Geno Smith did, every flag on the field would have been thrown (as Aaron Glenn suggested to referees on Sunday): Actually, Allen would have probably already been in the end zone. So it wouldn’t have even come to this," Orr wrote.
ESPN oddly had the Bills falling from No. 1 to No. 2 after beating the struggling New York Jets by 19. Meanwhile, they were surpassed by the San Francisco 49ers, who beat the struggling Dallas Cowboys by six and surrendered 40 points.
They don't dive into the explanation, but instead, Nick Suss discusses the team's top non-quarterback MVP. For the Bills, Suss says that title belongs to Greg Rousseau.
"The transition from 4-3 defensive end to 3-4 outside linebacker has worked wonders for Rousseau. He is in the midst of a career season, leading the NFL in quarterback pressures (41) and quarterback hits (27). He is also tied for fourth in sacks (eight). Just over halfway through the season, Rousseau has already matched or set career highs in just about every meaningful pass rushing or defending stat," Suss wrote.
Once again, Josh Kendall and Chad Graff of The Athletic have the Bills at No. 1. They decided to highlight every breakout player for each team in their rankings, and again, Rousseau was the choice. Although, they also gave some kudos to wide receiver Keon Coleman.
"The sixth-year outside linebacker has been good for a long time. He’s trending toward great this year and has already tied his career high in sacks with eight, which ranks fourth in the league. Third-year wide receiver Keon Coleman is also on track for career highs in yards and catches. Despite just one reception for 11 yards (and one concussion check) on Sunday, Coleman has 24 catches for 315 yards."
Nick Shook discussed the level of competition as of late, but says the Bills still deserve credit for taking care of business the way they have.
“Look, I know the Bills’ recent victories aren’t of the chest-thumping, braggadocious quality. In their last three, they took down the Joe Fagnano-led Ravens, the Carson Wentz-led Vikings and the lowly Jets. But there’s something to be said about a top team simply taking care of business,” Shook wrote.
Moe Moton kept the Bills at No. 1 and he sees them wrapping up the division by the holidays.
"I ranked the Buffalo Bills No. 1 in these rankings last week, and that didn't change after they went on the road and thumped the New York Jets. Buffalo has faced backup quarterbacks Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz and Cade Klubnik over the previous three weeks and will face Kyle McCord in Week 11," Moton wrote.
"Expect the Bills to continue their dominance for their sixth straight win and remain atop the power rankings. With all of the New England Patriots' recent injuries, Buffalo could be the first team to claim a division title shortly after Thanksgiving."
Again, the QB question comes up here, but Pete Prisco says the schedule coming up will help answer a lot of questions about this defense.
"The defense has played better the past three weeks, but they've faced a lot of backup quarterbacks. The schedule toughens up in the coming weeks," Prisco wrote.

title: Bryce Young’s Stats Have Dipped, But NFL Analyst Rightfully Points Finger Elsewhere
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have seen a decline in quarterback Bryce Young's statistics as of late, resulting in criticism from some analysts. However, according to NFL analyst Brent Sobleski, there is another aspect of the offense that is currently being overlooked.
Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski is taking a look at some of the key takeaways from Week 10 of NFL play. He takes a look at the struggles of Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young. While his numbers have been on the decline as of late, the offensive line and the pass protection they are providing the quarterback also deserve attention.
Young started the season strong with 11 touchdowns through the first six games of the season and just two interceptions. In those games, Young seemed to be getting better as the season progressed and looked to be the Panthers' answer at quarterback that they were hoping for when they drafted him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 draft.
This season has been somewhat of a regression for the fourth-year quarterback. He had a three-touchdown game against the Broncos in Week 9, but outside of that, he has struggled. He has been under 57% completion in four of the last five games.
In the win over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Young threw for 200 yards on 17-of-30 passing. He threw no touchdowns and no interceptions, but helped lead the Panthers to a game-winning field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. The passing game, however, still has a lot of room for improvement.
While the quarterback has some responsibility for getting the ball out sooner, the offensive line has to be able to protect him on passing plays. Through nine games this season, Young has been sacked 29 times, more than the 27 sacks he suffered during the entire 2025 season.
For the most part, the offensive line has been a mess with injuries and inconsistency all season. Many of Young's problems can be blamed on him holding onto the ball too long at times, but he cannot be expected to play well on passing plays when he is constantly being harassed by opposing defenses.
This has been an issue for the Panthers as of late as well. In the game against the Buccaneers, Young was sacked five times. In the game against the Packers, he was sacked six times. In those games, it was clear that the Panthers were not giving the quarterback enough protection to make things happen on the field.
As Sobleski explained in his Week 10 breakdown of the Panthers , Young's sack total is a major part of the conversation when evaluating his recent passing numbers. The same issue was highlighted in an earlier On SI breakdown of the numbers behind Young's sack problems.
Carolina can improve Young's passing game, but in addition to improving the passing game, the Panthers need to address the problems with the offensive line. Young is having a hard time developing a passing game when he is constantly under pressure from the defense.
Carolina can help Young by finding ways to make things easier for its young quarterback. This can be done by providing better protection, having Young get the ball out quicker or using the running game to help take pressure off him.
The Panthers are coming off a big division win over New Orleans, but there is still plenty of room for improvement on offense. Young has shown that he can play at a much higher level, but the Panthers must find a way to help protect their quarterback.
While Young has had plenty of mistakes to account for in the last few games, it would be unfair to put all of the blame on his shoulders. The offensive line has been just as concerning, and Carolina has several issues to fix before the team can reach its full potential.

title: The Panthers Managed a Win, But More Is Needed Moving Forward
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers ' first win since October 18th wasn't pretty; the offense managed just 20 points and just 200 passing yards from Bryce Young. That doesn't mean Young had a bad performance against the Saints; it just wasn't spectacular.
Panthers OnSI's Mark Livingston gave Young a C+ for his performance against New Orleans, doing just enough to secure a win. Chuba Hubbard carried the Panthers on Sunday, having the best game of his career. Hubbard posted 172 scrimmage yards, and both of Carolina's touchdowns
It's a game where penalties were the biggest talking point for Carolina afterward, and it's certainly not the first time a Panthers game has been defined by penalties .
After each week, various power rankings will be released, and teams will be ranked accordingly based on their weekend results and their performance throughout the entire season thus far. The Panthers rose on basically every power ranking one can find, yet, there's still major skepticism, and rightfully so.
Bleacher Report dropped its Week 11 NFL power rankings on Monday, and those rankings featured the Panthers rising to No. 16, a two-spot improvement from last week's No. 18 slot.
In explaining Carolina's ranking, the win itself matters most, but Bleacher Report's Moe Moton remains aware that the Panthers have a low ceiling. His argument focuses on Bryce Young's dip in production; since Week 6, Young has dropped from top-two in passing yards per game to now being No. 6.
Another point that Moton pointed to, the offensive line has crumbled, and that's a major reason that the Carolina passing game isn't thriving like it was for the first month of the season.
Carolina has surrendered at least 3 sacks per game in the last four weeks. Expanding on that point, Rasheed Walker is among the league leaders in pressures allowed at left tackle, with 45 surrendered so far.
The Panthers have to find more consistency in the pass blocking, the first four weeks of the season, Carolina posted over 30 points three out of four games, and Young was sacked 10 times in those four weeks.
Carolina hasn't scored more than 30 points since Week 4 against Detroit. Since Week 7, another four-game stretch, Young has been sacked 17 times, including back-to-back games where he was sacked 5+ times.
It may sound repetitive, it may be beating a broken drum, but the offensive inconsistency truly begins and ends up front.

title: Panthers' Bryce Young Earns C+ Grade After Win Over Saints
full_text:
Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski has been tracking the play of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young throughout the season. Following Carolina's 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Sobleski gave Young a C+ grade for his performance against the Saints. Young threw for 200 yards on 17-of-30 passing with no touchdowns and no interceptions in the win.
A huge part of why the Panthers were able to win was the offense's final two possessions, according to Sobleski. Carolina was able to go 98 yards and score 10 points on the final two possessions. On the first of those two drives, Young threw a pair of passes to Chuba Hubbard for 29 and 34 yards, setting up the running back for a 1-yard touchdown run to give Carolina a 17-14 lead with 1:49 left in the game.
After the Saints had tied the game up with a field goal on their next drive, the Panthers' offense got the ball back with a chance to win the game. After moving down the field for a potential long field goal, a pass interference penalty was called on Kool-Aid McKinstry. Fitzgerald made the 54-yard field goal as time expired to give the Panthers the win.
Despite his subpar numbers against the Saints, the Panthers' passing attack still needs to improve. Young threw no touchdowns on the day, but did not turn the ball over in the win. His connection with Hubbard on the late touchdown drive was key in the Panthers' win.
While Young received a C+ grade against the Saints, the grade does not completely reflect his play throughout the season. He has had some ugly games, but has also shown the ability to be a very competent passer on numerous occasions. He needs to continue to build on those better performances and display his ability to play at that level on a more consistent basis.
Carolina is still in the thick of things in the NFC South, but the Panthers need more from quarterback Bryce Young. Even when things aren't going well, the offense needs to keep moving, and Young is a big part of that. There is still plenty of room for Young to grow as a passer, and Carolina needs to see more consistency from him as the season continues.
There have been some great moments this season, but the Panthers need to see that talent more consistently.
On SI previously took a look at Bryce Young's recent statistical regression, but that doesn't mean that the Panthers' quarterback has completely stopped growing as a player this season. There are plenty of games left for Young to prove that he can be a more consistent quarterback for the Carolina Panthers.

title: Panthers Could Save Millions and Upgrade Offensive Line With First-Round Draft Pick
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers will have a lot of decisions to make this offseason with regards to their offensive line. Even though they have spent a great deal of money to protect quarterback Bryce Young, the unit has had trouble keeping pressure away from him throughout the 2026 season.
This may result in some changes when the offseason comes around. CBS Sports' Josh Edwards has the Carolina Panthers picking Minnesota interior offensive lineman Greg Johnson with the 19th pick in the 2027 NFL Mock Draft. This would provide the Panthers with another option up front and create the possibility for the team to part ways with one of its highest-paid players.
Edwards feels that the Panthers may look into parting ways with right guard Robert Hunt this offseason, which could save the team $14 million in regards to the salary cap. Hunt signed a five-year, $100 million deal with the Panthers in 2024 and was named to the 2025 Pro Bowl Games following that season.
However, his play in 2026 has brought up many questions regarding the future of the position. The Panthers have had numerous issues throughout their offensive line, and Edwards stated that the unit had the second-highest pressure rate allowed in the NFL this season, according to TruMedia.
Young has demonstrated that he can make plays when things are going well offensively; however, consistent protection remains crucial if the Panthers hope to continue to take steps forward.
The Panthers have already made substantial investments into their offensive line. As On SI pointed out previously in its article on the expensive offensive line for the Panthers, the Panthers have invested heavily into providing a strong group around Young. Improving the interior of the line without increasing the investment significantly may be a key component of the offseason plans.
Johnson is listed as a 6-foot-6, 325-pound senior interior offensive lineman from Minnesota. He is ranked by Edwards as the No. 14 overall prospect and the second-ranked player at his position in this mock draft.
Edwards thinks Johnson can help stabilize the Panthers' offensive line. If Carolina opts to move on from Hunt, selecting a first-round guard would provide the team with a potential replacement while creating further salary-cap flexibility.
It is uncertain what direction Carolina will decide to go in terms of moving on from Hunt or if Johnson will be available when Carolina picks. The mock draft is simply an initial projection, and many things can occur between now and the 2027 NFL Draft. Regardless, using a first-round pick to address the interior is something to consider considering the issues Carolina has faced up front.
The Panthers also need to assess other needs prior to determining how they should proceed. Their offensive line has been a prominent subject of conversation throughout the season, and questions regarding potential changes to the starting group have already begun to emerge. On SI recently reported that the Panthers could consider changes to their offensive line.
Carolina must determine if their current offensive line can provide Young with enough protection moving forward. While they have invested heavily into their group, the results have not always met that level of commitment.
Parting ways with Hunt would be a big decision, especially since Carolina signed him to a large contract in 2024. However, the potential salary-cap savings could allow general manager Dan Morgan more room to operate on other parts of the roster.
While selecting Johnson in the first round won't solve all of the problems up front, it provides Carolina with another young player to develop. If Carolina believes that they need a reset on the interior, then Johnson may be an option worth keeping an eye on as the 2027 NFL Draft approaches.

title: Regression Has Come for Bryce Young, But Here's What That Really Means
full_text:
Bryce Young had Panthers fans feeling pretty confident during the opening weeks of the 2026 season. He was completing throws that didn't always seem to be there in his first two NFL seasons. His numbers were starting to look like what Carolina hoped to see from the first overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. For a short time, Young was in the conversation for NFL MVP.
Now, though, the Panthers' quarterback's numbers have taken a turn for the worse. So which version of Young should Carolina's fans believe in? The one who was playing like one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL early in the season? Or the one who hasn't been able to put up the same numbers as of late? Carolina still has questions about how well it has supported Young .
The first four games of the season saw Young put up some of the best numbers of his NFL career. He threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns in a loss to the Chicago Bears, 287 yards and three touchdowns in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, 291 yards and one touchdown in a loss to the Cleveland Browns, and 329 yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Detroit Lions.
In his first four games of the season, Young had over 300 passing yards in three games and multiple touchdown passes in three games as well. He looked like he was in complete control of the offense, making tough throws and leading the Panthers down the field for long drives. It was everything that Panthers fans had hoped for from the first overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. But even the best quarterbacks have off days, and it would be unreasonable to expect Young to be able to sustain that level of play for an entire season.
The first few games of the season were special for Young and the Panthers, but that doesn't mean that the last few games have been bad. He is still growing as a quarterback and having some struggles along the way.
After the Detroit game, Young's passing yards began to drop. He had 281 passing yards in a loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, 163 passing yards in a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 209 passing yards in a loss to the Green Bay Packers, 276 passing yards and three touchdowns in a loss to the Denver Broncos, and 200 passing yards in a win over the New Orleans Saints.
It is worth noting that Young has been hit a lot in recent weeks. The Buccaneers sacked him five times, while the Packers brought him down six times. The numbers behind Young's sack problems point to bigger issues with Carolina's protection . The Panthers' offensive line has had its struggles with injuries this season, and when healthy, it has been up and down as a unit. This can be challenging for any quarterback, let alone one who is trying to develop as a passer and make the most of the time he has in the pocket.
As much as Young needs to do a better job of dealing with pressure, it is also important to note that Carolina can do a lot to help the quarterback. First, getting the offensive line healthy and giving Young more time to read defenses would be a huge help.
As mentioned earlier, Carolina has a higher floor at quarterback this season than it did last year. Yes, there have been some bad games from the young quarterback, but there have also been some very good games from him. He has kept the Panthers in games that they could have easily lost.
Last Sunday's game against the Saints was not his best, but the Panthers pulled out a win, and that's what matters most. Young was 17-for-30 for 200 yards with no interceptions. He also helped set up the game-winning field goal with time running out, as Carolina improved to 6-4 on the season. Young did enough to help the Panthers secure the win over New Orleans.
We are still trying to figure out what kind of quarterback Young is. There will be games like the ones against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, but also games like the ones against Chicago, Atlanta and Detroit.
We may not be seeing MVP numbers from Young right now, but that is probably for the best. He is growing as a quarterback and has shown that he can be a good quarterback for the Panthers. His start to the season was as good as it gets, but these last few games have shown that he still has a lot of work to do to reach that level on a regular basis.

title: Todd Wash Giving Panthers Rookies More Opportunities to Make an Impact
full_text:
Todd Wash, interim defensive coordinator for the Carolina Panthers, continued to make adjustments on defense in Sunday’s 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints. As the Panthers look to get more out of their young players, several saw more time on defense, including rookie defensive tackle Lee Hunter, who played 15 defensive snaps on Sunday after seeing 13 in the Panthers’ game against the Denver Broncos last week. Hunter made a huge play in the second quarter when he stopped Saints running back Travis Etienne for a loss on a fourth-and-inches play from the Panthers’ 25-yard line.
The Panthers have been hoping to get more out of the rookie, but his snaps have been somewhat limited so far this season. The Panthers have a number of defensive linemen and utilize a variety of defensive fronts, so it’s been difficult to find a consistent role for the rookie.
During the week leading up to the Saints game, Wash spoke about getting the rookie more playing time on the field. Hunter had 15 defensive snaps in Sunday’s game after seeing 13 in the previous game against the Denver Broncos.
“It is a major, major point of emphasis to make sure he gets more. I’ll take that. He has to play more. He’s a good football player, and it is as simple as getting him in the game, and he will be in the game more,” Wash said.
Hunter had three tackles on the day, including one for a loss. He made a big play on a fourth-and-inches from the Panthers’ 25-yard line when he burst through the Saints’ offensive line to bring down Etienne for a loss.
The Panthers continued to make changes on defense in Sunday’s game, as rookie safety Zakee Wheatley played 63 defensive snaps while veteran Nick Scott played 28 defensive snaps, or 44% of the defensive total.
Wheatley took over the every-down role at safety alongside Tre’von Moehrig, as Scott moved to a role as the third safety in the Panthers’ secondary. Wheatley was inactive for the season opener against the Broncos but has played in every game since then, making his first start on Sunday.
Prior to the game, Dave Canales spoke with Scott about the change in role. Canales said that Wheatley’s development, along with his communication with his teammates, played a part in the decision to give the rookie safety more responsibility in the Panthers’ secondary.
Wheatley finished with three tackles, including one for a loss of 3 yards, and was targeted twice in coverage. He allowed one reception for 18 yards. Canales highlighted Wheatley’s communication with teammates, tackling and his ability to get the secondary on the same page.
It is clear that interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash is doing everything possible to help the Panthers be successful on defense. In addition to making changes to the defensive strategy, Wash is also making adjustments to give Panthers players opportunities to produce on the field.
These are positive moves by Wash and the rest of the coaching staff as the Panthers look to determine what a number of their younger players can provide on the defensive side of the ball. There is still a lot of work to be done on defense, but hopefully some of the younger players can continue to produce when given the opportunity.

title: Early NFL Week 11 Odds Reveal Panthers' Chances of Starting Win Streak vs. Ravens

title: Panthers’ Super Bowl Odds Rise Once Again with Huge Win Over Saints
full_text:
A much-needed victory. The Carolina Panthers go on the road and steal a win over the division rival New Orleans Saints . The 20-17 win is Carolina's first since Week 6, a road win against the Philadelphia Eagles.
It was a win filled with drama, controversy, and penalties galore for the Panthers. Carolina set a franchise record on Sunday, finishing the game with 17 accepted penalties for 152 yards. The game ended decisively when Jalen Coker drew a pass-interference call that split NFL fans and gave the Panthers field position for a game-winning field goal.
A division win is always crucial, especially in a tightly contested division such as the NFC South. Even if the division is bad- and it is- one of these teams is going to host a Wild Card game, which means the Super Bowl isn't totally out of reach.
After a win that solidified first place in the division, Carolina's Super Bowl odds shifted.
Sports Illustrated's Peter Dewey released his NFL power rankings , which are based on Super Bowl odds. These odds aren't just based on the shortest odds, but on which teams have the best value at where they sit on DraftKings Sportsbook.
With that said, the Panthers landed at No. 17 on Dewey's list, one spot ahead of the Dallas Cowboys, and one spot below the New York Giants.
The No. 17 ranking is a jump from last week, when the Panthers were sitting at No. 20, and coming off a third straight loss, in brutal fashion against the Denver Broncos at home. The next highest-ranked team is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, at No. 20, followed by the Saints at 24 and then the Falcons right behind them at 25.
Carolina's win over the Saints is their fourth of the season, making them the only team in the NFC South with four wins currently. The NFC South is 5-19 against non division teams, now the Panthers have an opprotunity to improve that record, with a home game against the Baltimore Ravens.
The Ravens will have a slightly shorter week, since they played on Monday Night Football. Baltimore played its first game with new QB Jacoby Brissett, and that first game was a loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who were 0-8 entering Monday night.
Carolina has to capitalize on an opportunity for back-to-back wins and beat a team that's starting a backup quarterback.

title: Saints Players, Coaches Complain About Penalty vs. Panthers, But They're Wrong
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers beat the New Orleans Saints on a walk-off field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald. The Panthers got into field-goal range thanks to a defensive pass interference call against Kool-Aid McKinstry. After that, they simply ran the ball to set up Fitzgerald to win it.
According to Mike Triplett, McKinstry was frustrated by what he called a "horrible, horrible" call. He also revealed that his teammates came up to him and just kept saying it was a "bad call" after the play.
Head coach Kellen Moore said, "Obviously, there’s disappointment when a call goes like that and now they’re in field goal range." He did admit that the Saints had plenty of calls go their way, but he was still upset about that one.
What is OPI https://t.co/u9V3deB1JD
Cam Jordan got online after the game, in which he recorded one tackle, and quote-tweeted the video with the caption "What is OPI," indicating that he believes this was a missed call.
Complaining about a consequential call is nothing new in the NFL. If ever there is a penalty that sets up a winning score, someone's going to comment about it. The coaches, players, and more usually do express their frustration.
But there seems to be some misunderstanding the Saints players and coaches have. For one thing, this is textbook defensive pass interference. Running into the receiver, preventing him from making a play on the pass, and not even looking at the football is pass interference.
Complain about the way the rule is written because it is a silly rule that often bails out underthrown passes, which this one from Bryce Young was. But it is the rule, and this was as clear-cut as it gets. McKinstry interfered with Jalen Coker.
But the bigger issue is that the Panthers were flagged for the same exact thing earlier, setting up New Orleans' go-ahead score. Corey Thornton did literally the exact same thing against Chris Olave near the goal-line.
He crashed into Olave before the ball got there and never remotely turned his head. It was rightly flagged (one of many valid penalties the Panthers committed ), and Moore wasn't outraged about the rule then. No one in New Orleans was.
The final ironic fact here is something Moore alluded to. The Saints got a ridiculous number of favorable calls from the replacement referees. For a full list, check out our coverage here . It's truly shocking.
Among many things, an incorrect horse-collar call set the Saints up to score (on the same drive as the Thornton DPI) and take the lead. A ridiculous, phantom facemask put the Saints basically in field-goal range to tie it with under a minute left.
The Panthers got hosed on numerous occasions, and the call against McKinstry was correct. Complaining about it only makes the Saints look bad, but it could provide more fuel for the rematch in Charlotte later this year.

title: Bears Fans Shouldn't Worry About Ben Johnson's 3-2 Record After Bye Weeks Before Saints
full_text:
The first half of the 2026 NFL season could not have gone much better for the Chicago Bears. They went 7-2 through nine games and climbed to the top of the NFC North, but they took a bye-week tumble down the standings after Detroit and Minnesota secured big wins in Week 10. Nevertheless, the Bears are big favorites in their Week 11 game against the 3-6 New Orleans Saints and appear primed to extend their winning streak to five.
However, there is one reason for Bears fans to feel some trepidation ahead of what looks like a tune-up game, and that has to do with head coach Ben Johnson. Since becoming a play-caller in 2022, Johnson's teams are just 3-2 after bye weeks, including a playoff bye. Taken at face value, that's a concerning record for a head coach as obsessed with details and fundamentals as Johnson, but there may be more to this than meets the eye.
With that in mind, let's pop open the hood of Johnson's post-bye record and take a deeper look, starting with last season.
After a shaky 2-2 start to the Ben Johnson era, the Bears entered an early Week 5 bye, which seemingly came at just the right time. They ended up beating the Washington Commanders on the road in rainy conditions, with backup kicker Jake Moody sealing a 25-24 victory with a walk-off field goal.
This wasn't the prettiest game from Chicago's offense, especially in regard to the passing game, but the run game finally got going for the first time all year, racking up 150 rushing yards. This post-bye victory showed that Ben Johnson understood what wasn't working for his offense and that he could make the necessary adjustments.
Johnson's final game as a Detroit Lion was probably not what he'd hoped it would be: a stunning playoff loss . The Lions got rolled by the Commanders in the Divisional Round of the playoffs after securing a Wild Card bye, but it's hard to blame this one on Johnson, try as some Lions fans might.
His offense put up 521 total yards and 30 first downs, besting the Commanders in each category. They put up 31 points. The problem was that a heavily injured defense gave up 45 points and Jared Goff threw three mind-numbing interceptions. Johnson can call the plays, but he can't throw the ball for his quarterback.
Ben Johnson just seems to have the Cowboys' number over the last two years. He got his first win as a head coach in a dominant 31-14 Week 3 win against Dallas last year, and less than a year before that he led a 47-9 shellacking of the Cowboys as the Lions' offensive coordinator after an early bye week.
The Lions scored on every single drive of that game except two, with one being a one-play kneel-down to end the first half and a turnover on downs at the end of the game, after the starters had already been pulled. The game was effectively over by halftime as Johnson's offense raced out to a 27-6 lead and never looked back.
This post-bye victory was another statement win for Ben Johnson, which came right around the time when he became the hottest head coaching candidate in the NFL. Back when the Chargers were actually a well-coached, tough team, Johnson's offense dropped 533 yards on them while going 8-for-18 on third and fourth downs en route to a 41-38 win.
In this game, Detroit's defense once again came up short, allowing the Chargers to hang around the entire game. But a walk-off field goal from Riley Patterson secured the win and boosted Johnson's national profile.
Johnson's first post-bye game as a play-caller didn't go quite as well as subsequent performances. In fact, it was mostly a disaster. They lost to the Cowboys 24-6 in a game where they only ran 56 plays for 312 yards.
However, there's not much from this game that can inform Bears fans on Johnson's post-bye tendencies. The Lions were still in the middle of a rebuild, and Johnson was still learning the ropes as a play-caller. At that that point they were still taking their lumps and trying to find a groove.
As aforementioned, Johnson's 3-2 post-bye record doesn't look great on its face. But after looking through the details of each game, it's plain to see that very little blame can be laid at Johnson's feet for those two losses. One was in the middle of what looked like another dismal season for the Lions as their rebuild continued, and the other was a playoff game in which the defense gave up 45 points.
Returning to the present, I see no reason for Bears fans to fear that Johnson has the post-bye yips. There are reasons to fear the Saints in Week 11 , and there's a non-zero chance that they pull off the upset, but it won't be because the head coach wasn't up to the task at hand.

title: Who is Chicago Bears' Midseason Non-QB Most Valuable Player?
full_text:
As the Chicago Bears prepare to return from their bye in Week 11 to face the New Orleans Saints , we are also officially halfway through the 2026 season.
The Bears have played in nine of their 17 contests and sport a 7-2 record. The biggest reason for that is quarterback Caleb Williams, who is easily the team's Most Valuable Player as he continues to cement himself as an elite signal-caller .
But, if we had to name another player as the team's midseason MVP, who would it be?
Well, in my mind, it comes down to two players.
Burden has cemented himself as the Bears' No. 1 wide receiver in 2026 after playing better and more consistent football than his fellow wideout, Rome Odunze.
Burden leads the Bears with 49 receptions, 644 yards and four touchdowns. That puts him on pace to finish with 92 catches, 1,216 yards and seven touchdowns.
But it isn't only about the numbers with him, as Burden is easily the Bears' most consistent pass-catcher while both Odunze and Colston Loveland have struggled with drops.
During a season in which Williams has taken the next step in his career, Burden has been one of the biggest reasons why.
As for Muhammad, the rookie has been far better than expected after being a fourth-round pick back in April. The Texans product is giving up a completion rate of 54.8% and a passer rating of 79.9 when targeted.
What makes his season more impressive is the fact that the rookie has played great football at multiple spots, which is not something you see from rookies often.
First, he started off in the slot with the injury to Kyler Gordon , and Muhammad played well there despite having very little slot experience from his days in college.
Muhammad then moved to the boundary in place of the struggling Tyrique Stevenson upon Gordon's return and his play has not dropped off at all.
As we mentioned, Stevenson has struggled this season, but so has Jaylon Johnson, who is having the worst campaign of his career.
Muhammad's play has been a much-needed boost for Chicago and one has to wonder just where the Bears' defense would've been had the rookie not stepped up.
We're giving it to Burden over Muhammad, and for one very specific reason.
There was nothing more important for the Bears than Williams taking that next step in his career, which he obviously has done.
Because Burden has been Williams' top and most consistent target, that means he has played a huge role in the Bears quarterback's ascension
It's tough to find more value than what Burden has provided for the Bears this season, but we will say Muhammad is very close.

title: Everything Chicago Bears Have to Fear About New Orleans Saints in Week 11
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and New Orleans Saints will do battle at Soldier Field in Week 11 in a matchup that features two teams going in opposite directions.
At 3-6, the Saints are headed toward another disappointing season after entering the 2026 campaign with some hype after showing promise late in 2025. The saving grace for New Orleans comes from the fact that the team is in one of the worst divisions in football, so its playoff hopes aren't dead yet.
At 7-2, the Bears have looked like a true Super Bowl contender in the third year of the Caleb Williams era. The Bears quarterback is ascending to elite status , if he isn't there already, and Chicago's defense has been a great complement.
Despite how poorly the Saints have played this season, they are still a dangerous team and the Bears cannot take them lightly. Here's three things in particular the Bears need to be ready for.
The Saints already had a solid one-two punch at wide receiver in Chris Olave and the ascending Devaugh Vele, but New Orleans added rookie Jordyn Tyson into the mix a few weeks ago.
Tyson was on the shelf for the first seven games because of a hamstring injury. After a quiet game in his NFL debut, Tyson emerged in Week 10 with 11 catches for 80 yards.
Tyson has played the majority of his snaps in the slot, where the Bears have an injury concern this week with Kyler Gordon, who is dealing with a shoulder injury that has him labeled as day-to-day.
But, as we noted, Tyson isn't the only one the Bears need to be worried about. Both Vele and Olave are in the midst of career-best seasons and can cause major head aches for a Bears secondary that has seen struggles, and namely with Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson.
Luckily for Chicago, rookie Malik Muhammad has been better than expected in his first season and has provided some stability on the outside. That said, he has missed the last two games with an injury, so he's someone to keep an eye on during the week.
The Saints might actually have one of the best edge rusher duos in the entire NFL right now.
On one side, New Orleans has Carl Granderson, who has already matched his career-high with 8.5 sacks that are tied for the second-most in the NFL this season.
On the other side, former No. 2 overall pick Chase Young is also on pace to have his best season with eight sacks in nine games, which is just two shy of his personal best.
While it doesn't guarantee the Saints' edge rushers won't have any success, the Bears are well-equipped to handle Granderson and Young with a strong tackle duo of Theo Benedet and Darnell Wright, who have combined for two sacks and 30 pressures allowed this season, per Pro Football Focus .
One way the Bears can neutralize the Saints' talented receiver trio is to get home on Shough and prevent him from throwing the football, or at least bother him when he tries to.
That might be tough, though, as the Shough presents plus mobility that allows him to escape pressure to extend plays — which forces defensive backs to cover for longer — and pick up yards with his legs.
The Bears need to make sure they are securing the edge and not allowing Shough to roll out and have extra time to find his pass-catchers, which could lead to chunk gains.
Chicago also needs to maintain gap integrity so Shough can't find holes up the middle to run through.

title: Kyler Gordon on Injury Watch as Bears Return From Bye to Face Saints
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have had some good injury news to start the week, but not everything has been positive on that front.
On Monday, we found out that both running back Kyle Monangai and wide receiver Luther Burden were practicing , and then it was revealed by head coach Ben Johnson on Tuesday that Burden cleared the concussion protocol .
However, on the flip side, Johnson not only noted that edge rusher Dayo Odeyingbo isn't likely to be back from injured reserve , he also noted that cornerback Kyler Gordon is dealing with an injury.
Here's what we know about that.
The Bears decided to hold a pair of practices on Monday and Tuesday this week before taking off on Wednesday.
In both of those sessions, Gordon did not take part, which puts his status up in the air for Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints.
Johnson told reporters that Gordon is dealing with a shoulder injury and is viewed as day-to-day, ESPN's Courtney Cronin relayed.
"Bears practice just wrapped. Second consecutive practice this week for Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb)," Cronin wrote. "No Kyler Gordon (shoulder). Ben Johnson called it a 'day to day' injury. Gordon missed Monday’s session as well."
According to Brad Biggs of The Chicago Tribune , it appears Gordon came down with the injury in the second quarter of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers game in Week 9. Gordon exited the game to get checked out in the locker room but managed to return and finish out the game. He also played a season-high 52 snaps.
The Bears have not put out an injury report so far this week since they are not required to until Wednesday. However, that practice report will be an estimation. Still, it'll give us a better idea of how Gordon is coming along.
For now, we would expect Gordon to be listed an estimated non-participant based on his lack of participation over the first two days of the week.
That said, the day-to-day label is a good sign for his chances of suiting up.
Replacing Gordon on defense will not be easy because of both his blitzing and coverage skills.
We've seen Gordon's impact in the pass-rush with four sacks, and the veteran defensive back is permitting a completion rate of 57.1% and a passer rating of 86.6.
What could also complicate things is if Malik Muhammad doesn't play again. The rookie has missed the last two games with a toe injury, although it appears he was practicing on Monday and Tuesday, so he might be good to go.
Tyrique Stevenson got hurt in Week 9 , but as is the case with Muhammad, it appears he has been practicing, so his odds of suiting up are looking good.
Because less is more with Stevenson, we'd prefer the Bears move Cam Lewis from safety to the slot and have Elijah Hicks take that starting spot if Gordon is ruled out. Lewis has played 76 snaps in the slot this season because of injuries, and he has played well.
The other approach would be to move Muhammad to the slot, where he played well while Gordon was out earlier in the season, and have Stevenson play on the boundary, but we know how Stevenson has struggled this season.
Hopefully for the Bears, none of this will be necessary and Gordon ends up playing.

title: Punishing the Copy Cats a Goal for Caleb Williams and Bears Offense
full_text:
Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson have addressed the copy cat effect and think the Bears are ready to attack it.
This would be the possibility defenses try to do what Tampa Bay's defense did to get back into their Week 9 game, when they nearly knocked off the Bears by taking away the ball five times. It's not an extraordinary tactic. It's the old A-gap or B-gap blitz.
“Like you said, it's a copycat league," Williams said Tuesday at Halas Hall. "So it's going to show up at some point here soon. Who knows, it could be this week, it could be next week, it could be the week after, it could be postseason, when we get there, whenever that is. It's going to show up at some point.
"Like I said, we've gone back and looked at it already. We'll fix it. For myself in that situation, if it does happen; I mean, there's times when people get through, and it's happened throughout my career. It's going to happen for the rest of my career. Just get the ball out of bounds or anything like that. Then on the other ones, just don't make bad decisions.”
"That's also one of the coolest things about being here in Chicago and what we're building here. It's not just Chicago Bears, it's us as Chicago athletes." Caleb Williams talked about being part of PCA's MVP celebration video shared by the Cubs, and what their friend group is… pic.twitter.com/XbsGasyUfy
The Saints might not seem like the ideal candidates to use this tactic because they have plenty of pass rush from defensive ends Chase Young (8 sacks) and Carl Granderson (8 1/2), and they also have edge Cameron Jordan, who has yet to record a sack in his eight games. Maybe the Bears dodged a bullet by not signing him, if indeed they were interested as many rumors suggested during free agency. However, Jordan remains an imposing physical threat on the line.
However, Johnson thinks they could be bringing the heat.
“These edge players, between the two of them, or really I should say three of them, but the guys that are playing the most right now, Chase Young and Carl Granderson, they're leading the team in sacks, I think they have eight apiece and they're good not only in the pass game, they're great edge setters in the run game as well," Johnson said. "Big challenge there on both sides.
LUTHER BURDEN TOUCHDOWN! Caleb Williams beats the blitz and Burden does the rest! Chicago is HUMMING on Sunday Night Football! pic.twitter.com/CwgObQTkEW
"And then I think this (linebacker Kaden) Elliss that they got back at linebacker, I think he's one of the better pressuring linebackers in the NFL. And so, they're not afraid to plug him in A- or B-gap and make it tough on your protection scheme. That combination, I think, from the interior with him with those two edge rushers is what makes their pressure package so dangerous.”
Elliss is the most likely to be blitzing because of his success. The 6-foot-2, 238-pound 2019 Saints seventh-round pick left New Orleans for Atlanta and then returned. He has two sacks this year, 22 1/2 for his career.
How they actually stop these blitzes better is the mystery Johnson won't reveal, but guards Jonah Jackson and Joe Thuney, and especially center Garrett Bradbury, have the greatest responsibility.
4 turnovers. Bad throws all night. And with the game on the line? Caleb was still Caleb. 🐻 @_JeffWillis on the dime to Loveland that set up the game-winner 🎯 #Bears #DaBears #CalebWilliams pic.twitter.com/qhmXs8ixBr
"There are some things protection-wise that we certainly have to clean up," Johnson said. "We care about the integrity of the A- and B-gaps, and there are too many times on tape right now where we're allowing free runners through those gaps. So we've got to tighten the screws a little bit there, feel good about our rules, feel good about the guys that are up front and getting the calls made.
"We've just got to make sure we're all on the same page, we have our eyes in the right spot. Anytime you see a little something on tape, we're going to get more of it. Until we have proven that we've taken care of that problem, there's more to come.”
For Williams, it wasn't just the blitz that he needs to be concerned with but the mistakes he made. He had to stew on four bad interceptions, two when he tried throwing it away and it was caught just off the ground by defenders.
Todd Bowles refused to let Caleb Williams sit back and pick apart his secondary. When the Bears lined up in 11 personnel on early downs, the Buccaneers changed the math with one pressure type in particular: "Hot" Blitzes. Against Chicago, Bowles used a whole menu of Hot… pic.twitter.com/55PYySdqAm
“Two of them were funky," he said. "One was a bad decision and the other one, the ball popped up in the air. The ball just didn't hit the ground in those situations, which it has in the past. But obviously it's frustrating.
"You don't want to go out there and throw four picks. That's never what you want to do. That's never what the plan is, obviously."
In other words, Williams' way of combatting the A-gap and B-gap blitzes is play smarter.
"The biggest thing in the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me personally, I don't want to let my teammates down," Williams said. "That's always big for me. In those situations, I feel like I did. So that's the frustrating part that lingers. I think that's what lingers.
Highest blitzes faced per dropback rate this season Bears              45.8% Bills                  37.9% Falcons           37.5% Colts                36.1% Browns           35.8% pic.twitter.com/JIWrGQaD8o
"But the other half of it is, like I said, I've thrown three picks before in big games. I've thrown picks before, picks that seal the game and things like that. So I'll move on from it, I've moved on from it. It's more of a how can I get better, what can I be better at; just finding ways to be more consistent.In those other situations where I'm not making a dumb decision like the first one, I'm trying to either get it out of bounds, to just juice it out of bounds."
Williams should know how to handle the pressure from such blitzes by now. Per Pro Football Reference, he faced more blitzes last year than anyone in the league at 174. This year it's come at about the same rate or slightly even higher, but he's not at the top of the league with 100 blitzes faced. Jordan Love has faced 132.  The 100 blitzes if fourth most.
After what happened against Tampa Bay, he can expect the number to start going up unless it's nipped in the bud soon.

title: Devin Bush is the Chicago Bears' Most Improved Player on Defense
full_text:
The Chicago Bears expected Devin Bush to step in and immediately fill the role Tremaine Edmunds left behind. Their decision to sign Bush to a three-year, $30 million deal on the first day of free agency was one of our favorite moves they made on the open market. We thought they landed a certified steal.
Unfortunately, that didn't exactly look to be the case over the first month of the season. He was virtually non-existent against opponents' rushing attacks and often got overwhelmed when being blocked one-on-one.
In late September, we wrote that the linebacker unit was an underrated issue on Chicago's defense. Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman had to do mop-up duty against opposing backs far too often.
However, Bush seemed to turn the corner in their Week 4 matchup against the Jets (he had only 4 tackles, but the defense was on the field for 31 plays), and he's been on an upward trajectory since that point. You really can't play the position much better than he did in their Week 9 clash against Tampa Bay.
The 28-year-old is coming off his most impressive performance of the season. He had 9 tackles (including 1 TFL) and 2 pass deflections against Tampa Bay. Bush also nearly sacked Mayfield and forced him out of the pocket into the waiting arms of Shemar Turner.
While that contest might've been his best of the season, it was far from his only quality showing. He's been one of their most consistent defenders over the past six weeks .
Bush has 34 tackles since their Week 5 matchup against Green Bay. While Dillon Thieneman still leads the team with 57 takedowns, Bush is now hot on his heels with 53 of his own (he also has 7 more since Week 5). A few of those hits have also set the tone against opposing offenses.
Devin Bush hit pic.twitter.com/wXZgsXveya
Bush's versatility is one of the most significant factors that saw them land on him in free agency. He's equally comfortable dropping back into coverage as he is filling a lane to put a big hit on a running back. His size (5'11", 234 lbs.) is virtually his only weakness, as he can often get washed out of plays if opposing linemen get their hands on him early.
Still, that hasn't been an issue in recent weeks. He's leveraged his speed to get around them and make plays in the backfield. ESPN's Bill Barnwell named Bush to his midseason All-Pro team last week, and it's tough to argue with that opinion .
Bush's yearly average of $10 million per year is tied for 19th among linebackers . Interestingly, that mark is tied with teammate T.J. Edwards. Through the first half of the season, Bush has 32 more tackles, 2 more sacks, and 4 more TFLs than his running mate (albeit in two more games, as Edwards dealt with a nagging hamstring injury earlier this season).
He's not only outplaying Edwards, though. He's been playing like one of the league's best 'backers since catching his stride. While Cam Lewis' contract gives him a slight edge in the battle for Ryan Poles' best free-agent addition , Bush's recent emergence makes it a close competition.

title: Bears Running Game Lacks Chunks and There's No Other Way to Slice It
full_text:
Besides providing tons of sleep he hadn't been able to get, Bears coach Ben Johnson said his bye week included a self-scout identifying issues in a running game now ranked fourth after it was first through the early part of the season .
At his first press conference since before the bye week, Johnson still wasn't about to divulge specifically what has been the issue with the running game.  Well, he did say something but it's tough to buy this.
"There's some things schematically that we can clean up and make things a little bit easier and more advantageous for us going forward," he said. "But up front, it's just a commitment to our principles of running off the football in our zone schemes."
Anyone can always block better. Instead, what Johnson did point out is what is NOT the problem. It's not the inability to break of chunk gains on the ground, he said. At least he claimed this wasn't the problem.
Actually, this whole idea about chunk runs was something Johnson himself brought up before the bye.
"We're going to need to lean on that run game more and it's going to need to come through for us," he said at the time. "I've got to look at, is it the fact that we're not getting as many explosives in the run game right now? Is that why the average is low?
I know Ben Johnson doesn’t brag about it because he’d like 1-play touchdowns (and who wouldn’t?). But this is still foot-on-throat, nuts-in-vise, impose-your-will, manhandling stuff. And it’s fun to watch. https://t.co/1GmbebQoEf
"Or is it we're just not moving the line of scrimmage? What are those factors?"
So he looked at it and now determined it wasn't a lack of chunk plays.  At least that's his story and he's sticking to it.
"Well, I don't see it as bigger chunk runs necessarily," Johnson said. "The yards per carry is a deceiving statistic in a lot of ways; we just mentioned that we run the ball a lot in the red zone. When you're down there, a 4-yard carry is really an explosive down there. We go off of efficiency, and we are under 50 percent efficient running the ball.
"We set our bar higher than that. We want to be closer to 55 percent and so we have some work to do. All of our guys know it. Like I said before, it's really just a commitment to those fundamentals. We talk about in the springtime what we want each scheme to look like and how it all comes together. It's bringing that vision to life right now."
A little truth serum might be necessary here for the Bears coach.
Sure, 55% success rates are impotant, but In the first nine weeks last year the Bears had 44 big plays in the running game. That is, they had 44 runs of 10 yards or longer. In the first nine games this year, they've had 26.
That's a lot of yards and two chunk runs per game difference.
The running game does help with ball control and the Bears have had no problem with this as they're No. 1 in time of possession, but the big runs can mean more points. The Bears just haven't had them with Swift carrying the load almost entirely by himself.
Everyone will rise to their feet, rejoice & sing.  I can’t wait for Monangai Mania! pic.twitter.com/1I6WFJNZkt
There is importance to success percentage, as Johnson said. They're at a 47.1% success rate with Swift carrying. A successful run is 4 yards on first down, a second-down run leaving third-and-4 or less, and then a first down gained on a third-down or fourth-down run. Monangai is at 51.7% success rate. Last year Swift had a 54.7% success rate and Monangai 50.9%.
Swift's overall average might be down per carry to 3.7 yards, but some of this is because he's been making runs in situations with a lid on top when he didn't always carry on those plays last year. For instance, Swift is fifth in the league with seven rushing TDs from inside 5 yards. He's had 15 rushes inside 5 yards, the third most in the NFL. When a back carries so often in short yardage with a big gain limit of 5 yards, it's naturally going to limit average yards per carry. He can't do any better than 5 yard.
KYLEEEEE  MMONNNANGAI — THE BOWLING BALL Before his injury Kyle was simply our best back & that’s with D’Andre top TD running back in the league! That 1-2 punch has been sensational His 2026 numbers in just 4 games: 🏈 60 carries⁰🏈 324 rushing yards⁰🏈 5.4 yards per carry… pic.twitter.com/8XUCdlnv3a
"Guys, I've been saying it since I came in; he's a really good runner," Johnson said of Swift. "I think I've been consistent with that message. He hasn't changed anything about his game. He's been given opportunities and he's taken advantage of that. He's decisive; he knows where the ball is, where we want it to hit down inside the 5. I think it's a credit to all of those guys.
"We usually have a lot of nuance in those five-to-goal line runs. They come in on a Friday, and there is brand new runs for them to digest and make sure we have them down pat going into the red zone. He does a great job with that. I know he's explosive and he's great in space, but he's able to put his pads down and run through contact as well."
Kyle Monangai may play, but he'll be hurting the rest of the season.  So it's mixed news from the #Bears as Luther Burden hopes to be cleared. And we sort through some telling numbers to assess the #Bears coming out of the bye. Forward Progress on @312SportsChi .  Links below.
Actually Kyle Monangai's return should mean something whether Johnson wants to admit it or not. That's not a slight on Swift, just fact.
They had 18 of their 26 big runs this season when Monangai was playing in the first four games. They had eight in the five games since he left. This difference seems obvious.
The blockers don't see Swift hauling the load by himself and suddenly just say, 'That's it, I give up.' Yet, the efficiency rate and the chunk play totals have been fewer for the team overall without Monangai complementing Swift.
Getting Monangai back should make a ton of difference whether Johnson admits it or not. And it wouldn't hurt for everyone to block now if they weren't when Swift alone was playing, if that was even a possibility.

title: Bears' Ben Johnson 'Doesn't See' Dayo Odeyingbo Returning from IR in Week 11
full_text:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson's injury updates on Tuesday were a mixed bag for Bears fans. On the one hand, Luther Burden should be ready for Week 11 after clearing concussion protocol, and Kyler Gordon is considered day-to-day after sustaining a shoulder injury in Week 9. However, he 'doesn't see' Dayo Odeyingbo returning from IR for Week 11, despite being eligible to return, according to ESPN's Courtney Cronin .
Odeyingbo had started the 2026 season with a bang, racking up three sacks through the first four games before a leg injury took him out of the Bears' Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Week 11 would have been his first opportunity to get back into action, but it appears that's unlikely to happen.
While this is not a major setback, it's a disappointment, to be sure. The fans, and probably the coaches, too, had been looking forward to seeing what a ' motivated Dayo Odeyingbo ' could do for Chicago's defense since they added superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in a blockbuster trade.
At the risk of counting chickens before they hatch, the silver lining from Ben Johnson's injury update is that the Bears' Week 11 opponent is the hapless New Orleans Saints, who are 3-6 on the year and just lost to the Carolina Panthers. This should be a relatively easy game for the Bears, a badly needed tune-up after a rough Week 9 outing. If Odeyingbo has to miss this game before he's ready to play, they should be fine without him.
Once you look past Week 11, however, the Bears' schedule becomes a horrifying gauntlet of Super Bowl contenders. They still have four divisional games left, and there are no slouches in the NFC North. They also face the Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills in December.
If the Bears are to successfully defend their NFC North division crown, they're going to need to win a majority of these brutal matchups. As I said in my post predicting the Bears' final games of the season , a 13-4 record will likely be the absolute minimum they can get and feel confident about securing the NFC North and at least one home playoff game. That means they can only lose two of these six games, and that's assuming they take care of business against the Saints and Miami Dolphins.
Credit where credit is due. After a 2025 season in which he appeared to be a lost cause, Odeyingbo's hot start in 2026 reflected well upon Ben Johson and general manager Ryan Poles. He's proven to be versatile in where he can line up and clearly took all the offseason criticisms to heart. Once he's back in the starting lineup alongside Simmons, I daresay that Chicago's front-four will be the cream of the NFC North crop.
If Odeyingbo takes another step forward in his game upon his return, he's going to force the Bears into a tough offseason decision. They can easily free up a large chunk of salary cap space by releasing Odeyingbo in 2027, but if he's proven to be a major contributor, the team will have to decide whether the salary cap relief matters more than on-field production.

title: Luther Burden Injury Update From Ben Johnson Confirms Bears WR's Week 11 Status
full_text:
The Chicago Bears went into their Week 10 bye with a question mark at the wide receiver position in Luther Burden.
Late in the Week 10 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Burden came down with a concussion after taking a hard hit to his head while making a catch, which led to a fumble.
Burden wasn't able to finish out the game after he was diagnosed with the concussion, which left him uncertain for Week 11 because concussions can be multi-week injuries.
However, head coach Ben Johnson provided a positive update on Tuesday that confirms Burden's Week 11 status.
The Bears were back on the practice field on Tuesday, and before they went outside, Johnson revealed that Burden has cleared the concussion protocol, which means he will play in Week 11.
"Bears coach Ben Johnson says WR Luther Burden has cleared concussion protocol," The Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs said.
We got our first indication that Burden would be good to go this week when he was spotted on the practice field on Monday and looked to be taking part in full.
Still, you never can be too sure with a concussion, so it's great to hear it from Johnson that Burden has recovered.
Of course, it was always more likely than not that Burden would play. After all, the Bears had a bye last week , so Burden had a full extra week to get right, which he clearly was able to do.
After Burden put together an impressive rookie season and Rome Odunze failed to cement himself after an injury-plagued year in 2025, the No. 1 wide receiver title was up for grabs in 2026.
Instead of Odunze keeping his loose grip on the title, Burden has clearly seized it in what is a breakout year for him in his second season.
The former second-round pick has 49 receptions for 644 yards and four touchdowns entering Week 11, all of which are tops on the team. Odunze ranks second in receiving yards with 528, but he's third in receptions (32) and receiving touchdowns (one).
Burden entered the season with high expectations, especially from his head coach and general manager. So far, Burden has been everything the team could've hoped he'd be.
At his current pace, Burden will finish the season with about 92 catches, 1,216 yards and seven touchdowns.

title: Kyle Monangai Makes Troubling Admission About Turf Toe Injury Ahead of Return for Bears
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are likely to be getting a major reinforcement on the offensive side of the ball this week thanks to the return of running back Kyle Monangai.
Monangai has missed each of the last five games becuase of a turf toe injury. It was initially expected that he wouldn't miss more than three games because he wasn't placed on injured reserve, but that ended up not being the case, of course.
Head coach Ben Johnson revealed recently that Monangai did not suffer a setback and it was simply a case of the Bears not knowing exactly how long it would be until Monangai's situation improved.
But none of that matters now. Monangai has taken part in each of the last two practices the Bears have held, including the Monday session out of the bye, and he told reporters after his latest practice that he expects to go in Week 11 .
Monangai went into detail about his injury while speaking to the media on Monday and he made a troubling admission.
Monangai said his toe isn't 100% and won't be until the offseason, when he has more time to heal it.
"The time off definitely helped but I mean (the injury is) going to be there," Monangai said. "Offseason I'll heal it. That will be for then."
"It's something I can manage now," Monangai added. "The time off was needed, though, for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago."
The obvious concern there is the risk of re-injury, something the Bears can ill-afford given the fact that Monangai has been the team's best running back this season..
Monangai went on to note that the injury is "very painful" for guys at his position in particular, but he was fortunate because he did not come down with the most severe case of turf toe, which is a season-ending issue.
"Yeah, like it's very painful, because especially at my position I'm cutting off (his big toes)," Monangai explained. "And when you're cutting off your insteps you need your big toe to bend and all of these things."
"So you know sometimes guys tear ligaments and that's why you see like some guys get season-ending injuries but some are just a couple weeks," he added. "Luckily I had the blessing of being able to come back. So mine wasn't as extreme. Yeah, it's a painful injury. That's what I'll say."
According to the Cleveland Clinic , turf toe is "an injury that affects your big toe joint" and "It happens when your toe remains on the ground and your heel lifts, causing your toe to hyperextend. This motion causes soft tissues and ligaments in your big toe joint to stretch or tear (toe sprain)."
The most extreme cases require surgery, which Monangai clearly didn't need. Lesser turf toe issues get better with rest, ice and medications like ibuprofen or acetaminphen.
Turf toe recovery timelines can be anywhere from as little as a week to several months, depending on the severity. Monangai's issue appears to be around the middle range.

title: Former Bengals Star Drops Key Reason Why Joe Burrow is NFL's Best Quarterback
full_text:
Former Bengals wide receiver and current NFL analyst Andrew Hawkins dropped some big praise for Cincinnati star Joe Burrow this week.
He appeared on the Dan Le Batard Show and broke down why Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL this season, along with a secret superpower that helps him stay around the top year in and year out.
Statistically, no passer in the league has touched Burrow this season, ranking first in the following categories so far: Yards Per Game, Completions, Completion%, Adjusted Comp %, Passing TD, Total Touchdowns, NFL Passer Rating, PFF Overall Grade, PFF Passing grade, ESPN QBR.
"I think for Joe Burrow, he is the best quarterback when healthy in the NFL," Hawkins said on the show. "I think what this year is showing us is it's always been the case. Does that mean he's perfect every time? No, but he just plays the position better than anybody. And I'm not excluding anybody from that conversation. That is the Mahomeses. That is Josh Allen. The Lamars. When Joe Burrow is healthy and protected, he is just a savant when he is in the pocket."
Hawkins got solid quarterback play lining up with Andy Dalton from 2011-13, but he's never played with a passer close to the caliber of Burrow.
Burrow's unwavering, fearless mentality helps him make all the great throws and can get him in hot water too.
"Joe Burrow doesn't have that, and so it's a weird thing. It's why he gets injured as much as he does," Hawkins said about his fearlessness. "Because he doesn't have a certain regard for his body and very dangerous proximity to defenders, which allows him to wait to the very last possible second to throw passes and to just again be laser-like and evaluating the defense and not worry about his own livelihood, and that's why he's special because there are quarterbacks that are scared to death, and you can see it the moment they take the snap; they can't wait to get the football out.
"For Joe Burrow, he has that very weird thing that he's born with that you can't teach; you can't learn it in college, high school, or the pros. No guru can give it to you. He has it mixed with the other qualities. That's why he's better than everybody else."

title: Joe Burrow Wins Cincinnati Bengals' 5th AFC Player of the Week Award of the Season
full_text:
For the fourth time in four games, a member of the Cincinnati Bengals has been named AFC Player of the Week.
And for the second time in that span, it’s quarterback Joe Burrow.
The league named Burrow the AFC Offensive Player of the Week following his performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers in which he completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns.
“He’s just on it,” Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said of Burrow after the win. “I thought the protection was really good. There are times that they are going to create some movement, but its blocked movement. I think Joe did an excellent job keeping his eyes down the field and finding guys for some big plays. Those guys made big plays and tremendous catches — all of those guys really. Everyone stepped up and made some plays for us.
“Obviously, he (Burrow) set the tone.”
It’s the 10th career Player of the Week honor for Burrow, who also won in Week 7 for his performance against the Baltimore Ravens. He surpasses Boomer Esiason for the most in franchise history.
That same week punter Ryan Rehkow earned the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week, and the following Sunday, wide receiver Tee Higgins took home the Offensive Player of the Week for his big game against the Tennessee Titans.
It was the first career weekly honor for both Higgins and Rehkow.
Back in Week 1, Bengals kicker Evan McPherson was named the Special Teams Player of the Week.
With five player of the week awards already, the Bengals are closing in on the franchise record of seven, which was set in 2021 season. Second most is six, which occurred in 2022.
The NFL record for most career player of the week awards belongs to Tom Brady with 32.
The active leader is Josh Allen with 19.
Given Burrow’s performance in each of the last games since the calendar flipped to November, he has to be the front runner to win AFC Player of the Month, an award he’s already captured twice (November 2024 and December 2024).
“This is just how he is,” Taylor said when asked how Burrow is in such a good rhythm. “I feel like I’ve seen him in this rhythm quite a bit. He has a lot of confidence. Like I’ve said before, the offensive line is blocking so well, it allows us to play confident. At one point we had 24 passes and six runs. It is what it is. As long as these guys are doing that and we are making our way, that’s how it’s going to be.”

title: Former Super Bowl Champion Details Why Bengal CAN'T Win Super Bowl During 2026 Season
full_text:
Former Super Bowl champion Jeff Saturday isn't buying the Bengals' chances to win it all this year. He appeared on ESPN's Get Up this week and highlighted how Cincinnati's lack of a heavy rushing attack will be their downfall in the playoffs.
Cincinnati is tied with the Packers for the fewest carries per game (21.9) because they have the best passer on Earth in Joe Burrow. Still, they rank in the top half of rushing efficiency metrics despite the low volume.
"I don't think so," Saturday said about them winning the Super Bowl. "I think you play into the other team's hands too much. You depend on weather. You depend on the ball bouncing your way; you depend on offensive line help, all of those things. It's high risk and high reward the way they're throwing it around. Where it's lower risk, high reward when you can run it and be efficient that way.
"I can think back to Peyton Manning, all the different records he was setting, when we finally won the Super Bowl, it was through the run game, right? We rushed the ball for almost 200 yards. All of those things are important. I know Steve (Smith) thinks that receivers win it all. That's just not how it works. I wish it did work that way."
There isn't much evidence this decade that you have to run the ball at a high-volume, elite level to win a title.
SB Champs by rushing success rate this decade: Tampa Bay (22nd during the 2020 season), Los Angeles Rams (20th), Kansas City (sixth), Kansas City (26th), Philadelphia (ninth), Seattle (23rd).
Cincinnati is right in the middle of the pack this season, at 13th in rushing success rate and 14th in rushing EPA. That's perfectly good enough to win a Super Bowl while adding the second-best passing EPA/success rate mark in the NFL.
The Bengals should not be running the ball more; they just need to maintain this efficiency at the current rushing volume level. The days of only winning titles by pounding the football and shortening games to win with defense are long gone.
You have to be able to dial up explosive passes consistently to win titles in the NFL, and the Bengals clearly can do that. Since Week 5, Cincinnati's offense ranks first in EPA/play with a 0.263 mark. That's double the next closest offense in the 49ers, and shows just how nuclear this team has been to opposing defenses since Burrow got into the rhythm of the season.
