title: Referee Report: White Hat for MNF Will Work His 20th Bengals Game as Head Referee
full_text:
For the second year in a row, the Cincinnati Bengals are getting Bill Vinovich as the referee in Week 11.
Last year it was a road game at Pittsburgh in Week 11, with the Steelers prevailing 34-12 following the Bengals’ bye week.
This will be Vinovich’s 20th Bengals game as a head referee, putting him ahead of Clete Blakeman for the most among active white hats.
Blakeman originally was scheduled to work his 18th Bengals’ game on Sunday Night against the Steelers last week, but the FAA’s ground stoppage of flights Friday forced the NFL to shuffle the assignments.
That resulted in Don Willard working his first and second career games as a head referee – and on the same day Willard did the Dolphins-Colts game in Indianapolis then drove with three other officials, including Cincinnati resident Terry Killens, to Paycor for the Sunday night game.
The Bengals are 8-11 with Vinovich on the call.
The Commanders are 6-13 with him.
One of the longest tenured officials in the league, Vinovich became a head referee in 2004, although he took a five-season hiatus from 2007-11.
He’s earned playoff assignments every year since he returned, including three Super Bowls.
Among Vinovich’s 19 Bengals game is the 2021 AFC Championship Game victory against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Including that game, three of the last five Cincinnati contests Vinovich has worked have gone to overtime.
Vinovich ranks 16th among the 17 regular referees with just 12.5 accepted penalties per game.
He worked the Raiders-Seahawks game Sunday, which featured just two accepted penalties. That’s the fewest in the league this year. The next lowest number is six (49ers-Rams in Week 1 and Seahawks-Chiefs in Week 7).
Last year Vinovich and his crew had the fourth most accepted penalties at 13.53.
Vinovich’s crew has called just 27 offensive holding penalties this year, the fewest in the league.
Their 24 pass interference penalties are second most.
Here is a look at the previous 19 Bengals games Vinovich has worked:
Week 11, 2025: Steelers 34, Bengals 12

title: Bengals QB Joe Burrow's 2026 Season is Reaching a Historic Level
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night is a game that this fan base will be talking about for years to come.
It was the kind of performance that put the rest of the league on notice. The Bengals played a nearly perfect game against their longtime rival and made it clear that they are a threat to the AFC crown.
One of the biggest reasons behind the dominant Bengals win was the performance of quarterback Joe Burrow. While the national media begins drooling over Burrow again, his performance Sunday night was something Cincinnati is just accustomed to now.
In the win over the Steelers, Burrow went 35 for 44 on pass attempts, throwing for 409 yards and four touchdowns. Burrow finished the game with a passer rating of 135.7.
Having just nine incompletions on 44 pass attempts sounds like video game numbers, but that's just who Burrow has been this season.
NFL on CBS shared on their X account that Burrow's accuracy this season is reaching historic levels.
As things currently stand, Burrow is second all-time in most touchdowns per game at 3.33. Peyton Manning is the current owner of that record, which he earned during his 2013 NFL MVP season with 3.50 touchdowns per game.
If the season ended today, Burrow would hold the highest completion percentage in an NFL season, as the Bengals star currently has a completion percentage of 74.7, putting him just ahead of New Orleans Saints legend Drew Brees.
Burrow is also throwing for an average of 310 yards a game while having such a ridiculous completion percentage. To put that in perspective, Brees threw for 266 yards per game during the 2018 season, which saw him claim the completion percentage crown.
If you're chronically online like most sports fans, then you have seen posts where people talk about how, a generation ago, "We watched gods play quarterback." Those people might want to take off their nostalgia goggles and realize there is some elite quarterback play happening right now.
The MVP discussion now starts with Burrow. Heading into Week 11, Burrow leads the league in touchdown passes (27) and passing yards per game (310). If the game is on the line and you need a quarterback to go out and win you a game, nobody is looking past number nine in Cincinnati.

title: Checking In On The Bengals 2026 Offseason Departures
full_text:
In the 2025 offseason, eight notable Bengals players found new homes for the 2026 season. Let’s see how they are doing with their new teams.
After a frustrating two seasons with the Bengals, Geno Stone signed a one-year, $1.4 million deal with the Buffalo Bills in the Offseason. The Bills cut him before the regular season began, but he rejoined the Bills' practice squad and has played just 44 snaps this year across two games after being elevated.
Taylor-Britt signed a one-year, 1.4-million-dollar contract to play for the Colts and reunite with former Bengals defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo. Taylor-Britt is currently on the injured list with a groin injury,  but appeared in six games for the Colts and logged 91 snaps across those games, allowing four catches on seven targets for 41 receiving yards.
Ossai was a big signing for the Jets this past offseason, signing a 3-year, $34.5 million contract. He has been plagued by injuries as he began his new chapter in New York, getting injured twice already this season. He started the year with a plantar fascia injury in his foot and, after recovering, appeared in only three games before injuring his ankle; he has been out since. In the three games he has played, he has gotten zero sacks, three pressures, and nine tackles on 107 snaps.
The biggest villain of the offseason, Trey, signed a massive 4-year, $112 million contract. The 31-year-old has amassed a solid 33 pressures in eight games. He also has two sacks and 11 tackles on 301 total snaps and is receiving a PFF grade of 66.1, which ranks him 51st out of 111 eligible edge rushers.
The former Bengals fourth-round pick, who started 48 games, including the 2022 AFC Championship Game, signed a one-year, $3.2 million deal with the Tennessee Titans. He was cut by the Titans before the start of the regular season and has bounced around on the Packers' and Seahawks' practice Squads.
After appearing in only six games, with one start for the Bengals, and losing his starting job to Dalton Risner, Patrick signed a one-year, $1.48 million deal with the New York Giants and was released ahead of the regular season. He quickly found a home with the Washington Commanders and became their starting center. He has logged 345 snaps across seven games (six starts) with a 57.8 PFF grade while allowing zero sacks and five pressures.
After a one-year stint with Cincinnati, where he recorded 34 receptions for 288 yards and 3 touchdowns across 15 games, Fant signed a two-year, $8.75 million contract with the New Orleans Saints. He has appeared in eight games for New Orleans this season, logging 12 receptions on 19 targets for 96 receiving yards and 3 touchdowns while playing roughly 50% of the Saints' offensive snaps.
After serving as Cincinnati’s primary backup quarterback over the past few seasons, Browning signed a one-year, $1.33 million contract with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the offseason. After being released ahead of the regular season, he has since signed with the Los Angeles Chargers' practice squad.

title: Hamilton County Hiring Firm to Attract More Events to Paycor Stadium
full_text:
The leaders of Hamilton County are putting in the work to bring more premier events to Paycor Stadium. The Bengals' home field just got locked in on a new lease between the team and the county last year; part of that agreement included trying to add more use cases for the stadium outside of just home Bengals games.
The county announced this week that they are hiring a firm via a Request for Proposals to help “identify potential events, build relationships with promoters and touring organizations, evaluate opportunities and develop strategies to attract additional programming."
That was part of a full release from the county, detailed further below:
“Paycor Stadium is one of our region’s greatest assets, and we want to see it used to its fullest potential,” Commission President Stephanie Summerow Dumas said. “More concerts and major events mean more visitors, more business for our local economy and more opportunities for our community. It also means that Hamilton County is fulfilling its commitment to the taxpayers.”
Cincinnati has typically hosted one major concert at Paycor Stadium, along with the annual Cincinnati Music Festival. Getting 3-4 or more major headliners to fill the space in the late spring and summer should just bolster the economic health of the area even further.
Paycor Stadium is also set to continue hosting a regional high school football playoff game this fall. The Ohio High School Athletic Association (OHSAA) Division I, Region 4 Football Championship is going down there on Friday, Nov. 20 at 7 p.m. ET.
The County leaders are happy to see this partnership continue, along with new avenues for county revenue on the way via the incoming event firm.
"We're fulfilling our commitment of continuing to make Paycor Stadium a place of and for the people of Hamilton County. This is all about the kids and families. These young athletes have worked so hard to get here, and giving them a chance to play on the same field as their NFL heroes is a dream come true," said Commission President Stephanie Summerow Dumas. "We are proud to host and give them this special opportunity once again and into the future."

title: Joe Burrow Makes History in Bengals' Dominating Win Over Steelers
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals were in prime time for their Week 10 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the home team did not disappoint.
From the opening kick, the Bengals offense was on a different level, leading the team to an impressive 38-18 win over their long-time rival.
This game was a lot different than the one these two played back in September, which saw the Steelers get the upper hand. The Bengals were on a mission Sunday night, and that was easy to see from the performance of quarterback Joe Burrow. It was a good night for the Bengals faithful, but it was a historic night for Burrow.
Burrow's numbers were eye-popping Sunday night. But for anyone who has followed the Bengals this season, it was just another week.
The Bengals quarterback went 35 for 44, throwing for 409 yards and four touchdowns. Burrow's performance was the Bengals' quarterback's fifth straight game with 4+ passing/rushing touchdowns. That performance makes Burrow the second quarterback to ever do that, tying Peyton Manning from the 2004 season. A season in which Manning won the MVP.
Burrow's name was already one of the top names in the MVP discussion prior to Sunday night. Now, it feels like he should be leading that conversation.
This team has been on another level offensively this season, but Sunday night's performance was easily the best of the season.
One of the biggest reasons the Bengals' offense has been an unstoppable force has been due to the play of the offensive line. Burrow was sacked just one time by the Steelers. Most of the night, it looked as if the Bengals quarterback could stand in the pocket all night.
Fans should celebrate this one. There aren't many times when the Steelers come to town and leave with a loss this bad. However, let's take a closer look at the road ahead.
Sunday night's win put the Bengals atop the AFC North. The Bengals moved to 7-2 on the season and now control their postseason destiny.
The Bengals still have two matchups with the Cleveland Browns remaining, and a chance to sweep the season series against the Ravens in Week 17.
While the divisional games are important, the Bengals have a massive chance to stretch their lead in the AFC North with games against the Washington Commanders and the New Orleans Saints coming up.
For the first time in what feels like a long time, the Bengals are on a path where the AFC may run through Cincinnati.

title: Cris Collinsworth Compares Bengals’ Passing Attack to 2007 Patriots
full_text:
Cris Collinsworth is comparing the Cincinnati Bengals' recent passing surge to some of the most memorable offenses in NFL history.
The NBC analyst on the call during Cincinnati's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh on Sunday Night Football pointed to Tom Brady and Randy Moss' 2007 Patriots and the Rams' Greatest Show on Turf when discussing the Bengals' offense.
Cris' son, Jac Collinsworth, also praised Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, citing Burrow's league-leading PFF grade and describing both receivers as playing at a top-five level across the league.
“One of the hottest passing months I've ever seen," Cris Collinsworth said. "Not just from a Bengals team. You start going back to what Tom Brady and Randy Moss did in '07, the Greatest Show on Turf. I mean, they really have been that dynamic here with some spectacular plays."
Cincinnati has won four straight games, scoring at least 31 points in each win. During that stretch, Buurrow has completed 77.0% of his passes for 1,215 yards and 16 touchdowns, with only three interceptions.
PFF's QB rankings confirm what Jac Collinsworth said about Burrow being the highest-graded player (95.2) at his position. Lamar Jackson (91.3) and Drew Lock (90.8) are the only two QBs with grades over 90, though neither has played in every game this season.
Jac also cited Burrow's 18 big-time throws before praising the receivers he throws to every game.
“Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase both playing like top-five receivers in the league,” Jac said.
Both receivers delivered in Cincinnati's Spain win, a 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown, including a memorable 47-yard score in the first half. Higgins added five catches for 32 yards and two touchdowns.
The Bengals and Steelers both entered Sunday night's matchup at 6-2, with first place in the AFC North on the line. Pittsburgh won the first meeting, 30-27 and took it on the chin under the White-Bengal lights
It marked the first time the Bengals played on Sunday night since Nov. 17, 2024.

title: Browns Have One Major Problem to Fix During Their Much-Needed Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns can't run the football.
Let's just say it how it is.
To begin the 2026 NFL regular season, the Browns entered as one of the league's most unexpected sides. Not because they made a bunch of high-level additions, but because they made a few small, team-fitting moves.
Offensively, they added a whole new chunk of youngsters through the NFL Draft, all while bringing in some veterans through free agency and trades.
But unfortunately, the changes made to the offensive line haven't quite panned out the way the front office had hoped they would.
Through the first half of the year, the Browns are 6-4, yet the offensive line has hurt them countless times. The pass protection has led to starting quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders being sacked a whopping 42 times, while the rushing game has barely been able to get out of the backfield, averaging a measly 3.8 yards per attempt.
That's not going to cut it long-term, especially if the Browns want to legitimately compete in the playoffs.
During the bye week, the Browns must focus on finding more success for the offensive line. According to Pro Football Focus, the unit ranks 19th overall out of 32 teams.
Watson and company will be okay in the passing game, but if that rushing attack can't get going, the Browns are going to be limited.
Through nine games, Judkins has rushed for 423 yards and four scores on 126 attempts, all while picking up 22 first downs along the way. He is only averaging 3.4 yards per attempt , though, and 47 yards per game.
That just isn't enough, especially when the Browns' offense is trying to expand the passing game more.
But it isn't all Judkins' fault.
Rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano, who have stolen much of the offensive line's spotlight this season, have done a good job at protecting the pass, but even they both have struggled in the rushing game. Fano's ranking sits at 26th out of 72 in the league , while Barber's is 25th out of 77.
The rest of the group, Elgton Jenkins (29th/35), Zion Johnson (26th/77) and Tytus Howard (52nd/72), all need to make better strides in their ability to free up lanes for both Judkins and counterpart Dylan Sampson.
While Judkins' numbers are down , Sampson's usage is practically nothing.
He was injured in the early parts of the season, but has still not been in the equation much when healthy. Averaging more yards than Judkins, though, he has 19 carries for 79 yards and zero scores. Jaleel McLaughlin, who got a lot of work when both backs were injured, also has been pretty effective in limited opportunities . He has 11 carries for 72 yards and one touchdown.
The offensive line may not be all to blame for the rushing attack's struggles this season, but the protection and ability to free up lanes start with them.
From there, the coaching staff needs to find better usage of Judkins, Sampson and McLaughlin, giving each a chance to establish themselves in a running back room that is averaging well below 100 yards per game.
After all, somehow, Watson ends up carrying the total rushing yards in a game at times.
The Browns are a really well-rounded side, but it is obvious that the running game is lackluster. If they can make ample improvements during the bye week and come back out on the other side stronger, they will be better positioned to not just make a push for the playoffs, but for the top spot in the AFC North as well.

title: Cleveland’s 6-4 Start Has Put This Unexpected Browns Storyline in the Spotlight
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns enter their bye week with a surprising 6-4 record and sit in the last wild card spot. They were projected to have five wins, which they have already exceeded. Each of their six wins has been of the fourth-quarter comeback variety.
No one is more emblematic of their success than Deshaun Watson.
Coming off the lack of success, baggage, and a host of injuries since an all-time failure of a trade , Watson’s career was considered over. However, in his fifth season in a Browns uniform, his resurgence was not an expected storyline going into the bye week.
Todd Monken pitted Watson against Shedeur Sanders in training camp to find a starting quarterback. Reports out of training camp were not good for either quarterback, and videos came out of practice of the football hitting the ground. Then the final nail in Watson’s career was just about hammered in during the preseason.
Sanders got the start in the second preseason game , and Watson relieved him in the second half. After an optimistic first half from Sanders, Watson came in and missed a lot of throws. The fans sensed that this could be their last time having to watch Watson, and the boos were heard through the television.
After the game, Watson spoke to the media and called out the fans for their actions. Monken still believed in Watson and named him the starting quarterback. Fans and pundits alike were shocked and it was only a matter of time before the offense got handed over to Sanders. Then the Browns got walloped against Jacksonville in their first game, and the offense looked lost.
Reports were that if they lost their second game in Tampa Bay, then Sanders would start for their first home game. After the first half in Tampa Bay, the Watson experience’s light nearly died out, but then came the second half that changed his career.
They came back and won against their former first-overall pick, Baker Mayfield, and Watson kept his job. He did not relinquish it as he continued to provide incredible play in the fourth quarter on their way to five more wins.
The performance has not always been pretty, but Watson has made play after play when it counted the most. He has looked more comfortable in the offense each week, evidenced by him throwing for 300 yards in each of his last three games. The offense was at its best down 17-0 last week against the Houston Texans when Watson started to show off his arm.
Watson threw the ball downfield more than ever as a Cleveland Brown on Sunday, which led to big plays. He is not only affecting the offense with his arm, but he has been just as important on the ground. Watson is second on the team in rushing yards and has been able to escape collapsed pockets to gain crucial first downs.
Last week, Monken opened up the offense by running read options with Watson. He led the team in rushing for the game and used his read-option ability for the first touchdown of the game.
He is getting more comfortable with his receivers and is more in tune with the flow of the game. After all the time that he missed, Watson is relearning what it takes to be an NFL quarterback. There was never a belief that Watson would play past this season for the Browns, but now they may have to seriously look at a new short-term contract.
The Browns are in the playoff hunt and have been the surprise team of the year in the league. Nothing is more surprising than Watson leading the team to six wins while improving with each start .
Watson has risen to the occasion every time his back was against the wall, which was a storyline ranked lower than the Browns' playoff hopes at the beginning of the season.

title: 5 Browns Players Who Could Benefit Most From the Team’s Bye Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns will have a chance to unwind during their bye in Week 11 before gearing up again for the home stretch of the season, one that could still deliver a postseason berth .
Usually, the time off is great for players coming back from injury, but it also affords a chance to refocus for a number of guys who might be losing some steam as the campaign progresses.
Here are five Cleveland Browns who could end up benefiting the most from the team’s bye week :
Bond was supposed to be a big factor for the Browns’ offense in multiple receiver sets, but his role seems to be shrinking.
Bond hasn’t seen a target in the team’s last five games, with his contributions coming only on special teams, where he’s taken over kick-returning duties. For the year, he’s caught five balls for 86 yards, and if he keeps his current pace, he’ll end the season with nine receptions for 146 yards, way below the 18 catches for 338 yards he compiled last year as a rookie.
Maybe the week off will allow Bond to figure out how to get back into the lineup and recover some of the lost targets that he saw at the start of a very promising year.
The first-round rookie has been struggling off the edge lately, particularly since the ugly loss at Pittsburgh.
Expecting a rookie to slump during the year while playing a high-pressure position is totally normal, so there’s no need to sound the alarm . But Fano might benefit from using this week to take a step back, catch his breath, and then roll up his sleeves again for what’s coming up next.
Graham started out 2026 with a bang, collecting four tackles through the first three games. He has had none since.
After an MCL sprain and an ankle sprain forced him to miss two games, Graham returned to the lineup. But he’s struggled at times, along with the rest of the defensive line.
Graham went two full games without a single stat, although he did record three tackles for a loss on the road against the Steelers and a quarterback hit against the Saints. And while Graham’s sacks are missed, the Browns’ run defense needs solid improvement, fast.
The fourth-year defensive back missed last weekend’s matchup against the Texans due to a concussion, so he needs all the rest he can get at this point.
If all goes as expected, Hickman will retake his starting spot alongside Grant Delpit in no time.
The mental block was supposed to be gone. The first sack in a Browns uniform has yet to arrive.
Perhaps no one in Cleveland’s organization needs the week off more than Verse, who's working with a psychiatrist to shake off the criticism after 10 sackless games and re-center his focus on just playing the game the way he knows how.
Verse’s snap percentage on defense has dipped a little over the past two weeks, so having the bye at Week 11 could do wonders for his body, too.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns' 17-Point Comeback Win Revealed Something Important About Todd Monken's Team
full_text:
The Browns are finding ways to secure unexpected victories, as shown again on Sunday. Cleveland found itself trailing 17-0 at the start of the second quarter against the Houston Texans, but rallied to win 27-24.
Much of this success can be attributed to the Browns' head coach, Todd Monken.
Monken has boosted players' confidence and created a new culture that empowers them to win in any situation. In many ways, the Browns mirror Monken, who has an inspiring underdog story of his own.
The 60-year-old head coach has spent 37 years working toward his dream of walking the sidelines as an NFL head coach. Monken began his coaching career as a graduate assistant at Division II Grand Valley State and worked his way up through various coaching roles over the years. However, he never had a chance to be an NFL head coach until the Browns hired him at 59, just a few weeks before his 60th birthday.
Monken took on difficult jobs in both college and NFL ranks to become an NFL head coach, and he never stopped fighting for that dream. It sounds like what the Browns do every Sunday: never stop fighting until the final whistle blows.
Defensive tackle Maliek Collins even thinks the Browns take on Monken's personality.
"We're a reflection of our head man. You know what I'm saying? He's a gritty, gritty [expletive] old, you know what I'm saying? And we do our best to show that," Collins said on Sunday, via Chris Easterling.
In four of their six wins this season, the Browns overcame double-digit deficits, trailing by 10 points against the Buccaneers (Week 2), Ravens (Week 6), 14 points against the Titans (Week 7) and 17 points against the Texans (Week 10).
All six wins came on a fourth-quarter game-winning drive led by quarterback Deshaun Watson.
The Browns might not have the talent advantage in most of these games, but they've shown they have the fight and heart to pull out these wins. There is no reason why the Texans should have lost a 17-point lead to the Browns, especially given all the talent Houston has. But the Browns just wanted it more, which reflects on Monken.
Cleveland will head into its bye week and then return to play the Las Vegas Raiders on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 12.
A win would improve the Browns' record to 7-4, putting them in a good position for a wild-card playoff spot.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Highly Anticipated Browns Matchup Against 2026 No. 1 Pick Flexed to Primetime
full_text:
On Tuesday, the NFL announced that the Cleveland Browns vs. Las Vegas Raiders matchup in week 12 will be moved from 1:00 p.m. to Sunday Night Football.
The game takes over the spot of Chargers vs. Patriots. The change comes after the poor 1-8 start for Los Angeles and the recent injury to Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.
This game will be the second primetime game of the season for the Browns, who may have some big advantages in the game.
Flex: The Week 12  Raiders at  Browns game will move to Sunday Night Football while the Patriots at Chargers game will move to 4:05 p.m. ET and the Titans at Jaguars game will move to 1 p.m. ET.
Heading into this AFC matchup, the Browns get some much-needed time off with a bye in week 11. Meanwhile, for Las Vegas, they will be coming off a game in Denver against the Broncos.
This should play a big factor for Cleveland. Not only has the team played 10 straight games, six of them have been on the road.
The other thing to note is the upcoming schedule after this game.
The Browns were gifted with five straight weeks at home in the heart of the season, and still have three to go.
Being able to get rest, spend time with family, and not have to worry about traveling for nearly another month should give a morale boost to the locker room.
In recent memory, any time you think about the Browns at home in a prime time game, you think of a memorable win.
Not only is this another winnable game for Cleveland, history also shows that their odds to win were boosted the very second the flex was made.
The last time the Browns lost a primetime game at home was week 14 of the 2020 season, when the Baltimore Ravens came to town and provided us with a fantastic 47-42 game.
Regardless, its been over half a century since the Browns have lost one of these big games, and after a look at the game itself shows why the Browns should be in a great position to win.
Not only should this be a fun game to watch, but the playoff implications make it even more important.
Taking a look at the AFC side of the playoffs, here are the current standings:
For the Browns, they are currently in the playoffs as the last wild card spot. Looking at Las Vegas, they barely sit out at the ninth seed.
Looking at the standings as a whole,  the Patriots and Ravens are now without their quarterbacks , while the Browns just beat the Texans.
In other words, a win here for Cleveland puts them in a really good spot to at least sneak into the postseason.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Weighing the Pros and Cons of Browns Signing Deshaun Watson to Contract Extension
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns face many major decisions going into the 2027 offseason. At 6-4 entering the bye, the Browns have seven games left to evaluate their roster and decide what comes next at quarterback.
Prior to the 2026 season, it seemed like a foregone conclusion that the Browns would move on from who they once thought was their franchise quarterback, Deshaun Watson. Cleveland acquired Watson and a 2024 sixth-round pick from Houston in 2022 for three first-round picks, a third-round pick, and two fourth-round picks.
Despite high expectations, Watson struggled to deliver in his first four seasons with Cleveland. An 11-game suspension and injuries limited him to 19 games, during which he threw for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions.
Watson and new head coach Todd Monken, however, had other plans.
Despite major pushback, Watson was named the Browns' starter for the 2026 season. Cleveland opened with a loss to Jacksonville, but Watson has since led the game-winning drive in all six of the Browns’ victories.
strollin' into the end zone! #HOUvsCLE on Fox pic.twitter.com/wwrB6r3qBi
Watson has thrown for 2,118 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. He’s topped 300 yards in each of his last three starts, but he hasn’t thrown a touchdown pass in his last four. His play late in games is what makes the case for bringing him back for another year.
In March 2025, Browns co-owner Jimmy Haslam said the team  “took a big swing and miss” with Watson. Now Cleveland has to consider whether he could serve as a bridge while the team develops a younger quarterback.
The Browns Owner Jimmy Haslam said "the team is still recovering from a big swing and a miss on Deshaun Watson." He adds, "hold me and Dee accountable". pic.twitter.com/okFloN5tOE
Watson could command a large amount of money, more than Browns fans may expect, to return to Cleveland as that bridge. Looking at the recent quarterback market, names like Aaron Rodgers and Jacoby Brissett come to mind when trying to compare what a contract may look like.
Pittsburgh guaranteed Aaron Rodgers $22 million for 2026, while Arizona guaranteed Jacoby Brissett $15.5 million. Those deals suggest a one-year contract around $18 million before incentives could be a realistic starting point for Watson.
That would be a new expense for Cleveland.
The Browns still have roughly $86.2 million in cap charges left from Watson’s fully guaranteed $230 million contract, before any insurance credits.
The Browns’ decision to trade for Deshaun Watson divided the fan base amid multiple allegations of sexual misconduct stemming from his time in Houston.
If Cleveland considers an extension, the team has to decide whether another season with Watson as a bridge quarterback is worth prolonging what many fans see as a dark chapter in franchise history.
#Browns HC Todd Monken on how Deshaun Watson has turned things around from the Bills preseason game where he called out fans who booed him: "When we met after that, it really wasn't about his physical traits; it was really where you are mentally and emotionally...'Did you get… pic.twitter.com/aAhPQt54Kh
Watson already knows Monken’s offense and could give a younger quarterback time to learn it before taking over. The arrangement would make sense only if Watson were comfortable mentoring that player and stepping aside when the Browns felt he was ready.
The Browns still have time to make a decision on Watson. With seven games left, Cleveland can see whether Watson stays healthy and sustains the play that has put him in the Comeback Player of the Year conversation.
Watson has given the Browns a reason to consider another year. How he finishes the season will help them decide what that year is worth.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: This Underrated Defensive Back Is Making A Major Case For All-Pro Consideration
full_text:
There seems to be a revolving door of talented cornerbacks in the NFL each season.
However, none seem to stick around and provide lockdown coverage week in and week out like the Cleveland Browns' Denzel Ward. No matter which wideout he is expected to cover, he plays lights-out.
And although he may not always get the respect he deserves, it should be coming his way soon.
On Sunday, Nov. 15, the Browns took down the Houston Texans in a nail-biting finish, 27-24, to improve to 6-4 on the year. While starting quarterback Deshaun Watson stole the headlines with his sixth game-winning drive of the season, Ward was just as important to the Browns' ability to sneak out a victory.
Denzel Ward is the best CB in the league idc pic.twitter.com/UX24NDRGEV
"A lot of man-to-man, a lot of blitzes … they got their money’s worth out of this week," Ward said with a smile, speaking on the Browns' defense against Texans quarterback CJ Stroud.
He finished the game with three pass deflections and four total tackles, limiting Stroud from getting the team back in the game. According to Next Gen Stats, he allowed just four catches for a measly 16 yards on nine total targets.
Heading into the game, Texans wideout Nico Collins praised the lockdown cornerback and knew the day was going to be tough.
"Denzel, man, been one hell of a player for a long time in this league. Great Pro Bowler, man. Great with his feet, hands, technique," Collins said. "It's a great feeling to go against the best in this league, man."
Ward would go on to be awarded the Browns' game ball due to his efforts.
Most forced incompletions in Week 10 Denzel Ward             3 14 players tied         2 The Warden stays CLAMPING the offense 🔒 pic.twitter.com/aZOwmivuO1
"That is what it is all about," he said when asked about receiving the game ball. "That's why I play the game. Whatever happens on the field, you know, it doesn't matter; all that matters is coming home with the win."
On the season, the 29-year-old sits at just 3.8 yards allowed per target this season, which is the second-fewest among defensive backs entering the late window.
Browns cornerback Denzel Ward allowed 4 catches for just 16 yards on 9 targets against the Texans, recording 3 passes defensed. Ward has allowed 3.8 yards per target this season, second-fewest among CBs entering the late window (min. 30 targets). @HOUvsCLE | #DawgPound
He also has 38 combined tackles, one quarterback hit, 12 pass deflections, two forced fumbles and three interceptions . His total in interceptions is tied for the most in a single season in his entire career, flashing that, although he may be aging, he is still one of the game's most reliable cornerbacks.
As selfless as he is, and has always been, earlier this season, he credited his ability to keep playing at a high level to the image of success the Browns have embodied.
"Yeah, [Monken and Rutenberg mean] a lot. Just their leadership and the schemes that they brought in," he said. "I think the entire team has bought into it, and that's the biggest thing, once all guys are on the same page and bought into the system and believe in what they're coaching and what we're doing. After that, it's just about playing fast and letting your talents and abilities take over. I think that's the biggest thing for us.
"You can't do nothing but appreciate that you want somebody that's going to tell you what it is and be honest with you and like, okay, this is what you need to do to get better, or this is what you're not doing good at. That just gives you direction and can help you get to where the whole team wants to go."
No one else wants to say it.. fine I got yall. Denzel Ward needs to be in the running for DPOY. 🔒 https://t.co/THnMBjEZad
While he has five Pro Bowl selections across nine seasons in the NFL, somehow, someway, he has yet to earn All-Pro honors.
And if he keeps up the current pace he is on, there shouldn't be a shadow of a doubt that this year is finally the one where he gets the national recognition he deserves. After all, Pro Football Focus does have Ward honored as a mid-season All-Pro selection with a 90.6 overall grade , the best in the league.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: 3 Browns Who Deserve More Credit After Cleveland’s Comeback Win Over Texans
full_text:
In their week 10 matchup, the Cleveland Browns defeated the Houston Texans 27-24.
As a team, the Browns managed to once again make an incredible comeback. This time, from a 17-0 deficit.
Here are three players who stepped up big in Cleveland's win on Sunday :
In just his second season, Harold Fannin Jr . is already proving to be one of the best tight ends in the entire NFL.
Over the past three games, Fannin has caught 19 passes for a total of 287 yards and that huge overtime touchdown against the New Orleans Saints.
Despite a slower start to the season, Fannin is emerging as a trustworthy pass catcher for any Cleveland quarterback and has also shown his incredible playmaking ability after the catch.
In this game specifically, Fannin posted seven catches for 91 yards. Included in this stat line was his major 30-yard play, which set up the go-ahead touchdown by Quinshon Judkins with less than a minute remaining.
Really upset that this INT didn’t count for #Browns rookie SAF Emmanuel McNeil-Warren. Another young playmaker that has been awesome this season. pic.twitter.com/l0zTReeOKS
It seems as if every game he plays, two things get clearer about Emmanuel McNeil-Warren. First, he gets better in every outing. Second, the Browns got the steal of the draft by selecting him at pick 58.
In this contest, the rookie recorded the team's third most tackles with eight. If it weren't for a penalty (which could have gone either way), he would have had his first career NFL interception as well.
However, the stat line can only say so much.
If you were to actually sit down and watch the film from this game, your first thought probably wouldn't be rookie.
Already, McNeil-Warren is playing like one of the league's best. The Browns most definitely have a bright future as well with the Toledo product.
Arguably the most surprising performance of the week came from the former Texan himself. And I'm not talking about Deshaun Watson.
This offseason, Cleveland made yet another trade with Houston. The Browns acquired Tytus Howard in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round pick.
Since the deal, Howard has been the starting Right Tackle for the Browns. Now, before this game, he put up average numbers and ranked in the middle tier of all tackles in the league, according to PFF.
That was until the Texans showdown.
Howard finished the game with the second-highest PFF grade on the Browns, posting an 83.3 rating. Not only is that a great number to receive, but Howard achieved it in 68 snaps.
While the Browns still have some things to figure out as they head into their Week 11 bye week, the playoffs are most definitely still on the table.
Having these players step up just proved Cleveland can win tough games against teams with great players.
If anything, these three guys should give Browns fans hope that the future of this team may actually be brighter than most think.

title: It Took a Bit of Time, But Deshaun Watson Finally Seems To Understand Browns Fans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns weren't expected to be competing for a playoff spot at this point in the 2026 campaign.
Yet somehow, someway, led by controversial starting quarterback Deshaun Watson, the Browns have a clean path to not just making the playoffs, but winning the AFC North.
This past Sunday, the Browns took down the Houston Texans at home from Huntington Bank Field, with Watson leading the charge. He led the offense down the field for his sixth game-winning drive of the season, helping the Browns improve to 6-4 on the year with a 27-24 victory.
"That was one of the reasons I chose here...," Watson began when asked about Browns fans. "You know, growing up and playing against Cleveland over the years when I was in Houston... all they want, again, is winning: a winning quarterback, a winning team, and everything will be pretty good. So, giving them something to cheer about this Sunday...
"One day out the week, to be able to walk around and be proud. To say they are a Cleveland Brown."
Deshaun Watson on Browns fans: All they want is a winning quarterback and a winning team … pic.twitter.com/fgZGbdGDqn
And although just months ago Watson was at war with the fans, the two sides have found some middle ground. What is at the center of it?
"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance. It's a little bit [more] personal than that," Watson said following a Browns preseason game where he was booed off the field. "So I think it's a disrespectful thing....Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. And that same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt.
"So what does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially for your own city, and they cheer?"
At the beginning of the 2026 season, the 31-year-old was at odds with the fanbase. The Browns had just lost an absolute blowout to the Buffalo Bills, 31-7, as he finished the game completing 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards with one interception.
While he may have believed the boos were personal, they just simply weren't. The Browns fans just wanted to see Watson play good, especially if he was going to be the starting quarterback.
And it may have taken a few weeks to settle in, with a lot of growing pains along the way, but Watson is starting to look like the quarterback he once was in Houston.
Browns fans ADORE Deshaun Watson pic.twitter.com/2zWS7oyqji
In the Week 10 win, he threw for 312 yards on 40 attempts, completing 25 of them with a mark of 7.8 yards per reception. He did throw one interception, which really wasn't his fault, while also adding eight carries for 49 yards and one touchdown on the ground.
On the season, he is now up to 2,118 yards through the air, seven touchdowns and four interceptions . With his game expanding on the ground, he has 266 yards and two scores.
Following Sunday's win, head coach Todd Monken echoed Watson's sentiment. He also gave deeper insight into his decision to make him the starter.
'Did you get this off your chest? Have you really let go? Have you really let go of the frustrations over the last few years that's been on your heart," Monken said about the conversation he had with Watson after his preseason comments. "But if haven't—you can say it—but have you really let go of it? And if you haven't then it doesn't matter what we do; it doesn't matter if you're physically healthy, mentally you're not in a really good place.' And I felt like our conversation was on point. I felt like he had let it go; he had got it off his chest.
"I didn't see someone who was broken; I saw someone that was hurt. And there's a difference. I think he was hurt, I don't think he was broken. And I think that was the first step in terms of 'Where do we go from here.'"
#Browns HC Todd Monken on how Deshaun Watson has turned things around from the Bills preseason game where he called out fans who booed him: "When we met after that, it really wasn't about his physical traits; it was really where you are mentally and emotionally...'Did you get… pic.twitter.com/aAhPQt54Kh
Browns fans really only want to see one thing: wins.
And finally, Watson is doing enough to deliver them.
The squad and Watson return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a nice two weeks off due to a bye. They will take on the Las Vegas Raiders in Cleveland at 1:00 p.m. EST, with a chance to move three games above .500.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Examining What Shedeur Sanders’ Future in Cleveland Looks Like
full_text:
The most popular player for the Cleveland Browns tends to be the backup quarterback. At this time in most Browns’ seasons, fans start clamoring for a change at the position to find any glimmer of hope for the next season.
But this year, the Browns are 6-4, and if the season ended today, they would be in the playoffs. Deshaun Watson is coming off three straight 300-yard games , and the offense was humming against a very good Houston Texans defense.
Todd Monken chose Watson to be the starting quarterback after a competition with Shedeur Sanders in the offseason. Monken cited that Watson gave the team the best chance to win. The decision was to the chagrin of everyone outside of the Browns’ locker room due to Watson’s preseason performance both on and off the field.
Sanders got his lone start in New Orleans when they came a two-point conversion short of another comeback win. His performance was similar to that of Watson’s, but the result was a loss.
Now the Browns are headed into their bye week with Watson cementing his grip on the starting position. The team chasing the Browns for the last playoff spot just lost their starting quarterback , and they have a challenging schedule to finish out the season.
#Browns Todd Monken said he hasn't talked to GM Andrew Berry about Deshaun Watson's future with the club. Said they have 7 games left and he's only worried about walk-through on Wednesday.
Watson’s contract expires at the end of the season, and the Browns have too many wins to draft a quarterback high in the draft. While Watson has won six games so far with the Browns, he has not played well enough overall to guarantee that the Browns have to extend him at the end of the year.
His contract will still count against the salary cap for the next two years, and they need a quarterback on a rookie contract.
Sanders will be on his rookie contract for the next two years while Watson’s cap hit is in effect. He will have a full year learning under Monken, so the playbook should come easier to him. Monken was hired for the head coaching job due in part to his confidence that he could squeeze out production from the quarterback room.
Watson has had his best season in a Browns uniform, and Monken has been correct every step of the way.
Monken had enough confidence in Sanders to start him in New Orleans after Watson cleared concussion protocol. The playcalling looked similar to a Watson-led offense, and when the offense needed Sanders the most, he came through. Monken will have a full offseason to create an offense around Sanders’ skill set.
If the season ended today, the Browns would be picking 18th (from the Los Angeles Rams) and 20th overall in the draft. The quarterback class does not look as deep as it did at the beginning of the season, and several teams need a quarterback draft pick before them.
The Browns already have three quarterbacks on rookie deals, and taking a flyer on a mid-round quarterback may be a waste of a roster spot.
The quarterbacks in free agency are no better, as Kyler Murray would be the best option. Murray would not cost much, but his tenure with the Minnesota Vikings was not as fruitful as they had hoped. Kirk Cousins is also a free agent, but he would not be a long-term answer at the position.
Sanders presents the Browns with their best option at quarterback for next season . Monken can tailor the offense towards him and he proved that he can make plays down the field with the rookie wide receivers. The Browns will have to start extending their young talent after next season, and his fifth-round rookie contract is team-friendly.
Although this season belongs to Watson, the future may very well belong to Sanders.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Christian Parker Now Lame Duck Defensive Coordinator, NFL History Shows
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have been looking for a scapegoat after failing to live up to expectations through the first half of the season, and they finally found one in defensive coordinator Christian Parker .
On Wednesday morning, just two days after head coach Brian Schottenheimer failed to give Parker a vote of confidence , it was reported that the team stripped the first-time DC of his play-calling duties . Now, the question everyone is asking is, "What's next?" for Parker's long-term future in Dallas.
Conventional wisdom would tell you this is the nail in the coffin for Parker, and the team will likely move on at the end of the season and search for a new defensive coordinator , marking the fifth change at the position in the past five years.
In fact, NFL history backs up the thought that Parker is now a lame duck defensive coordinator, much like the recent examples of men in his situation who also had their play-calling stripped in the middle of the season.
We can all see how the next chapter of this story plays out. The Cowboys will either move on from Parker after another lost season, or Parker will walk away after being undermined and having his play-calling duties stripped.
There is no reason for Parker to return as "defensive coordinator" if he has no defensive coordinator responsibilities. And as recent NFL history shows, the most likely outcome is the team hiring a new defensive coordinator during the offseason, as Bobby Belt of 105.3 The Fan points out.
There is no need for the Cowboys to continue the charade for the rest of the season, because everyone can see the writing on the wall.
Dallas rolled the dice on an unproven, first-time defensive coordinator and it didn't work. The team bet on potential, and with the spotlight in Dallas, coaches aren't going to be afforded the grace and time to develop as a coach with Jerry Jones' expectations hanging over them.
That's the harsh reality of the Cowboys organization, and it's why Jones needs to open his wallet and pay for a coaching staff that has been around the league and understands what comes with leading America's Team. Whether it be Parker or Brian Schottenheimer, the "first-time" experiment has not worked out in Dallas.

title: Dallas Cowboys Desperate Defensive Change Is Indictment of Brian Schottenheimer
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys made a desperate but necessary change on Wednesday morning, after failing to show any signs of improvement on defense and an embarrassing second-half collapse against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10.
Defensive coordinator Christian Parker was stripped of play-calling duties , with senior defensive assistant and former NFL head coach Mike Pettine taking over play-calling moving forward .
While Parker fell on the sword after head coach Brian Schottenheimer threw him under the bus , you have to wonder what changes should be made next in Dallas. It's not fair that Parker is the only one catching heat for the team's failures.
It all starts at the top, and Dallas' main problem has been a lack of preparation. While Parker is the defensive coordinator, it ultimately falls on the head coach to ensure that the coaching staff and players are all prepared on game day. Schottenheimer has failed to do so. It's easy to blame Parker for the defense's continued struggles . It's equally as easy to blame Schottenheimer for the team's overall failures.
Dallas has fielded a putrid defense for the past two seasons. That's two miserable defenses with two different defensive coordinators. There has only been one constant: Brian Schottenheimer as head coach.
At the end of the day, it's on Schottenheimer to make sure everyone is prepared and in the right position to succeed. That has never been done. Like Parker, Schottenheimer seems to be in over his head and has shown an unwillingness to alter his strategies.
If the head coach is okay with getting stagnant with his game plan, why wouldn't the defensive coordinator follow? Now that Parker has been thrown under the bus , it's all on Schottenheimer to turn things around.
If nothing changes in Dallas with Pettine calling the plays, Schottenheimer should be the next domino to fall. The Cowboys are at a point where they need to strongly consider cleaning house, and if the team takes the next step of removing Parker as defensive coordinator after the season, the best move would be to hit the reset button and completely revamp the coaching staff.
Something needs to change, as Dak Prescott pointed out , and that something may just be the entire coaching staff.

title: Dallas Cowboys Midseason MVP: Identifying Team's Brightest Player in Gloomy Season
full_text:
At 4-6, it’s hard to find too much to get excited about with the Dallas Cowboys. They entered the 2026 season with renewed hope after re-tooling their defensive roster and brought in an ascending talent at defensive coordinator in Christian Parker .
Through 10 games, their defense hasn’t been good at all and Parker is feeling his seat warm up in a hurry . Even with the struggles on defense, the Cowboys still have a shot at the NFC East . That’s surprising given their shortcomings among the coaching staff, which includes head coach Brian Schottenheimer who has been guilty of building a boring and predictable game plan.
The fact that they’ve won four games and remain alive in the division is a testament to the talent they have. Here we give some credit to that talent by identifying the midseason MVP for the Cowboys.
Entering Week 11, the Cowboys have one player who has stood out as their most reliable. Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb is in the midst of another spectacular season and  should cross the 1,000-yard mark this weekend against the Tennessee Titans. Doing so would mark the sixth consecutive season that Lamb has surpassed that mark.
With nine games left to play, Lamb already has 77 receptions for 976 yards and eight touchdowns. Lamb has consistently produced, but also proved he can completely take over a game when necessary.
He did so during their Week 4 win over the Houston Texans when he hauled in 17 receptions for 189 yards and a touchdown. In Week 9, he had 195 yards and a touchdown on 10 receptions, although he was only focused on his lost fumble afterward , vowing to be better going forward.
As good as Lamb has been, he’s not the only player who deserves praise for their individual performance. Two players who have put together excellent seasons and deserve praise are defensive tackle Quinnen Williams and quarterback Dak Prescott.
Williams has been the most reliable player on defense, currently sitting second on the team with 46 tackles. He also leads the Cowboys with six sacks and has 15 tackles for loss.
Also worthy of mention is Dak Prescott. The star quarterback is playing under immense pressure as the defense is surrendering nearly 30 points per game. Prescott also doesn’t have consistent help from the run game, yet has 2,724 yards and a 21-to-6 touchdown-to-interception ratio.
Without these three players, it’s frightening to think how poor the record in Dallas would be.

title: 3 Dallas Cowboys DC Candidates Who Could Replace Christian Parker in 2027
full_text:
The change that Dallas Cowboys fans have been calling for finally came on Wednesday morning, with reports that defensive coordinator Christian Parker has been stripped of play-calling duties .
Play-calling duties now belong to Mike Pettine, who the team hired as a senior defensive assistant earlier this season. When Pettine was brought in after the Cowboys' early defensive struggles , it was a safety net for the Cowboys. It turned out to be a safety net the team needed.
Parker never showed the ability or willingness to adapt his game plans, and after Brian Schottenheimer threw him under the bus following Sunday's second-half collapse against the San Francisco 49ers, the writing was on the wall.
Schottenheimer refused to give Parker a vote of confidence earlier in the week, and now everyone is left wondering what his long-term future with the team could be. Without play-calling duties, Parker is a defensive coordinator in title only, which means he is expendable once Dallas' season is over.
Who could be the next defensive coordinator in Dallas if the team moves on from Parker in the offseason? Let's take a look at the three realistic options.
If the Cowboys' defense can improve with Pettine calling plays and the team miraculously wins the NFC East to punch its ticket to the postseason, it may just save Schottenheimer's job. And if Schottenheimer gets another crack at leading the Cowboys after struggling in back-to-back seasons, he may just owe Pettine a favor.
Pettine brings previous head coaching experience and a lengthy resume, and he would add some stability and continuity to the staff that has already gone through four defensive coordinators in the past four seasons.
Schwartz fits the mold of what Jerry Jones has previously looked for in his defensive coordinators. Jones loves to hire assistants with previous head coaching experience, and Schwartz checks that box. After the failed Parker experiment, it would make sense for Jones to go back to his old ways.
Schwartz most recently served as defensive coordinator of the Cleveland Browns, and watched Myles Garrett win back-to-back Defensive Player of the Year awards.
The best option for the Cowboys would be to completely clean house. Fire Brian Schottenheimer, and let the team's next leading man hand-pick who he has confidence in.
If the team crumbles down the final stretch of the season, it's not fair for Parker to be the only coach who is being held accountable. It all starts at the top, and we know Jerry Jones isn't going to fire himself, so the team should start by firing Brian Schottenheimer, hiring a defense-minded head coach, and letting them pick a protege they can help mold.

title: Dallas Cowboys Officially Make Change With Christian Parker's Defensive Duties
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys promised they were evaluating everything on the defensive side of the ball and would not rule out any changes, and on Wednesday morning, a change finally came. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker has officially been stripped of play-calling duties .
Former NFL head coach Mike Pettine, who was brought in as a senior defensive assistant, will take over play-calling duties. As we called for after the collapse against the San Francisco 49ers, turning the defense over to an experienced coach like Pettine will only help the Cowboys improve on defense .
Parker, however, will remain as defensive coordinator. The change in defensive play-calling duties comes after head coach Brian Schottenheimer refused to give Parker a vote of confidence earlier this week.
"At the end of the day, the tackling and some of the covered stuff really led to the [explosive plays]," Schottenheimer told the media on Monday. "I'm taking a deep dive and looking at everything. "
Now that Parker has been stripped of defensive play-calling duties, you have to wonder what the long-term future holds for him in Dallas. If Parker isn't calling plays on defense, he is essentially nothing more than a glorified secondary coach.
And if the team wants to move forward next season with Parker being a defensive coordinator in name only, it's a demotion that he may not be willing to except, so it's going to be interesting to monitor how the defense responds under Pettine and how Parker responds to losing his most important duties.
Luckily for Pettine, and unfortunately for Parker, the Cowboys' next two games are at home against the1-8 Tennessee Titans and the division rival Philadelphia Eagles, who are just 2-7.
Total Defense: The Dallas Cowboys are officially the league's worst-ranked defense, ranking No. 32 overall. The team allows 393.8 yards per game and has given up 33 total touchdowns, behind only the Las Vegas Raiders (36) and the Arizona Cardinals (35).
Pass Defense: The Cowboys rank No. 26 in the league after allowing 239.7 yards per game and 19 touchdowns. The pass defense has shockingly not been the worst part of Dallas' defense, largely due to the failures against the run.
Run Defense : Dallas is back at the bottom of the barrel when it comes to the team's ability to stop the run, allowing 154.1 yards per game and a league-high 14 rushing touchdowns.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Confirms Why DeMarvion Overshown Played 5 snaps for Cowboys vs. 49ers
full_text:
After the dust had settled from the Dallas Cowboys' Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, one thing that stood about about the snap counts was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown's lack of play time.
Overshown saw the field for just five snaps on defense in the 46-40 loss, which is strange because not only is he a starter, but the Cowboys were getting gashed in the run game and certainly could've used him on the field.
We figured it was Overshown getting punished for his egregiously bad penalty in Week 9, when he ran onto the field to celebrate and was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct because he wasn't an active player for the game due to injury.
However, head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed that was not the reason behind Overshown having his playing time cut.
Instead, Schottenheimer said it was because Dee Winters and Shemar James have been playing very good of late, The Dallas Morning News' Joseph Hoyt reported.
"Cowboys (head coach) Brian Schottenheimer said DeMarvion Overshown’s defensive snap count (5) was more about the play of Shemar James and Dee Winters recently and not a punishment from the penalty the week before. Schottenheimer also commended Overshown’s play on special teams."
Just when we were giving kudos to Schottenheimer for doing the right thing and punishing Overshown, he finds a way to make the decision to cut the linebacker's playing time look puzzling.
Even if he has been happy with James and Winters of late, you would think that after it was abundantly clear neither one was doing much of anything to help step the 49ers on the ground, Schottenheimer would have pivoted to his starter.
Instead, Schottenheimer was content with watching the Niners run roughshod all over his defense to the tune of 214 yards and three touchdowns in the contest.
This is probably a case of Shottenheimer just not wanting to disclose Overshown's punishment publicly, but we certainly wouldn't be surprised if his explanation is true given the incompetence we've seen from Schotty this season.
We suspect that Overshown is going to be back to his normal role in Week 11 against the Tennessee Titans, which would signify either Schottenheimer did punish him or he realizes a James-Winters duo isn't the best Dallas can deploy at the position, because in reality, it isn't.

title: Dallas Cowboys' 3 Biggest Concerns Entering Week 11 vs Tennessee Titans
full_text:
Entering Week 11, there's no shortage of doubt surrounding the Dallas Cowboys. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker are both feeling their seats warm up following a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .
Dallas has a chance to make a run still , but they're running out of time. Fortunately for them, their schedule is soft over the next couple of weeks as they host the 1-8 Tennessee Titans on Sunday, followed by the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles who are without Jalen Hurts.
As for this weekend, the Cowboys are favored over the struggling Titans . That doesn't mean they should consider this an easy win, especially with the following three major concerns looming over their heads.
The Dallas defense was absolutely torched on the ground this past weekend by the 49ers. Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel, and Kaelon Black all had huge runs as San Francisco rushed for 214 yards on 29 attempts.
That's been a theme this season, with Dallas currently ranked 32nd in the NFL in rushing yardage surrendered. In Week 11, they face a Titans' offense that isn't exactly explosive on the ground, but they do have one dangerous back the Cowboys know well.
Tony Pollard is well on his way to a fifth consecutive 1,000-yard campaign, a streak he began in 2022 with the Cowboys. Pollard, who also had more than 1,000 yards in 2023 for Dallas, is in his third season with Tennessee. He's averaging 4.4 yards per attempt and has 628 yards on the year. He's the type of player who can pick up chunks of yardage in open space and the Cowboys are susceptible to leaving a whole lot of space wide open. That's why their run defense is a huge concern against this veteran back.
The run game has not been kind to Dallas on either side of the ball. Entering Week 11, they're just 21st in the league with 1,028 yards rushing. What makes that number feel worse is knowing they have the tools to be very good on the ground.
Dallas boasts an elite interior offensive line and a bruising running back in Javonte Williams. The problem is that they're wildly inconsistent. Williams averaged 3.9 yards per carry in Week 10 after putting up 5.0 the week prior against the Indianapolis Colts. During the Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, he had 2.3 yards per carry, which came after he put up 6.2 yards per rushing attempt.
Unsurprisingly, over their past four games, the Cowboys won the two games when Williams ran well while losing the other two. While they would love to get him on track this week, his lack of consistency has been a real problem.
During their loss to the 49ers, the Cowboys allowed San Francisco to convert on six of 11 third-down attempts. That number was aided by the 49ers running the ball three times at the end of the game to force Dallas to use its timeouts. Without that, the Cowboys were allowing a 60 percent conversion rate.
That's not surprising to anyone who has watched this defense in 2026. The Cowboys simply can't get off the field and are dead last in third down defense. Entering Week 11, they've allowed a conversion 48.8 percent of the time .
Despite being at home and favored, the Cowboys could find themeslves on the wrong side of the scoreboard if they don't address these concerns, with their third-down defense standing out as the most pressing issue.

title: Dallas Cowboys' Path to NFC East Title is Much Simpler Than It Looks
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have had a 2026 season to forget.
There's been massive questions surrounding the ability of head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who have failed to meet the expectations that come with having one of the more talented rosters in the NFL. The Cowboys are 4-6 headed into Week 11's home matchup with the Tennessee Titans.
But despite all of that, Dallas still has a realistic shot at winning the NFC East, hosting a playoff game and giving itself a chance at making a run in the postseason.
ESPN's Football Power Index predicts that Dallas could have an ugly yet simple path to winning the NFC East and simultaneously hosting a playoff game.
Here is what the Cowboys' path to the playoffs could look if they finish 8-9 this season:
Week 11 - vs. Tennessee Titans: WIN Week 12 - vs. Philadelphia Eagles: WIN Week 13 - at Seattle Seahawks: LOSS Week 14 - BYE WEEK Week 15 - at Los Angeles Rams: LOSS Week 16 - vs. Jacksonville Jaguars: LOSS Week 17 - vs. New York Giants: WIN Week 18 - at Washington Commanders: WIN
We're not asking for much here. Losing three games in a row with a bye week squeezed in between isn't exactly "getting hot at the right time."
Dallas could go 0-3 during its tough stretch against Seattle, L.A Rams and Jacksonville -- which would put the team's record at 6-9 after Week 16 -- and still be in position to host a playoff game.
Staring at a 6-9 record headed into a Week 17 matchup with the Giants is dangerous territory to be in. The Cowboys would obviously be in must-win mode against a team they have already lost to this season.
While wins over Washington, New York, Philadelphia and Tennessee -- all of which have a combined record of 11-23-2 headed into Week 11 -- appear more than doable on paper, we've seen that the Cowboys can lose any game to any opponent.
This year's team could truly lose the rest of its games and it wouldn't come as much of a surprise. That's how poor they have been at times.
When it comes to overall talent, the Cowboys have the edge over all four of these teams, but that was also the case against the Arizona Cardinals and Tampa Bay Buccaneers, two poor NFC squads that Dallas has lost to.
Mixing an awful defense with an inconsistent offense leads to a wide range of results, as Dallas has shown.

title: New 2027 Dallas Cowboys Mock Draft Lands LSU Playmaker With Inspiring Story
full_text:
Right now, wide receiver is a major strength for the Dallas Cowboys. They currently have CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens, and Ryan Flournoy, who are all playing well.
That depth could look much different in 2027, however, with Pickens set for free agency. The explosive wideout has proven himself worthy of a massive contract and with Lamb already making north of $30 million per season, the Cowboys might not be willing to invest in Pickens long-term.
Dallas could also prioritize paying cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who is a free agent as well in 2027 and has been lights out when healthy . That's why NFL Draft On SI's Justin Melo believes the Cowboys could be in the market for a wideout in Round 1 next year.
In his latest mock draft, Melo has the Cowboys on the clock at No. 21, which is a pick they received from the Green Bay Packers in the Micah Parsons trade. With that selection, Melo has Dallas brining in Jackson Harris , a 6-foot-3, 205-pound wide receiver who has had a long and interesting journey to get to where he is in his career.
"LSU wide receiver Jackson Harris is starting to see his story be well documented, with an impressive rise from Hawaii to Stanford and Baton Rouge. Harris has been unbelievable this season, and his two-touchdown performance against Texas further improved his pre-draft stock," Melo wrote. "With the Dallas Cowboys potentially heading for another standoff with George Pickens, this pick could end up making sense."
Harris was a top recruit coming out of Berkeley High and was poised to be a star in Stanford. He was a redshirt as a freshman and managed a total of six receptions in two years with Stanford.
He knew he needed a fresh start, which led to a transfer to Hawaii, where Harris had a breakout campaign. Harris caught 49 passes for 963 yards with 12 touchdowns, leading to his transfer to LSU.
Now facing elite competition every week, Harris continues to shine. In 10 games, he has 864 yards and nine touchdowns on 55 receptions. He's inserted himself into the conversation as an early draft pick, and Melo believes he could be the answer if Pickens winds up leaving Dallas in the offseason.

title: Tyler Booker Injury Forces Dallas Cowboys O-Line Shuffle With Latest Roster Moves
full_text:
Losing in Week 10 was bad enough , but the Dallas Cowboys also saw two starters suffer injures as well. During the loss to the San Francisco 49ers, cornerback DaRon Bland and right guard Tyler Booker both suffered high ankle sprains and will miss multiple weeks .
Bland's loss will hurt because of their lack of depth at cornerback, but he hasn't been playing at an especially high level. That's not the case with Booker, however, as the second-year guard is the fourth-highest rated player at his position, according to PFF, with a grade of 83.0 . He's also first in run-blocking with a 90.5.
With Booker out, the Cowboys will turn to TJ Bass, who started four games early in the season when left guard Tyler Smith missed time following thumb surgery . Bass is an experienced reserve, who is 29th at the position with a 66.5 from PFF . While he won't be as impactful as Booker, Bass should keep the line moving forward.
That said, Bass was more than just the backup guard. He's also the primary backup center. That means with him moving to the starting lineup, the Cowboys signed Nick Leverett from their practice squad. To make room for Leverett, they waived guard Ajani Cornelius.
The @dallascowboys waived G Ajani Cornelius and signed OL Nick Leverett to the active roster from the practice squad.
Leverett spent time at guard and center during the preseason and began the season on the practice squad. He was signed to the active roster in September and was released in early October. Leverett re-signed with the practice squad the following day.
A former undrafted free agent out of Rice in 2020, Leverett has spent time with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New England Patriots, and Arizona Cardinals. He joined the Cowboys during the 2025 season and made five appearances this year, playing only on special teams.
Cornelius was a sixth-round pick out of Oregon in 2025 and began his career at tackle. He moved to guard this season, but has appeared in just three games with 14 snaps on special teams.
While he has not been a huge part of the team's plans, the coaching staff appreciates his versatility and would assumedly prefer to continue working with him. For that reason, it wouldn't be surprising to see Cornelius signed to the practice squad should he clear waivers.

title: Courtland Sutton Closing in on Bittersweet Demaryius Thomas Milestone
full_text:
It's been a rough season for Courtland Sutton.
But the Denver Broncos' veteran wide receiver has been an absolute trooper in the face of Jaylen Waddle's rise as the most-targeted pass-catcher, play-calling changes, an early-season Bo Nix slump, and the toughest schedule in the NFL based on opposing defenses.
The Pro Bowler is on pace to post career-low statistics this season, but all that being said, Sutton is poised to join the late, great Demaryius Thomas in the Broncos' all-time record books. By just taking one snap on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders , Sutton will tie Thomas for the fifth-most games played by a wide receiver in team history.
It's fitting in so many ways. Thomas is one of the Broncos' two most historically prolific receivers all-time, along with Rod Smith. And it'll likely be a bittersweet moment for Sutton, knowing that Thomas is no longer with us, having passed away suddenly in December 2021.
Thomas was around in 2018 when the Broncos drafted Sutton in the second round to shepherd and show him the ropes. Thomas was later traded to the Houston Texans during Sutton's rookie year, which created a WR1 vacuum in the Broncos' offense.
Although Emmanuel Sanders remained in Denver, for a time, Sutton would be the one to fill that vacuum by season's end. Like Thomas, Sanders would be traded away the following year, which left no doubt about who the Broncos' top gun was at wide receiver.
Sutton dealt with some serious obstacles in Year 2, catching passes from three different starting quarterbacks, including Joe Flacco, Brandon Allen, and a rookie Drew Lock. That only made Sutton's production all the more impressive, finishing with 72 receptions for 1,112 yards and six touchdowns and earning the first Pro Bowl selection of his career.
Fast forward to today, and Sutton is now the second-longest-tenured player on the roster, behind only left tackle Garett Bolles. Sutton has become one of the Broncos' elder statemen, and is looked to for his leadership as a team captain.
At 31, Sutton is still plugging away. Despite the arrival of Waddle, who has outearned him in targets (52 to 46), Sutton remains Nix's security blanket. Sutton stood behind Nix when the going was tough, confident that "the tide" would turn for his quarterback. And it did.
Over the past three weeks, as Nix's confidence and swagger have returned , Sutton's star has risen alongside his quarterback. We're seeing Sutton come down with those contested-catch balls that have been his signature as a pro.
Sutton only has 25 catches for 266 yards and two touchdowns, but he's moved the chains 18 times. The last three games have seen him catch 15 of his 25 balls for 143 yards and a touchdown, so it's clear that something has changed.
Now that the worst of Denver's schedule is in the rear-view, there's every reason to believe that, as Nix continues to build momentum, so will Sutton. When Sunday's game rolls around, it's going to be a cool moment for Sutton to join his former mentor and friend in the Broncos' record books.
