title: Grading Every Broncos Position Group at the Midway Point
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are about to emerge from their Week 10 bye.
On Wednesday, the Broncos will begin practicing to host the Las Vegas Raiders this weekend, so this is our last chance to take stock of the team at the midway point of the season — or about as close as is possible to halfway with an odd-numbered 17-game schedule.
We've already posted our individual player grades at the bye and handed out our midseason awards . In our last bye-week deep dive, we're grading each Broncos position group.
Let's get to it and see if we can get a feel for which positions are trending in the right direction for the Broncos' stretch run and which ones need to improve fast.
Bo Nix hasn't been great and for the first six weeks of the season, he was downright bad at times. He was hesitant in his decision-making and jumpy in the pocket, which led to offensive stagnation for long stretches in several games.
However, we must factor in two important things: 1. Nix was recovering from a broken ankle that required two offseason surgeries, and 2. He had to do so while going against the NFL's toughest schedule based on opposing defense .
Because of that, Nix always had the benefit of my doubt. But beginning in Week 7, he no longer needed it, as his confidence came flooding back, and he started looking like the quarterback we saw late last season and in the playoffs before he got hurt.
Despite his protracted slump, Nix still played a winning brand of football. He avoided the negative play — sacks and turnovers — and turned it on in the fourth quarter. Without him, the Broncos aren't anywhere close to 7-2 after the toughest first-half-of-the-season schedule I've ever seen.
Given that Nix's last three games have been so vastly improved, and the fact that he helped to keep Denver winning even while he was still going through a personal storm of sorts, he gets a B- as the only Broncos quarterback to take a snap this season.
The only thing keeping the Broncos' running back grade from a D- or worse has been the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman. Since he returned from injured reserve in Week 7, the Broncos' rushing offense has improved, but the rookie needs help.
J.K. Dobbins is having a career-worst season, averaging 3.3 yards per carry, while RJ Harvey, before he got hurt, was a relative non-factor as a ball-carrier and not quite as productive as a receiver out of the backfield. Harvey will be eligible to return from IR in Week 13.
This is a position group that could finish the season with a much better grade. But I shudder to think where the Broncos would be without the promise of Coleman.
The Broncos' wide receivers have performed drastically below expectations. But remember: it's a quarterback-dependent position.
Not only were the Broncos' wideouts stuck with Nix's slump and the early-season schematic issues of first-time play-caller Davis Webb, but they also had to go against some of the best secondaries in the NFL. Because of these factors, the benefit of the doubt plays a big part in their midseason grade.
I expected more from Jaylen Waddle, sure. But when Nix has been willing to challenge defenses vertically, he's made great use of Waddle. Now that Nix is hunting again with the football , I expect the second half of the season to be much more prolific for Waddle.
I won't deny that Courtland Sutton has disappointed me this season. He seemed woefully slow early on and unable to separate in coverage. Worst of all, he wasn't fighting for the ball, let alone coming down with it, in contested-catch situations, which has always been his signature play.
Like Nix, though, Sutton has begun to turn it around over the past three weeks, so I'm optimistic that what we saw early on was, again, more a reflection of the level of competition and the quarterback inefficiencies than a true sign that Father Time had taken his toll.
Pat Bryant, when healthy, has been a tremendous boon to the passing offense. Alas, he missed four games with an ankle injury, plus half of the game in which he suffered the injury. But he's back, and immediately made his precence felt by leading the Broncos in receiving yards in Carolina and finding the end zone.
This is another position that could finish with a higher grade than it has at the midway point.
What can I say? The Broncos' top two tight ends can't block, and neither has been able to affect the passing game and create exploitable mismatches.
That's an indictment on Adam Trautman as the Broncos' Y tight end, who is expected to at least be a competent blocker, and Evan Engram , who was signed a year ago to be the 'Joker' weapon that Sean Payton just couldn't wait to plug into this offense.
At this stage, the Broncos are stuck with Engram through the 2026 season, but they'd be wise to give Nate Adkins more of Trautman's reps as the Y tight end, especially if they want to help this run game get off the mat.
I'm not holding my breath, though.
Imagine what this grade might be, were it not for the All-Pro contributions of left tackle Garett Bolles and right guard Quinn Meinerz holding things together. Even their impact hasn't been enough to keep center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey from turning in bottom-of-the-league bodies of work at their respective positions.
Left guard Ben Powers has been solid, though he unfairly catches some lashings from fans that should be directed at Wattenberg. Powers has been the least of the Broncos' primary O-line culprits.
Garett Bolles simply REFUSES to give up sacks https://t.co/DZjMOmP80c pic.twitter.com/NmM1LSR8cW
The good news is that McGlinchey has begun to play much better over the past few weeks, so I'm hopeful that the bye, combined with the Broncos not having to face an elite opponent on a weekly basis, can lead to Wattenberg improving, too. Again, the run blocking hasn't been good, but the Broncos' O-line stays in the green grade-wise, thanks not only to Bolles and Meinerz, but also because they've allowed the fewest sacks in the NFL.
It could and must be so much better, though.
Zach Allen is once again delivering All-Pro results, with the most QB pressures on the team and co-leading in sacks, with 4.5. He's also one of the NFL's most stout interior run defenders; he's as good as it gets.
D.J. Jones has been hit-and-miss, while Eyioma Uwazurike failed to launch as the Broncos' succession plan for John Franklin-Myers, or at least half of it. Malcolm Roach, though? He represents the other half of the Broncos' post-JFM plan, and he's been more than equal to his opportunity.
With Uwazurike on IR for the next few weeks, the Broncos will have to rely more on Sai'vion Jones, Jordan Jackson, and rookie third-rounder Tyler Onyedim. Hopefully, we see Onyedim continue to dress and get more snaps, because he can actually help turn around the Broncos' woes against the run, as he flashed in Week 9's win over the Carolina Panthers in his first-ever game.
Allen and Roach make this grade. D.J. Jones does well as an interior pass rusher on a part-time basis, but he's been straight mugged in the run game. It's been nice to see Sai'vion Jones get more playing time, but the Broncos' best hope of elevating this D-line may be getting Onyedim on the field more.
Nik Bonitto struggled to get home over the first few weeks of the season, but it wasn't for a lack of trying. He still impacted the game with consistent pressure, and at the halfway point, shares the team sack lead with Allen (4.5).
Jonathon Cooper's return came at an opportune time. Que Robinson continues to do a great job as a depth rusher, but Jonah Elliss did not seem ready to start opposite Bonitto for the first six weeks while Cooper was on the commissioner's exempt list, and then he suffered a lower-leg injury in Week 6 that landed him on IR.
Robinson has been one of the Broncos' biggest pleasant surprises of the season. With Cooper back in the starting lineup, the Broncos' edge presence again looks like we've come to expect over the past few…

title: This Jaw-Dropping Bo Nix Stat Changes the Conversation
full_text:
Say what you will about Bo Nix, but he's a winner.
Despite all the shade Nix gets, nobody can take that away from the Denver Broncos' quarterback, especially after he led his team to a 7-2 start in the face of a gauntlet of tier-one defenses and top-gun quarterbacks in the first half of the season.
Nix's winning ways are nothing new. He delivered 10 wins as a rookie in 2024, snapping the Broncos' previous eight-year playoff drought.
In Year 2, Nix tied the Broncos' single-season record of 14 wins, dethroned Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs as AFC West champions, and secured the AFC's No. 1 playoff seed. Alas, that magical 2025 campaign came to a crashing halt when Nix suffered a broken ankle on the third-to-last play of Broncos' 33-30 overtime win over the Buffalo Bills in the divisional round.
Every Broncos fan can remember where he or she was when the Nix injury news broke. It was devestating.
Bouncing back from that ankle injury, which required two offseason surgeries, was arduous for Nix. His physical injury seemed to heal a bit faster than his psychological wounds, as his early-season struggles seemed to illustrate, but he still found ways to win against some of the NFL's best teams.
According to Gridiron Stats & Info , Nix and the Broncos have faced "the hardest schedule of opposing defenses" so far this season. That's why Nix and Denver's offense deserve the benefit of the doubt, and why optimism should reign supreme as the schedule opens up.
Despite that tough row to hoe, Nix finds himself among elite company in terms of winning percentage halfway through his third season. As Pro Football Focus illustrated in the graphic below, Nix currently ranks sixth all-time in winning percentage through a quarterback's first three seasons since the NFL merger (1966).
Fast starters pic.twitter.com/5rgYdrLWaP
Only Lamar Jackson (.811), Dan Marino (.805), Patrick Mahomes (.774), Russell Wilson (.750), and Ben Roethlisberger (.725) had a better winning percentage thorugh their first three seasons than Nix currently does. And with the Broncos' schedule opening up dramatically after the bye, Nix will have the chance to climb well into the top-five in this statistical area.
Nix wasn't quite himself to start the 2026 season, which was as concerning as it was disappointing . Despite his assurances that he was healthy, something between the ears seemed off, but his confidence and swagger returned with gusto after he rushed for a 62-yard touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7.
BO NIX 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN RUN DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sxC4uWF33r
Counting that game, Nix has exceeded the 200-yard passing mark in the three games leading into the bye. He's built up a nice head of steam for the stretch run.
The hesitancy and jumpiness in the pocket we saw from Nix over the first six games are gone, and he's playing with so much more confidence. The most exciting development? He's hunting with the football again , which will pay dividends coming out of the bye with Jaylen Waddle returning from a concussion.
Amid his early-season slump, as some Broncos fans and local media pundits began calling for Nix to be benched, he shrugged off the criticism and talked about his goal of "peaking" at the right time, which he just reemphasized on the Manning Cast — joining Peyton and Eli Manning — during Monday Night Football .
"I feel good about the spot we're in. Obviously, we've had a tough schedule thus far. We've played some really good teams, but we feel like there's a lot more out there for us that we can accomplish," Nix said on the Manning Cast .
"We don't feel like we're playing our best in certain spots, but it's a long season, and in my opinion, you definitely don't want to peak at the beginning. You want to be peaking as you're going into the playoffs, so we're 7-2, and we're in a good spot."
Bo Nix on the #ManningCast tonight talking to Peyton and Eli about how he feels about the #Broncos coming out of the bye week. And breaking a record held by Peyton. #BroncosCountry @DenverChannel pic.twitter.com/6L8dhJv7rV
The "Star Wars" numbers haven't necessarily been there for Nix, in terms of individual stats, and yet, he became the only quarterback in NFL history to pass for 7,500-plus yards and 50-plus touchdowns while winning 20-plus games in his first two seasons. So it's not as if he's turned in Tebow-esque statistical numbers.
Nix has already set many franchise and NFL records. His first three years have been unprecedented in Broncos history, and while it's a shame he suffered that ill-timed ankle injury on the doorstep of the Super Bowl, his hard work to get back for this season has already paid off.
The Broncos are in a great situation coming out of the bye. It feels like Denver is on a collision course with the Bills to decide the No. 1 seed, which could be decided when the two teams throw down on Christmas Day (Week 16) at Mile High.
The Broncos' bye came at a beneficial juncture this season. The NFL may have brutally frontloaded their schedule, but at least the Broncos' bye came at as close to the midway point of the season as it gets.
It's going to be fun watching Nix continue to stack wins down the stretch, as he looks to climb well into the top-five quarterbacks in winning percentage over his first three NFL seasons.

title: Sean Payton Cracks Door for Broncos ILB Red Murdock to See Field
full_text:
Speaking for the first time since the Denver Broncos completed their bye week, Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton addressed the failed trade for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley that occurred during that period .
While insisting that no " loophole " had been invoked to veto the deal, Payton generally kept a casual tone toward Henley, whom the Broncos admittedly still covet.
“Nothing changed. It was already stated," Payton told reporters via conference call on Monday. "Everything was pretty clearly spelled out. I’m not going to get into the specifics. He’s a prospect we thought—and still do [think]—very highly of. It just didn’t work out and it’s not uncommon with trades. That’s kind of where it went, and I’ll leave it at that.”
More interestingly, Payton was asked for his thoughts on the state of Denver's current inside linebacker corps, which would've been shaken up had the team acquired Henley.
“I don’t view it the same way you do," he said. "We’re going to play the starters and then guys that earn reps certainly will earn playing time. Yes, that’s all I could say to that.”
The Broncos' botched acquisition of Henley was, intentionally or not, an admission that they aren't perfectly satisfied with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad as the starting ILBs. Henley was specifically targeted — from a division rival, no less — and Denver wanted him badly enough to give up two draft picks.
They can claim he was supposed to be "depth," but the Broncos likely had long-term plans for a 27-year-old who wears the green dot in Los Angeles, is an excellent blitzer, and is solid in coverage. (And who's scheduled to become a free agent in 2027.)
With Henley now out of the picture, there's theoretically a chance the team could promote intriguing seventh-round rookie Red Murdock from the practice squad — perhaps not in the days ahead, but by the end of the season.
Murdock had a strong preseason and, as the NCAA's all-time leader in career forced fumbles, would bring a different element to an already elite defensive unit.
“It’s pretty up there," he said in August regarding his confidence level. "I’m very confident I can play at this level, but also confident in the little margins that I need to improve on [because] it can make a big difference when playing at a high level.”
One way or the other, whether it's with Murdock, Karene Reid, or Jordan Turner, the Broncos must begin preparing for their long-term future at the position, which almost certainly won't include Singleton or Strnad. If somebody can be that guy, they need to find out sooner rather than later.

title: Broncos' 7-2 Start Has Overshadowed These Five Disappointments
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 7-2 coming out of the bye, which means there's way more positive to focus on than negative.
But it hasn't all been pretty. It's tough to be too hard on the Broncos, though, given how brutal the first half of their schedule truly was.
The Broncos faced the Kansas City Chiefs twice, all four teams of the NFC West, plus the Jacksonville Jaguars, so a little benefit of the doubt is warranted. But as we take stock of this team entering its stretch run , I'm breaking down the Broncos' biggest disappointments of 2026.
Don't worry; there will be a biggest pleasant surprises edition, too. With that said, let's dive in.
Everyone was excited for Sean Payton's wunderkind to get his chance to call the plays. The hope was that Webb's close relationship with Bo Nix, combined with his talent for offense and coaching, which were heard about often from Payton himself, would lead to big things for the Broncos.
Alas, it didn't. The Broncos were a mostly out-of-sync offense through the first quarter of the season, and Nix looked like a quarterback who'd regressed alarmingly in Year 3. The Broncos weathered the storm at 2-2, but both of their wins were of the comeback variety.
That hasn't changed since Payton took back the play-calling , by the way. Six of Denver's seven wins have been by a single-score margin. But since Payton began calling the plays again in Week 5, Nix and the offense have steadily improved.
I'll always wonder how it may have shaken out for Webb as the play-caller if the NFL had structured the Broncos' schedule a bit more evenly this season, instead of frontloading it with a gauntlet of opponents with top-tier defenses. Webb has taken his demotion of sorts in stride, but in the wake of his meteoric rise through the coaching ranks since 2023, it was the first setback of his young career.
I wish it were otherwise, but Dobbins has been a colossal disappointment this year. Part of the reason for that is the fresh memory of how good he looked in the 10 games he played for the Broncos last year, rushing for 772 yards, but he's looked like a shell of that player.
Dobbins still leads the Broncos in rushing (324 yards), but his 3.3 yards-per-carry average is a career-low. He still has time to improve his rushing efficiency, but he'll be doing so as the No. 2 running back behind Jonah Coleman.
The Broncos re-signed Dobbins to a two-year, $16 million extension in the spring, which amounted to a 4x raise, and that's another reason why the disappointment surrounding his season thus far has been so sharp. The Broncos sniffed around the running back trade block ahead of last week's deadline, and ultimately didn't make a move, but Dobbins's name was reportedly floated in some of those talks.
Since Coleman returned from injured reserve in Week 7, Dobbins has been relegated to a supporting role, and it's not even close. Payton maintains that Dobbins is still "a big part" of what the Broncos are doing offensively down the stretch, but after nine games of relative impotence, I'll believe it when I see it.
Denver's All-Pro tandem of left tackle Garett Bolles and right guard Quinn Meinerz get a pass, because they've been excellent this season, but the other three starters have been a disappointment. There's no way around it.
Center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey have been two of the NFL's worst players at their respective positions, and it's been reflected in the Broncos' run-game inefficiency. Pass protection-wise, they've been a little bit better, but these two are a big reason for the run game's failure to launch.
So, in that sense, it's not all on Dobbins, but Coleman has been able to still make hay behind this O-line, and create for himself, thanks to his burst and vision. The O-line could do so much more to help Coleman and Dobbins coming out of the bye, and we know that Payton and company have been hyper-focued on improving it.
Time will tell, but don't blame left guard Ben Powers . He hasn't exactly played at a Pro Bowl level, but he's the least of the Broncos' O-line culprits this season.
Man, Engram's season started off on the right foot, scoring the Broncos' only touchdown in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs. But it's pretty much been all downhill for the veteran tight end since then.
Engram has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games. He's been asked to block a lot more than he did last year, as the Broncos have moved to more two-tight-end sets, but it hasn't translated to more targets or production.
This is the last year of Engram's deal. He's on the wrong side of 30, and has failed to live up to expectations. He'll likely hit the bricks in the offseason, but the Broncos have to find a way to get younger and better at tight end in 2027 because that position's inefficiencies have also played a big role in their rushing struggles.
Nix makes this list, but he was also my selection for team MVP at the midway point of the season . He remains the Broncos' most valuable player, though that doesn't mean he's their best player.
Without Nix and his clutch-time excellence, the Broncos don't weather the storm of that initial gauntlet at 7-2. We'd be talking about a 2-7 team, maybe a 3-6 squad, if Jarrett Stidham had been the quarterback against defenses like Kansas City (twice), the Rams, the Jaguars, the 49ers, and even the Chargers.
That being said, it wouldn't be a fair list of disappointments if Nix wasn't mentioned. His first six games of the season were concerning. He was indecisive, hesitant, and jumpy in the pocket.
Bo's ankle may have been 100%, but his psyche, in returning from that injury, hadn't quite caught up to the physical recovery. His confidence needed a big boost, and that was honestly a big reason why Payton made the fateful decision to take back the play-calling from Webb: he needed to get Nix back on track, and salvage his self-confidence before it was possibly too late.
Nix's confidence and swagger came flooding back in Week 7 when he rushed for a 62-yard touchdown on that surgically-repaired ankle, and he hasn't looked back. The Broncos are still questing for a full four-quarters version of Nix, but his comportment over the past three games isn't even comparable to his first six games.
I've consistently maintained that the Broncos will go as far as Nix can take them, and even amid his early-season slump, he was still able to do enough to beat some damn good teams and outduel some top-tier quarterbacks, including Patrick Mahomes, Trevor Lawrence, Matthew Stafford, and Justin Herbert, the last of whom makes this short list because Nix had never beaten him before until Week 5.
The Broncos could still get out to a 7-2 start without Nix playing his best ball along the way. Now imagine the heights this team could reach with him firing on all cylinders.
Nix is on the rise, and his goal of peaking at the right time — down the stretch and into the playoffs — is very much on the table. He's back; of that, I have no doubt. But I couldn't go through this article without mentioning how disappointing his first few games of this season truly were.

title: New Mock Draft Predicts Broncos Will Fix What Trade Deadline Couldn't
full_text:
The Denver Broncos had linebacker on the brain ahead of last week's NFL trade deadline.
Given the missed tackles and coverage miscues of Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, the Broncos agreed to a trade for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, but the deal fell through when he failed his physical. Henley would have brought tackling reliability and coverage chops to the middle of the Broncos' defense.
Still unsigned by the Chargers, there's a chance Henley will hit free agency in March, at which point, the Broncos could try to pursue him with a compensation package more in line with their concerns about the arthritis in his knee. But if that doesn't happen, for one reason or another, Denver could be resolved to look to the draft for a linebacker.
NFL Draft On SI 's Justin Melo has mostly been mocking tight ends to the Broncos in Round 1. Last week, he mocked an offensive tackle — which could well be in the cards this time around — but in his latest post-trade-deadline iteration, Melo had the Broncos taking Notre Dame linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa at No. 24 overall.
"Denver Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton turns 33 in December. It will be among the positions that require an investment this offseason. Notre Dame linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa has been a riser. He's an athletic specimen with more upside to explore," Melo wrote .
Age is definitely a factor for Denver at linebacker. Both Singleton and Strnad are on the wrong side of 30, even if both are under contract through the 2027 season.
Viliamu-Asa would offer the Broncos great run-defending upside and also some coverage chops. He would need to develop both aspects of his game further to really thrive in the NFL, but the tools are there.
Listed at 6-foot-3 and 234 pounds, Viliamu-Asa has the prototypical size NFL teams like at linebacker, which was one of the potential drawbacks with Henley, who checks in at 6-foot-0 and 225 pounds. Viliamu-Asa can get off blocks and has the size and strength to mix it up in the box.
It's been a long time since the Broncos drafted an inside linebacker in the first round. The last linebacker to hear his name called by Denver in Round 1 was D.J. Williams back in 2004 during the late-era Mike Shanahan regime.
Since then, the highest the Broncos have drafted an inside linebacker is in Round 3, with Nate Irving in 2011 and Drew Sanders in 2023. Neither linebacker panned out well, though Irving at least played out his rookie deal in Denver.
The Broncos drafted Red Murdock with the last pick of the 2026 draft, but he didn't make the 53-man roster. He has stuck around on the practice squad, though, developing under the watchful eye of this coaching staff, so he'll live to fight another day, and maybe make a push in 2027.
But Denver can't bank on that happening. Singleton and Strnad have displayed their limitations, and with how talented the Broncos are up front and in the secondary, they've been able to get away with it at he second level of the defense.
However, it's high time the Broncos invested some premium resources in an inside linebacker. I'm not 100% sure Viliamu-Asa is the right fit for Denver, and time will tell whether he lives up to Melo's first-round projections, but drafting him would certainly signal a recognition on the team's part that it needs to improve dramatically at linebacker after this season.

title: Broncos Could Dodge a Major Bullet This Week Against Raiders
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' struggles to cover opposing tight ends dates back years. In fairness, though, as NFL tight ends have become more athletic and explosive, they've become an increasingly featured aerial component, so covering the position is a challenge for all defenses.
It just so happens that Denver has been one of the worst defenses at covering tight ends, and that includes this season. The Broncos have given up the second-most receiving yards to tight ends entering Week 10, and with the Las Vegas Raiders coming to town this week, the issue may again take center stage, especially in the wake of the failed Daiyan Henley trade .
Kirk Cousins is now calling the signals in Minnesota, pushing rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza into the starting lineup this week. Raiders tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer accounted for more than 1,000 of Cousins's passing yards this season before he was dealt to the Vikings.
Mendoza targeted his tight ends just six times in his first career start against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, but a big reason for that was Bowers suffering an early ankle injury that kept him out of the second half, finishing with just two receptions for 18 yards.
The Broncos may not have to worry about Bowers this week, as head coach Klint Kubiak revealed on Monday that his star tight end's injury is "significant," even if it isn't as bad as the Raiders feared.
"It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury," Kubiak told The Athletic 's Sam Warren on Monday .
Bowers is "day to day," per Kubiak, so Denver has to plan for the Pro Bowl tight end, just in case. It will be interesting to see how the practice reports for Week 11 take shape, beginning on Wednesday.
Mendoza will be making just his second NFL start this week against the Broncos. That's a tough row to hoe for any quarterback — regardless of whether he's the No. 1 overall pick in the draft — having to face the Seattle and Denver defenses back-to-back to begin his career as a starter. I don't envy the former Heisman Trophy winner.
If Mendoza must face the Broncos without his security blanket, Bowers, he's likely to still look his tight ends' way early and often. Kubiak knows how his bread gets buttered and will likely test the Broncos' leaky tight end coverage when the Raiders are in their base offense, attacking linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad.
Singleton is having one of the best years of his career, but he's struggled mightily in coverage. Teams have identified that and schemed to isolate Singleton in coverage . Strnad is better in coverage, but in relative terms.
Neither is an ideal candidate to run with Bowers, Mayer, or Ian Thomas, so Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph will need alternative plans of attack if the Raiders start attacking with tight ends.
Mendoza will trust Mayer and Thomas if Bowers is unable to go, as he told Hondo Carpenter of Las Vegas Raiders On SI .
"So the next guy up, I have as much confidence in, and so I just need to get the ball to the right players on time, efficiently and accurately," Mendoza told Carpenter.
The Broncos need a better coverage plan moving forward because they're giving up way too many yards, and not just to tight ends. No NFL team have up more receiving yards to running backs entering Week 10 than Denver, and guess who Mendoza's stop target was against Seattle?
You guessed it: running back Ashton Jeanty. Mendoza connected with Jeanty on all four of his targets for 46 yards against Seattle, and once with rookie running back Mike Washington.
Joseph has, at times, deployed cornerback Jahdae Barron as a tight-end eraser, with varying degrees of success. Most of Barron's one-on-one wins against tight ends came last year as a rookie; nobody in Denver has done a good job of blanketing tight ends this season.
Whether Bowers plays or not, you can expect Kubiak and Mendoza to target the middle of Denver's defense with running backs and tight ends. The Broncos were well aware of this vulnerability, which is why they tried to trade for Henley — an experienced linebacker who excels in coverage — but the deal with the Los Angeles Chargers fell through when he failed his physical .
With the NFL trade deadline in the books, the Broncos' linebacker personnel is what it is. To improve against tight ends in coverage, it's going to require some Xs and Os adjustments by Joseph, and maybe some additional help from the secondary players.
If the Broncos can limit the tight ends and backs in the passing game and stop Jeanty and Washington as runners, it could be a long day for Mendoza, making his second career start. We'll keep a close eye on Bowers's status on the practice reports as the week progresses, so keep it locked with Denver Broncos On SI .

title: Sean Payton Pinpoints What's Holding Broncos Back Ahead of Stretch Run
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 7-2, but head coach Sean Payton knows some things need to change coming out of the bye.
The Broncos were back in the building on Monday, and in the first team meeting since Week 9's road win over the Carolina Panthers, Payton laid out to the players "certain areas" that need to improve moving forward.
“Specifically, I mentioned this last week, we need to block better on offense and we need to be in the right place," Payton said on Monday morning. "I thought we did an average job against Carolina, and I think that’s an area of focus relative to more consistency in our run game."
The Broncos' run game has failed to launch this season, and the only thing keeping it out of the NFL doldrums has been the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, since he returned from injured reserve in Week 7. J.K. Dobbins has struggled as a ball-carrier, but the Broncos' biggest issue has been their run blocking, whether it's the offensive line or the tight ends.
Payton sounds much more forgiving of the Broncos' blocking foibles in Carolina now than he did a couple of days after the game. On Wednesday of last week, Payton appeared on The Herd with Colin Cowherd, pointing to the Broncos' run-blocking woes vs. Carolina, and hinting that personnel changes could be in store as he and the coaches drilled down on the subject over the bye.
In Monday's Zoom presser , though, Payton was a bit dismissive of the potential for personnel changes on the offensive line, doing his level best to walk back his comments to Cowherd.
“I don’t think there’s any tie to the interview last week with Colin. I just want to make sure we’re clear," Payton said. "I think in that interview, I made sure to make a point about evaluating all assets of what we’re doing in our front in the offense. So I want to make sure one story doesn’t lead to another. We’ll spend an inordinate amount of time looking at mid-season cutups where we’re at relative to scheme and personnel.”
I'll say it again, just as I wrote last week, the Broncos were always extremely unlikely to bench one of their O-line starters. This team is proud of the fact that it returned the same starting five for the third straight season, and it has a lot of money invested up front; the problem is that Denver has been completely unable to capitalize on such a football blessing.
The Broncos rank 26th in rushing, averaging 91.4 yards per game on the ground through nine weeks. Again, Coleman has moved the needle, and while that's been encouraging, the rookie can't be expected to elevate the Broncos' entire rushing offense on his own. He needs help, and that's, ostensibly, what Payton and run game coordinator Zach Strief spent a lot of time on over the bye.
The Broncos' pass protection early in the season wasn't on par with the previous couple of years, with Bo Nix taking pressure at a career-high rate, but they turned that ship around starting in Week 5 when Payton took back the play-calling responsibilities from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb. Since then, the Broncos have done well in protecting Nix; he remains one of the NFL's toughest quarterbacks to sack.
Speaking of Nix, he's taken some big leaps forward since Payton took back the play sheet, but he really began to build momentum in Week 7. Nix's 62-yard touchdown run against the Arizona Cardinals seemed to unlock something in his return from offseason ankle surgery, and his confidence came flooding back.
Nix has thrown for over 200 passing yards in each of the past three games, which, on the surface, isn't exactly an illustration of a quarterback blowing the doors down, but compared to the four sub-200-yard passing days he had between Weeks 1 and 6. If the Broncos can get the ground game truly rolling, it'll open up all kinds of passing opportunities for Nix, especially in the play-action game.
"The run game hasn't been great. It's something we need as an offense, [that] Bo needs as a quarterback, we need some play-action. It just ties everything in," tight end Adam Trautman said on Monday via 9NEWS ' Mike Klis . "That's our biggest emphasis on offense and we're working to get it fixed."
Payton and the coaches dove deep into the run-game subject over the bye, we can assume with confidence. With the players back in the building to prepare for Sunday's home game against the Las Vegas Raiders, now it's time for the coaches to begin implementing the points of emphasis they discovered over the bye.
Payton is looking for improvements on defense, too. Vance Joseph's unit has been great at rushing the passer and has established itself as one of the NFL's best clutch-time defenses, but Payton demands better execution on third and fourth down.
"Then there were some third-down, fourth-down-and-longs defensively that was an Achilles heel for us a year ago, and the other day became one," Payton said. "Those are just a few things.”
The Broncos rank 21st in third-down efficiency, allowing conversions on 41.2% of opponents' attempts. That's actually an improved mark, compared to where the Broncos ranked for much of the season on third down, so there's reason to believe the improvements have already begun.
On fourth down, the Broncos' defense ranks 20th, allowing conversions 58.8% of the time. Teams are going for it on fourth down more frequently in the modern NFL, and the Broncos will need to improve this area of defense for their stretch run into the playoffs.
The Broncos are 7-2 for a reason. This defense keeps most games close, buying Nix and the still fledgling offense the time to come together and finish strong in the fourth quarter.
Payton would still prefer not to be in so many one-score games, his team's success in them notwithstanding. Denver's early-season gauntlet of a schedule played a big role in some if the inefficiencies Payton addressed in his Zoom presser.
With the schedule opening up now, it's time for the Broncos to prove they can make use of the callus they built up from going against the NFL's toughest first-half-of-the-season schedule. Next up, it's Fernando Mendoza — the No. 1 overall pick in the draft — and the 4-6 Raiders.

title: Sean Payton Pushes Back on Chargers' Accusations: 'There's No Loophole'
full_text:
The botched Daiyan Henley trade has garnered no small amount of scrutiny and criticism around the NFL, intensified by Los Angeles Rams head coach Jim Harbaugh's complaint that a " loophole " in the rulebook allowed the Denver Broncos to ask for a lesser compensation package after the linebacker failed his physical.
Some have all but accused Denver of operating in bad faith, or at the very least, trying to exploit a post-deadline opportunity, while L.A. had no other options, given that the deadline had passed.
In his regular Monday morning Zoom press conference, Broncos head coach Sean Payton declined to go into detail about the trade that never was, but he did dismiss Harbaugh's "loophole" critique.
“I saw it all. There’s no loophole," Payton said. "It just is part of the trade process every step of the way.”
Payton's morning presser began with a question about what had changed with the in-principle trade agreement Denver had with L.A. for Henley.
“Nothing changed. It was already stated," Payton said on Monday. "Everything was pretty clearly spelled out. I’m not going to get into the specifics. He’s a prospect we thought—and still do [think]—very highly of. It just didn’t work out and it’s not uncommon with trades. That’s kind of where it went, and I’ll leave it at that.”
Payton wasn't interested in stirring the pot, but he came prepared on Monday, knowing that it was the media's first chance to get a Broncos shot-caller on the record regarding the Henley trade. But Payton's a savvy guy who'd been around the NFL block, so he offered nothing really, besides "there's no loophole."
It's important to remember that both the Broncos and the Chargers spoke with the NFL front office after Henley failed his physical in Denver. The Broncos sought clarity on what their rights were and whether they could ask to amend their offer to L.A. for Henley, while the Chargers needed to hear from the NFL that Denver had the right to do so.
It didn't go anywhere, and the trade was canceled. That was that. It disappointed Broncos fans, though, that's for sure.
Henley returned to L.A. and promptly practiced in full on Thursday and Friday, with no restrictions or limitations on his puportedly arthritic knee that so scared the Broncos. That only enflamed fans who were trying to understand how bad Henley's knee must have been to cause Denver to back out of the trade.
Daiyan Henley was a full participant in the Chargers' two final practices of the week after his brief sojourn to the Mile High City. Playing on that arthritic knee, no problem, it would seem. *Sigh* pic.twitter.com/FBirY7OTAu
Cynics said, "Well, of course Henley practiced in full. The Chargers would have listed him as a full regardless just to score points in the PR arena." I'm not so sure.
One thing we know is that Denver really likes Henley. Payton's comments further reinforced that, so if the Chargers are unable to get him re-signed between now and the new league year in March, expect the Broncos to pursue him in free agency.
The Broncos saw Henley as more than a short-term rental, which is why they were willing to give up a fourth- and fifth-round pick to acquire him, and were still willing to offer up the fourth-rounder and an additional pick after he failed his physical, just not a fifth-rounder, from what I've gleaned.
It's all water under the bridge now. What hasn't changed since the botched Henley trade is Denver's need for a coverage linebacker . Going into Week 10, the Broncos had allowed the most receiving yards to running backs in the NFL, and the second-most yardage to tight ends.
This team will now have to figure out how to solve that problem with the horses it has. The Las Vegas Raiders are up next, as the Broncos emerge from their bye week.
Whether it's been Kirk Cousins or Fernando Mendoza, the Raiders like targeting their tight ends and running backs in the passing game, so let's hope Vance Joseph has a good plan in place when the Broncos host their long-time division rival on Sunday at Mile High.

title: 5 Unsung Broncos Who've Made Their Case to Stay in 2027
full_text:
The Denver Broncos currently have 25 players set to hit free agency after the 2026 season ends. Some of Denver's free agents will be unrestricted, while others will be of the restricted and exclusive-rights variety.
The Broncos have several key players who could be extended before the 2026 season ends , though with the bye week ending without such a deal, the likelihood has diminished. However, looking past this season, the Broncos have several players who should be retained in 2027 for low-cost deals, even if some of them are better suited as depth or special teams.
These players don't need to be extended before the end of the season, but they should be up for either restricted free-agent tenders or short-term deals as free agency is about to get underway in the spring.
With half the season in the books, let's examine five such players who shouldn't be overlooked when the Broncos start making decisions in 2027.
Key is set to become a restricted free agent in 2027. The Broncos could go in one of two directions: tender him at the second-round level or sign him to a short-term deal.
The second-round tender is estimated at $6.26 million, which is a bit high for a depth and special -teams player, even though Key has been decorated as a third-phase All-Pro. However, if Denver tendered him at the original-round level, another team could sign him to an offer sheet.
The best move for the Broncos is to sign Key to a two-year deal. The original-round tender is $3.82 million, but the Broncos could come in between the two tender levels and give Key, say, a two-year, $9.5 million deal as a reward for his contributions over the past two seasons.
Adkins was a restricted free agent in 2026 whom the Broncos signed to a one-year deal at the veteran minimum. He made the 53-man roster and has proven to be a good blocking tight end and a solid pass-catcher.
The Broncos would be wise to retain Adkins, who might get more than the veteran minimum this time around. A possibility could be a two-year, $7.5 million deal, similar to what Adam Trautman got in 2024.
Speaking of Trautman, it will be difficult to move on from him in 2027 because of his guaranteed money, but the Broncos could cut him in 2028 without much trouble. Keeping Adkins in the fold would give the Broncos an option to eventually take over Trautman's role in the offense.
Tillman is set to become a restricted free agent in 2027. He has proven to be valuable depth on defense, particularly when Jonathon Cooper missed time on the commissioner's exempt list to start the season.
In Tillman's case, the second-round tender would be fine, as $6.26 million is a reasonable salary to pay for what he brings to the defense. But the Broncos could opt for a two-year deal here as well.
A two-year deal for $10 million might be possible and a way to recognize Tillman for his contributions and continued role. It would also allow the Broncos to keep the edge rusher around for more than one season.
It might seem odd to list Badie here, but let's look at the facts. J.K. Dobbins might not be with the Broncos in 2027 , and though Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey would form a good pairing, the team still needs reliable depth.
Badie would give the Broncos an experienced back who could be the No. 3 or No. 4 option in the backfield, particularly with his pass-blocking ability, and would be a much cheaper alternative to Dobbins, who is due $8 million in 2027. Badie has also been good on special teams.
Badie will be a restricted free agent and isn't worth the second-round tender, but the Broncos should be able to keep him for the veteran minimum.
Skinner has had a few highlights on defense , but his play hasn't been good enough to warrant a starting role. However, he's been valuable on special teams.
While the Broncos do have seventh-round pick Miles Scott on the practice squad, they should keep Skinner around because of his experience. That would put less pressure on Scott to fill an immediate hole in 2027.
Skinner will be an unrestricted free agent, and like Badie, is a player the Broncos should be able to retain at the veteran minimum.

title: Jahmyr Gibbs Earns NFC Offensive Player of Week After Patriots Win
full_text:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has been recognized again by the National Foorbtal League for his stellar efforts against the New England Patriots in Germany.
After securing 153 rushing yards on 22 carries, two touchdowns and seven receptions for 99 yards, (252 all-purpose yards) the former first-round draft pick was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff commented postgame about Gibbs' monster performance in a
“I think we got to pinch ourselves sometimes and not take it for granted how special he is. He’s just so explosive with the ball in his hands. We threw that check down to him; it goes 50 yards. That’s so rare for a guy to be able to do all the things he does," said Goff. "Now he’s becoming this back that can protect as well. It’s a complete back. He’s as good as anyone in the league. I love playing with him.”
Among the biggest reasons the Lions' rushing attack has been potent has been the willingness of receivers and tight ends to block for Gibbs.
Second-year wideout Isaac TeSlaa was rewarded for his blocking efforts with a receiving touchdown against New England.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 2026 Midseason Offensive Grades
“I don't think I could express enough the appreciation for that. I've pointed out numerous times to him, to the offense. It's a huge part of who we are," said offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. "Ultimately, it's who he is, which makes him - like yes, he's not showing up on the stat sheet every week, but he has an immense impact on the game and how we do things as an offense. And I think he knows that. I hope he knows that. I've made that very clear to him, I think, because it is. It's a big part of who we are and it's not an easy thing to do and he takes a ton of pride in it."
While TeSlaa has not lit up the stat sheet, his contributions have not been overlooked by his teammates or the coaching staff.
"I think his teammates have a tremendous amount of respect for the way he goes about it. It is. It's impressive and it makes us better, but ultimately, it's a testament to him and who he is and how hard he works," said Petzing. "I think the other element of that is you watch the other two guys who do get the ball a little bit more and they do that in the run game and they do it consistently.
"And to me, if you're going to walk into that room or really this offense and not do that, you've got to look those guys in the eye every day and that's probably not an easy thing to do.”

title: Detroit Lions Are Touchdown Favorites Against Buccaneers in Week 11
full_text:
The Detroit Lions (7-2) will look to capture their sixth straight victory when they take on the likely Baker Mayfield-less Buccaneers (3-6) Sunday.
The Lions are coming off a 35-10 beatdown of the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. Meanwhile, Tampa Bay, which has won two of its last three games, had its bye in Week 10.
Per DraftKings, the Lions, without defensive captains Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson, are presently seven-point favorites to beat the Buccaneers in the Week 11 tilt.
The Buccaneers last played in Week 9 on Sunday Night Football against the Bears, suffering a 27-24 loss to Ben Johnson's team. Mayfield did start the game, and proceeded to throw two interceptions and complete just 56.3 percent of his passes.
The ninth-year passer has had a rough season in Tampa Bay. In six games, he's thrown for more interceptions (four) than touchdowns (three), and has completed only 60.6 percent of his passes. Additionally, his QBR of 32.0 ranks 29th among 31 qualified signal-callers.
Mayfield's backup, rookie Jalon Daniels, hasn't fared much better. Daniels has suited up for five games and made three starts, and has completed 61.2 percent of his passes while throwing for three touchdowns and five interceptions.
Altogether, the Buccaneers have struggled to do much of anything through the air. In fact, they've amassed the least amount of passing yards (1,277) and passing touchdowns (six) through the season's first 10 weeks.
To add insult to injury, Mayfield’s status for Sunday is uncertain as the result of a foot strain. Subsequently, it'll be very interesting to see the type of injury designation Tampa Bay tags him with on its injury report Wednesday.
Meanwhile, on defense, the Buccaneers have been much more productive. They've not only allowed the sixth-fewest points per game (19.8), but they've also been extremely stout against the run. In fact, the Todd Bowles-led squad has allowed both the fewest rushing yards (712) and the fewest touchdowns on the ground (three) so far this season. It's a testament to the fact that Tampa Bay is a better team than its record indicates.
Lions head man Dan Campbell shares the sentiment and expects a dogfight with the Buccaneers Sunday.
“This will be a big one. It's a physical team. These guys play with violence,” Campbell told reporters Tuesday. “(Buccaneers head coach) Todd Bowles has always done a great job. The record is not indicative of the type of team that they are. They're in the hunt for the South. And so, we know what we have in front of us, but no excuses. We're back from Germany. We know this is number two here in this little stretch we've got, and our guys will be ready to play.”
The Lions and the Buccaneers are set to kick off from Ford Field on Sunday at 1 p.m. (EST).

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Midseason Grades: Offense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are off to a solid start, finishing the first half of their season with a 7-2 record.
While they still have work to do over the season's final two months, Detroit has the ability to be serious contenders for a third NFC North crown in four years. They will enter Week 11 with the No. 2 seed in the NFC playoffs, and have an opportunity to continue helping themselves against NFC opponents.
The Lions have been fueled by a number of solid performances on the offensive side of the ball. They currently have multiple players who could be realistic awards candidates should they continue to play at a high level.
Here are grades for each Lions offensive position group as the season passes its midway point.
For the better part of the first half, Jared Goff was playing at an elite level with no turnovers through the first five games. However, things have turned a bit sour as he has turned the ball over four times over the team's last three games.
Though this recent stretch of turnovers has put a damper on his performance, he has still been one of the most consistent passers in the league throughout the first half. He's fifth in the league in passing yards per game, and has largely been efficient during the team's 7-2 start.
While Goff has had his flaws with mobility exposed at times, the Lions have been able to rely on him throughout the season with how consistent he's been. He remains one of the most effective pre-snap quarterbacks in the league, which allowed him to have success against defenses like Minnesota's earlier in the year.
Jahmyr Gibbs is making a serious case to be named Offensive Player of the Year with his phenomenal start to the season. Gibbs has shown himself to be one of the most dynamic players of the league, with four games of over 150 rushing yards within the team's first nine.
Gibbs has undoubtedly asserted himself amongst the league's top running backs, and continues to make strides in other facets of his game as well. The running back is growing as a pass-protector, and has been utilized heavily in the passing game at times as well.
With Isiah Pacheco missing the entire season up to this point, the Lions have leaned on Sione Vaki as the backup to Gibbs. It's proven to be a good fit, as Vaki runs tough and has some pop as a ball-carrier as he's shown.
Like Gibbs, Vaki is also making improvements in the pass-protection element of the game. It remains to be seen whether Gibbs' hefty workload is sustainable, but he's on pace for a stellar season with the way he's started the year.
The Lions have gotten plenty of production out of wideout Amon-Ra St. Brown , who appears to be trending toward another 1,000-yard season in his fifth NFL campaign. He has proven to be one of the league's most durable players, and this year has been no different.
St. Brown is tied-for-third with seven receiving touchdowns, while he ranks ninth in receiving yards at 755.
Jameson Williams has not had the level of consistent production that has been to be expected from him after back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons, but he has still proven to be a big play threat at times. His explosive play rate is down, but he appears to be more well-rounded as a receiver and has delivered big moments such as the game-winner against Minnesota.
Elsewhere, Isaac TeSlaa hasn't had the breakout season many believed he would but has still delivered in some key situations, such as fourth-downs and his first touchdown of the season in the red-zone last week.
The Lions and Sam LaPorta have had some back-and-forth and appear to have reached a standstill in terms of a future contract extension. With all this going on, the Lions have utilized LaPorta less in recent weeks, coincedence or not.
LaPorta is ultimately a huge part of the Lions' offensive attack, as his presence alone is another weapon other teams would have to account for on Detroit's roster. It wouldn't be easy at all for Detroit to replace him, which is why I think a deal ultimately gets done.
Still, LaPorta hasn't had an elite season at this point in the year, and could be utilized more in the coming weeks. Brock Wright has been reliable as a run-blocker, while Tyler Conklin has usurped the youngster Jackson Meeks for the third tight end spot.
The Lions' offensive line has been maligned at times for all the changes they've undergone. Taylor Decker is gone, while Penei Sewell has switched over to the left side to account for that loss. As a result, the team is playing two necomers in center Juice Scruggs and right tackle first-round pick Blake Miller.
Scruggs has been thrust into action, and made the most of it by how well he's playing. Added via the David Montgomery trade last year, Scruggs was forced into playing center after an injury to Cade Mays who has made just two starts this season.
Scruggs and Miller have been solid additions, while Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge have both taken their abilities up a notch at the guard position. Moving forward, the Lions have positioned themselves to have one of the best young offensive lines across the board, as they have been solid particularly in the run game paving the way for Gibbs.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly of Detroit Lions Win Over Patriots
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions started the NFL action for the day, taking on the New England Patriots at 9:30 a.m. EST. The Lions overcame injuries and slippery turf to take down last year’s AFC Super Bowl representative with ease, 35-10.
It was a statement game for the Lions in all aspects, and there was plenty of good in this week’s edition of the good, bad, and ugly.
The Lions offense was prolific in Munich, as Jahmyr Gibbs dominated the Patriots defense with 153 rushing yards in only 3 ½ quarters of action. Gibbs benefited from strong lead blocking, with the left side of the line (Penei Sewell and Christian Mahogany) paving the way.
On Gibbs’s 28-yard touchdown rush, his final carry of the game, the back went nearly untouched, with Sewell pulling and paving the way as Gibbs merely followed behind. Sione Vaki had a few rushes as well, looking just as solid as Gibbs. The line was humming on all fronts in the overseas contest.
It was a prolific day on offense, and Jared Goff was taking what the defense gave him. The Pro Bowl passer found his quartet of receiving threats with ease, as Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, and Jameson Williams all having strong plays. Isaac TeSlaa also added his first touchdown of the season on a beautifully designed play by Drew Petzing.
Gibbs led the team with 99 receiving yards, with Amon-Ra St. Brown directly behind him at 98 yards. Williams had 50 yards and LaPorta had 16 yards on the day, with the Goff finishing at 303 yards passing.
Defensive Pressure and Pass Defense
The Lions got after Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito, finishing with 5 sacks on the day. The corners responded with their own shutdown day, only allowing 129 yards receiving on over 30 drop backs, with Roger McCreary intercepting DeVito.
Once Drake Maye exited the game injured, there was no hope for the Patriots, as their only scoring drive from DeVito occurred when down 25 points. Derrick Moore had a two-sack performance, Alim McNeill finished with a sack and came close on three more occasions, and Aidan Hutchinson and DJ Wonnum added one each as well.
While he did not get home on a rush, Eric O’Neill added a tipped ball at the line of scrimmage on the banner day for the defensive line.
Rock Ya-Sin added a pass breakup while Brian Branch added two of his own. Mack Hollins and AJ Brown, the leading receiver duo for New England, combined for 75 yards receiving. It was a lockdown day for a previously suspect Lions defense.
It was a complete day on offense and defense for the Lions, with the Patriots held to under three yards per carry. In fact, when taking out Maye and Devito scrambles, Kelvin Sheppard’s unit contained the Patriot rushing attack to 17 carries for 31 yards.
The entire unit, from Branch to McNeill to Tyleik Williams to Derrick Barnes, held the Patriots to a season low in rushing yards.
Special teams was not relied upon often on Sunday, but Jake Bates did send a kickoff out of bounds during the game, setting up New England in excellent field position while the game was still close. Although it did not result in a Patriot scoring drive, it is on the margin of error that the Lions cannot afford in later games.
Bates has now been penalized three times on the season, twice for kickoffs short of the landing zone and most recently for a kickoff out of bounds on Sunday.
While the Lions had stopped one of their recent woes on Sunday in finishing in the red zone, they did not plug the turnover problem. Jared Goff threw two interceptions, both directly to defensive backs on pre-determined reads.
One of those passes came with the Lions set to extend the lead to 25 points before halftime. The Lions saw another red zone drive stall out, but their overall day puts this on the back burner.
Jared Goff had set a record for his start to the season without an interception, so a multi-interception game is highly uncharacteristic of the former top overall pick.
The field conditions were abysmal, and it led to multiple Patriots being knocked out of the game.
It also likely contributed to Aidan Hutchinson’s injury after a first quarter sack, where the EDGE immediately went down grabbing his right knee. If the NFL wants to be serious about having more international games, there needs to be a higher standard for playing fields.
There is too much player safety at stake for the field to be a slip and slide for players when they try to plant.
Lions’ Star Suffers Season-Ending Injury
Entering the game, the Lions were already down Jack Campbell after his horrific injury two weeks ago. Kerby Joseph’s status is still week-to-week as he looks to make his season debut. The last thing the Lions needed was another defensive injury.
Unfortunately, that was exactly what happened for Detroit. Aidan Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye in the first quarter, and proceeded to celebrate by jumping in the air and landing awkwardly, hurting his right knee area.
It was a play that was not smart, especially when Hutchinson’s celebration antics have already been discussed with the organization to prevent injuries. Instead, the Lions will be looking to make up for a Hutchinson-sized hole the remainder of the season. It is a brutal blow on a defense that is already down one leader in Campbell.

title: Detroit Lions Cut DL From Practice Squad
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have made a decision on veteran defensive lineman Ben Stille.
Ahead of the teams Week 11 home contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the front office has decided to cut the 29-year-old from the practice squad.
After previous stints with the Browns, Cardinals, Buccaneers and Falcons, Stille was inked by Detroit this summer during training camp.
While he did not make the initial 53-man roster, he has been on the practice squad for the past couple of months.
Stille was elevated for the home-opener against the New Orleans Saints, a 31-30 victory. His versatility made him an ideal candidate to have on the practice squad, as he could lineup at nose tackle, defensive end or at three-tech.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Aidan Hutchinson Is To Blame For Freak ACL Injury
Head coach Dan Campbell expressed the team is now expecting the defensive line to step up even more, given the season-ending ACL injury suffered by Aidan Hutchinson.
The former NFL tight end indicated the most frustration felt was immediately after defeating the Patriots, when he initially learned Hutchinson's fate.
“I'd say the most frustrating was right after the game when you find out. Defense played their tails off in that game without Hutch. Hutch started it off for us now," said Campbell. "That was a big sack that created the - ended up turning into, we had a stand there to make it three points, but we did a heck of a job man, picking up the slack. And so, when you find out, that's the most disappointing. And at that point, you could put it behind you immediately and you say, 'What do we have in that room? What do we have on defense? How are we playing? What's the strength of what we have? Can we do this?' Absolutely we can do this. We will do it.
"This roster is built to be able to sustain these types of injuries, these types of things," Campbell added further. "Does it hurt? Absolutely. It's just going to require more of other guys around him. It's going to require more offensively. It's going to require more on special teams. And we are capable of all that. It's about finding a way to win.”

title: Detroit Lions Core Defense Has Played Shockingly Little Together
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have invested heavily on both sides of the football. Unfortunately, the defense has not had the benefit of having their core group all play together in the past three NFL seasons.
According to CBS Sports , "Lions defensive core of Hutchinson, Campbell, Branch, Joseph & McNeil have all been on the field for just 3% of team's defensive plays in the past 3 seasons. Detroit has gone 38 straight games without all 5 playing together. Injuries have eaten away at Lions' Super Bowl window."
Interestingly, the team was also decimated by injuries back in 2024. Again, the defense lost several key players, but were able to go on and finish with a 15-2 record in the regular season. The season did end bitterly following an upset playoff loss to the Washington Commanders.
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking in front of local reporters for the first time since landing home from Germany, demonstrated leadership and a rallying message, when asked about the mounting injuries to his defense.
Dan Campbell is refusing to become a Miserable Piece of Shit thinking about all the defensive injuries suffered by Detroit Lions pic.twitter.com/AaISgff73U
“Yeah well, I think there’s time where if you’re not careful, you lay in bed in night, and you start thinking about all the what-ifs. And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of s**t,” Campbell said. “And I’m not going to do it. We’re not doing it. I refuse to look at it that way . Does it stink? Yeah, it sure did in the moment.
“It’s time to move on. We have to. And what has happened with Jack Campbell, and with Hutch now, will not be in vain. We can’t allow it to. They got us to this point, and so what are we going to do about it, man? Are we just going to let it go to waste, or are we going to do something and pick up the slack?”
The former NFL tight end expressed that being on the job for the past six seasons has taught the organization the significant value of having depth on the roster.
With veteran defensive end DJ Wonnum returning from injury and the emergence of Derrick Moore, the coaching staff is demanding more from everyone on the defense and is even rallying the offense to do more to pick up the slack from Hutchinson's loss.
“That’s the reason why we have the depth that we have in that room," said Campbell. "We knew that was important. I mean, these are the things you learn over a six-year period. It’s how important depth is. And so, we feel really good about that room.”

title: Dan Campbell Reacts To Aidan Hutchinson Tearing ACL Celebrating
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell made his first public comments since star defensive end was lost for the 2026 season after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament.
What makes the injury so disappointing is the fact that the former first-round pick was hurt celebrating a sack against Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.
Appearing on 97.1 The Ticket for his weekly radio interview, the former NFL tight end
"Well man, what a gut punch. Very much like Jack, he’s such a phenomenal player, an impact player, but more importantly he’s an unbelievable teammate and he’s one of our captains. It just stinks, man. It hits you. And I hate it for him, man, because he was on a heater," said Campbell. "What a hell of a year he was having. He’s just improved every year and to come off the injury he had in 2024.
"But, I also know this, man, this guy will overcome this. He will come back better than he was, too. It’s just the way he is, it’s the way he’s wired, and he’ll come out better for this."
Campbell said he would not limit his players from celebrating in the future.
I think what happened speaks for itself. We’re not talking to eight-year-olds here. And I’ll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play, and I freaking pumped my arm up. I’m pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn’t tell anybody," Campbell said. "I was just excited. I just pumped my arm. It’s not like I, so if you say, 'Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic, man.' This game is built off of emotion.
"If you have to contain yourself after a play is made, I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you gotta keep your head, then you’re really becoming something you’re not."
Now, the team is likely to lean on rookie defensive end Derrick Moore, who has been productive the past two weeks.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 6 Winners, 1 Loser Against Patriots
The Lions' defense has been battered by injuries as of late. Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, D.J. Reed, DJ Wonnum and Jimmy Rolder all missed the team's game against Miami, with Campbell and Rolder both being placed on injured reserve. Wonnum has returned to the lineup and is having a stellar first season in Motown.
Without Campbell and Rolder, the Lions leaned on the trio of Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske and Malcolm Rodriguez against the Dolphins. They also signed K.J. Britt to the active roster from the practice squad of the New England Patriots, though his role has been primarily on special teams.
At cornerback, the Lions had signed Nick Whiteside to the active roster from their own practice squad to help supplement the depth they have on roster. He was waived in a corresponding move after the team added defensive end Tyrus Wheat to the active roster.
One day prior to the official trade deadline, Holmes swung a trade with the New York Jets for safety Andre Cisco, sacrificing a 2028 sixth-round pick to make the move. Cisco began his career as a 2021 third-round pick of the Jacksonville Jaguars, and spent four years there before signing with the Jets prior to the 2025 season.
Cisco's presence creates an interesting situation at the safety position. Once depleted for depth, the Lions have gotten much healthier in the secondary with Brian Branch returning from injury. Additionally, Kerby Joseph is amidst his return to practice window and could be activated very soon.
The trade deadline saw rampant activity since the end of the Sunday slate of Week 9 games. In particular, the Jacksonville Jaguars have clearly pushed their chips to the center of the table by making a trio of trades, including giving up a first-round pick in the upcoming draft to acquire Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis.

title: How Latest Kerby Joseph News Impacts Detroit Lions Defense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have made their decision on the rest of the season for safety Kerby Joseph.
Head coach Dan Campbell explained on 97.1 The Ticket this week that barring any injuries, the plan is to activate Joseph and have him play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field.
The 2024 All-Pro has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list since the start of training camp dealing with a knee injury that reports have indicated is degenerative. He returned to practice on Oct. 28, starting his 21-day return to practice window.
Detroit had until Tuesday to decide whether to activate him or revert him back to the PUP list for the remainder of the season.
Joseph has yet to appear in a game in over a calendar year, with his last appearance coming on Oct. 12, 2025 in a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. In that game, Joseph struggled with a knee injury and left the game.
Speaking with media during training camp, Joseph stated that the injury dates back to a training camp practice last year where he woke up with swelling in his knee. He tried to play through it last season, and notched three interceptions in the first six games, but ultimately couldn't continue after the pain he suffered in the Kansas City game.
Joseph has proven to be one of the NFL's most dynamic takeaway artists when healthy, as he has logged 20 interceptions and two forced fumbles in 55 career games.
Joseph is in his fifth NFL season, and entered the league as a third-round pick of the Lions in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Illinois. Initially expected to be a depth option right away, Joseph was thrust into action beginning in Week 4 of his rookie season when veteran starter Tracy Walker III suffered a torn ACL.
The Illinois product proved to fit right in, as he recorded his first two career interceptions just weeks later against the Green Bay Packers at home. Joseph would finish with four picks in his rookie season, asserting himself as a starter moving forward.
After another four-interception season in 2023, Joseph broke out in 2024. He recorded a league-leading nine picks, earning First Team All-Pro honors as a result as well as a four-year contract extension that made him the NFL's highest-paid safety at the time.
The Lions added safety depth prior to the trade deadline with a move to acquire New York Jets safety Andre Cisco.

title: Playoff Picture, Week 10: Detroit Lions Climb to Top of NFC North
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are in first-place in the NFC North.
With a 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, the Lions improved to 7-2 with their fifth-straight win and put themselves in a first-place tie with both the Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings.
Detroit has the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Vikings, and a better divisional record than the Bears. Both of Chicago's losses this year have been in the division, which gives the Detroit the advantage and the top spot in the NFC North with eight games to play.
In the three-way tie, the tiebreaker is decided by winning percentage in head-to-head meetings between the three teams. The Lions have beat the Vikings, and the Vikings beat the Bears. Because the Lions have the head-to-head over Minnesota, they're currently in first.
Detroit was unable to gain any headway on the San Francisco 49ers, who defeated the Dallas Cowboys to move to 8-1 on the season.
Chicago was on its bye week this week, and returns to action next week against the New Orleans Saints. If they defeat New Orleans and the Lions handle business Sunday against Tampa Bay, the Thanksgiving meeting at Ford Field will carry massive divisional stakes.
A lot can still happen, but at this point Detroit controls its own destiny in it's pursuit of a third NFC North title in four years. Half of their final eight games will be against divisional opponents, including that Thanksgiving matchup with the Bears looming in less than two weeks.
The Lions will have to run the gauntlet of the division without two of their top defenders, as Aidan Hutchinson is expected to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, while Jack Campbell is on injured reserve after a scary injury against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8.
The NFC North remains the best division in football with all teams at least two games over .500, but the Minnesota Vikings knocked the Green Bay Packers out of the playoff picture for the time being with their 30-10 victory Sunday at Lambeau Field.
Green Bay dropped to 6-4 on the year with the loss, but are currently on the outside looking in as the Los Angeles Rams claimed the seventh seed for now thanks to having a better record than the Packers against NFC opponents.
The Packers and Rams have a big matchup looming, as both teams will be on their bye weeks this upcoming week before squaring off on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at SoFi Stadium. That game will be a big factor in the postseason picture, as the winning team will gain the valuable head-to-head tiebreaker in addition to going a game up in the standings.
Meanwhile, the Vikings have the opportunity to impact the standings in a big way next week with a matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football.
