title: Texans vs. Colts Injury Report: Latest on Danielle Hunter, Marvin Harrison Jr.
full_text:
The Houston Texans have released their second injury report of the week ahead of their upcoming Thursday Night Football matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .
And based on the latest intel from the Texans, it's looking like they could be without a select few impact players for their Week 11 matchup.
Let's take a look at the latest from the Texans' Tuesday practice and see who practiced, who didn't, and what each status could mean heading into this week's game against their division rival Colts:
RB Woody Marks (concussion) DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring) WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) TE Brevin Jordan (foot/illness) *CB Kamari Lassiter (wrist)
RB David Montgomery (groin) WR Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) OL Febechi Nwaiwu (knee) S Reed Blankenship (hand) OL Blake Fisher (thumb) OL Keylan Rutledge (shoulder) OL Wyatt Teller (back)
* - change in status from Monday's walkthrough
For the Texans, not much has changed compared to Monday's walkthrough . The only adjustment of note was the fact that starting cornerback Kamari Lassiter shifted from a full participant to a DNP, which will be something to monitor as we creep closer to game time on Thursday.
However, for those that were listed as a DNP on Monday's walkthrough who continued to have such status a day later, it's trending as if we won't see those players take the field against the Colts, barring some noteworthy shift over the next 48 hours.
The biggest name of those DNPs is none other than the Texans' Pro Bowl edge rusher Danielle Hunter, who hasn't practiced with the team since he was listed as a limited participant with a hamstring injury last Thursday before facing the Cleveland Browns.
Without Hunter in the mix, the Texans will likely roll with a similar setup on their defensive line as they did this past weekend: Will Anderson will maintain his same role as Houston's top edge rusher, while Jadeveon Clowney steps in by taking ahold of Hunter's snaps .
Last weekend, Clowney was on the field for over 75% of the Texans' defensive snaps, and there's no reason to believe this week against the Colts will be any different.
Another noteworthy name who is trending to miss a second straight week: wide receiver Marvin Harrison, who, like Hunter, has been sidelined since suffering a hamstring injury in last week's practice, and hasn't shown any signs of being able to give it a go against the Colts on a short week of preparation.
That means the Texans' wide receiver unit will be left down to Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, and Kayshon Boutte; just as the case was this past weekend against the Browns.
On a more positive note, veteran running back David Montgomery was officially able to log another full practice, which seems to hint that he'll be able to play for the first time since getting injured in Week 5.
And without Woody Marks in the mix because of a concussion , Montgomery be due for a significant share of the workload in the backfield–– so long as he's truly back to 100%.
DT Jerry Tillery (calf) OL Jalen Travis (knee) LB Jaylon Carlies (neck) TE Will Mallory (hamstring) CB Sauce Gardner (calf) CB Charvarius Ward (knee) OL Bernhard Raimann (concussion) *OL Charlie Heck (personal)
WR Anthony Gould (toe) *LS Luke Rhodes (hamstring)
OL Dalton Tucker (shoulder)
Not much has changed from the Colts' injury report from Monday's walkthrough either––outside of offensive tackle Charlie Heck popping up as a DNP due to personal reasons, while long snapper Luke Rhodes was upgraded as a limited participant.
The names to continue to keep an eye on for the Colts are their pair of starting cornerbacks, Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward. Both being unable to practice just a couple of days away from their trip to Houston is certainly an indication that they might not be able to play in Week 11.
If both cornerbacks are sidelined for the Colts, their starting boundary corners will likely be Jonathan Edwards and Kenneth Harris. Needless to say, that could mark a big opportunity to exploit their passing defense and open up a big day for C.J. Stroud and the Texans' air attack.
The Texans and Colts will release their final injury reports and game statuses after their Wednesday practice, which will provide even more clarity around what to expect for each side’s availability for Thursday Night Football.
But by the current look of things, expect some key absences to be in play for both teams in a pivotal game to keep their hopes of a postseason appearance alive moving forward.

title: Texans Have Obvious Offensive Line Change to Make, But They Won't
full_text:
The Houston Texans' offensive line looked a tad bit different this past weekend against the Cleveland Browns.
In the midst of Keylan Rutledge's one-game absence due to a stinger that he suffered in Wednesday's practice, the Texans were forced to shuffle around their interior from their typical setup.
Rather than Rutledge settling in at left guard, the Texans decided to start fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu for his third-ever game in the league. Evan Brown and Ed Ingram took their usual spots at center and right guard, respectively.
So how did the adjusted Texans' offensive line perform?
Well, they've certainly seen better days . But it wasn't because of any lackluster performance from Nwaiwu.
In reality, outside of a costly fourth-quarter holding penalty, the rookie actually held his own by allowing just one total pressure on quarterback C.J. Stroud. The issues actually stemmed elsewhere around Houston's offensive front.
Where the Texans' offensive line really struggled was at their center position.
Starting center Evan Brown allowed six total pressures from the Browns' defensive line, by far the highest on Houston's offensive line throughout the day.
Texans OL pressures allowed today vs Cleveland via @SumerSports . Aireontae Ersery - 3 Febechi Nwaiwu - 1 Evan Brown - 6 Ed Ingram - 1 Trent Brown - 2 Stroud was pressured 22 times total with many of those being free rushers.
It's been a bit of a recurring theme for Brown to have left a little more to be desired on a weekly basis. Brown's 49.1 overall grade via Pro Football Focus on the season ranks 30th among 35 qualified centers, while his 45.7 run blocking grade ranks second-lowest among that same group.
Statistically, Brown has been a weak link on the Texans' offensive front throughout most of the season. He's incurred 11 total pressures and three penalties over the first nine games of the season, and was a sizable part of Houston's demise this past weekend against Cleveland to drop them to 3-6.
So where do the Texans go from here? Is there a better starting unit that the Texans could roll with that takes Brown out of the equation and creates an improved five-man front?
Well, one easy option the Texans could lean into to better their offensive line's production is to continue starting Nwaiwu––who performed well in his first-ever start this past weekend––while shifting Rutledge over to the center spot, who's expected to return from injury in Wek 11.
Rutledge was drafted earlier this year in the first round with the expectation that he could start as Houston's center from day one before he inevitably settled in as Houston's full-time left guard.
Rutledge spent most of his time playing right guard during his two previous seasons at Georgia Tech, but ran some center at the Senior Bowl and during the Texans' training camp to show that he's more than capable of having that necessary positional flexibility.
Such a move might give the Texans the necessary upside and security needed upfront for the second half of the season, while also moving off of a weak-link in Brown who has been a replacable-level center in the opportunities he's seen so far.
However, based on the latest presser from Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans, it seems the team has no plans of pivoting off of their regular five-man front from how they've looked for most of the season.
Ryan’s was asked during his Tuesday press conference before taking on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 11 about whether or not the team would consider any changes on the offensive line.
His response? He's expecting things to look no different than they have when the unit has been fully healthy this season.
"We're rolling with what we have right now," Ryans said of the offensive line. "Guys have done a good job. So we'll continue to keep going with that."
That means, rather than giving Nwaiwu a call-up for his second start on Thursday after a positive debut, Rutledge will be expected to fill back into his typical role as Houston's left guard, while Brown will continue to operate as their center.
Perhaps the Texans' offensive line at full health can have a bit more success against the Colts compared to their lowly performance from this past weekend in Cleveland . At least, that seems to be the hope from Houston's coaching staff.
Considering Houston allowed over a 54% pressure rate against the Browns, they'll have no choice but to improve on their offensive front if they want to find any sustained success moving into the second half of the year.
But if their offensive line continues to stumble in their next game against the Colts' defensive line that hasn't been too inspiring through the first 10 weeks of the season, the chatter surrounding a shake-up on their offensive front will only begin to get louder.
And if there was a shake-up to be made, Nwaiwu feels like the first guy who would get that promotion into their starting five-man front, and hope that he can provide the necessary spark to get this protection to a serviceable level.
For now, the Texans are rolling with the status quo. Only time will tell if such a decision to stand pat will pan out in their favor.

title: How Texans' Defense Will Adjust With Azeez Al-Shaair on Injured Reserve
full_text:
The Houston Texans' defense took a big hit heading into their Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .
Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was placed on injured reserve due to a lingering groin injury . Al-Shaair missed this past weekend against the Cleveland Browns after missing last week's team practice, and now, he'll be set to miss the next four games as he recovers.
The Texans have placed Azeez Al-Shaair on the injured reserve list. Al-Shaair missed Week 10 against the Browns with a groin injury, and he’ll now be slated to miss the next 4 weeks. The earliest he can return will be in Week 15 vs. the Jaguars.
But the Texans not having Al-Shaair in the mix is a big loss for their overall defensive success. Al-Shaair is a captain, the green-dot signal caller, and an every-down player for Houston's defense. Not having him on the field for any stretch of time––let alone four weeks––is a significant loss.
So how might the Texans adjust now that Al-Shaair is set to miss multiple weeks, and who on their defense will be due for a bigger role now that he won't be a part of the equation until Week 15?
In terms of the personnel that the Texans will be running on a down-to-down basis, things won't be looking much different outside of taking Al-Shaair out of the equation.
We've seen the Texans make bigger shifts on their defense without someone like Jalen Pitre on the field, and instead run more 4-3 looks rather than their typical nickel sets. However, Houston probably won't be taking that approach without Al-Shaair on the field.
Instead, their defense will expect to look pretty similar to last week's setup: their regular nickel defense with five defensive backs and two linebackers on a down-to-down basis. But instead of Al-Shaair being on the field, Jake Hansen will be in line to take his snaps as their middle linebacker.
Last weekend against the Browns without Al-Shaair on the field, it was Hansen who took ahold of 97% of the Texans' total defensive snaps , only coming off for two plays over the course of the day. Henry To'oTo'o took ahold of 100% of the defensive snaps.
When Al-Shaair missed Week 4 against the Dallas Cowboys, the setup was similar for the Texans and their defensive personnel . Hansen claimed 95% of their defensive snaps, but then-practice squad call-up Kenneth Murray was deemed their green dot signal-caller and saw over 80% of the defensive snaps.
Moving forward, though, it's easy to imagine that Hansen will be the Texans' new green-dot signal caller for the extent that Al-Shaair is out of the picture.
Kenneth Murray is still a part of Houston's practice squad, but with all three of his call-ups used on the season, he'd have to be signed to the 53-man roster to be on the gameday roster once again; something that hasn't happened to this point.
So moving forward, you can expect the Texans' defensive personnel to more than likely consist of Hansen and To'oTo'o leading the way. Murray also remains a name to keep on the radar, but only if Houston decides to ink him to a traditional contract for the 53-man roster.
Will that be enough to keep the Texans' defense afloat while shorthanded? It's tough to say. Houston's defense has been underwhelming this season with Al-Shaair on the field, and Hansen didn't perform much better in Week 10 when he saw an increase in opportunities.
Hansen allowed over 100 yards and eight catches on the 10 plays he was targeted against the Browns; the most of any player on the Texans' defense. Houston will have to be better in coverage moving forward, and a large part of that relies on Hansen's ability to keep the middle of the field in check.
Time will tell if the Texans can hold things together without their defensive leader, because for the next four weeks, they have no choice but to move forward with him out of the picture.

title: Texans Get Brutal Update on LB Azeez Al-Shaair's Lingering Injury
full_text:
The Houston Texans just announced a pretty concerning update regarding the injury status of Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair.
According to the Texans, Al-Shaair has been placed on injured reserve ahead of Houston's Week 11 game against the Indianapolis Colts.
Al-Shaair was on the Texans' injury report dating back to last week's game against the Cleveland Browns , which led to him missing all three days of practice and being ruled out for Sunday's action.
And now, it appears that Al-Shaair's absence will linger much longer than just that Week 10 game against Cleveland.
Per Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle , Al-Shaair's groin injury is one that is deemed “significant" and will require surgery.
Azeez Al-Shaair's groin injury is one that is significant and requires surgery, per a source. He's not been ruled out for the season, though.
Al-Shaair has been dealing with the same groin injury that's now placed him on injured reserve dating back to Week 3 against the Indianapolis Colts .
That injury led to him missing the following week against the Dallas Cowboys, but then returned in Week 5 against his former team, the Tennessee Titans. But now, he'll be forced to miss a little more time with that same issue.
Al-Shaair has yet to be ruled out for the remainder of the season. Yet, at the very least, he'll be due to miss around a month simply because of his status on injured reserve.
Al-Shaair's injured reserve designation will keep him out for the next four weeks at a minimum: against the Colts, the Baltimore Ravens, the Pittsburgh Steelers, and the Washington Commanders.
His first chance to return to the lineup comes in Week 15 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in the event he's only sidelined for the minimum four weeks that come with an injured reserve placement. However, it remains to be seen just how quickly his rehab process will go in the weeks ahead.
Al-Shaair, while he hasn't been up to the same standard this season that he was during his Pro Bowl campaign of 2025, is still a critical component of the Texans' defensive success when he's healthy and on the field.
In the seven games that he's played this season, Al-Shaair has put together 68 total tackles, one tackle for loss, and three passes defended. He currently leads the Texans' defense in combined tackles, and ties for third in solo tackles behind only Calen Bullock and Kamari Lassiter.
The Texans will now be forced to adjust on their defense in the weeks ahead without Al-Shaair. And in all likelihood, their starting linebackers will look pretty similar to what they rolled out this past weekend against the Browns while he was ruled out.
Jake Hansen was elevated to start next to Henry To'oTo'o within the Texans' front seven, just as he did when Al-Shaair was out for Week 4 against the Cowboys.
In the weeks ahead, Hansen could be in line to be Houston's starting middle linebacker, or at least until Al-Shaair is ready to return to the field. Fourth-round rookie Wade Woodaz could also have a route to getting more reps on the defensive side of the ball as well.
Regardless, being without Al-Shaair––one of the Texans' team captains and their green dot on the defense––is a devastating loss for the success on that side of the ball as a whole.
We'll see how Houston winds up performing without him, but there's no doubt that his absence makes the climb out of their 3-6 hole a whole lot tougher than it would be with him as a part of the equation.

title: What to Expect From the Texans' Backfield vs. Colts on TNF
full_text:
The Houston Texans' backfield is setting up to look a bit different than usual heading into their Week 11 matchup vs. the Indianapolis Colts.
During the Texans' latest contest against the Cleveland Browns this past weekend, Houston's lead in the backfield, Woody Marks, wound up suffering a concussion that would lead to him leaving the game in the third quarter, and thus be put in concussion protocol for the week ahead.
And on a short week before facing the Colts on Thursday Night Football, there's little to no chance that Marks will be able to give it a go . Concussion protocol typically takes one to two weeks for players to clear, and with only a few days of preparation, Marks won’t have much of a lengthy timeline to bank on.
So what can we expect from the Texans' running back room heading into Week 11 without Marks in the picture? Let's break the situation down.
While the Texans have been without their veteran counterpart to Marks, David Montgomery, dating back to Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, signs continue to point towards his return to the field coming as soon as this week against the Colts.
Montgomery was a full participant in the Texans' team practice on Friday before facing the Browns, and was deemed a full participant during Houston's walkthrough on Monday ahead of their Thursday Night Football matchup.
While his participation during the Texans' upcoming two practices will be a better indicator of whether or not he'll be able to play, a couple more full participations would be a pretty solid sign that his return will be in play for Week 11.
And if that's the case, you can expect Montgomery to claim a vast majority of the Texans' work in the backfield, perhaps just simply taking the role that Marks has when healthy; someone logging around 16 rushes per game, gets work in the passing game, and is on the field for upwards of 70% of the offensive snaps.
If Montgomery is good to go and Marks is out, that places Emari Demercado in line to take the Texans' RB2 role, just as he has for the past couple of weeks that he's been signed while Montgomery has been sidelined.
Through the past two games, Demercado has seen an average 27% snap share on the offensive end, along with 6.5 carries and one reception per game.
So while Montgomery claims about three-fourths of the reps in the backfield, and most of the work on the goal line, Demercado will likely claim the remainder as a change-of-pace back, and still get his fair share of opportunities.
With just three running backs on the active roster, and one of those in Marks likely not suiting up for Thursday, it puts the Texans in a situation where they'll be best served to bring another running back onboard for this game against the Colts, even if just a short-term depth plug-in.
And the name who makes the most sense to be that short-term depth option is Dare Ogunbowale, who was cut from the active roster earlier last week as the team signed Nikko Remigio to the 53-man, but was then re-signed to the practice squad in time for their matchup against the Colts.
Considering the Texans still have two more call-ups to use on Ogunbowale as a part of the practice squad, it would make sense for Houston to use one more of those for Week 11 while Marks is absent, and give Ogunbowale work as a part of their special teams unit, with a few looks on the offensive end as well.
Over the past three weeks, the Texans have given Ogunbowale an average of 10 offensive snaps per game, but have only given him one carry and two receptions over those appearances. Expect more of the same this week, in the event he is indeed called up from the practice squad.

title: Texans vs. Colts First Injury Report: Who's at Risk of Missing TNF
full_text:
After a rough Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns , the Houston Texans are already beginning their preparation for their upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, which comes on a short week for Thursday Night Football.
And on that short week, we already have a glimpse of the Texans and Colts' first injury report of three, which comes after both teams hosted a walkthrough on Monday with estimations of each players' practice participation.
Let's take a look at the latest on the injury front for both the Texans and Colts heading into Thursday night's action:
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) RB Woody Marks (concussion) DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring) WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) TE Brevin Jordan (foot/illness)
RB David Montgomery (groin) WR Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) OL Febechi Nwaiwu (knee) CB Kamari Lassiter (wrist) S Reed Blankenship (hand) OL Blake Fisher (thumb) OL Keylan Rutledge (shoulder) OL Wyatt Teller (back)
The Texans have a handful of injury concerns worth noting–– many of which are still lingering from this past weekend against the Browns.
The biggest absence from the Texans' practice estimation was none other than Danielle Hunter, who missed this past weekend against Cleveland, and could be trending towards another absence for Week 11 as he continues to rehab from his hamstring injury.
Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was also a DNP in practice with his groin injury , which is worth keeping a close eye on over the course of the week. While Monday's session was a walkthrough, his estimation marks his fourth DNP in a row.
The newest name worth noting as a DNP for the Texans in practice is running back Woody Marks, who left Sunday's game in Cleveland with a concussion, and is not expected to play this coming week against the Colts.
As for the Texans' veteran counterpart in the backfield, David Montgomery, he was estimated as a full participant in practice for the second session in a row.
If Marks can't play as expected due to being stuck in concussion protocol, there's a good chance that Montgomery will be able to return for his first game played since he went down with his groin injury in Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans , and will have Emari Demercado backing him up as Houston's RB2.
LS Luke Rhodes (hamstring) DT Jerry Tillery (calf) OL Jalen Travis (knee) LB Jaylon Carlies (neck) TE Will Mallory (hamstring) CB Sauce Gardner (calf) CB Charvarius Ward (knee) OL Bernhard Raimann (concussion)
OL Dalton Tucker (shoulder)
As for the injuries the Colts are dealing with, they could be down a few key names for Thursday, depending on how their status shifts throughout the week.
The one area of Indianapolis' roster to keep a close watch on is their secondary, as both of their starting cornerbacks, Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, were estimated as DNP during their first practice of the week.
We'll get a clearer picture of what to expect for the Colts and Texans' availability as the week progresses, and as both teams officially hit the field for a true practice. But based on the intel we have now, there's a good chance some big names will be forced out of the action for each side.

title: Grading Every Texans Position Group From Week 10 Loss to Browns
full_text:
The Houston Texans dropped a critical Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns this weekend in a 24-27 loss that now leaves their record at a rough 3-6 record through nine games on the season.
And in the midst of their Week 10 loss, the Texans certainly saw a few position groups around the roster leave a bit more to be desired on the field. Yet, there were also a handful of position groups who didn't exactly drop the ball as much as others and deserve some credit for their performance.
So that makes now a pretty good time to sort through the Texans' lineup from this weekend's action and grade how every position group performed, thus breaking down where exactly Houston came up short for their humbling loss.
With that, let's go through each Texans position group one by one and determine who shined and who didn't from this Sunday in Cleveland.
It's tricky to evaluate C.J. Stroud's performance in this game.
On one hand, his first half was spectacular, as he threw just four incompletions for his 190 passing yards and two touchdowns.
Once the second half arrived, he completed just 5 of 19 passes for less than 25 yards, the offense dried up, and turned out to be a huge component as to why the Texans couldn't finish the job after a fiery start to Sunday's action.
The offensive line's performance didn't help, nor did the lack of a run game, the excessive penalties, or the second-half play-calling. So Stroud might still squeak by with a B-minus grade thanks to an extremely hot start, but a better performance at the end might've made the difference for a fourth win on the season for Houston.
It was tough to imagine the Texans' run game generating much traction after Woody Marks went down with a concussion in the third quarter. And things certainly dragged to a halt on the ground once he left the game and didn't return .
Marks finished with 12 carries for 50 yards, while the running backs outside of Marks finished with eight carries for 18 yards. The Texans better hope that David Montgomery can give it a go on Thursday night, or things could look pretty similar on the ground against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 11.
While the Texans' offense took a nosedive in the second half, it was a game where their receiving talent did show up in a big way; particularly as it relates to Nico Collins en route to his nine receptions for 94 yards and a touchdown on a season-high 16 targets.
CJ Stroud into a tight window to Nico Collins for 6! HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gZg6uDeOlt
Xavier Hutchinson also turned in a respectable performance with over 50 receiving yards, while Tank Dell turned in his sub-50% snap share for a solid three catches and 21 yards. Without Marvin Harrison Jr. in the fold, all in all, it's hard to be too upset with the production from Houston's receivers this week.
It was a pretty uninspiring performance from the Texans' tight ends in this game. While Dalton Schultz did help take the second half lid off of Houston's offense thanks to an 11-yard touchdown reception from C.J. Stroud, the position remained mostly a nonfactor outside of that one play.
Schultz, Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein, and Cade Stover combined for just two targets on the day; both of those going to Schultz. We've seen much better performance and involvement from this Texans tight end unit compared to the product that was shown on Sunday.
While the Texans did limit Stroud to just one sack throughout the day in Cleveland, it didn't come without the offensive line allowing several pressures and some pivotal penalties that changed the tides pretty significantly in this one.
The Browns generated an impressive 52% pressure rate on the Texans in Week 10, with eight different defenders from Cleveland finding their way to multiple pressures in the game. That's far from a recipe for success, and a big reason as to why the end result looked as it did for Houston on Sunday.
Even without Danielle Hunter in the mix due to a hamstring injury, the Texans' defensive line still managed to generate a good amount of pressure on Deshaun Watson over the course of the day. Houston found their way to four total sacks for a loss of 32 yards, and limited Cleveland's running backs to a little over three yards per carry.
Big man doin' big things 📺: @nflonfox pic.twitter.com/w7QUD1FgzK
If only the Texans could've contained Watson on his scrambling plays a bit better, their defensive line grade could be the best of anyone around the roster. However, his ability to extend plays was a big reason as to why this offense found success against Houston's defense.
The Texans' linebacker group has seen their struggles throughout the stretches in which they're forced to play without Azeez Al-Shaair manning the middle of the field, and that was the story of what happened to this unit on Sunday as Al-Shaair was sidelined with a groin injury.
Jake Hansen was particularly underwhelming, as he allowed a rough eight receptions for 109 yards on his 10 total targets, and led to multiple explosives being let up within the middle of the field. The Texans need to get their linebacker group healthy as soon as possible for better results to come to fruition.
We've certainly seen some darker days from this Texans' cornerback group this season as a part of their schematic lapses in the first half of the season.
This game wasn't exactly perfect, considering Watson surged to an impressive 312 passing yards, but Houston's cornerback duo of Derek Stingley and Kamari Lassiter only allowed a combined 63 yards on their 12 total targets.
Lassiter's fourth-quarter unnecessary roughness call does sting, for sure. But that call was debatable in its own right. Outside of that blip on the radar, there are more concerns worth highlighting on this Texans defense from Sunday than the performance of their cornerbacks.
The Texans' safety unit certainly gets some bonus points thanks to Calen Bullock's big interception in the fourth quarter, which now leads him to being the team's interception leader on the season with a pair of takeaways through nine games.
As for M.J. Stewart's performance, though, things could've certainly been better. He allowed three receptions for 86 yards on seven targets, which was his highest yards allowed on the season so far. It remains to be seen if the Texans will continue to stick with Stewart or roll with Reed Blankenship once again, who was a nonfactor in this game.

title: Deshaun Watson Admits Win Over Texans Was Especially Meaningful
full_text:
The Houston Texans couldn't get it done this weekend for a Week 10 victory on the road, as the Cleveland Browns would take care of business in a 24-27 result and inevitably sink Houston into a lowly 3-6 record on the season.
And as a part of the Texans’ latest Week 10 loss, they also came up short to a pretty familiar face on the other side: none other than their former quarterback, Deshaun Watson , who led the way for their offense for four seasons up until his trade to the Browns back in 2022.
On Sunday, Watson got another taste of revenge against his old team for the second time since his deal out of Houston. The last time Watson saw the Texans in a regular-season matchup came back in 2022 en route to a 27-14 win for Cleveland, and now, he's extended his head-to-head record to 2-0.
And for Watson, there's no doubt that this win over his former team wound up meaning a bit more than your average NFL victory.
Watson spoke about the meaning behind playing and beating his former team over the weekend in his postgame presser, expressing that the victory was "definitely special," simply because of the history he has with the organization.
“Oh, most definitely. It was definitely special," Watson said of the win over the Texans. "I even mentioned it to the guys last night at the hotel. So, it was definitely a big win for us tonight, overall. But personally, it was definitely special.”
Between his spats with executives and ownership from the tail end of his time with the franchise, the legal trouble that transpired from his time with Houston , and his 2021 trade request that ultimately led to his trade to Cleveland , Watson had no shortage of ups and downs that led to some clear friction with the Texans.
And while it's been five to six years since Watson and the Texans had been dealing with said drama that led to the end of his time with the franchise, there's no doubt that Houston's former quarterback still takes pride in claiming revenge in the form of handing them their sixth loss of the season on his own home field in Cleveland.
Watson expressed after the win that while "it's all love" for the city, the fans, and the players of Houston–– and even some of the staff and ownership–– the win over them and the Texans did mean a little bit more to be a part of.
“I think people know the history behind it. Didn’t leave on a good note, but it’s all love for the city of Houston; the fans there, the players there, some of the staff there, most definitely, that I got to see today. And even the older ownership," Watson continued.
"So, it was good to see a lot of people, familiar faces. It's still love, but it's definitely a good win."
For the Texans, claiming their first-ever win over Watson would've been sweet, and also have come at a good time knowing they could've used that victory in a big way to move onwards with their 2026 campaign.
But instead, Watson gets the last laugh once again, and thus puts the Texans in a difficult hole to climb out of for what remains of their regular season schedule, while also bringing his Browns one step closer to a postseason appearance in what would be his first since being with Houston in 2019.

title: Colts Rookie Report: More Opportunities Arising for Several Draft Picks
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are entering the final stretch of the 2026 season, and their rookie class has experienced a variety of different developments along the way. Some players have established themselves as regular contributors, while others are still working to carve out their respective roles.
With Indianapolis looking toward the future, the remaining games will be especially important for evaluating the team's young talent. Several rookies have already taken on larger roles, providing the Colts with a better understanding of what they have moving forward.
Here's a look at how Indianapolis' rookies have performed through 10 games of the 2026 season.
CJ Allen's rookie season has taken a positive turn over the last several weeks. After dealing with injuries that limited his availability early in the year, the second-round pick has found his footing and established himself as the new leader of the Indianapolis defense, likely for years to come.
Allen has recorded 34 tackles, two tackles for loss, and two sacks across seven games (three starts). His first career start against the Jacksonville Jaguars was particularly encouraging , as he finished with a team-high 10 tackles, a tackle for loss, and his first NFL sack.
Since then, Allen has only gotten better. He followed up his performance in Jacksonville with anouther double-digit tackle performance against the Dallas Cowboys. Sunday's matchup with the Miami Dolphins proved to be his most complete yet, finishing with nine tackles, a pass defended, a game-sealing sack and an interception that was called back due to a penalty.
It took a little while for Allen to fully kick things into gear, but now that he's playing consistently, he's improving with every passing week . The Colts absolutely have found a player they can build around on defense going forward.
AJ Haulcy has had a difficult introduction to the NFL despite earning the starting strong safety job alongside Cam Bynum coming out of training camp.
The Colts' third-round pick has been a regular presence in the Indianapolis secondary, starting nine games, but his performance hasn't necessarily justified the consistent playing time. His 43.4 overall grade from Pro Football Focus ranks 96th among 100 qualified safeties.
The coverage concerns have been particularly evident, with Haulcy allowing a 137.5 passer rating when targeted and recording just one pass breakup. He's also been credited with nine missed tackles, giving him plenty of areas to address as he adjusts to the professional level.
Haulcy has shown some flashes throughout his rookie campaign, but the overall numbers paint a difficult picture. There's still plenty of time for him to acclimate to the NFL game, but the early returns on investment haven't been great for Indianapolis.
Jalen Farmer has gradually worked his way into a larger role along the Colts' offensive line after beginning his rookie season as a reserve.
The Colts' fourth-round pick out of Kentucky made his first career start against Jacksonville following the Quenton Nelson trade, and his transition hasn't been without some growing pains. Per Pro Football Focus , Farmer has yet to allow a sack, but holds a pass blocking grade of only 41.8.
Bengals on both sides of the ball in the Week 10 Team of the Week! 🐅 pic.twitter.com/6CdxXk6pTf
There have been some encouraging signs recently, though. Farmer put together his best performance of the season against Miami, earning an 83.8 overall PFF grade that ranked third among all NFL guards in Week 10, good enough to make the Pro Football Focus Team of the Week.
The Colts are still figuring out what they have in their young offensive lineman, but his recent improvement is an encouraging development as he continues adjusting to the NFL level.
Bryce Boettcher has started to earn a larger role in the Colts' linebacker rotation as the season has progressed. The fourth-round pick out of Oregon has appeared in eight games, making four starts, and has taken advantage of increased opportunities with Akeem Davis-Gaither sidelined. Boettcher recorded a season-high 12 tackles against Dallas before following that performance with seven more against Miami. His 44 total tackles are encouraging, though there is still plenty of room for development.
Boettcher has been considerably more effective against the run, earning a 53.8 run-defense grade compared to a 36.0 coverage grade. He also recorded an 87.4 run-defense grade against Miami, the highest mark among Indianapolis defenders in the game. His limitations in coverage remain an area to improve, but the rookie has shown that he can hang with the big boys.
With Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies both on injured reserve for at least the next four games, more opportunities are coming Boettcher's way. If he can take advantage of the opportunity, he could have a longer-term future with the Colts than one might think.
George Gumbs Jr. has had a relatively quiet start to his NFL career, largely due to limited opportunities in a crowded Indianapolis defensive front. The fifth-round pick out of Florida was always going to be a bit of a project at first, but he has appeared in six games so far. He has yet to record a sack or make a significant impact statistically, recording only four total tackles and two quarterback pressures.
Gumbs is still a developmental piece for the Colts, and there isn't much to evaluate given his limited playing time. With several veterans ahead of him on the depth chart, his immediate opportunities may remain limited, but the remaining games should provide another chance to get the rookie some valuable experience.
Caden Curry has become one of the more intriguing developments among Indianapolis' rookie class. He's had a relatively slow start to his NFL career, but his role began to expand considerably in the middle of the season.
Curry recorded his first career sack against Dallas in Week 9, adding a fumble recovery after also recovering a fumble against Jacksonville the previous week. He's now up to 23 tackles, one sack and two fumble recoveries through 10 games.
Curry's recent production is encouraging, particularly considering how limited his opportunities were early in the season. However, his playing time took a hit against Miami following Arden Key's return from injured reserve, as the sixth-round pick played just 13 defensive snaps. The Colts have several established players ahead of him along the defensive line, but Curry has shown enough in recent weeks to warrant continued opportunities.
His development will be worth monitoring as Indianapolis evaluates its young defensive front.
Seth McGowan has arguably been the most productive offensive rookie on Indianapolis' roster this season. The seventh-round running back has steadily earned more opportunities in the Colts' backfield, proving to be a valuable complement to Jonathan Taylor.
Through 10 games, McGowan has rushed for 285 yards and two touchdowns on 55 carries, averaging an impressive 5.2 yards per attempt. He's also forced 11 missed tackles, showcasing the physical running style that has made him an effective option when given opportunities.
McGowan is coming off his best performance yet , rushing for 77 yards and a touchdown on just 12 carries in Sunday's victory over Miami. He averaged 6.4 yards per attempt and consistently made the most of his opportunities, while also setting new career highs in carries and rushing yards.
Taylor will remain the focal point of the Colts' backfield, but McGowan has done more than enough to establish himself as a promising piece of Indianapolis' future at running back.
Deion Burks hasn't had many opportunities to make an impact during his rookie season, spending much of the first half of the year buried on Indianapolis' wide receiver depth chart.
His outlook could look considerably different over the second half of the season , however.

title: Colts Film Review: Seth McGowan's Finest Rookie Performance To Date
full_text:
It's been quite some time since an Indianapolis Colts running back not named Jonathan Taylor performed well enough to warrant a film room.
For this reason and perhaps several more lamentable ones, the Colts' 2026 campaign has been full of surprises in Indianapolis.
The Indianapolis Colts' rookie running back, Seth McGowan, has been a pleasant surprise this year, going from a penciled-in backup and special teams contributor to a legitimate running mate alongside Taylor .
On Sunday, the Colts' seventh-round draft pick compiled a season-high (and thus a career-high) in both carries and yards, while also notching his second professional touchdown.
pic.twitter.com/20cseM8tOU
The Colts line up in condensed 11 personnel set and send Anthony Gould in motion, which brings Michael Taaffe down into the box.
On the snap the Colts run what looks to be duo wrap, with Ashton Dulin wrapping into the C gap to block the most dangerous man. When Taaffe and Chris Johnson fit at the same time, Dulin is left in a bind.
His solution, a valiant one I'd add, is to throw an arm out and slip/roll into Johnson, who is impeded enough to be late fitting down into the voided space.
Dulin's attempt creates the slightest hesitation from Taaffe, who tries to bring Seth McGowan down with an arm tackle.
This is an angry run from McGowan that is punctuated by a fabulous "deuce" block from Matt Goncalves who moved over to right tackle on Sunday.
pic.twitter.com/bjgKnfWNVt
The Colts go back to a duo play here that starts with good movement on the nose tackle. Jalen Farmer and Tanor Bortolini do a nice job on this "ace" block, and once McGowan spots the Mike defender coming into the fit, in this case #10 Jacob Rodriguez, he presses the playside B gap until Rodriguez commits into the line of scrimmage.
McGowan then bends the run backside and puts his head down to brace for the oncoming onslaught of the Dolphins. Luckily, the entire Colts offense joined in the effort to shove McGowan across the goal line for his second touchdown of the year.
I think if Jonathan Taylor gets this same read from the Mike, he looks to bounce the run outside to get the edge on the unblocked corner.
Plays like this demonstrate the sometimes stark contrast in running styles between the Colts' two top running backs.
pic.twitter.com/BcCLUdHJdf
This isn't world-class pass protection, but it's just enough from a rookie running back put in a tough situation.
Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley loves to run these "pick" stunts out of Double Mug alignments. Whichever way the center slides, the linebacker to the slide drops into coverage. The rest of the offensive line is then in man-up protection.
The pick stunt is designed to get big guys on little guys in pass protection. Kenneth Grant is the quintessential "big man", so when Jacob Rodriguez collides with Jalen Farmer and gets his shoulders turned, Grant is coming right off his hip into Seth McGowan.
McGowan aggressively steps up to take Rodriguez, only to be confronted with all 330 pounds of Grant alongside the other half of Rodriguez.
The rookie does a good enough job of "dying slowly" to allow Daniel Jones to get this throw off to Ashton Dulin. If he doesn't step up so aggressively at the snap, he likely gets swallowed up alongside Jones in the backfield for a sack.
pic.twitter.com/IO6e9h7PKp
First of all, as should be customary with most big runs, shoutout to the offensive line on this one.
Tanor Bortolini and Dalton Tucker work a fabulous combo on the playside 3 tech up to the Mike, where Bort seals him to create the lane.
Moreover, hats off to Jalen Farmer for getting his helmet across the backside 2i and getting just enough of him to spring this; that's a tough block.
Finally, as for the run itself, McGowan does a nice job seeing the "bang" read and then sticking his foot and getting vertical upfield before getting skinny through the hole. Once he bursts into the open field, it takes contact from several defenders to bring him down.
The rookie is a tough, between-the-tackles runner who can also stretch the defense horizontally when given the opportunity. While he's no stallion in the open field, he bounces off defenders like a bowling ball does those lane bumpers they put up for kids at the bowling alley.
In other words, he's entertaining and a bit destructive.
For as tenebrous as the Colts future looks right now, if the next general manager can find more players who fit that description, the team will be alright.

title: Colts Midseason Awards: An Unexpected MVP and Few Bright Spots
full_text:
Let's be real. The Indianapolis Colts haven't exactly given us much to celebrate through 10 games.
At 3-7, this team has been an absolute mess, and Sunday's narrow victory over Miami doesn't change that.
Still, a few young guys have stepped up, and a handful of individuals deserve some recognition.
Here are my Colts midseason awards for 2026.
Yes, we're giving the MVP award to the owner. And I don't think it's particularly close.
After the 2-4 start and an embarrassing loss to Tennessee, Irsay-Gordon fired Chris Ballard, put Ed Dodds in charge of personnel, and helped lock up budding star Adetomiwa Adebawore.
Indianapolis then traded four expiring contracts for draft capital and now holds 10 picks in 2027. For a franchise desperate for direction, those are bigger wins than anything we've seen on the field.
JT hasn't exactly lit the world on fire lately. But with 739 rushing yards and eight of the Colts' 20 touchdowns coming from him, he's quite literally the only option.
Big Q is gone, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen have been traded, and the passing attack has been brutal. Who else could you possibly give this to?
Ade has been one of the lone bright spots on this defense.
His snap count has climbed since DeForest Buckner was traded, and he hasn't missed a step. With four sacks and a new two-year, $35 million extension, he's becoming a big part of this rebuild.
On a defense allowing 27.1 points per game, the competition for this award isn't exactly fierce.
This might be the easiest award of the bunch.
The seventh-round pick is averaging 5.2 yards per carry and just put up 77 yards and a touchdown against Miami, scoring in back-to-back weeks. His running style is so different from Taylor's, and they're developing a legitimate one-two punch.
Ballard deserves credit here. This late-round pick looks like an absolute home run.
Allen hasn't played a ton, but he's making the most of his opportunities. Against Miami, he finished with nine tackles, a sack, and two tackles for loss, and he's already handling the green dot.
Justin Walley deserves some love, too. The 2025 draft pick missed last season with a torn ACL, struggled early this year, and delivered a HUGE performance against Miami, including a strip-sack that led to a Colts touchdown.
Allen gets the rookie award, but both look like legitimate pieces to build around.
After suffering a season-ending knee injury last year, Shrader opened 2026 looking like one of the NFL's best kickers.
His play has cooled down lately, but he's still made 23 of 25 field goals, including nine from 50-plus yards. On an offense struggling to score touchdowns, that kind of reliability is enormous.
These awards aren't exactly a celebration of a good season. They're a look at the few people giving Colts fans something to believe in moving forward.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: 2 Colts Who Have No Business Playing Another Snap in 2026
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts finally snapped their five-game losing streak Sunday, escaping with a 24-22 win over the Miami Dolphins .
But let's not pretend one ugly win changes where this franchise is heading.
At 3-7, Indianapolis is clearly looking toward 2027. The priority over these final seven games should be simple: get the young guys on the field, figure out what you've got, and protect the players who matter to this rebuild.
That doesn't mean tanking. Remember, the New York Jets own the Colts' 2027 first-round pick, so there is absolutely ZERO incentive to lose games.
With that in mind, here are two Colts who should be shut down for the rest of 2026.
I've said it time and time again: Daniel Jones is only as good as the team surrounding him.
Put him on a decent team with receiving weapons, a running game, and a serviceable defense, and Danny can look pretty good. Put him in a terrible offense on a terrible team, and this is what you get .
Through 10 games, Jones has thrown for 1,830 yards, seven touchdowns, and an NFL-leading 12 interceptions. Against Miami, he completed just 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards, one touchdown, and two picks.
He's playing like one of the worst quarterbacks in football , and after trading Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, I don't see that changing anytime soon.
But this is bigger than his play.
Jones has roughly $10.5 million in injury-guaranteed money for 2027, which could become payable if an injury prevents him from passing a physical when the Colts try to release him. That $10.5 million becomes fully guaranteed on March 15 if he's still on the roster.
Why take that risk for a quarterback who isn't going to look good in this dismantled offense, especially when the franchise is clearly focused on the future?
Let someone else take the snaps and see what you've got.
This one is different, because Gardner absolutely should be part of Indianapolis' long-term plans .
The Colts gave up two first-round picks and Adonai Mitchell to acquire him, and he's on a four-year, $120.4 million extension. That's a massive investment in someone who's supposed to be a cornerstone of this rebuild.
Gardner injured his left calf again against Miami, marking the third issue with that same calf since arriving in Indianapolis. He didn't return and was listed as a nonparticipant in Monday's walkthrough.
With Thursday night's matchup in Houston approaching, there's no reason to rush him back. Frankly, there's no reason to rush him back at all this season.
Let the young defensive backs keep developing, let Sauce get fully healthy, and get him ready for 2027.
The Colts should still play to win. But they shouldn't gamble with their future just to chase a few more victories in a lost season.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: 3 Reasons Steichen Frustratingly Starts Daniel Jones Over Anthony Richardson
full_text:
Would you look at that? The Indianapolis Colts won after dropping five straight, but it was truly an ugly victory over the even worse Miami Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium, 24-22.
The victory isn't what is buzzing around Indianapolis though. Rather, it's why Shane Steichen continues to roll with Daniel Jones despite the quarterback putting up the worst numbers of his veteran career.
Through 10 games, Jones has put up a stat line that could make you want to shield your eyes. Below are the numbers.
Colts fans are screaming from the rafters for Indianapolis to give Anthony Richardson Sr. a shot with how bad Jones has been.
However, Steichen continues to trust Jones to start under center and seemingly avoids Richardson as a replacement.
Shane Steichen’s opening statement. Daniel Jones will remain the starter on a short week. pic.twitter.com/DlM8eTbLCt
However, if you read between the lines, the reasoning is very clear, and it comes in three formats.
Let's dive into the hot topic.
Trust is arguably the biggest emphasis when it comes to an NFL head coach and quarterback, but especially for the offensive-minded playcallers like Steichen.
Now, answer this question: Has Richardson ever given Steichen a real chance to trust him? Not really.
Starting with his on-field play. Outside of the four games from his rookie year, Richardson has been absolutely awful, there's no sugarcoating it.
Richardson got 11 of his 15 career starts during the 2024 season, and he couldn't have been worse. Whether it was pre-snap adjustments, progressing through reads, accuracy, or turnovers, Richardson struggled with them all.
David Ojabo just LEVELED Anthony Richardson pic.twitter.com/aGHb2PCPe7
Richardson has a career record of 8-7, but outside of a few game-winning drives against meager competition, it didn't feel like the Colts won because of his performances.
Following that is Richardson's discipline as a professional quarterback. Whether it's not bringing the locker room together or extracurricular issues, Richardson has essentially had a childlike mentality when it comes to how seriously he should take the gig.
Put these factors together and it's obvious that Steichen can't trust Richardson.
It's not necessarily that Steichen doesn't want to; it's that Richardson hasn't given him much reason to.
Don't you think if Richardson were truly better than Jones that the Colts would thrust him into the starting role? Absolutely they would.
After investing their future and the 2023 fourth-overall pick in Richardson, the Colts would probably love nothing more than for him to show he can beat out Jones and hit the stride they were praying he would.
Going back to the 2025 season, Richardson was supposed to have his limelight and beat out Jones in the QB competition. That season, the Colts handed Jones a one-year, $14 million deal.
They didn't sign Jones in the hopes that he'd start; they did it to push Richardson, and the latter did not answer the bell.
If we jump to current times, the performance-related reason Steichen continues to go with Jones is that Richardson isn't showing in practices he's better.
This isn't proven of course, but it makes high-level sense. If Richardson was showing he's above Jones as an overall quarterback, he'd be the starter.
You can't tell me Steichen wouldn't love to have the far more talented Richardson as the QB to make defenses consider a bevy of outcomes.
However, whether it's his recent issue with marijuana possession or lack of execution during practice, it's fair to speculate he's simply not performing during prep like Jones.
Whether the Colts cut Jones and sign a one-year bridge QB for 2027 isn't what fans should be examining when it comes to Richardson not starting.
It's that he hasn't shown enough capability to be the feature piece of a complete NFL rebuild. If he isn't in their plans, what does starting him for eight games in what's likely Steichen's last year really do?
Indianapolis no longer has Josh Downs or Michael Pittman Jr., and when they did, Richardson still couldn't make the most of those targets. Alec Pierce was also healthy and on the field with Jonathan Taylor in the backfield.
Now with Downs in Kansas City and Quenton Nelson in Seattle, it's hard to imagine that Richardson is suddenly going to morph into a good enough quarterback to lead a team that will be as rough as Indy in 2027.
Even considering the cap space Indy will have and the best free agents they can sign, it still doesn't convince me he's a fit for the Colts' situation.
Pair with this that Richardson will be a free agent and requested a trade that went nowhere in February of this year, and it makes even more sense to omit him as next year's QB and beyond.
It's a foregone conclusion that Richardson will don a new uniform in 2027, and his days as the franchise savior hopeful are over. Ultimately, this is why it makes no sense to make Richardson the replacement for the rest of the year.
Jones is the starter, and Colts fans need to accept that Steichen isn't switching things up with Richardson.
The rebuild for the Colts is underway, and with Richardson not in the future game plan, it is illogical to give him the offensive reins for the final eight games.
The Colts' quarterback situation looked promising last year, but clearly Jones was a one-hit wonder, and that stings the franchise.
Pack onto the heap that the team has to wait until 2028 for their next QB and go with Jones for the gap and it makes things even tougher to stomach.
Regardless, we'll see what Jones has in store for the Colts for the rest of a brutal 2026 campaign.
