title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Which Receivers Should Get the Largest Workload in the Second Half of the Season?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 7-2 after their comfortable victory over the Atlanta Falcons , and with an impressive Chiefs debut for wide receiver Josh Downs , the Chiefs' passing game looks to be the healthiest it's been in quite some time.
Where does that leave the wide receiver rotation just after the midway point of the year? That's where we'll begin in today's Chiefs On SI mailbag.
What is the ideal, gotta-have-it, three-receiver set for this team with the players currently available on the roster today? (And if Worthy isn't on your list, do you think the coaching staff will reach the same conclusion?) - @oscarbobo.bsky.social
Downs and Rashee Rice are the obvious No. 1 and 2, regardless of which order you'd rank them in. The third spot is the tricky one.
In his third season, Xavier Worthy leads Chiefs wide receivers in snaps taken by a healthy margin, having taken 478 snaps to Rice's second-place 273. Worthy has been on the field more than Travis Kelce and Kingsley Suamataia this year; he's fifth in snaps on the Chiefs' offense. That doesn't look like a player who's about to see his role decrease significantly.
However, we've seen the same issues in recent weeks. Despite his experience and health, he hasn't been making a significant impact in the box score or on film. With a few sideline-related miscues gaining traction amongst some Chiefs fans on social media, I understand why Worthy's stock appears to be in decline.
Worthy's 33 catches on 50 targets for 278 yards adds up to more than double rookie Cyrus Allen's early-season production (seven catches on 14 targets for 109), but Worthy has quadrupled Allen's offensive snaps (108).
I've seen enough flashes from Allen and enough miscues from Worthy to at least be willing to hear out an argument on behalf of the rookie being a more useful weapon in this "gotta-have-it" scenario. For now, I do think Worthy retains that spot for the KC coaching staff. Still, Worthy's role seems destined to decrease with the addition of Downs and the return of the now-healthy Rice; if Worthy doesn't start making plays again soon, Allen will continue to close that gap.
Cyrus Allen is two months older than Xavier Worthy. They're both 23.
What playoff team in the AFC would be toughest to beat at home? My money is on the Broncos strictly based on the pass rush. When Mahomes loses in the playoffs, he isn't able to overcome his offensive line. They could overwhelm us. - @jaymaul4.bsky.social
Bo Nix aside, I think this logic for Denver absolutely holds water. The single area on the team that I am the most short- and long-term worried about is the offensive line, so we logically have to pick a team that has the ability to challenge that unit.
The question the Chiefs will need to see answered over the next month or so: Do the Bills and Bengals have enough defensive firepower to push through KC's questionable line? Maybe this is out of blind loyalty to Mahomes, maybe it's because he's been so good behind such an iffy group already this season , but I think that any team planning to beat the Chiefs in January will need to have a solid day rushing the passer and an offense that's better and more consistent than what Denver offers... which is also where the perpetually under-the-radar Jaguars come into play for their part of the conversation.
With how our offense looks, both with the elite running game from either K9 or E10 and our passing game looking WAY better now that Josh Downs is already making an impact for us, do you think we can come out of the gauntlet of games to end the season 5-2 or better? - @zandersahlia.bsky.social
For record-keeping, here's the gauntlet in question: at Buffalo, at Cincinnati, vs. New England, vs. San Francisco. Then, the Chiefs go to LA to face the Chargers and host the Raiders. You have to expect that Kansas City wins the final two AFC West showdowns of the year, leaving that brutal five-game stretch where you're asking about going 3-2.
The Rams are significantly depleated from their preseason hype, and the Patriots are expected to be without quarterback Drake Maye. The Bills, Bengals and 49ers are all legitimate Super Bowl contenders.
Going even 2-3 down that stretch would be plenty for a playoff spot, sending KC to a hypothetical 11-5 season if they do handle those final two divisional games after the gauntlet. Even if the Chiefs are underdogs at Buffalo, at Cincy and home to the Niners, I'd be a bit surprised if they lost all three of those games.
Now, if they beat the Bills and Bengals, we're back to talking about their chances at the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
Can this team win the Super Bowl with this offensive line? - @MarkKnopke
Yes! I'm quite concerned about the state of the O-line, but (yes, even after two Super Bowl losses enabled by completely overwhelmed offensive line play) if you give me Mahomes, a fully stocked array of weapons both through the air and on the ground, and a defense that might be hitting its stride, that team can absolutely win a few one-off games while trying to hide the line's deficiencies.
Would it be more likely with better performances across the trenches? Absolutely. But the AFC doesn't have a singularly dominant team, and the Chiefs are just as plausible of a Super Bowl representative as anyone else in the conference.

title: Making Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes’ Case as the 2026 NFL MVP
full_text:
Considering how well he's performed in 2026, it's almost easy to forget that Patrick Mahomes is coming off a torn ACL and LCL . Just nine months removed from suffering a potentially career-altering injury, Mahomes made his comeback in the season-opening win over the Broncos and has appeared in every game since.
While it took the future Hall of Fame quarterback some time to rediscover his rhythm, he has returned to his usual form in his 10th season in the NFL. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns without an interception in the Chiefs' dominant win against the Falcons last week, putting him ahead of Peyton Manning for the most combined touchdown passes in a player's first 10 seasons. Nobody could have expected Mahomes to re-establish himself this quickly, but that's exactly what's happened. After his stellar Week 10 showing, Mahomes now holds the fifth-best odds to be named NFL's Most Valuable Player, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Could he capture his third MVP award by season's end?
Since the Chiefs inked running back Kenneth Walker to a three-year deal in the offseason, Andy Reid's offense has become more balanced and less reliant on the aerial attack. Even so, Mahomes ranks inside the league's top 10 in passing yards, passing touchdowns, and is second among all quarterbacks in touchdown-to-interception ratio (19-to-4).
The last three weeks alone, Mahomes has averaged over 300 yards through the air per contest, tossing 10 touchdowns without an interception on 70.1% passing. Those are numbers that could earn him serious MVP consideration if they persist.
Currently listed above Mahomes on the MVP ladder are Joe Burrow (+100), Josh Allen (+350), Brock Purdy (+400), and Trevor Lawrence (+550). But aside from Purdy and the injury-riddled 49ers, the other three quarterbacks don't come close to sharing Mahomes' predicament at wide receiver. Tyquan Thornton suffered a likely season-ending ankle injury in Kansas City's win over the Raiders in Week 4, while Rashee Rice missed time with a hamstring ailment. Those developments have compounded an already unpredictable receiving corps entering the campaign, yet Mahomes' production hasn't wavered one bit.
Not to take anything away from Burrow's historic first half of the season, but Mahomes doesn't have the luxury of throwing to the best receiver tandem in football in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins every week. The Chiefs also have a more dependable defense that allows the offense to play with a lead, whereas Cincinnati's defensive struggles often force Burrow to throw 40+ times just to keep the Bengals competitive. There's far more to consider in the MVP discussion than yards and touchdowns.
Although Mahomes still has some ground to make up in the passing-yardage department, his efficiency has been difficult for the other MVP hopefuls to match. He has been able to limit turnovers in addition to showcasing his new-and-improved deep ball, something that has contributed to Kansas City's offensive resurgence.
With former Colts slot wideout Josh Downs now in the mix , Mahomes can finally maximize the weapons at his disposal. That was made evident in the Falcons game when five different pass-catchers recorded 40 or more receiving yards and Mahomes was distributing the rock to everyone. MVP voters put a lot of stock into a team's record when evaluating prospective award contenders. Burrow, Allen, Lawrence, and Mahomes are all battling to secure AFC's top playoff seed, which could go a long way in determining the eventual winner. A 13 or 14-win finish for the Chiefs may be enough to push Mahomes over the top if the other candidates lose ground in the playoff race.
It understandably took time for Mahomes to trust his surgically repaired knee and gradually learn what his body could withstand on the field. His comfort levels have steadily improved throughout the year, and he's now playing even better than he did in the past few seasons. There is no better time for Mahomes to start hitting his stride than now.
Burrow will remain the consensus favorite for the award until further notice, but if he experiences a second-half slump and Mahomes keeps playing at this level, don't be surprised if the three-time Super Bowl champ receives first-place MVP votes at the end of the year.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: Emmett Johnson, Cyrus Allen Take the Cake
full_text:
As the home stretch of the 2026-27 campaign arrives, the Kansas City Chiefs have one more game against a struggling team before a gauntlet of a schedule in Weeks 12-16. If there's one thing recent outings have shown, though, it's that the club's young players have plenty to offer.
With the war of attrition setting in and injuries piling up, the organization's depth will undoubtedly continue to be tested. Is it a good or bad thing that Kansas City could be asking the future of the team to rise to the occasion in the present?
Following Week 10's win over the Atlanta Falcons , let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each qualifying 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, who is running low on time to be activated to the roster from the physically unable to perform list , isn't included here.
Left tackle Josh Simmons remains off the list after going to injured reserve . The same applies to running back Brashard Smith .
No young Chiefs player — and very few members of the team in general — was more productive than fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson in Week 10. The halfback made his starting debut due to a groin injury to Kenneth Walker III and ran with it, both literally and figuratively. Johnson was fantastic on the ground and kept dicing up the defense as a pass catcher, cementing him as a force to be reckoned with .
Elsewhere, defensive end Ashton Gillotte is coming on strong after a slow start to the season . The 2025 third-round pick has a sack in back-to-back games and is no stranger to playing plus run defense.
The cornerback duo of Nohl Williams and Mansoor Delane was far from perfect, as Williams lost to Drake London a couple of times and Delane seemed to get banged up, but the former logged an interception to cap off Sunday's blowout win.
One of the stories of Sunday was wide receiver Cyrus Allen, the second of Kansas City's two fifth-round selections back in April. The Cincinnati product scored the first touchdown of his professional career against a quality cornerback in A.J. Terrell, making it look easy with a masterclass of a route:
Cyrus Allen with a nasty double move to cash in the long TD🥵🥵 Sully gonna have to leave the app pic.twitter.com/M8GfmtekqM
Rounding out the top tier of Chiefs youngsters is defensive end R Mason Thomas. Thomas was quiet down at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, going without a pressure for the first time in his KC tenure. We'll chalk this up to a one-off.
Even after the trade acquisition of now-former Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs, sophomore pass catcher Jalen Royals logged 19 snaps in Week 10. For the first time since Week 1 of the regular season, however, he went without a single target on offense. Left tackle Kahlil Benson also had a rough outing , surrendering a new career-high figure in pressures and continuing to look like he's crumbling as the foundation of the line.
Defensive tackle Peter Woods stays in his usual spot after missing Sunday's showdown with a lingering neck injury. Keep an eye on the injury report to see if he'll play this weekend against the Arizona Cardinals.
Speaking to the media this week, head coach Andy Reid made it a point to allude to how wideout Andrew Armstrong is a lesser-known player both in Chiefs circles and nationally. He made a name for himself in Week 10, though, when he hauled in a beautiful 43-yard bomb from quarterback Patrick Mahomes for the Dallas native's first touchdown.
THAT'S 5 TOUCHDOWNS FOR 15 ⏰ pic.twitter.com/d6NkVGDKyI
It'll be interesting to find out whether the potential return of Norman-Lott will impact Bryson Eason's status on the roster. He's squarely in the rotation along the interior of the defensive line, playing 20 snaps in Week 8 and rising from five in Week 9 to 11 in Week 10, but he doesn't stand out a ton when on the field. Sometimes, that isn't a bad thing for the waiver pickup .
With tight end Travis Kelce hurting his calf/ankle on the club's opening possession and Jared Wiley sustaining an ankle fracture, 2025 undrafted free agent Jake Briningstool wound up getting more of a workload than most anticipated. He played a career-high 17 offensive reps, hauling in one of his two targets for 20 yards in the process.
Last is fourth-round cornerback Jadon Canady, whose stint as a rookie for the Chiefs has been tumultuous to this point. His snap count swelled to 26 on defense and 18 on special teams in Atlanta, seeing him record three tackles but also look more vulnerable in coverage.
Nothing to see here regarding 2025 fifth-round linebacker Jeffrey Bassa, who continues to be a trusted special teams ace for coordinator Dave Toub. Now several weeks into his return from injury , fellow 'backer Cooper McDonald saw the field just once on defense in Week 10 but set a season high with 25 special teams snaps.
Former Iowa standout, safety Xavier Nwankpa, recorded two tackles on a combined 31 reps (five on defense, 26 on special teams). He's settled into a consistent role in his debut campaign.
For the first time in his career, tackle Diego Pounds got into the lineup and split time between offense and teams. Given how banged-up the offensive line was and the game script of a lopsided contest, this was a nice reward from the Chiefs for the UDFA's work since coming over via trade .
Seventh-round pick Garrett Nussmeier continues to be Kansas City's emergency third quarterback on game days. Rookie running back Jaydn Ott sat this one out with a hamstring injury, whereas cornerback Melvin Smith was a Week 10 inactive after playing special teams in Weeks 8 and 9.

title: Chiefs Stock Watch: Reality Check Time After Week 10's Blowout Win
full_text:
For the second game in a row, the Kansas City Chiefs squared off against an inferior opponent and actually managed to make the quality of each team obvious on the playing field.
Week 10's showdown with the Atlanta Falcons seemed destined to be a Kansas City victory from the beginning. Within the final result of a 35-13 blowout triumph on the road, there were plenty of positives but also a few negatives to take away with a new week arriving.
Let's dive into the good and bad from the Chiefs' Week 10 win against Atlanta and single out three players whose stock is trending up, as well as three who could use a better showing in Week 11 and down the stretch of the year.
These players stood out for positive reasons on Sunday, potentially changing the trajectory of their seasons in the process.
Given how fantastic starter Kenneth Walker III has been when on the field, there wasn't much need for premium reps for rookie running back Emmett Johnson in Weeks 1-9. He still found ways to impact the game, but Sunday was his coming-out party with Walker sitting due to a groin injury. The Nebraska product logged a whopping 28 touches down in Atlanta, averaging 6.1 yards per opportunity and scoring two touchdowns in the process.
Johnson's ability as a receiver out of the backfield is second to very few at the position right now. He's logged at least a catch in two of his last three outings, going for 11 receptions on 12 targets for 198 yards and three scores in that span. The fifth-round pick has clearly adapted to life as a professional at a rapid pace and made the most of his first NFL start.
There's a case to be made that Johnson is a starting-caliber player for multiple teams. That includes the Chiefs. Even though Walker is the superior option and will resume the role once he returns, having such a dangerous backup has to make Kansas City feel good with tough, cold-weather football on the horizon.
Yards per Route Run Leaders 1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.09) 2. Mike Evans (3.65) 3. Emmett Johnson (3.13) 🔥👀⁉️🤯 RB Leaders by Yards From Scrimmage per Touch 1. Emmett Johnson (7.63) 🔥 2. Jaylen Warren (6.66) 3. Christian McCaffrey (6.13) RB Leaders by Missed Tackles Forced… https://t.co/9XcDTPzidE
Coming into Week 10, first-year wideout Cyrus Allen was an interesting case. Were the Chiefs truly planning to give him more snaps and opportunities, or would the trade acquisition of Josh Downs put a cap on the fifth-rounder's ceiling within the offense in 2026-27? Considering Allen had averaged 22 snaps and a pair of targets in the three games leading up to Atlanta, there were reasons for the answer to go in either direction.
Fortunately for the former Cincinnati man, the club found a perfectly happy medium for at least one week of play.
Allen had the best showing of his young career to date on Sunday, turning four targets into two receptions for 44 yards. His snap count of 23 was good for 35.4% of those available, which is more than enough time to make a play or two. That's precisely what Allen did, as he was held on a non-call for a potential touchdown earlier in the contest but rebounded with a masterpiece of a route against A.J. Terrell later on for his first-ever score:
Filthy route from Cyrus Allen 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/YNh2IdJZjU
It's not just that Allen found the end zone. It's how he found it. The rookie was lined up on the boundary of the formation with tight coverage and won with technicality and some burst. That's more of what the Chiefs need in the receiver room; that highlight will be remembered in Allen discussions for weeks and months to come.
Before the season, many thought the Chiefs' defensive line would live and die with what All-Pro tackle Chris Jones could provide. While there's still some truth to that, defensive end George Karlaftis has emerged as a worthy running mate for the veteran pass rusher in more ways than one.
He's also established himself as one of the more valuable assets on the team after plenty of folks questioned the four-year contract extension he was previously signed to before the expiration of his rookie deal.
Karlaftis was tremendous once again in this one, recording a second-down sack on Atlanta's second drive, batting down a pass early in the third frame and also combining for a quarterback takedown with Jones later on. The former first-round pick is the only player this century to log both a tackle for loss and a pass defended in seven straight regular-season games.
Add in that all five-and-a-half of Karlaftis' sacks have come since Week 6, and you get the full picture of a 25-year-old who's having a breakout in season No. 5.
These three players didn't meet the bar in Week 10 and need to recover moving forward.
Back in the spring and summer, nobody expected undrafted rookie free agent tackle Kahlil Benson to still be in the Chiefs' starting lineup. That's especially true when considering it was the right tackle job he wound up competing for . Once Josh Simmons' health became an issue again, however, the Indiana product was thrust into the lineup and actually didn't look too bad early in the season.
With Simmons still on injured reserve and the Chiefs' offensive line becoming increasingly banged up, though, Benson is struggling to string together effective performances.
Pro Football Focus tracking metrics aren't everything, but the 24-year-old surrendered a then-career-high four pressures in Week 7's loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He followed it up with an improved one-pressure outing versus the Denver Broncos, but those figures are five and eight, respectively, since then.
Rolling into Week 11, Benson is tied for seventh in most pressures ceded (30) by a tackle. He's got a significant lead in quarterback hits, allowing 16 to second-place Kolton Miller's 12. For all the talk about how much Kansas City needed a wide receiver at the deadline, the return of Simmons would have a massive swing for the floor and ceiling of the offense as well.
If there's one thing you can't accuse the Chiefs of, it's not trying to make 2024 first-round pick Xavier Worthy a legitimate weapon. Before Sunday's game, the lowest single-game target total he'd logged this year was two, and he only did it once. In all other contests, his average was 6.4. Despite him repeatedly showing that he isn't worth the on-field investment, it doesn't seem to be going anywhere.
Worthy saw three passes thrown his way in Week 10, although none connected for a completion. On the afternoon, he drifted too much on a second-and-15 drop, ran a bad route and lost the ball on a fourth-quarter first-and-10 and also let an onside kick get recovered on special teams. His 57 snaps were the third-most for him this season; being on the field for 87.7% of opportunities isn't a signal that the club is moving away from him.
Perhaps it should, though. In all, Worthy has turned 50 targets into 33 receptions, 278 yards and a single touchdown this year. According to SumerSports , he leads the Chiefs' wide receiver room with a 17.92% target share but is fourth in yards per route run with 0.93.
Only 40 receivers have run at least 250 routes in 2026-27. Worthy is one of them, yet he's 38th in YPRR. He needs either a change of role right now or a change of scenery in the offseason to find whatever best form he's got left.
It's been a strange season for one Kingsley Suamataia, as the left guard has put excellent reps on tape but also completely whiffed on other occasions and looked totally out of place. There's the matter of availability, too, with head coach Andy Reid benching him on two separate occasions ahead of road contests but not revealing why that was the case.
The third-year man bounced back in Week 9 with a splendid overall game, but that didn't translate to this one.
Suamataia was charged with seven pressures and five quarterback hurries against a Falcons defensive front that's far from elite. Last year, the most he'd given up in a game was five. You have to go all the way back to Week 10 of…

title: Why George Karlaftis Has Been the Unsung Hero for the Chiefs’ Defense
full_text:
Despite a strong 7-2 start for the Chiefs, many Kansas City fans were underwhelmed with how the defensive line performed early in the season. The lack of production along the front four became a major talking point during a lengthy sack drought that lasted 15 quarters.
Since that prolonged dry spell, though, the pass rush has come alive for Steve Spagnuolo's unit. The Chiefs have recorded eight sacks over the past two games while surrendering just 12.5 points per contest during that span. While critics have been calling for "CEO of Sack Nation" Chris Jones to elevate his play, George Karlaftis has flown under the radar. In the final year of his rookie contract , the fifth-year defensive end is quietly putting together the best statistical season of his NFL career.
Across the last five weeks, Karlaftis has totaled 11 QB hits, eight tackles for loss, and 5.5 sacks. More impressively, the Athens native has been better than anyone else in the NFL at batting balls down at the line of scrimmage.
🚨 NFL HISTORY! George Karlaftis becomes the FIRST player since at least 1999 to record both a tackle for loss and a pass defended in SEVEN consecutive regular-season games! pic.twitter.com/zkpnKrlcju
When evaluating edge rushers, it's easy to dismiss their contributions when their sack total is low. However, Karlaftis would remain among the most disruptive defensive ends even if he hadn't started racking up more sacks.
Right now, Karlaftis is tied with a few other players for eighth in the league with 10 pass deflections. That's a remarkable number for any position other than defensive back. Only one other defensive end in the NFL (Jaylahn Tuimoloau) has managed five or more pass breakups — and Karlaftis is doing it on a weekly basis. Even when he isn't getting into the backfield to pressure the quarterback, Karlaftis is obstructing passing lanes, making life difficult for opposing signal-callers. It has become a valuable and underrated weapon for a Chiefs defense that still ranks in the NFL's bottom half in sacks.
With the 32-year-old Jones having a relatively quiet year by his standards, Karlaftis has needed to assume more responsibility within the defensive scheme. After receiving a massive contract extension last offseason, any questions about whether he was worth the investment have seemingly been put to rest.
Karlaftis caught a lot of flak from the fanbase after being sackless heading into the team's bye week. He certainly heard the noise and has responded emphatically in recent weeks. There have been few pass rushers more productive than Karlaftis since the beginning of October. Now that the defensive line has broken out of its slump, Chiefs fans can finally appreciate what Karlaftis has done this season. He'll continue to play a key role anchoring KC's defensive front throughout the remainder of the campaign.

title: Much More Than a Backup: Emmett Johnson Shows Star Potential in Atlanta
full_text:
Kansas City Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson made plenty of plays to earn praise throughout his first eight games as a professional. Chiefs fans were already rightfully excited about the fifth-round pick based on his explosive moments when he took snaps that allowed star back Kenneth Walker to take a breather. Then, in a late-week surprise, Walker was ruled out due to a groin injury ahead of the Chiefs' game against the Atlanta Falcons. Johnson would be getting the first start of his pro career.
By the time Sunday's game arrived, the running back room had thinned out on both sides of Johnson. Walker didn't travel to Atlanta. Undrafted rookie Jaydn Ott was inactive due to a hamstring injury. Second-year back Brashard Smith has been on injured reserve since October 24. Practice squad elevation Nate Carter was the Chiefs' only other active runner on Sunday. The stage was set for Johnson to have a breakout game, and he delivered.
Johnson took 22 carries for 101 yards and added six catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns, but his impressive 28-touch, 171-yard box score still somehow undersells his actual performance.
If you've watched the Chiefs even somewhat closely this season, you've noticed that Johnson jumps off the screen as a no-doubt-about-it NFL-caliber player and a uniquely explosive weapon, both on the ground and through the air. Some backs carve out long, productive NFL careers by being good in all phases and taking what's available when they're given the ball. Others excel in particular roles, extending their time in the league with excellence in short-yardage scenarios or expertise as pass-catching backs who can also be trusted to hold their own in pass protection. Yet another class of player might continue to find landing spots by bringing explosive plays on occasion, offset by underwhelming skills or inconsistency in other areas.
The best backs have the ability to do multiple things at high levels while maintaining that game-breaking ability that defenses fear. The remarkable thing about the Chiefs' running back room is that they, quite clearly now, have two running backs who offer consistency, explosion, and high-end skills in multiple phases. We've seen that proven by Walker in Week 1 and many times since. It has been on the horizon for Johnson for more than a month , seen on display in flashes on multiple occasions. But now, there's no reason to pump the brakes on the rookie's standing as one of the league's most alluring young runners.
Last week, I was listening to some NFL podcasts that discussed their picks for an array of midseason awards, and I realized that there wasn't a clear runaway winner for Offensive Rookie of the Year. Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston appeared to be the favorite, but I briefly wondered if Johnson would be considered, even as the Chiefs' backup running back. On the other hand, maybe I was looking at Johnson's season through Chiefs-red-tinted glasses.
Well, imagine my delight when seeing this post from Ted Nguyen of The Athletic .
Emmet Johnson would be the rookie of the year if he had a RB1 workload pic.twitter.com/afLXkMUKYI
"[Emmett] Johnson would be the rookie of the year if he had a RB1 workload," Nguyen wrote.
At this point, how could you disagree?
Even without a starting workload, Johnson is second among rookies in yards from scrimmage this season (519), behind only Boston (523). He also has one more touchdown than Boston (four to Boston's three). Even if he's still a long shot to haul in any hardware by the end of the year, his impact to the Chiefs is undeniable.
With Walker expected to return to the lineup soon, a slightly more well-balanced Walker/Johnson split seems both plausable and worthwhile. Yes, Walker still is the rightful alpha of the Chiefs' backfield, but it's remarkable to look at KC's running back room through the lens of the last several seasons.
A Chiefs running back has recorded 130+ scrimmage yards in seven games this year between Ken Walker (5) and Emmett Johnson (2). KC had just five such games from 2021-25.
As noted by Chiefs team reporter Matt McMullen , Walker has recorded at least 130 scrimmage yards in a game five times this year, while Johnson has now done it twice. From 2021 through 2025, Chiefs running backs had just five games over that threshold. An average of one per season. Walker and Johnson have done it seven times in nine games.
Also from McMullen : Against the Falcons, Johnson forced 10 missed tackles. He has forced a missed tackle on 45.6% of his touches this season. Read that again. The fifth-round rookie has forced a missed tackle on nearly half of his 68 touches this season.
So, what's the perfect balance between Walker and Johnson in the weeks to come? Eh, who cares? That's not the important part right now. The most impactful development out of the Chiefs' backfield is that the team has a fringe Rookie of the Year candidate backing up a likely Offensive Player of the Year nominee.
When Walker misses time, the offense doesn't have to retool on short notice. If Johnson misses time, we know Walker can take a heavy workload. As the season rolls on and the weather gets colder, opposing defenses won't have an opportunity to wear Walker down in hopes of getting to a significant downgrade when Kansas City goes down the depth chart.
If it's with 15 snaps per game or 50, Johnson has proven that he is a legitimate threat with the ball in his hands, adding one more high-octane weapon to the Chiefs' offense and one more headache for defenses that will have to plan for a long day, regardless of who's running the ball.

title: Biggest Winners and Losers From the Chiefs’ 35-13 Win Over the Falcons
full_text:
Like a week ago, the Kansas City Chiefs took about two quarters to get going, but once they did, they looked like one of the most unstoppable teams in the NFL.
It came against the now 3-7 Atlanta Falcons, but they are still an opponent who beat both the 6-4 Green Bay Packers and the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers earlier this season.
In the end, the Chiefs cruised to a 35-13 road win with ease. Here are the biggest winners and losers from Week 10 in Atlanta.
Quarterback Patrick Mahomes put together his best game of 2026 in several different ways. The numbers were there, he got multiple receivers involved, did it with injuries piling up around him, and had his offensive line play as poorly as it has all year. Under constant pressure, he went 22-for-35 for 348 yards, five touchdowns, and no interceptions.
He also made good use of his new weapon. Josh Downs ran just eight routes, caught four of his five targets, and moved the chains three times, including a back-shoulder fade for a touchdown that made it 14-3 at halftime.
The most encouraging development was Mahomes’ willingness to push the ball downfield. His average depth of target was 10.1, according to PFF, a far cry from the 2.9 he posted last week against the Jets. Seven different receivers caught a pass of 20 yards or more, including a 50-yarder to Rashee Rice, a 43-yard touchdown to Andrew Armstrong, and a 39-yard touchdown to Cyrus Allen. He averaged 9.9 yards per attempt, his most since Week 3 against Miami.
When news broke on Saturday that Kenneth Walker , the NFL’s second-leading rusher, would miss Week 10, it was easy to see what kind of day Emmett Johnson could have. His skills have been bubbling up all season, on the ground and through the air.
As the main back against Atlanta, he delivered and then some. He produced 171 yards from scrimmage and caught two touchdown passes from Mahomes. He was elusive in space all game and forced six missed tackles, according to PFF.
He carried the rock 22 times for 101 yards on 4.6 yards per carry and was even better as a receiver, catching six passes for 70 yards, averaging 11.7 yards per catch. With the 3-7 Cardinals coming to Arrowhead next week and a big matchup with the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving four days later, it wouldn't be shocking to see him as the featured back again in Week 11.
Atlanta came in 11th in sacks allowed, giving up just 1.8 per game. Michael Penix is known for getting the ball out quickly, and the Falcons lean on Bijan Robinson to run the ball, which makes it hard to get home. The Chiefs, meanwhile, ranked 29th in sacks, with just 14 through eight games.
Despite the unfavorable matchup, Kansas City’s front seven pressured Penix 23 times, its most since Week 6 against the Chargers, and sacked him three times. That makes eight sacks over the past two games, against two decent offensive lines.
George Karlaftis led the way again with seven pressures, 1.5 sacks, and a batted pass. Ashton Gillotte had a sack on six pressures, and Chris Jones shared one with Karlaftis. Perhaps the group's most impressive feat was limiting Robinson, the league’s leading rusher, to 71 rushing yards, even though the game was tight for most of the first half. Drue Tranquill and Nick Bolton tied for the team lead with nine tackles apiece, and Bolton added a tackle for loss and forced a fumble on tight end Kyle Pitts.
On a day when Travis Kelce got hurt and Mahomes spread the ball to eight different pass catchers, Xavier Worthy missed the passing-game party entirely. Mahomes targeted him three times, and the box score reads zero catches for zero yards. He also made a special teams blunder. Lined up on the hands team for an onside kick, he seemed to watch Atlanta’s Chris Blair recover it, setting up 10 quick Falcons points in the fourth quarter.
Rice continues to stack good performances, Downs looks like a great fit, and Allen may turn his best day in the NFL into more opportunities. All of that could mean a smaller role for Worthy. He played 56 of 64 offensive snaps on Sunday, but comparing his production with the snaps for Rice (30), Allen (22), and Downs (10) paints a rough picture.
Mahomes’ performance looked even more impressive because he did it under constant duress, with the odds stacked against him. According to PFF, he was pressured 24 times and hit eight times. Right tackle Jaylon Moore was out with an ankle injury, and right guard Trey Smith left early with a concussion. With those circumstances, Kahlil Benson allowed eight pressures, Kingsley Suamataia allowed seven, and Mike Caliendo allowed four pressures and a sack while filling in for Smith.
With the weapons shaping up the way they are, a healthy line is paramount to the Chiefs’ Super Bowl hopes. They have run-blocked well in recent weeks, but all of the lineup shuffling has cost them in pass protection.
This is an area where Downs should help once he earns more snaps, but the Chiefs finished just 4-for-13 on third downs and 0-for-1 on fourth. Scoring 35 points while converting only four third downs is impressive, but it doesn't make it a good process.
They came out strong, with a five-minute, 10-play, 80-yard touchdown drive. After that, things got ugly. Once Smith left, Mahomes struggled to settle the offense, and four straight punts netted just 63 yards between two touchdown drives. The two-minute offense brought the unit to life, putting them up 14-3 at the break, but they started the second half with two straight three-and-outs as well.
After that, the Chiefs drove for three straight touchdowns, but Matt Araiza still had to punt on seven of 13 drives, and Kansas City turned the ball over on downs after recovering a fumble in good field position. The Chiefs averaged 7.3 yards per play, second only to their Week 6 game against the Chargers. That shows how good they were on their five scoring drives and how bad they were on the other eight.

title: Believe It or Not, Josh Downs Had a Career Day in His Chiefs Debut
full_text:
In the first week of play with the annual NFL trade deadline in the rearview mirror, teams had the first chances to see how their new additions would boost their lineups. The Kansas City Chiefs, who addressed their most pressing need last week, got some positive early returns.
Wide receiver Josh Downs had a limited workload in Sunday's 35-13 drubbing of the Atlanta Falcons, but the former Indianapolis Colts standout made a huge impact. In a handful of key offensive snaps, his new team already received a glimpse of what he's capable of.
Head coach Andy Reid is encouraged by what he saw in Week 10, especially considering it's just the tip of the iceberg.
"Our new guy, Downs, it looks like there's a connection there," Reid said. "They worked well today, and that's on two days of practice. Look forward to incorporating him maybe a little bit more into the offense as we go along."
In all, Downs finished with five targets, four catches and 53 yards. He also scored his first touchdown as a Chief on a beautiful throw from quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Late in the first half, Mahomes saw Downs in a favorable position and gave his newest weapon a chance to capitalize:
Mahomes steps up and drops a dime to Josh Downs for a TD! KCvsATL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dwTMy1qZYC
Speaking to the media on Sunday afternoon, Mahomes walked through the sequence and tipped his cap to Downs for making his presence felt.
"Yeah, he kind of got matched up one-on-one with the nickel, and that was the play," Mahomes said. "Xavier (Worthy) did a great job of running that post route, grabbing the corner and bringing the safety with him, getting two guys. Before the corner could redirect back there, I gave him a chance to make a play one-on-one, and he made the play.
"Like you said, we haven't got a ton of reps, and that's why I think there are some times you're going to see on tape where he was open and I didn't give him chances. But whenever you do it in a game, those are are the best reps to get. I'll be able to have that trust as the season goes on."
While Downs didn't produce career-best volume stats, he managed to set two personal records elsewhere right out of the gate.
According to NFL Pro , Downs' 62.5% target rate on eight routes and his 7.6 yards per route run were both tops for his time in the league. He also ran each route from the slot, with the yardage total being his second-most from such an alignment in the 2026-27 campaign.
The 25-year-old has posted some gaudy numbers before, going for double-digit targets on six occasions since entering the league in 2023, and he's went for 100-plus yards twice. From an efficiency standpoint, though, this is the best he's ever fared in a single game.
Considering that Downs is weeks away from mastering the Chiefs' offense and was essentially flying by the seat of his pants on Sunday, it's hard not to think this was close to the best-case scenario. Mahomes, on the other hand, believes there was some meat left on the bone.
"I kind of said I think I need to do it even more," Mahomes said of trusting Downs. "It was earlier in that game I didn't trust him to win on a leverage that wasn't a great leverage for him, but he ended up winning. You see it on the tablet and you're like, 'Alright, he won.' So then later on that drive, the next drive, I threw it to him on a trust play like that.
"You get one-on-one, and you've got to let your guys go out there and make plays. He's here for a reason, and it's to make those plays, so I've got to trust him to go out there and make the play. He proved that he can do it."
If week one of the Downs era was any indication, this trade could shape up to be a heck of an in-season transaction .

title: Chargers’ Victory Lap at 1-8 Feels Hollow, Concerning for Future
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers picked up their first win of the season and the narratives have flowed, coursing through media in pretty predictable fashion.
Joe Hortiz, Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers have been overly concerned with messaging in the media this year, to the point one report even attempted to suggest that the failed Daiyan Henley trade was some sort of master plan to get draft picks for his departure , then re-sign him in free agency.
Next up is a note from NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , who suggested during a television appearance that the Chargers moving to 1-8 should be viewed as proof of what they’re building.
“And they did get validation with a win,” Rapoport said. “Perhaps they will get some more. But I really do wonder if just the good feeling in the locker room right there to show the players that what they are building is worth it was worth giving up on those late-round draft picks.”
There are problems with the idea, to say the least.
The Chargers aren’t mathematically eliminated from the playoffs, but they aren’t making the postseason, either.
That out of the way, there are some serious concerns with this idea that the Chargers suddenly have proof of the building concept.
There are other examples, but onlookers get the idea. It’s great for the players in the locker room to get a win and avoid the stigma of 0-17.
But what could be Rapoport echoing what the Chargers front office wants to put out through the grapevine here as a big sign of things to come is just misguided.
The cold reality is that what the Chargers put on tape through 10 weeks might not be good enough to win another single game, and the entire coaching staff and even Hortiz in the front office could be on the hot seat as soon as the season ends.
Tough spot, though. The Chargers could also be “right” and win a few more times, knock themselves out of the top-10 draft order and keep everything the same before doing it all again in 2027.
It should be mildly entertaining to watch and see which way it goes for the Chargers at least, right?

title: Mike McDaniel's Mistake: Why Omarion Hampton Should Be Chargers' Every-Down Back
full_text:
This should be obvious by now, but Omarion Hampton has shown enough to make a strong argument that he deserves to be the primary running back moving forward.
His performance against the Baltimore Ravens was another reminder of what he can bring to the offense when he is given the opportunity to take control of the backfield .
He looked comfortable handling the workload and demonstrated why his presence can make a difference
The biggest reason Hampton should become the main workhorse is that he has consistently shown the ability to make the most of extended playing time. A running back needs opportunities to find his rhythm, understand how the defense is attacking, and establish himself throughout a game. Giving
Hampton only a handful of touches does not necessarily allow him to display everything he can do. When he is involved throughout the contest, he has a much better chance to become a major part of the offensive game plan.
He is not simply a player who should be brought onto the field for a few specific situations. He has the ability to be involved on early downs, passing situations, and important moments when the offense needs someone to step up.
One of the most important things about developing a starting running back is allowing him to build consistency. It is difficult for any player to establish a rhythm when his opportunities constantly change. Hampton needs the opportunity to get comfortable and become the dependable centerpiece of the rushing attack. The more responsibility he receives, the more chances he has to demonstrate that he can handle different defensive looks and situations. There is also something valuable about having a running back who can bring physicality to an offense. Hampton has the kind of running style that can make defenders work for every tackle.
Another important factor is what happens when Hampton is allowed to play the majority of the game. His performances suggest that increased involvement benefits his overall effectiveness. Rather than constantly dividing the workload, the coaching staff should consider letting him establish himself as the primary option while using the other backs in supporting roles. That does not mean the other running backs should disappear from the offense. Having additional options is important, especially during a long season.
However, there should be a clear leader in the backfield and Hampton has earned a legitimate opportunity to fill that position. It’s not very common for a team to use three backs equally and have their production at its peak.
Omarion Hampton has played over 60% of the snaps twice this season - Week 2: 115 yds, TD - Week 10: 102 yds, TD

title: Chargers’ Jim Harbaugh Gets a Little Sean Payton, Jesse Minter Drama Amid First Win
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers ’ first win of the season wasn’t drama free for Jim Harbaugh’s club as they moved to 1-8 and surrendered the top pick in the NFL draft order .
There are levels to drama, of course. The weird NFL trade deadline mishap with Daiyan Henley is one example. That plays a role in this weird afterglow of the Chargers’ first win.
Harbaugh, of course, was his usual self regardless after the win.
"Just cherish this team. A lot of fight in this team," Harbaugh said after the win, according to Omar Navarro of Chargers.com. "Been seeing it. To come across the country, guys just battled, fought and made the plays, really in all three phases. Thrilled."
We’d be remiss not to mention, though, a few awkward things around Harbaugh before and after the game.
First, a note from Denver Broncos land.
Harbaugh was very critical of the Broncos this week after the failed deadline deal. He (and other teams, based on the speculation) have asked the NFL to close the “loophole” that prevents the backing out of deals and/or renegotiating deals even though the trade deadline has passed.
Broncos head coach Sean Payton had something to say about the matter on Monday.
“There’s no loophole,” Payton said, according to PFT’s Mike Florio . “It just is part of the trade process every step of the way.”
Maybe not a loophole by definition and it might be how trades have always worked, but that doesn’t mean the NFL will agree.
We’ll see if something changes after this problem popped up multiple times, as teams appearing to use alleged problems with physicals to negotiate better trade terms after an initial agreement and after a deadline seems like a big issue.
Just don’t expect to hear Harbaugh talking about this anymore, for the time being.
Here’s an odd one from after the game: We got a weird Jim Harbaugh and Jesse Minter exchange.
Onlookers wondering about the exchange after Monday’s game posted it all over social media:
Anyone else find this Harbaugh/Minter interaction weird? I'm assuming they talked pregame/that's just a classic Harbaugh postgame interaction. I wasn't aware of any beef between these two. pic.twitter.com/3IMRJdU5jS
Probably nothing. Harbaugh and Minter likely had all their fun exchanges before kickoff and kept it business after the game.
Still, not hard to see why fans are asking about it. Minter followed Harbaugh to Los Angeles and became a premier NFL coordinator before taking the head coaching gig in Baltimore. One would expect a little more here, perhaps.
Hardly a big deal in the grand scheme of things, considering the slog both teams are attempting to climb free of right now.

title: Chargers First Win Shakes up Draft Order: Latest Updates and Prospects to Know
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers finally won a game on Monday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens. The Chargers defense showed off their capabilities and held the Ravens to their third-lowest rushing total in franchise history and left Baltimore with a 23-20 victory.
The Chargers now hold a 1-8 record and have moved down the draft order behind the Tennessee Titans. The Chargers have eight games remaining on their schedule and will face a handful of the teams in the bottom ten of the NFL as well as multiple teams dealing with upheaval at the quarterback position including this upcoming week against the New York Jets after Geno Smith was knocked out of the game after taking a massive hit on Sunday.
The Chargers may end up drafting closer to pick five than pick one when all is said and done. Ohio State wide receiver and Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith is the presumptive favorite to go number one overall in the 2027 draft unless the team with the number one overall pick needs a quarterback like Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker.
If the Chargers keep winning, the dream of pairing Smith with Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers may be long gone. Smith may end up out of range for Los Angeles but there are several blue chip prospects that will be available in the top ten, let's run through some prospects to know.
Texas’ Colin Simmons is so explosive and flexible. Simmons had 26 pressures, 16 TFLs, and 10.5 sacks in the first six games of the season before his injury pic.twitter.com/ckFh8hoQbw
Colin Simmons is the best pass-rushing prospect in this upcoming draft class. He is twitchy and explosive coming off the edge. He is on the lighter side under 250 pounds but would provide the Chargers with the fastball and instant winner off the edge.
CHARLIE BECKER DOING HIS THING pic.twitter.com/6ozcy7nuXs
Indiana's Charlie Becker may be the best downfield receiver in this draft class. He has track speed and elite ball tracking. He does not have the versatility that Jeremiah Smith has but Becker is a reliable, speedy, boundary receiver who catches everything.
Leonard Moore! 🔒🔒🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/A69B514LSm
Notre Dame is absolutely loaded on defense and cornerback Leonard Moore is likely the top draft prospect for the Fighting Irish. Moore is big, fast and can cover. His only weakness is his open-field tackling can be inconsistent but he is capable of stepping in and going toe to toe against elite NFL receivers.
Tennessee DT Xavier Gilliam (#2) has been good all season, but the past two weeks have been a bloodbath. 3rd-year Soph who continues to rise 📈 Disruptive nose w/ the twitch and violent hands that give Byron Murphy II flashes. pic.twitter.com/S8gcZBzsLx
Xavier Gilliam burst onto the scene this season and began creating absolute chaos in the middle of Tennessee's defense. The NFL is prioritizing defensive tackles as we saw with the trades for Jeffery Simmons and Jordan Davis. A game-wrecking interior defensive lineman is highly valuable and Gilliam could be next.
Another week, another standout game for Georgia LB Chris Cole. Rare size/speed athlete with diverse range and nose for the ball. Cole entered 2026 as a top-25 draft pick, but he's playing like an NFL prospect who wants to go in the top-12 picks. pic.twitter.com/8bepi555c2
The NFL is starting to value linebackers again as offenses adapt to defenses living in light boxes to reduce explosive plays. Versatile linebackers and safeties are becoming mainstay figures in the best defenses around the NFL. Chris Cole is a monster athlete with incredible range.
Cole is a swiss army knife and can be used in a variety of ways, similar to current Washington Commanders rookie linebacker Sonny Styles. Cole currently has 60 tackles and five sacks on the year with 28 total pressures. With the Chargers gearing up for a rebuild of the linebacker room, a blue chip linebacker could be in the cards.
#Clemson DB Ashton Hampton has challenged wide receivers at the LOS and at the catch point consistently this season. Against Syracuse, had a couple of PBUs on passes downfield, and has the discipline to play through WRs hands without being called for a flag. Had an INT later in… pic.twitter.com/Wgty7gGDjs
The cornerback position has been exploding in value in recent years. The Chargers have two starting corners heading into 2027 but as the past few seasons have proven, they can never have too many. Clemson's Ashton Hampton is an enormous physical cornerback.
The Chargers may miss out on Jeremiah Smith but there are several blue chip prospects that will be available in the top ten. How many games the Chargers win this season will determine their draft slot, and how they look will determine if there are any offseason changes coming to the organization.

title: Chargers’ Win Sacrifices Top Spot in NFL Draft Order
full_text:
One only needs to see a single clip of the Los Angeles Chargers ’ locker room in the aftermath of the win over the Baltimore Ravens to know just how important a victory was for the guys on the team.
No disputing that, even if the win was a 23-20 road escape of a Ravens team in the middle of a nosedive without a starting quarterback. Shaking free of the 0-17 potential while moving to 1-8 while giving fans something to be happy about for the first time in almost a year is a really big deal.
But in the process, the Chargers also shook free of the top spot in the NFL draft order.
The question now is pretty simple: Does it matter?
A small shift, but one that could have big ramifications for the Chargers. They entered the week at No. 1. Now they’re down a spot:
Painting in extremely broad strokes, the move might not mean that much for the Chargers in the long run if the Tennessee Titans are hot after whatever quarterback emerges as No. 1 in the class. The Chargers will also play teams like the Jets and Dolphins later in the season.
The Chargers, after all, don’t need a quarterback. And while we’re on the topic, the list of needs is so extensive that one single draft pick in the top five isn’t going to dramatically turn around a team that has been so poorly constructed for a number of years.
And yet, there’s value beyond the obvious. Keeping the top pick in the order and leveraging it in a trade while playing multiple buyers against one another would create a landfall of draft picks and assets while trading down, for example.
Obviously, this is getting ahead of things a bit. We’ll have to see if the Chargers build on this on the field, or if it was a weird one-off against a team that might not win a game the rest of the season.
Either way, it’s a notable result that could have a serious domino effect on how well the Chargers can rebuild the roster around Herbert next offseason and beyond.

title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers Finally Get Their First Win, Defense Rises Up
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have finally finished a game and left Baltimore with their first win of the season on Monday Night Football. The Chargers were 0-8 heading into the game against their former defensive coordinator Jesse Minter and had been struggling on offense and struggling to find their identity.
It may only be one game, but the Chargers may have finally found their identity on offense. Los Angeles and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel kept his move to the booth to call plays and also seemed to make a few changes to the gameplan and reverse course on how they attacked with the run game.
McDaniel may have finally taken a page out of his mentor Kyle Shanahan's playbook or potentially Sean McVay's and changed up the run game. Second year running back Omarion Hampton, despite an early fumble that was not lost, ran very had and the gameplan kept him running downhill and attacking the Ravens second level.
Omarion Hampton finished the night with 22 carries and 105 yards on the ground. The volume of carries was the second most this season for Hampton and most since week two against the Las Vegas Raiders. McDaniel seemed to lean into designed runs and constant rotations at running back in the past six weeks, preventing Hampton from building confidence and building momentum, something critical for bigger bruising running backs.
Hampton also finished with four runs over 10 yards but more interestingly he had five more gap runs compared to zone. The Chargers ran just shy of 60 percent zone plays in their first eight games, against the Ravens, Hampton was significantly more gap-heavy but the offense in general with Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell ended up just over 50 percent gap run calls.
The run game was the big factor in this game, as was Justin Herbert appearing to be in control for most of the game and turned up his scrambling, leading to an opening-drive touchdown. Tre' Harris showed up big in the first half and Charlie Kolar appears to be Herbert's favorite outlet.
Los Angeles' defense stepped up when the lights were bright on Monday night. Ravens running back Derrick Henry finished with ten carries for ten yards but did get in the endzone twice. The Chargers held the Ravens to zero yards in the first half and the third-fewest rushing yards total in their franchise history.
The Ravens ran for 16 yards on 15 carries, which is the 3rd lowest rushing total they've had in a single game since 2000, per @TruMediaSports . The other 2: - 2005 Week 2 against the Titans: 14 yards on 13 carries - 2016 Week 7 against the Jets: 11 yards on 11 carries
After putting together valiant efforts throughout the losing streak only to be fighting an uphill battle from terrible field position, the defense showed what they could do when the offense and special teams didn't shoot themselves in the foot. The defense had their moment to shine as well. The Ravens had the ball, down by three and started moving down the field.
The Chargers defense kept the team in games for the most part all season. It was poetic they finished out the game when cornerback Tarheeb Still stripped the ball from Zay Flowers and safety Elijah Molden recovered. The moment felt reminiscent of the Chargers' Monday night win over the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025, the defense finished it.
The season is not over and the 2027 draft order is not set. The Chargers, with a win, have fallen from the top draft pick slot, down to the second. The Chargers will face most of the other teams at the bottom of the draft order including the Jets this upcoming week and the Dolphins just after Christmas.
The dreams of the Chargers landing Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith took a hit but the good news is that if the Chargers have their heart set on adding a wide receiver in the early rounds of the 2027 draft, there are multiple options to pick from.

title: Chargers Win Doesn't Clear the Hot Seat For Players and Coaches, as Questions Still Remain
full_text:
They actually did it. The Chargers finally have a victory to celebrate after defeating the Ravens on Monday Night Football.
However, not everyone in the building should be celebrating just yet. A long losing stretch exposed several weaknesses . Unfortunately one win does not automatically change the questions surrounding the coaching staff and veteran players.
Perhaps the biggest concern is that younger players are beginning to challenge established names for opportunities.
Harbaugh can breathe a little easier after finally getting a win, but his seat should not be considered completely safe. The team’s disappointing start created serious questions about preparation, consistency and overall direction.
The expectations were much higher than what this group delivered during its losing stretch. Harbaugh must demonstrate that he can get this roster moving in the right direction. One victory is encouraging, but another stretch of disappointing performances could bring the criticism right back.
Congratulations to Jim Harbaugh on his first win of the season. Tough loss for Jesse Minter, but heartwarming to see two coaches banned from college football in a pillow fight between the NFL’s two most disappointing teams.
McDaniel might have one of the most uncomfortable positions on the coaching staff. The offense has struggled to produce consistently, and the lack of results has placed additional attention on his play calling. The showing he put on during primetime was impressive compared to other matchups nonetheless.
The biggest problem is that the team has talent available but has not consistently turned that talent into production. With questions surrounding the passing attack and offensive line, McDaniel needs to show that his system can work on the regular.
Johnston is one of the players who should be watching the younger receivers closely. He entered the season with an opportunity to establish himself as a dependable contributor, but inconsistent production has kept questions surrounding his place in the offense.
Tre’ Harris is becoming an increasingly interesting alternative. His ability to take advantage of opportunities creates competition that Johnston cannot afford to ignore. Harris had a great outing against the Ravens, showing the skill that he truly has.
The organization needs receivers who consistently make plays, win contested opportunities and give Herbert dependable targets. Johnston has yet to prove that on a week to week basis.
Offensive line struggles have been a major issue, and his performance has already resulted in questions about whether another option could provide better results. That is not an encouraging sign for someone expected to provide stability in the middle of the offensive line.
Younger options such as Logan Taylor give the organization additional possibilities. If the protection problems continue, Strange could find himself losing more opportunities.
Chargers OC Mike McDaniel on RG Cole Strange's benching: "We see Cole as the starter but we have some players that have experience on the field that are chomping at his heels." "When his play is not as good as expectation or his standard, we have the ability to utilize our… pic.twitter.com/zqRZoJNeLz
Jackson is a well-respected, and at times elite cornerback in the Bolts locker room. Sadly, his play as of recently has been subpar at best. Recording some of his worst numbers of his career, Jackson could be declining at a faster rate than we thought.
He left Monday's game multiple times, adding on to the bad season he has been experiencing.
Younger players will eventually take over and some arguably already have. The veteran corner does have a lot left in the tank, but negative numbers and bad performances could become a bigger issue moving forward.

title: Chargers Players Rising, Falling After Week 10 Win, Season Turnaround Imminent?
full_text:
Now that the Los Angeles Chargers have finally gotten their first win of the 2026 NFL season, the team can find at least some solace in knowing they will not be the first team in NFL history to go winless in a 17-game NFL season.
Now at 1-8, the team has some players who contributed heavily to the Chargers' first win. Who are some guys to look forward to seeing as this lost season continues?
Tarheeb Still has been incredible for the majority of the 2026 season. With the team not being good enough for national media to give attention to the roster, Still has been a mainstay for this Chargers defense.
Tonight, Still helped spearhead the Chargers' defense, collecting four tackles, a pass deflection and a game-winning forced fumble. With a contract extension needed, Still has shown everyone during this primetime matchup why he deserves to stick around with the team.
In a game without Ladd McConkey and with Justin Herbert playing much better than in recent weeks, Quentin Johnston only had one catch for six yards. This came on his only target for the week.
Johnston has been very disappointing in 2026 , considering the hype he was building from his 2024 and 2025 seasons, seasons that showed some of the potential he had when the team drafted him in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft.
Omarion Hampton arguably was the biggest winner of the Chargers' victory, finally being given a real chance to be a starting running back who has the opportunity to find his rhythm in the offense. Even with a fumble early on (recovered by the Chargers), Hampton was spectacular.
His 22 carries for 105 yards is a 4.8 yards-per-carry average, which ranks as his second-best average of the season. The only other game with a higher average was his nine-carry, 45-yard (5 YPC) game back against the Seattle Seahawks. Hampton should continue to see a heavy workload going forward.
Even winning can be bittersweet at times, with many of the fans hoping for the Chargers to continue losing, ensuring that they can get a high draft pick that could be used on the likes of WR Jeremiah Smith or even EDGE Collin Simmons.
With this victory, the Bolts move to the second overall pick , with the Tennessee Titans moving up to number one overall. This is due to the Titans having a worse strength of schedule than the Bolts. The Chargers are also tied with the Miami Dolphins in record, with both of those teams playing later on in the year.
The final winner of this Chargers victory is defensive tackle Teair Tart. Even with Tart missing time during the game due to a few different injuries, he recorded two tackles, one of which for loss, a pass deflection and a QB hit. This also does not measure the multiple times that Tart timed the snap count perfectly and crashed the party that was a Ravens run play.
In large part due to Tart, the Ravens had 16 rushing yards on the night. Expect for Tart to continue being one of the league's most underrated defensive tackles moving forward.

title: Chargers Veteran Leader Forcefully Benched After Comments Attacking Front Office
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have been one of, if not the worst, teams in the entire NFL. With this continuous streak of losses, it will obviously bleed into the general vibe of the team's locker room, with the Bolts' locker room finally seeing some cracks begin to form.
These cracks go beyond the failed Daiyan Henley trade , a trade that facilitated one of the team's most beloved and well-respected defenders on the roster to the division rival, the Denver Broncos. It was coupled with one veteran speaking out.
On Nov. 13, 2026, The Athletic's Chargers beat reporter, Noah Furtado, shared a very good read into the team's view of the roster, with several quotes from general manager Joe Hortiz and players on the team. One of those quotes came from beloved locker room presence, 12-year veteran Bud Dupree .
Unprompted to the article itself, Dupree saw a group of media members standing by the locker room and said: "Don’t ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them.. Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull they cameras out and go upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them.”
Quite a damning quote on its own, but even more so coming from someone who has been around the league for a long time. Dupree has been on multiple teams, many of which had playoff success, giving his opinion to 'press' the front office even more validity.
On Nov. 16, 2026, the Chargers played their next game following the Dupree comments. Dupree, only listed on the injury report for one day of veteran rest, was not active for the Bolts game against the Baltimore Ravens. A game on Monday Night Football, a primetime matchup.
With a large audience watching, it seemed that Dupree was forced to sit out the game , likely due to a disciplinary reason stemming from his comments. This team has been notably obsessed with the media's opinion of them, and with Dupree giving the media ammunition to negatively change the wanted narrative around them, it gave the reason to sit the veteran in favor of young EDGE rushers Caleb Murphy and practice squad elevated player Myles Adams.
The Chargers are Dupree could be in for an ugly divorce if the team continues to lose football games, especially if the offense continues to be the main issue for such losses.

title: Is Ladd McConkey Playing Today? Chargers vs. Ravens Updates for Week 10
full_text:
The winless Los Angeles Chargers have Ladd McConkey injury concerns chasing them into the Monday night primetime game against the Baltimore Ravens.
There are other concerns, of course. The Chargers’ botched trade at the deadline has the front office spiraling while trying to do PR damage control . That’s a thing that is, in a word, difficult, considering the team is 0-8 and now star quarterback Justin Herbert will gut through an injury in a hopeless situation on the road Monday night.
But back to McConkey. Here’s a live-updating look at the latest on McConkey before the Chargers play the Ravens.
Ladd McConkey injury impact, Chargers fantasy football outlook
We recently wrote that it’s time for the Chargers to have uncomfortable Ladd McConkey conversations .
After the breakout rookie season, McConkey just hasn’t been able to stay healthy. This year alone, he’s had knee, calf rib, foot and now back issues, in addition to a concussion.
This obviously makes him a no-fly zone when it comes to fantasy football. But it’s worth wondering if he can keep making the "foundational building block” list when talking about the Chargers long-term, too.
As for fantasy football otherwise, the Chargers are a wasteland. McConkey has hardly played, yet still leads the team in receiving with 17 catches for 286 yards and one score. None of the other wideout options are a threat and the tight ends like Oronde Gadsden have no impact. David Njoku just got activated but doesn't figure to be a huge part of the game plan, either.
Even running back is a mess. Mike McDaniel oddly ignored former first-rounder Omarion Hampton early in the year. The former first-rounder averages just 3.6 yards per carry.
None of this is what anyone expected for a Herbert-McDaniel combo, but it’s become one of the most obvious must-avoids in fantasy football.

title: Rams May Have No Choice But to Turn to Justin Dedich After Latest Injuries
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have struggled with the injury bug all season and now will be managing injuries to the offensive line. On Monday night, the team announced that center Coleman Shelton would be out 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury and backup Dylan McMahon would be placed on injured reserve.
While the Rams have been managing injuries throughout the year, they have remained relatively healthy on the offensive line. With that said, the Rams already used a return designation on Justin Dedich to start the season.
Prior to the season, the Rams placed two key depth players on the offensive line on injured reserve. Justin Dedich injured his hand in a fireworks accident and Keagen Trost hurt his hamstring in the preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
When the Rams were without Alaric Jackson in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, the team took Trost off of injured reserve and added him to the active roster. However, despite some of their injuries, they have avoided doing the same with Dedich. With the added injuries to the interior of the offensive line, there has been some speculation that the Rams may look to bring Dedich to the active roster.
However, as the Rams enter the bye week, they are currently running out of potential injured reserve return designations. Teams are only allowed eight during the regular season and the Rams have already used half of those.
The Rams have used return designations on Keagen Trost, Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson, and Ronnie Rivers. They are projected to use return designations on Davante Adams, Puka Nacua, and Kobie Turner as well.
That would put the Rams at seven return designations used.
With that said, the Rams already previously used a return designation on Justin Dedich to start the season. Dedich was placed on injured reserve during roster cutdowns. Had Dedich been placed on regular injured reserve, he would have been done for the season without having the option to bring him back.
By using a return designation on Dedich, the Rams had the option to bring him back during the season once he got healthy. However, they also used one of their return designations. That would mean that the Rams are already out of IR return designations as they head into the back half of the season.
At this point, one potential reason Dedich hasn't returned to the roster is the lack of available roster spots. With Shelton hurt and McMahon on injured reserve, the Rams could use some interior depth even if they stick with Bill Murray. It makes sense at this point to bring Dedich up to the active roster.
That’s also likely a reason why the Rams haven’t placed Shelton on injured reserve. He is set to be out 4-6 weeks, but if they were to place him on injured reserve, he would be done for the season.
The Rams already activated Terrance Ferguson's 21-day practice window. If he were to not be brought back after those 21 days, that would still count as a lost designation. As it stands, the Rams would need to decide if they prefer another return designation or if it’s worth bringing back Adams, Turner, and Nacua.
It’s also why designating Ronnie Rivers off of injured reserve was so significant.The Rams used a return slot on their third-string running back who primarily plays special teams. That’s a role they likely could have replaced with Jordan Waters or another available running back on another team’s practice squad.
With the Rams now dealing with injuries to both Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon, bringing back Dedich should be a priority. The Rams used a return designation on Dedich before the season specifically to keep that option available. Now that the offensive line depth is being tested, it makes little sense to continue leaving him on injured reserve if he's healthy enough to contribute.
The Rams have been forced to make difficult roster decisions throughout the season because of injuries. However, those decisions are now beginning to catch up with them. With seven games remaining and several key players still working their way back from injuries, the Rams have left themselves with little flexibility.
