title: Under-the Radar Vikings WR Staring at a Golden Opportunity With Jordan Addison Hurt
full_text:
The Vikings may have dropped 30 points on the rival Packers in Kirk Cousins's return last weekend, but that doesn't mean the Purple and Gold's offensive issues have been solved. The wide receiver room still features more questions than answers, between Justin Jefferson's inconsistent usage, Jauan Jennings and Jordan Addison's injuries and the lack of production behind the top three WR options.
With a massive Sunday Night Football collision against the 49ers in the cards for Week 11, the Vikings will need all the help they can get from their wideouts. Although it's good to see Jennings trending in the right direction (h/t VikingzFanPage), he can't be fully trusted as the only reliable WR besides Jefferson. And can they really count on Myles Price to deliver back-to-back notable performances?
It's safe to say that Minnesota will need more bodies to step up against a San Francisco team averaging 31.2 points per game—second-best in the NFL. With that in mind, don't be surprised if the Vikings turn to a practice-squad option that's flying under the radar.
The trade deadline is behind us, meaning the practice squad and free agency are the Vikings' only paths for WR help . Head coach Kevin O'Connell might want to go with more familiar faces at this stage of the season, though, which could lead them to turn to undrafted rookie WR Dillon Bell.
Having just turned 23 earlier this month, Bell has been with Minnesota since April. He signed as a UDFA after the 2026 NFL Draft and eventually fought his way onto the 53-man roster. That only lasted a day, though, as he was cut before being re-signed to the taxi squad before Week 1 .
Bell has now had almost three months to develop and learn from the veterans and coaching staff around him. The Vikings clearly liked him enough to use a practice squad spot on him, and now it's time to see what he's made of—especially when the other options have proven to be futile.
Odell Beckham Jr.'s best days are clearly behind him, as he's recorded zero catches in four games played between the Giants and Vikings. Meanwhile, Jeshaun Jones only has a 32-yard catch in three appearances and has suited up just once since Week 5, as Minnesota has run out of elevations for him and would be forced to sign him to the 53-man roster.
Given that Beckham is slow and Jones isn't worth the 53-man roster spot, there's no reason not to roll the dice on Bell, who only saw three special teams snaps in his lone appearance (Week 2 vs. Bears). The preseason was a good indication of what he can do, catching seven of his 16 targets for 59 receiving yards (including 28 after the catch) and four first downs. Perhaps he could've been more productive if the Vikings had received better QB performances this summer (h/t Vikings on SI's Jason Harmon).
Poor Dillon Bell…. pic.twitter.com/KyNF9urLYv
Any UDFA signed to the practice squad is bound to be viewed as a project, but eventually it's time to see if the patience was worth it. That's the situation the Vikings currently find themselves in with Bell, who could see his first action since September because of Addison's absence. We already saw the positive impact that Cousins's presence had on Price, who tallied a career-high 49 receiving yards and his first-ever touchdown last weekend.
Could the Cousins effect lead to similar success for Bell? Maybe, maybe not; however, the only way to find out will be for the Vikings to throw the rookie wide receiver into the fire this weekend.

title: Kevin O’Connell Just Put More Heat on Jauan Jennings to End Rut Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers
full_text:
Your 7-2 Vikings have been through quite the November gauntlet, battling some of the league’s best teams. After going 1-2 against the Lions, Bills, and Packers, the Vikings will look to split a brutal four-game stretch by defeating the top-seeded 49ers in Mexico City this Sunday .
One Viking who’ll be especially motivated? Wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who signed with the team this past offseason after spending the first six years of his career in San Francisco.
After a slow start to his 2026 campaign, head coach Kevin O’Connell is expecting a big showing from Jennings against his former squad. With the team’s number-two receiver sidelined and a new quarterback throwing him passes, Jennings may be poised for a big game this weekend.
The Vikings announced Monday that wide receiver Jordan Addison would miss time after thumb surgery. Addison had been nursing the injury since camp, but a freak accident at Friday’s practice caused further complications. Now, it’s up to Jennings to step in during Addison’s absence, assuming he’s fully recovered from the calf injury that sidelined him for the last two weeks.
Kevin O’Connell joined local Twin Cities radio station KFAN 100.3 to discuss the upcoming matchup and what it means specifically for Jennings, emphasizing the need for him to step up .
#Vikings HC Kevin O’Connell on Jauan Jennings’ revenge game vs the #49ers : “With us being down Jordan Addison, we’re gonna need him to make some plays in the pass game.” (Via @KFAN1003 ) pic.twitter.com/BOjGi3HeuY
An international game against one of the league's best teams isn't exactly the ideal time to lose your WR2, but for Jennings in particular, Addison’s absence may offer the perfect chance to salvage a challenging season.
To say Jennings has had a rough start to his Vikings tenure would be a massive understatement. In six games, he’s brought in only six receptions for 54 yards and no touchdowns. Even though he was mainly signed for his run-blocking ability, no one involved could have expected his pass-catching production to be this frustrating.
Needless to say, the Vikings' quarterback woes haven't helped Jennings’s situation. Any all-22 viewing session repeatedly showcased Jennings getting open downfield, with Kyler Murray in particular simply not seeing him uncovered.
Kyler Murray's 35-yard run yesterday was great, and the #Vikings eventually scored a TD on the drive But... Before crossing the line of scrimmage, he missed a chance to throw to a WIDE OPEN Jauan Jennings for an easy TD pic.twitter.com/5a6CTK1Rdt
The 49ers and Vikings had even agreed to terms on a trade that would have sent Jennings back to San Francisco , but Jennings made it clear he wanted to stay in Minnesota despite the early struggles. Now, that decision may pay off, especially with Kirk Cousins taking over at QB and elevating the passing game to a level not seen in the past two seasons.
If Jennings wants to turn his 2026 fortunes around, Sunday’s primetime matchup against his former team is the best possible opportunity.

title: Vikings' Recent Late-Round Draft Success Generates Mixed Kwesi Adofo-Mensah Feelings
full_text:
The Vikings are 7-2 after one of the wildest ten-week spans imaginable to start an NFL season. The defense? Dominant. The offense? Dormant. The solution? Kirk Cousins. Needless to say, it’s been quite the ride.
The team has relied heavily on defensive stars like Andrew Van Ginkel and Blake Cashman, but one major reason for such an impressive start is the high-upside young players who are starting to step up. Interestingly enough, many of these late-round gems were drafted by a general manager the team fired 10 months ago .
With championship aspirations and a newly hired general manager in Nolan Teasley, there are fair questions to ask about the legacy that ex-GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah left behind.
Were the Vikings too quick to part ways with their former GM? Were the accusations that he “couldn’t draft” fair? Does he deserve credit for the success of the 2026 Vikings? The answers are a bit murky, but it seems he certainly left some gifts on his way out.
The NFL Draft is an inexact science, but it’s typically safe to assume that players selected in later rounds will have a significantly harder path to contributing consistently at the professional level. Ironically, the Vikings are seeing almost the exact opposite scenario play out for many of their young contributors. 2024 17th overall pick, Dallas Turner, has been one of the most impressive defenders in the NFL this season, but he wasn't the only star Adofo-Mensah and his staff found in that class.
Defensive tackle Levi-Drake Rodriguez may be one of the best stories in the entire NFL. After playing football and baseball at Southwestern Assemblies of God University, Rodriguez transferred to Texas A&M University–Commerce in 2022. The big man was the definition of a draft day underdog. But Adofo-Mensah, former assistant GM Ryan Grigson, and defensive coordinator Brian Flores liked what they saw and ultimately took a swing at pick 232.
Two years later, Rodriguez is starting at defensive tackle and has already recorded three sacks this season.
Vikings DT Levi Drake Rodriguez was unbelievably good on Sunday. 93.3 PFF grade. 8 pressures, 2 sacks on 24 pass-rush snaps. The former 232nd overall pick out of Texas A&M-Commerce has become a key part of this defense. pic.twitter.com/zUuEeaDKXj
There’s also Will Reichard, who was selected with the 203rd pick in the same draft. Reichard has become one of the league’s top kickers and is currently second in the NFL with 23 successful kicks this season. It turns out Adofo-Mensah may have solved one of the most frustrating positions in Vikings franchise history.
The 2025 class also has a few names that are starting to make some noise. Former Maryland wide receiver Tai Felton was selected 102nd overall in 2025, and while he may not be a true “late-rounder,” he certainly had his work cut out for him in a stacked wide receiver room. Now, he’s starting to show signs of potential, especially with Jauan Jennings and Jordan Addison missing time . A strong camp and preseason are setting Felton up for a growing role.
Cousins to Tai Felton gets the Vikings near the goal line on another 3rd and long conversion MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/T9zCEvmP3W
Defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins is another name Vikings fans are hearing more often. The former defensive tackle shifted outside this past offseason, slimming down along the way. He’s appeared in only three games this season and has battled through injury, but he’s proven disruptive in limited opportunities.
The Vikings’ final pick of the 2025 draft was tight end Gavin Bartholomew, who missed his entire rookie season with a lower back injury. One season later, the former Pitt Panther is starting to make waves. With T.J. Hockenson out against the Packers on Sunday, Bartholomew and Kirk Cousins quickly became friends as the second-year tight end caught three passes for 36 yards and his first NFL TD.
Kirk Cousins to Gavin Bartholomew for the TD pic.twitter.com/g1YUgVp8nr
For a team that has long battled through serious depth concerns, the emergence of young talent from later portions of the draft is a promising sign of what’s to come. But it doesn’t change many of the key reasons Adofo-Mensah was ultimately fired.
The Kwesi Adofo-Mensah era will ultimately be defined by much more than the success of his late-round draft selections. The fact that zero players remain on the roster from his 2022 draft class is a massive indictment. The 2023 class was not much better, as Jordan Addison and Jay Ward are the last remaining members of the six-player class. Then there’s the quarterback situation, which has been broken down ad nauseam.
Without an answer at the most important position in sports, and with little help from his first two draft classes, the resulting breakup seemed inevitable. At the same time, the Vikings’ former GM and his staff certainly didn’t leave Vikings fans empty-handed with some of his value selections.
For that, he deserves great credit.

title: Not Trading Ivan Pace Jr. at the Deadline Is Proving to Be a Genius Vikings Move
full_text:
This has been an interesting season for Vikings linebacker Ivan Pace Jr., to say the least.
Pace lost his starting job to Eric Wilson last season and appeared to be replaced when the team selected Jake Golday in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. While he looked to be expendable , the Vikings kept the 25-year-old defender through the final cuts to make the 53-man roster
Still, he looked like an even bigger afterthought after averaging just 8.4 defensive snaps in the first seven games of the 2026 season. No one would've blamed the Vikings if they traded Pace away, as it'd give the veteran a much-needed fresh start while opening more playing time for an up-and-coming defender.
Instead of a trade, Minnesota retained him at the deadline. It hasn't taken long for that move to look like a genius play by general manager Nolan Teasley and head coach Kevin O'Connell.
Pace is seeing more action on special teams than on defense this season, but having him available as depth while he fills a need on special teams has paid off in a big way for the Purple and Gold this season.
For the first time this season, Pace played more defensive snaps than special teams reps against the Packers in Week 10. He was in for a total of 57 plays against Green Bay, with 42 of those coming on defense.
As of Week 11, Pace has earned a 64.5 Pro Football Focus grade , as well as a 90.5 pass-rush grade, generating eight pressures and getting two sacks while blitzing. He has been a valuable defender to rotate in on defense or fill in when injuries keep a starter out of the lineup.
Ivan Pace Jr. brings the pressure 💥 📺 Watch live on @NFLonDAZN , @SkySports and @talkSPORT pic.twitter.com/O7XREgogYK
Starting linebacker Blake Cashman missed Week 10 with a concussion, and it is hard to know when a player will return from that kind of injury. Additionally, Andrew Van Ginkel is banged up with a quad injury after Sunday's victory. Having Pace ready to step in is a huge benefit in defensive coordinator Brian Flores's system.
Minnesota could have used Pace as a trade asset this season. Quite a few teams around the league could use an inside linebacker with his pass-rush skills, but the Vikings opted to keep him and are now benefiting from that decision. He is one of the 19 unrestricted free agents the Vikings will have to make decisions on in March, though, so it's hard to see how much longer he'll be around.
The Vikings are still using the fourth-year defender on special teams while having Pace fill in on defense when needed, so he is earning his roster spot. Minnesota's front office and coaching staff are showing foresight by keeping the team prepared for injuries, and Pace has risen to the occasion.
Now that the Vikings are being seen as serious contenders this season, having solid depth and youth at key positions could go a long way to ensure that Minnesota is prepared for any hardship that might come its way.
We'll see what kind of role Pace will play down the stretch, especially if LB-related injuries remain an obstacle.

title: Vikings Verdict Week 11: Judging Cousins's Return, Addison's Injury & More Overreactions Ahead of 49ers Clash
full_text:
And just like that, the Vikings are back on track.
A dominant win over Green Bay has Minnesota looking like a Super Bowl-caliber team . It's safe to say that there's nobody in the league who wants to see the Vikings on the schedule right now.
But has the addition of Kirk Cousins made this team unstoppable? Is Jordan Addison's injury really not that big of a deal?
Let's dive into those Vikings overreactions and more ahead of the Week 11 Sunday Night Football showdown against the 49ers.
Despite having only a few days to prepare, Cousins led the Vikings to a 30-10 dismantling of the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. His numbers—207 yards and two touchdowns to one interception—won't jump off the page, but the rhythm and consistency the offense experienced can't be overstated.
The defense got to Jordan Love eight times and forced four turnovers, but as incredible as their performance was, it's actually pretty easy to envision Carson Wentz losing this game. The Vikings' offense under Cousins held the ball for 35 minutes against the Packers. Compare that to the 41 minutes of possession combined over the last two losses before his arrival.
Gavin Bartholomew's first NFL TD makes it a three-score game! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LlozbGAGyJ
It certainly doesn't feel out of line to say that the 38-year-old Cousins took this team to a level they wouldn't reach otherwise. This was still probably a 10- or 11-win team thanks to their suffocating defense, but the Vikings are real contenders now with a guy who can make the plays an average quarterback should make.
On Monday, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced (h/t MicNuggets) that Addison's thumb injury will require surgery, effectively knocking him out for at least a few weeks . Obviously, it's not ideal to lose the No. 2 receiver just as a new quarterback enters the fold, but at the same time, things may not be all doom and gloom either.
Jordan Addison is likely a short-term IR candidate after aggravating a thumb injury Kevin O'Connell: “Just on Jordan Addison, tried to see if we could get him all the way to game day and see if we could possibly have him yesterday. But he did sustain a thumb injury, actually a… pic.twitter.com/emDjOFc7dn
Cousins clearly showed that he and Justin Jefferson still have a special connection after the two linked up nine times against Green Bay, and both Jauan Jennings and T.J. Hockenson should return to the lineup next week.
Jennings certainly hasn't lived up to expectations , but Cousins has a strong bond with Hockenson, and the pair has connected for 113 receptions for 997 yards over their 18 games together.
Losing Addison certainly hurts, as there's no question the offense is better with him on the field despite his modest 18 catches this season. At the same time, let's not forget what Cousins was doing in Las Vegas with Brock Bowers and a collection of unheralded wide receivers.
The Vikings' defense is the NFL's boogeyman, and the dark, shadowy figure at the center of all the fear is defensive coordinator Brian Flores.
Any way you slice it, the Vikings' defense ranks in the top five for most major metrics, and there's yet to be an offense that has figured them out. With such dominance, Flores figures to be one of the hottest names in next year's coaching carousel, but is he a goner for sure?
On paper, there's no reason Flores wouldn't get another shot at being a head coach, but reality is also a thing we deal with here on Earth, and the Vikings' defensive coordinator sits in a complicated situation. His current lawsuit with the league and controversial coaching methods in Miami make things complex, and his best option seems to be off the table already.
Many fans have called for Flores to be promoted to O'Connell's position, but after the win at Green Bay that included ownership presenting the head coach with a game ball, there's almost a zero percent chance the Vikings are moving on. Minnesota should throw every last penny they can offer at Flores in the offseason to retain him as defensive coordinator, but another team could still opt to make him their next head coach.
Flores' standing with the Vikings for 2026 is very much up in the air, and it's likely why the Vikings have waited to extend stars like Blake Cashman or Andrew Van Ginkel before they know who will be running the show.

title: Jordan Addison Injury News Will Likely Impact This Vikings Trio the Most
full_text:
The 2026 Vikings offense may have finally taken its first stride toward success in a promising performance against the Packers on Sunday, but Monday brought news that could delay our chance to see the unit at its full potential.
Jordan Addison was questionable heading into Sunday’s game with a thumb injury and was ultimately sidelined after testing the injury pregame. On Monday, head coach Kevin O’Connell shared that Addison will miss time after having the thumb surgically repaired .
Jordan Addison is likely a short-term IR candidate after aggravating a thumb injury Kevin O'Connell: “Just on Jordan Addison, tried to see if we could get him all the way to game day and see if we could possibly have him yesterday. But he did sustain a thumb injury, actually a… pic.twitter.com/emDjOFc7dn
While the news is certainly less than ideal with a matchup against the top-seeded 49ers approaching this week, three Vikings in particular will have a chance to prove themselves through the adversity.
Justin Jefferson is fresh off a season-high nine receptions without his main sidekick against the Packers, proving he can still take over games on his own when needed. Now, with Addison out for the next few weeks, Jefferson’s situation gets a bit complicated.
The Kirk Cousins to Justin Jefferson connection is so back MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VKdh3yVImv
It's safe to assume Jefferson will continue to get looks, especially now that his old friend Kirk Cousins is back under center, but Addison’s absence will allow defenses to focus more on number eighteen. I expect to see more double and even triple coverage against one of the best wideouts in the NFL.
The good news? We’ve seen Jefferson make plenty of spectacular catches in tight coverage before. He’ll certainly get more chances in the coming weeks.
One thought kept running through my mind after Sunday’s game in Green Bay: “Imagine what Cousins will be able to do once Addison is back!” Well, looks like we’ll have to wait a while longer to see what that looks like. The good news is Cousins seemed ready to rock in his return to the Vikings, even without one of his best weapons.
8️⃣ ball pic.twitter.com/2MVUeWF0zl
Cousins was decisive, finding eight different pass catchers during his first game back in purple on Sunday. Most impressively, Jefferson was the only one Cousins had played with before this week. After only a couple of practices, Cousins proved he’s willing to get the ball to his new teammates, which may be good news for one young receiver in particular.
Was Sunday the breakout performance for Myles Price ?
The second-year undrafted free agent has already proven his value as a kick and punt returner, but his performance this past weekend on offense was certainly eye-opening. With both Addison and Jauan Jennings sidelined, Price saw a career high in receptions (four), receiving yards (49), and his first NFL receiving TD.
Kirk Cousins with a dot to Myles Price for the TD! pic.twitter.com/LDWKjEjR9V
While these stats aren’t exactly jaw-dropping, it's clear Price’s speed and versatility could benefit the Vikings' offense. While Jennings will likely take the WR2 spot upon his return, I’d expect Price to get more looks with Addison recovering. If he continues to impress, he may prove to be another useful offensive weapon even after Addison's return.

title: What the Sudden Jordan Addison Injury News Means for the Vikings Moving Forward
full_text:
After popping up on the Vikings' injury report with a thumb injury late in the week, Jordan Addison missed Sunday's Packers game, and the news following the win isn't promising.
Kevin O'Connell told reporters on Monday that Addison's thumb injury will require surgery (h/t Alec Lewis of The Athletic ), knocking the star receiver out for at least a few weeks. The expectation is that Addison could land on short-term injured reserve, meaning he'll miss a minimum of four games.
The sudden news deserves one star and two enthusiastic thumbs down, as Kirk Cousins and the Vikings will now be forced to navigate life without their No. 2 weapon.
Against Green Bay, Cousins showed he can work with very little when Addison, Jauan Jennings, and T.J. Hockenson all sat, but losing Addison for the foreseeable future will be a tough hurdle for the offense to overcome as Cousins continues to settle into the system. Luckily, O'Connell also mentioned on Monday that he expects both Jennings and Hockenson to return this week against San Francisco.
And in the least surprising take of the century, the Vikings will now lean heavily on Justin Jefferson and hope Jennings becomes the receiver they hoped he would be when signing him this spring. Jefferson saw season-highs in both targets and receptions in his first game with Cousins, and that duo will need to be even more in sync now. But while Jefferson's outlook looks its brightest in years, Addison's injury makes one big decision even more difficult.
Addison's production has dropped in each year since his standout rookie season, and now, with the missed time coming up, the Vikings' offseason decision to extend him (or not) won't be so clear.
Inside the Vikings building, Addison is well liked, and his potential as one of the best No. 2 receivers in football is still very much in play. But now, with a recent thumb injury, Addison will see his catches, yards, and possibly touchdowns drop in three straight seasons.
Obviously, the injury isn't his fault. But without the next three or four games on tape, Nolan Teasley and company will be forced to base their decision on previous versions of their receiver unless they opt to let Addison play out his fifth-year option without a deal.
Jefferson has a cap hit of nearly $50 million dollars on 2027, and while Addison has seen his production fall, he's still a candidate for a $100 million deal himself based on his potential alone. He'll be just 25 next season, and the Vikings will likely be very tempted to pay two receivers top dollar despite the laundry list of other free agents.
Blake Cashman, Andrew Van Ginkel, Jalen Redmond, and more will be looking to get paid as well, so somebody will end up heading elsewhere. Could it be Addison? His slow start and unfortunate injury haven't helped his case, but neither Tai Felton nor Myles Price look to be ready for a WR2 role either.
Ideally, Addison can return quickly and show the Vikings why he deserves to be paid next year.

title: Harmon’s Vikings Longship Week 10: 4 Pressing Thoughts After Season-Saving Win vs. Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, W.I. — Vikings fans have certainly been on an emotional roller coaster through the first ten weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
From being the NFL’s last undefeated team after a 6-0 start, to watching two great defensive efforts be wasted by terrible quarterback play, then reacquiring Kirk Cousins , the last two months have been a ride. Sunday marked a fork in the road, a chance for Minnesota to reestablish its identity against its most bitter rival.
With a unique mix of uncertainty and optimism, the Vikings set sail for what would become a season-defining 30-10 victory over the Packers.
It’s fair to say there were more questions than ever heading into Sunday’s Border Battle, as the Vikings were missing one of their best defenders, linebacker Blake Cashman, and two offensive weapons, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Cousins’s job would be hard enough after only a couple of days of practice, but the injury report certainly didn’t help.
One thing was clear: this would be a perfect “prove it” moment for Cousins and the Vikings.
While Cousins’s stat line was less flashy than many past performances Vikings fans are used to, this may rank as the most impressive day of his career. Cousins finished with a hard-fought 207 passing yards and two TDs. Impressively, both came to pass catchers he had never thrown to before this week: Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew.
To come in and take control of the offense in less than a week is an incredible feat after spending the last two and a half seasons away from head coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense.
What a difference a week can make. pic.twitter.com/GfiRVSc4d0
As great as Cousins was, this was another day decided by defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit. The pass rush racked up an incredible eight sacks, the highest total by any team in the 2026 season. Their 37 sacks for the year now lead the entire NFL, while star outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel’s 8.5 sacks for the season are the second-most in the league.
The Packers were certainly feeling confident after their 45-point showing last week, but they left Sunday’s game with only 10 points on the board.
Safe to say Flores can ruin your mood in a hurry.
This likely won’t come as a shock, but it seems that simply adding a steady, competent QB may have been exactly what the Vikings needed to prove what they can do. Sunday’s showing previewed what could be possible once Cousins gets more comfortable in the offense.
Oh, and did I mention he was missing two of his top three pass-catchers? I feel like that’s important…
With a defense that continues to prove why it was worthy of general manager Nolan Teasley’s trade-deadline urgency, the sky truly is the limit once things start to click. Sunday represented an imperfect but hope-inspiring look into what Vikings fans everywhere hope to see in January.
An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq
I feel confident saying that the eventual NFC champion will have a distinct advantage in the Super Bowl. That is, if they aren’t too bloody and bruised from the path to get there. The conference is a beast, and the NFC North is a particularly terrifying gauntlet.
With the Bears on their bye week, the Lions kicked off Sunday’s festivities with a 35-10 win against the Patriots in Munich, but suffered greatly from the loss of star defender Aidan Hutchinson. Initial reports indicate that he may have torn his ACL while celebrating a sack.
From @GMFB : #Patriots QB Drake Maye could be lost for the season with a lower leg injury, while #Lions edge Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending knee injury, likely a torn ACL. pic.twitter.com/yBvpbU5g30
The Lions now leap into the top spot in the NFC North while the Vikings leapfrog the dormant Bears for second place. If the season ended today, the fifth-seed Vikings would travel to Charlotte to face the fourth-seed Panthers in the playoffs.
Luckily, there is still a lot of football left to earn back the NFC North title and a home playoff game at U.S. Bank Stadium, starting with a trip across the border.
The Vikings will head south next weekend for a primetime international matchup in Mexico City. Their opponent is their toughest conference challenge: the top-seeded 49ers.
The 49ers and Cowboys battled in an absolute shootout on Sunday, as San Francisco left Dallas with a 46-40 victory. The 49ers have been the clear favorite in the NFC this season, overcoming injuries to put together one of the most consistent and disciplined squads.
BROCK TO CMC OH MY SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JoKDvzWC3K
If the Vikings want to prove they now have all the tools needed to contend with the best, Sunday’s Mexico matchup is their best opportunity.

title: Expanding Myles Price’s Role Will Be in Vikings' Best Interest Moving Forward
full_text:
Week 10 sent the Vikings to Green Bay to face off against the Packers in an important NFC North showdown. It was also an opportunity for the Purple and Gold to rebound after a humbling defeat to the Bills on Monday Night Football.
Several factors weren't working in Minnesota's favor. The Vikings' starting quarterback, Kirk Cousins, arrived through a trade earlier in the week and had less than a week to prepare for the game. Not only that, but two wide receivers—Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings—missed the game due to injury.
With Addison and Jennings sidelined, second-year WR Myles Price stepped up to help the Vikings achieve a 30-10 victory over their rival . Price caught all four targets for 49 yards and a touchdown while adding one rushing attempt for 12 yards, giving him 61 of Minnesota's 312 offensive yards.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
Considering how the Vikings' WR depth behind Justin Jefferson has left much to be desired this season, it's in head coach Kevin O'Connell & Co.'s best interest to keep feeding Price the ball moving forward.
Heading into Sunday's game against the Packers, Price had been mostly used on special teams as a return specialist. He had only played 90 offensive snaps in the team's first eight games, and 29 of those came against the Bills last week, finishing with a six-yard catch on four targets.
Price played a season-high 33 offensive snaps on Sunday (four more than in Week 9) and got five touches on those opportunities. It was obvious that Jefferson would lead the wide receivers in snaps, but it was surprising that Tai Felton saw more offensive reps than Price.
Felton played all but 10 offensive snaps for Minnesota, participating in 59 plays. He was targeted more than Price, catching three of five passes for 33 yards. Considering Addison and Jennings were out, it was nice to see Felton step up, even if he was outplayed by Price.
O'Connell may need to re-evaluate his wide receiver room if Cousins develops a rapport with Price. Having him as the fifth wide receiver on the depth chart seems unreasonable if he can be more productive than the players above him. For reference, Addison has finished with 27 or fewer yards in five of his seven appearances, while Jennings has 54 receiving yards on the season.
That doesn't mean Price shouldn't continue as the team's return specialist, but it does mean that he could be ready to do more for Minnesota. The Vikings are used to rostering specialists who can contribute offensively, such as Cordarrelle Patterson and Percy Harvin.
Price may not have the pedigree of Harvin or Patterson, but he seems to rise to the occasion when given opportunities. Against the Packers, he played less than half of the team's offensive snaps, finished second in receiving yards, and found the end zone.
If given more chances, what else could the 24-year-old accomplish with the Vikings? We'll find out on Sunday Night Football in Week 11 against the 49ers, who allowed 343 receiving yards and five TDs on 30 catches in their 46-40 win against the Cowboys over the weekend.

title: Should We Give Up On the 2026 Patriots?
full_text:
What is there to look forward to for the rest of this season for New England Patriots fans? Truthfully, not much. But there are places where the Patriots can find success, and maybe even a playoff birth this season.
After what many are describing as a "Super Bowl hangover," the New England Patriots sit at 5-5 entering their bye week.
Losing half the amount of games in the first 10 weeks of play isn't what fans drew up for a team that lost just three regular season games and ran through the AFC playoffs. But there have been flashes of brightness, and despite a major setback, not all hope is lost for the Patriots.
Quarterback Drake Maye's injury during Week 10's game against the Lions is what has most people in New England ready to call it quits on the 2026 season.
Maye, whose ankle was fractured while being sacked on the final play of the drive , was ruled out indefinitely and reports say that he could miss extended time and potentially, the rest of the season.
Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito's performance on Sunday didn't give Patriots fans much to believe in either, as the fourth-year player completed 50% of his passes for 81 yards, as well as a touchdown and an interception.
While speculation remains about whether the Patriots stick with DeVito, switch to seventh-round pick Behren Morton, or look elsewhere for their starting quarterback , fans should pump the breaks at calling this team 'broken.'
There's no reason to have faith in DeVito as a backup quarterback yet. But if he can collect a few wins while Maye is recovering , then the Patriots stand a chance at earning a Wild Card spot.
Yes, you heard that correctly: while Maye is recovering. There is a very real chance that Maye plays football again this season. Though reports indicated Maye could be out for the rest of the season, the same insiders making these claims said that both Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson would miss extended time with separate injuries that caused neither of the two to miss game action.
The skepticism behind the reports that Maye's injury is season-ending should be discussed more when evaluating the near future of this Patriots team.
Currently, the Patriots are sitting one game back from the seventh seed in the AFC playoffs. New England has seven games to play in the 2026 season, with a majority of those games against teams with a winning record.
The biggest competitors for the Patriots spot in the playoffs are the Clevleand Browns (6-4) and the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6).
Cleveland has proven to be a challenging team to get through, but each of their wins this season has come in a one-score game. This should indicate that their legitimacy to contend for a playoff spot is overvalued. They could drop more than half of their remaining schedule, which includes to games against the Bengals and a trip to New Jersey to face the Giants.
🏈AFC Playoff Picture through Week 10!🏈 Is your team gonna make the playoffs? pic.twitter.com/3thecJox41
The Raiders, aren't as much of a concern for the Patriots, after New England dominated Las Vegas in Week 5 . This head-to-head victory for the Pats helps break a tie if the two teams find themselves in one. Las Vegas and New England will both play one of the best divisions in football in the reamining weeks of the season, but Vegas has to face the AFC West one additional time, compared to the three matches slated for the Patriots.
Realistically, New England should hope to win four of the last seven games to squeak into the playoffs. Finishing with a 9-8 record would allow the Patriots to secure a Wild Card spot and their second straight trip to the postseason. This record is commonly seen with seven seeded teams in the AFC.
Houston will also pose a threat to the final Wild Card spot, despite winning just three games this season. Last year, the Texans went on a large win streak to secure a playoff spot after a poor start to the season.
The familiarity of rooting for a tank is all too recent in the memory of Patriots fans, who watched back-to-back seasons where New England earned top-four picks in the NFL Draft.
Unfortunately, five wins is most likely too many for a pick that high, but New England could still end up close to the top 10 if they continue playing like they have over the past two weeks.
In the trade for A.J. Brown, the Patriots gave up a 2028 first-round pick instead of their first-round pick from this upcoming draft.
Mike Vrabel isn't the type of coach to tank for a draft pick. He build his idenitity on believing in the players that show up to the Patriots facility on day one of training camp.
The vibes in the Patriots building are “not good” Per: @DanGrazianoESPN He describes it as a “total Meltdown”. - ESPN insider @JFowlerESPN notes “Mike Vrabel is known for culture-building and tough-minded defense, and cracks in the foundation are showing on both fronts.” pic.twitter.com/CkzMiJhUqV
For this reason, it's unlikely that the Patriots will intentionally lose games, or put themselves in position to lose games, in favor of a better draft position.
However, if the Patriots don't make the playoffs, they'll likely miss it by a small margin (unless they completely collapse for the remainder of the season), which would put them in a difficult position, drafting in the late teens (where the not good enough, but not bad enough teams end up).
After the buy-in the front-office exercised this offseason, it's playoffs or bust for the Pats, whether or not Maye is their quarterback.

title: Is Drake Maye Coming Back This Year? Patriots Teammate Doesn't Think So
full_text:
The outlook for Drake Maye doesn't look great, and a fellow New England Patriots captain certainly didn't help.
Kevin Byard, who was voted a captain alongside Maye in his first season with the Patriots, was speaking on WEEI's Rich & Ken Tuesday and was asked about players stepping up in the wake of several major injuries across the board.
He mentioned how that's the reality of the situation the Patriots are in, and also offered some information about Maye's potential timeline.
"Like at the end of the day, our quarterback's out. He's probably going to be out for the rest of the season. And the reality of the situation is, is that we're going to have to get behind Tommy Two Chains (Tommy DeVito) at the end of the day," Byard said. "And you know, we're all going to have to do more, myself included. Everybody has to play better around our quarterback.
"I mean, this is honestly before Drake was injured as well. But we got to play better around our quarterback. We got two choices: we can rally behind this guy or we can pack it up. I mean, that's just where we're at right now in the season."
The Patriots haven't offered any additional comments about Maye's ankle, which was injured in the first quarter of Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions. Maye was sacked by Aidan Hutchinson — who tore his ACL celebrating the play — and would head to the locker room after a short time on the sideline.
DeVito came in to replace Maye, who is feared to have fractured his ankle.
"I'm not going to make any comments about his status until he gets back here," Mike Vrabel said Monday. "He's en route back here. He stayed with a few of our people, and they're en route back here. So, once he gets back here, and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer. But I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye."
The Patriots are 5-5 and now on their bye week , so they'll have some time to figure out their plans under center if Maye can't go for the remainder of 2026. If he isn't able to return in any capacity, it's a major blow for a team that was looking to get back to the Super Bowl after a season of great forture injury-wise.
This year? Not so much. Maye has been the latest player to suffer an injury that's put the team behind the 8-ball. Whether it's DeVito, rookie Behren Morton or an external signing , there will likely be a new quarterback leading the way.

title: NFL Flexes Week 12 Schedule: Patriots Bumped Off Primetime vs. Chargers
full_text:
In the wake of the New England Patriots losing Drake Maye to an ankle injury and the Los Angeles Chargers' 1-8 record, the NFL is stepping in to make a change to their Week 12 schedule.
The league announced Tuesday that they're flexing the Patriots vs. Chargers game, scheduled for Sunday Night Football, to a 4:05 p.m. start on CBS. The primetime game will instead be replaced by the Cleveland Browns vs. Las Vegas Raiders game, originally scheduled for 1 p.m. that day.
The Tennessee Titans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars game moves from 4:05 p.m. to 1 p.m. as a result.
Tuesday was the deadline for the league to reschedule the Week 12 games, and because of Maye's injury, moving the Patriots out of a national audience became an easy choice.
Heading into the season, the Patriots going on the road to face the Chargers felt like a great matchup. Two teams that made the postseason season ago with young quarterbacks leading the way was a great pick for a pre-playoff push game. In the AFC Wild Card game last year, the Patriots beat the Chargers 16-3 in a defensive slugfest.
Instead, the seasons of both New England and Los Angeles have fallen apart.
Maye got sacked in the team's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 10 and subsequently fractured his ankle on the play. Now with the Patriots rolling with Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton under center, the Patriots don't seem like an exciting product as they sit at 5-5.
The Chargers came into the year with high expectations, hiring former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike MacDonald to be their new offensive coordinator. That decision backfired, as the Chargers are currently in possession of the NFL's worst record. They picked up their first win of the year last night on Monday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens.
With the league scheduling games on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Monday of Week 12, finding a good replacement for Sunday Night Football was going to be tricky. The San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks would have been a good replacement, but it was unlikely that FOX would have given that matchup up.
This removes the Patriots out of what would have been at least three more primetime games this season. They're currently scheduled to host the Vikings on Thursday Night Football in Week 14 and travel to play the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 15 on Monday Night Football.
While the Patriots' game against the Chargers has fallen out of favor with a national audience, one big storyline elsewhere has made the new SNF game a bigger deal.
With the Raiders trading away Kirk Cousins at the deadline and having first overall pick Fernando Mendoza step up last week, it's an opportunity for the league to showcase a young star who scored his first-career touchdown in his first start last game.
On the other side are the Browns, who are currently in control of the AFC's seventh seed after beating the Houston Texans a week ago. Deshaun Watson has come back and played really good football and right now, the Browns are one spot ahead of the Patriots in the conference standings.
The Patriots aren't in action this week, but will look to try and beat the Chargers to get back over .500 — this time during the afternoon instead of the evening.

title: Former Patriots QB Tells Mike Vrabel to 'Hit Me Up' After Drake Maye's Injury
full_text:
Drake Maye goes down against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, and now the New England Patriots are looking for someone to step into the role at quarterback next week.
Tommy DeVito, the second string, came in and didn't look good . Third-string Behren Morton hasn't taken a snap yet. And while head coach Mike Vrabel didn't seem to indicate that the Patriots would be looking for an external quarterback just yet, one former teammate of Vrabel's has thrown his hat into the ring.
Matt Cassel, who played four seasons with the Patriots from 2005 to 2008 and was the primary starter during an 11-5 season in 2008, jokingly took to social media to see if the Patriots head coach would end up calling him. Cassel said he hadn't signed any retirement papers, but hasn't taken a snap in the NFL since 2018.
"Hit me up Vrabes!," Cassel wrote on a report from NFL insider Jordan Schultz about the Patriots potentially exploring the quarterback market Monday. "I never signed any retirement papers!"
Hit me up Vrabes! I never signed any retirement papers! https://t.co/lnpXnLU6Xw
Cassel was a seventh-round draft pick by New England in 2005 and was their top backup behind Tom Brady during his tenure. He's got some experience stepping in for an injured starter. After Brady tore his ACL in the opening week of 2008, Cassel took over the reigns and led the Patriots to a winning record.
Vrabel, once a linebacker for the Patriots, was a teammate of Cassel's for six seasons. After the 2008 season, the Patriots traded Cassel and Vrabel to the Kansas City Chiefs for a 2009 second-round pick (a draft pick that would turn into safety Patrick Chung).
He'd spend two years in Kansas City, going 6-12 as a starter. Cassel would later go on to play for the Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Dallas Cowboys, Tennessee Titans and Detroit Lions.
Obviously the Patriots won't be dusting off Cassel's old No. 16 jersey out of the closest, but they're going to have to find a new quarterback somehow, someway. There are some players with Vrabel/Josh McDaniels connections around the league that could end up coming in, like Jimmy Garoppolo, Bailey Zappe, Will Levis and Dorian Thompson-Robinson.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said Monday when he was asked about potentially adding some external help. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see."
The Patriots are currently on their bye week and won't have to suit up again until next Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. It's likely that they'lre going to have to start just their 11th quarterback since 2000 in the process.
And no, it certainly won't be Cassel under center.

title: Why Patriots Should, Shouldn't Sign QB Jimmy Garoppolo
full_text:
Could the New England Patriots reunite with a Super Bowl champion quarterback in the wake of Drake Maye's ankle injury ? It's not impossible.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz mentioned that Jimmy Garoppolo , a 2014 draft pick by the Patriots who was part of two Super Bowl teams as a backup, could be an option for the Patriots under center as they start to re-evaluate their quarterback options. Currently, Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton are the two on the roster, and for now, no external decisions have been made.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Mike Vrabel said. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see."
But should the Patriots replace the current No. 10 with a former No. 10? Let's weigh the options.
When you think of a typical Josh McDaniels quarterback, Garoppolo is one of those guys who can operate it very well. Spending the first three-plus seasons with the Patriots offensive coordinator in New England, and then for a short time in Las Vegas in 2023, Garoppolo is well-versed in the Patriots' offensive terminology.
Sure, what you might get out of Garoppolo isn't the same you'd get out of the explosive 24-year-old Maye, but it's not like you're getting a quarterback who's in over his head in the playbook. Both DeVito and Morton know what the system is, but Garoppolo has proven to operate it well in the past.
Garoppolo is 35 and has already contemplated retirement. He hasn't started a game since 2024 and hasn't made more than one start in a season since the year prior. He isn't getting any younger and for a Patriots team that still has postseason expectations, throwing a dart at this dartboard might not be the ideal scenario.
In his final year as a full-time starter (2023 with the Raiders, before injuries and McDaniels' firing sent him to the bench), Garoppolo went 110-for-169 with 1,205 passing yards, seven touchdowns and nine interceptions in seven games. Since then, you have no real productive snaps out of him.
At first, it felt like Garoppolo would be the future behind Tom Brady. Then Brady kept winning and Garoppolo was sent off to San Francisco in 2017. How funny would it be for the Patriots to somehow reverse course and bring back their former quarterback-in-waiting nearly 10 years after trading him away?
Patriots fans have proven to enjoy Garoppolo's play, at least before injuries in 2016 soured how people viewed him. It would be pretty poetic for the Patriots, seemingly dead in the water , to be saved by the player fans once assumed would be the heir apparent.
The Patriots likely woudn't sign Garoppolo to a contract to stick him on the bench. If they make this move, that feels like it would mean he's the starter over both DeVito and Morton. The Patriots agreed to a two-year extension with DeVito in the offseason to make him the QB2, so it might not be worth bringing in a quarterback who'd want to start on a deal that might not make sense.
If the team is looking for more depth and/or experience, there's certainly a lot more names that could be added for much cheaper (Will Levis, a fomrer Vrabel draft pick in Tennessee, is currently on the New York Jets' practice squad).
At this point, the Patriots are 5-5 and currently possess a roster that is capable — on paper — to make a playoff run . Injuries have hurt them beyond belief, but the hopes and expectations are still there for this group to succeed in the stretch.
If Garoppolo, who's played in a Super Bowl as a starter before, is the best chance to get this Patriots team there, then why not pull the trigger. Based on how DeVito looked against the Detroit Lions post-Maye injury, it can't get much worse. The Patriots have a chance to become a surprising second-half team, and maybe all it takes is Jimmy G to make those surprises happen.

title: Patriots QB Drake Maye is Injured, So Now What Happens?
full_text:
The New England Patriots' fortunes have gone from bad to worse . According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Patriots are concerned that quarterback Drake Maye suffered a fractured ankle in their Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions. Maye remained in Germany for further evaluation to determine the extent of the injury and whether surgery will be necessary. Regardless of the results, he is expected to miss an indefinite amount of time, with the possibility that his season is over. "Once he gets back here and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Monday. "I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye." The prospect of losing Maye for any amount of time, let alone the remainder of the season, is a devastating blow to the Patriots and their hopes of making a playoff run. Regardless, New England has to pick up the pieces. Maye's potential absence will have a ripple effect across the roster, forcing the coaching staff to reevaluate their approach heading into the second half of the season. So, what's next?
Will the Patriots bring in a veteran quarterback to help weather the storm, or will they roll with backups Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton? For now, the former seems more likely. New England handed DeVito a two-year, $7.4 million extension during the offseason and selected Morton in April's draft. Despite a difficult outing in relief of Maye, DeVito appears to have the coaching staff's confidence moving forward. "I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
However, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that New England is expected to explore the quarterback free-agent market during the bye week. Vrabel pushed back on those reports when asked about the possibility of bringing in another quarterback. “I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see." Still, several QB options remain available if New England wants to go down that route. Notably, former Patriot Jimmy Garoppolo, who was named in the aforementioned Schultz report.
New England and DeVito struggled to find much success through the air after Maye's departure, completing just 50% of his pass attempts for 81 yards, one touchdown, and an interception. That came against a Lions defense that entered Week 10 ranked dead last in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (260.9) and was without their top pass rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, for most of the contest. While the Patriots have mainly moved the ball through the air with Maye under center, they'll need to establish a more consistent rushing attack moving forward to take pressure off DeVito. New England currently ranks 17th in the NFL in rushing yards per game, averaging 114 yards. That's a middle-of-the-pack unit that will likely need to shoulder a larger share of the offensive workload with Maye likely out of the picture. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker will be eligible to return from injured reserve following the bye week, potentially giving the offensive line a significant boost ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Paired with the return of fullback Reggie Gilliam, New England could have some reinforcements to help get its ground game back on track.
Losing Maye is obviously a major blow to the on-field aspirations, but it also presents a significant challenge for Mike Vrabel and the coaching staff inside the locker room. New England is entering one of the toughest stretches of its schedule, with matchups against the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings, 8-1 Buffalo Bills, 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs, and 7-2 Denver Broncos looming. The Patriots have already dealt with considerable adversity this season. Now, they'll have to prove they can respond to another major setback without allowing it to derail the foundation they've spent the last year and a half building. "We'll have to look at all things that we possibly can and find ways to improve, find ways to be on the same page, find ways to believe that we're all in this together, which is the first thing I told them," Vrabel said. "That it starts with me, and we're all in this together, and that the coaches will be connected, and they'll find ways to help each other and be part of the solution." Ultimately, this stretch will test more than just New England's depth at quarterback. It'll test the culture, leadership and resilience Vrabel has been working to establish since arriving in New England.

title: Mike Vrabel Expresses Confidence in Both Patriots Backup QBs
full_text:
The New England Patriots, a few years removed from all the Mac Jones/Bailey Zappe hoopla, are back under the quarterback spotlight. Drake Maye's ankle injury is reportedly serious enough to potentially knock him out for the remainder of the season and now the job under center may fall on two of the team's backups.
Tommy DeVito, who earned a two-year extension in the offseason, came in to replace Maye after his first quarter injury and didn't look all that promising. Behind him is seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who's been working as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback in each of the team's 10 games this year.
While Mike Vrabel won't comment on Maye's status any more than saying he likely won't be available in Week 12, it's clear that the Patriots will have to roll with someone not wearing No. 10 for a bit.
"He stayed with a few of our people and they're en route back here," the head coach said Monday. "Once he gets back here and our people are able to visit with him again, and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer."
Currently, the Patriots have just DeVito and Morton in the building — and Vrabel is confident in both of them.
DeVito, who has experience as a starter in the NFL , came in to Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions and really struggled. The Patriots offense could not move the ball and he completed just 50% of his passes and threw under 100 yards. It wasn't a promising outing.
"I mean, the assessment was pretty much like the team. I don't think it was good enough," Vrabel said of DeVito's play. "I think there was some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp. And really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye.
"I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand — whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket or, you know, get us int he right play or get the ball out quicker, or look at protections or tations, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve."
DeVito has won games before as a starting quarterback, including one against these Patriots back in 2023. But with a tough slate of games and postseason expectations looming, this will be a tougher challenge for him.
"I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
Right behind DeVito on the depth chart is Morton, who the Patriots drafted with the 234th overall pick this year out of Texas Tec h . He's yet to step onto the field this year in a regular season game, but did have some positive plays in the preseason — including a game-winning touchdown pass to Nick DeGennaro in the closing seconds of their second game.
It's expected that the Patriots will have Morton jump into the QB2 spot, but maybe an external addition enters the picture as well. For now, Vrabel feels like his rookie is getting better.
"Tommy and Behren have been in our system, have been working," Vrabel said. "Behren's been improving. He's been working each week and I know that if he has to play for us, that he'll be ready to go. And I'm excited for his challenge and I hope that everybody else is because that's really what we're at. We're 5 and 5 in the middle of the season, just past the middle of the season."
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Patriots could potentially explore the market for a new quarterback , but Vrabel pushed back on that notion.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said, just mere moments before Schultz's report came out. "We'll, you know, I mean, we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see."

title: Exploring 4 QB Replacements For Patriots After Drake Maye's Injury
full_text:
The New England Patriots are faced with the daunting task of finishing the 2026 season on a positive note, while sitting at 5-5 and looking to find a solution to the biggest problem the organization has been faced with in years.
Star quarterback Drake Maye is expected to have an ankle fracture that will sideline him for an extended period of time, according to NFL insider Ian Rapaport.
With this news entering the NFL spotlight, the Patriots will need to rework the entire makeup of their team. On Sunday, the offense struggled to find any production under backup quarterback Tommy DeVito.
Sources: #Patriots QB Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a significant lower leg injury that will keep him out an extended period of time. It’s even possible that Maye will miss the rest of the season. Maye came back from Germany and will seek more medical information. pic.twitter.com/jaOFw9qLGu
"I don't think it was good enough, I think there were things that he missed," Mike Vrabel said on DeVito's performance.
He also shared: "I wouldn't imagine [Maye] being available when we come out of the bye."
Vrabel alluded to DeVito being the starter in their Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Chargers in two weeks.
While the game plan certainly changes with Maye on the sidelines, there's potential that the personnel changes too. In the coming weeks, New England may look at the practice squads of other teams or free agents for a solution at quarterback.
On Monday, Vrabel was asked about looking outside of the organization for quarterbacks and said that it's not "the case right now," but added that "we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it, and look and see."
If Vrabel and the front office look elsewhere for quarterbacks, here are some available players that the Patriots could sign in light of Maye's injury:
(Note: The Patriots cannot trade for any players signed to another team's 53-man roster, as the trade deadline passed on Nov. 10).
Bailey Zappe (Current Status - Free Agent)
Bailey Zappe started his NFL career in New England as Mac Jones' backup quarterback . He played in 14 games for the Patriots and was the team's transition player between the Jones and Maye era under center.
While Zappe never played under Josh McDaniels, his ties to New England and his experience as a depth player in offenses like Kansas City's and New York's would make his transition back to the Pats a fairly easy one.
Sam Hartman (Current Status - Washington Commanders Practice Squad)
The third-year quarterback could hit headlines for a second week in a row — this time, however, in an unrelated way to his participation in a reality dating show.
Hartman is a long-time friend of Drake Maye, having both grown up in North Carolina and played on the same youth football teams. While Hartman's notoriety isn't a product of his on-field performance, the Patriots could explore the potential of bringing in a second Carolina-born quarterback.
Jimmy Garoppolo (Current Status - Free Agent)
Ten years ago, if someone said that Jimmy Garoppolo would be the Patriots starting quarterback, it would have made a lot of sense. As crazy as it sounds now, Garoppolo realistically could compete for the Patriots starting job.
At 35-years-old, Garoppolo is well-seasoned, playing behind Tom Brady, of course, but also leading the 2019 San Francisco 49ers to the Super Bowl. Garappolo was hand-picked by McDaniels in the second round of the 2014 draft, and could reunite with his old offensive coordinator for a second time (after McDaniels signed Garoppolo to the Raiders in 2023).
Chris Oladokun filled in for an injured Patrick Mahomes in the back-half of the Chiefs 2025 season, where he threw for 235 yards and one touchdown in three games.
Oladokun was released by the Chiefs prior to the start of the 2026 season, but was given an injury settlement. Oladokun's health would obviously impact his ability to play with the Patriots, but his recent NFL experience and two-way ability as a runner and a passer would allow him to fit in the Patriots offensive scheme built around Maye.

title: Tommy DeVito Preparing as Patriots Starting QB After Drake Maye's Injury
full_text:
With Drake Maye down for the count (and the forseeable future) , the New England Patriots are going to have to figure out their quarterback decision after their bye week. The leader in the clubhouse is Tommy DeVito, who came in to replace Maye after his injury in Week 10.
DeVito and the Patriots offense struggled all game, scoring just once against the Detroit Lions in a 35-10 drubbing.
"Not good enough are the words I would say. Offensively, just never really got going," DeVito said. "Never really was able to get into a rhythm, really get drives going. Too many three and outs and just hurting ourselves. Even the one drive that we had that resulted in a touchdown took 16 plays and there were still errors on that that happened. We just need to be better at that and just sustaining drives."
DeVito didn't end up inspiring much hope in Maye's place, going 12-for-24 with 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception. They weren't able to to move the ball consistently and it took until the fourth quarter for them to find the end zone.
Now Maye, who's reportedly going to be out a long time with what the Patriots fear to be a fractured ankle , DeVito is going to be tasked with carrying this team through a tough stretch of games. The 28-year-old says he's prepared to do so.
"I'm going to continue the process I have been doing up to this point," he said. "Something that as a two, as cliche as it sounds, you have to be prepared to be a starter. So just keep doing what I'm doing, keep my head down, and then if something like that were to happen, you would have the reps and practice and the walkthroughs and everything going forward, so just keep on preparing and on to the next."
The Patriots have dealt with a ton of injuries on offense , putting that unit behind the 8-ball for most of this season. A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, TreVeyon Henderson, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Mike Onwenu, the list goes on and on. With Maye out, it's DeVito's team — and he'll have to pull them out of this mess going into a Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
"It starts with the quarterback, so it starts with me," DeVito said. "I just have to play better and sustain drives and get the thing going and stop feeling so lax."
This season in a reserve role, DeVito is 16-for-32 with 132 yards, that one touchdown to Lan Larison and an interception. The Patriots signed him to a two-year, $7.4 million extension in the offseason to be the top backup, so it's safe to assume he'll be under center through the next few weeks. Seventh-string rookie Behren Morton backs him up.
Sitting at .500, the hopes aren't that high for the Patriots . But DeVito isn't putting his head down, and that's all he can do at this point.
"I think we just focus on the next week," he said. "We have a bye week here, a lot of time to reflect and process the games that have happened and the games that are coming. All you can focus on are the games coming ahead."

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly: Can the Saints Do Anything Right?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had an opportunity to take control of the NFC South on Sunday, but instead delivered another frustrating performance that raised more questions about the direction of the franchise.
New Orleans (3-6) suffered a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers at the Caesars Superdome, surrendering a game-winning 54-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald as time expired.
Despite Carolina committing 17 penalties for 152 yards, the Saints couldn't capitalize, finishing with just 49 rushing yards, two turnovers and another disappointing offensive performance under head coach Kellen Moore .
The loss dropped New Orleans to 1-4 at home and 0-2 against NFC South opponents, leaving the Saints searching for answers as their season continues to unravel.
Here is the good, bad and ugly from Sunday's loss.
Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson led the Saints with 11 receptions, the most since Pierre Thomas caught 12 passes against the Chicago Bears in December 2007.
After missing the first seven games of the season, the rookie wideout has wasted little time demonstrating why New Orleans selected him eighth overall in April's NFL Draft.
His separation, contested catches, and reliability complement Chris Olave and should make this passing attack even deadlier.
However, the offense has become too predictable.
After a strong performance last week, the Saints' rushing attack went back to its old ways, gaining just 49 yards on 23 carries (2.1 yards per carry) against Carolina.
Quarterback Shough led New Orleans with 25 rushing yards, while Travis Etienne Jr. (14 yards), Audric Estime (6 yards), and Alvin Kamara (4 yards, 3-yard touchdown) combined for minimal output.
Although the absence of right tackle Taliese Fuaga and center Erik McCoy provides important context, the struggles within the ground attack were already present prior to their injuries.
Moore was hired because of his success as the offensive coordinator of the Philadelphia Eagles , one that had the NFL’s top rushing offense in 2024 and propelled them to a Super Bowl victory. He must fix the run game for New Orleans to sustain drives and score consistently.
Through nine games this season, the answer has been a firm no.
Carolina repeatedly handed the Saints chances by committing 17 penalties and struggling offensively, but New Orleans failed to capitalize.
The Saints were shut out in the first half, committed two turnovers, and generated insufficient offense against a sub-.500 Panthers squad. Even after Charlie Smyth tied the game with a 55-yard field goal with 41 seconds remaining, a pass interference penalty on Kool-Aid McKinstry set up Fitzgerald's game-winning kick.
More concerning is the lack of progress under head coach Kellen Moore.
Over nine games, the Saints have struggled with offensive inconsistency, poor execution and an inability to close games. Their 3-6 record inspires little confidence, and individual flashes from Tyson, Shough, and the defense cannot mask overall failure. To make matters worse, the Saints have trailed in all but one of the 26 games that Moore has coached in as the head coach of the Saints.
With upcoming road trips to Chicago and Cincinnati followed by a home game against the Green Bay Packers , the schedule provides no relief. Instead of making a statement in the NFC South, New Orleans showed just how far it remains from contention.

title: Saints Find Another Way to Lose as Panthers Steal NFC South Victory
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints had chance after chance to build momentum and secure their first consecutive wins of the season. Instead, it was another game that left a sour taste in everyone’s mouths like tomatoes in gumbo.
Kicker Ryan Fitzgerald connected on a game-winning 54-yard field goal as time expired, lifting the Carolina Panthers to a 20-17 victory over the Saints on Sunday afternoon at the Caesars Superdome.
The loss dropped New Orleans to 3-6 under second-year head coach Kellen Moore , while Carolina improved to 4-5 and strengthened its position in the NFC South standings.
Despite overcoming a sluggish first half and taking a fourth-quarter lead, the Saints couldn't finish the job, and Carolina escaped with a crucial divisional win.
Tyler Shough went 25-for-36 for 187 yards, with a touchdown and an interception, while rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson had a breakout game, leading New Orleans with 11 receptions for 80 yards.
Running back Alvin Kamara provided the Saints' biggest offensive spark, scoring twice in the second half on a 3-yard touchdown run in the third quarter and a 4-yard touchdown catch in the fourth.
However, New Orleans struggled offensively throughout the opening two quarters, committing two turnovers and failing to score before halftime.
Shough's first interception came on the Saints' opening possession when cornerback Marco Wilson deflected his fourth-down pass intended for Chris Olave , and linebacker Devin Lloyd intercepted it.
The Saints' defense kept Carolina from capitalizing, with Carl Granderson sacking Bryce Young on fourth down near the goal line.
Another costly mistake came in the second quarter when Shough and Audric Estime mishandled a handoff, allowing Panthers linebacker Jaelan Phillips to recover the fumble.
Carolina capitalized on the turnover with a 2-yard touchdown run by Chuba Hubbard , taking a 7-0 lead into halftime.
New Orleans finally found some traction in the third quarter.
Kamara capped a nine-play, 64-yard drive with a 3-yard touchdown run, tying the game at 7-7 with 6:33 remaining in the period.
However, Fitzgerald answered with a 55-yard field goal to restore Carolina's three-point advantage entering the fourth quarter.
The Saints responded with their best offensive sequence of the afternoon.
Shough connected with Kamara on a 4-yard touchdown pass, giving New Orleans its first lead at 14-10.
That advantage proved short-lived.
Hubbard scored his second touchdown on a 1-yard run, putting Carolina back ahead 17-14 late in the fourth quarter.
New Orleans refused to go away, with kicker Charlie Smyth drilling a clutch 55-yard field goal to tie the game at 17-17.
But Young and the Panthers orchestrated one final scoring opportunity, setting up Fitzgerald's game-winning kick as time expired.
Young finished with 200 passing yards, while Hubbard rushed for 92 yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries.
For the Saints, the defeat represents another frustrating setback in a season defined by inconsistency, offensive mistakes and an inability to capitalize on opportunities.
The Saints will now prepare for a road trip to the Buckeye State to take on the Cincinnati Bengals .

I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints.
While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season.
On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns).
The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key.
Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility.
However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude.
Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease.

I'm not quite sure what to think of this "new" Saints team. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places.
On Sunday, the Saints and Panthers play for first place in the NFC South in the Superdome. Admittedly, both teams have three wins in their eight games, but first place is on the line, nonetheless. It's hard to believe, but it was just 2021 that Tampa Bay , a team tied for the bottom of this division, won it all.
Point being, things change rapidly in this professional sport Americans love so much.
Neither of these teams is impressive in its own right, but here we stand with the mid-season top-of-the-totem position on the line.
Are the Saints finally starting to find an offensive rhythm? I mean, they did score in the first quarter against Cleveland, the first time this season they've put any points in the first period column.
Is the defense poised to stop the run better? They held Cleveland to under 100 yards rushing as a team, only the second time this year, the other being against the New York Giants .

Is the field goal crap shoot fixed with Charlie Smyth ? The Irishman made three of four field goals last week, missing from almost 50 yards from that pesky left hash mark.
There is hope, and I am going with it.

title: Saints Activate Travis Etienne Jr. From Injured Reserve Ahead of Panthers Game
full_text:
Running back Travis Etienne Jr. will be activated from injured reserve for the New Orleans Saints ' Sunday game against the Carolina Panthers , according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer.
The 3-5 teams face off for sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Etienne has not played since Week 3 against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sept. 27, when he suffered a hamstring injury.
Upon returning to practice this week, Etienne fully participated by Friday and was listed as questionable.
In New Orleans, Etienne is expected to share backfield responsibilities with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara . Estime posted a team season-high 72 rushing yards last week against the Cleveland Browns , while Kamara has recorded 157 yards with a 3.3-yard average through seven games.
The Saints rank 26th in the NFL in rushing, averaging 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 yards per attempt under head coach Kellen Moore . They will test a Panthers run defense that ranks 28th, allowing 133.4 yards per game and 4.6 yards per rush. In his three games this season before the injury, Etienne rushed for 128 yards (4.3 per carry), including 57 yards against Las Vegas, and added 11 receptions for 51 yards.
The 27-year-old running back joined New Orleans during free agency on a three-year contract after four seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars , who selected him in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Etienne topped 1,000 rushing yards in three of his four years with Jacksonville. A Louisiana native out of Jennings High School, he played at Clemson, earning All-America honors three times and twice winning ACC Offensive Player of the Year.
In additional roster adjustments, New Orleans placed defensive lineman Christen Miller on Injured Reserve. The team also promoted tackle Easton Kilty from the practice squad to the active roster and elevated kicker Charlie Smyth for Sunday's matchup with the Carolina Panthers.
Smyth stepped into the starting role following the release of Daniel Carlson and capitalized on the opportunity. The Irish kicker provided all nine of the Saints' points through three quarters in a low-scoring battle against Cleveland, going 3-for-4 on field goals with conversions from 30, 27, and 48 yards.
