The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center.
Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard.
Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup.

title: Giants vs. Jaguars: Where Trevor Lawrence Is Most Vulnerable
full_text:
The New York Giants begin the challenging part of their 2026 schedule this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are fresh off a 40-23 win over the Tennessee Titans. It will be the second career game for Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence against Big Blue, the first coming on Oct. 23, 2022, in a Giants win.
Lawrence will enter his next game against the Giants bearing the ninth-best completion rate (66%) in the league. He’ll face a Giants pass defense that has been very solid this season and currently ranks third in passing yards allowed (184.1/game) and second in average pass yards per play (6.2/attempt).
Meanwhile, on the defensive side of the ball, the Jaguars boast the ninth-best overall defense (319.2 yards/game) and the sixth-best run defense (91.0 yards/game), making for a formidable challenge for a Giants team that not only aspires to get to the postseason, but also to hang around.
The Jaguars have the fifth-easiest remaining strength of schedule , according to Tankathon. In their last three games, all wins, they have pounded their opponents (the Colts, Ravens and Titans) into submission, winning all three by two or more scores.
The key for the Giants? Stopping Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence.
Lawrence and company are averaging 29.9 points per game (fourth). But there is a stat the Giants can potentially play to their advantage that doesn’t get talked about much: batted balls.
Lawrence has posted eight batted passes this year , tied for the fifth most in the NFL among quarterbacks, and one of those batted balls turned into an interception for the defense.
This week, he’ll face a Giants defensive front led by defensive tackle Shelby Harris, who has two batted passes this year (tied for 15th) and 18 batted balls since 2020, tying him for eighth most in the NFL.
This is a surprising stat considering Lawrence stands 6-foot-6, but on film, he is more prone to having passes knocked down at the line of scrimmage when he’s under pressure, and he compromises his arm angle.
Therein lies one challenge for the Giants defense. The Jaguars, per PFF, have allowed the fewest quarterback pressures this season (86), so getting to Lawrence is not going to be easy, even with the Jags having a banged-up offensive line, the latest addition to which is center Robert Hainsey, who is expected to miss this weekend’s game with a knee sprain.
It goes without saying that this week in practice, the Giants defensive coaches will place a strong emphasis on getting their hands up in the passing lanes, particularly if they end up getting stonewalled at the point of attack.
Interesting fact: Lawrence has a 55.1% completion rate when facing man coverage and a 72.4% completion rate against zone coverage. The Giants have played man coverage on 25.6% of their snaps (sixth most) and zone on 69.1% of their snaps (seventh lowest).
Although the numbers suggest man coverage is the way to go against Lawrence, there is a hidden danger that should give New York pause: Lawrence’s legs.
When facing man coverage, Lawrence has taken advantage of defenders having their backs to him, rushing six times for 32 yards (5.3 average) and converting four first downs.
When facing zone coverage, Lawrence has run 14 times for 76 yards (5.4 yards/carry) and has just five first downs.
No defense ever plays 100% man or zone, and that’s unlikely to start this week.
But it wouldn’t be surprising if the mix of man and zone coverage tilts more toward the latter, and if the Giants emphasize aggressive man coverage against receiver Parker Washington, who leads the Jaguars with 645 yards on 36 receptions and six touchdowns this season.
The Giants host the Jaguars on Sunday, with kickoff set for 4:35 p.m.

title: Giants Fall in MMQB Power Rankings After Commanders Loss
full_text:
Just four days after riding the immense high of beating the Philadelphia Eagles on the road for the first time since 2013, the New York Giants were quickly brought back down to earth by a gut-wrenching 24-21 primetime loss to the Washington Commanders last Thursday.
What stood out as the bigger disappointment for John Harbaugh and company was their blown chance to deal the knockout punch to a second divisional foe’s season in that span while adding another game’s distance between themselves and the Dallas Cowboys, who are currently trailing them in second place.
As a result, SI’s senior writer Conor Orr put a lid on their three-week ascension, dropping Harbaugh’s group four spots to No. 15 in his latest MMQB NFL power rankings ahead of Week 11.
Even with their recent setback in the standings, Orr still views the Giants as the NFC East frontrunners.
“Coming out of the miniature bye, the Giants still control the destiny of the NFC East,” Orr said.
“Even with Jacksonville, Seattle, Detroit and San Francisco on the remaining schedule, taking care of business against a lackluster field featuring Indianapolis, Cleveland, Dallas and Philadelphia will land Big Blue in the postseason,” Orr added.
Despite losing a game to the Commanders that some could argue the Giants gave away multiple times, they did manage to earn some help from San Francisco, which kept the Cowboys at bay by dropping them to 4-6 with a thrilling 46-40 victory in Arlington.
At 5-3-1, the Giants are certainly not safe atop their perch as they prepare to welcome the red-hot Jaguars, tied for the league’s second-best record, to MetLife Stadium on Sunday at the start of a difficult four-game window.
Typically, it takes until the last couple of weeks of the regular season before any semblance of “scoreboard watching” would draw the attention of teams vying for postseason positioning, but in a tight NFC East where three teams are still mathematically in the running for the division crown, the Giants could find themselves falling into the trap beginning this weekend.
As tempting as that might be, Harbaugh has to make sure his men stay focused on what they can control. Relying on outside factors is never a bold strategy in the modern NFL; instead, the Giants will likely have to prove they can take down at least one of the goliaths standing in their way.
The cards might be stacked against them with the Jaguars, who have been dominating opponents on the scoreboard and have made major improvements across their defense, which excels at stopping the run and forcing turnovers. The only saving grace is that the Giants will have had extra rest from their mini bye after Thursday night's game.
If they don’t get an upset over Jacksonville, some outsiders might say the team has a shot against Seattle, whose quarterback situation has been in flux due to injuries, or Detroit, whose defense took a major blow with the loss of All-Pro edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who tore his ACL in Week 10.
Regardless of how they get to the eight or nine wins that could be enough to get them over the hump and win the division, the best approach the Giants can take is the one they’ve already pressed onto black T-shirts that have been seen at practice during media viewing periods.
That is, to strive to go 1-0 in each of their remaining eight contests, which surely include a few they could feasibly conquer. The rest of the chips can only fall where they may, especially considering the Cowboys and Commanders also have to play most of the same opponents down the stretch.
Of course, the Giants could have made this a little easier if they’d handled their business against Washington and put their chase to bed, but that hasn’t been the story of Harbaugh’s first season in New York.
Not one of his team’s victories has come easily, and that will most likely remain the case as the Giants’ pursuit of one of the coveted postseason spots is still theirs to lose.

title: Giants-Jaguars Week 11: Xavier Gipson, Zvada and Nabers Among Key Storylines
full_text:
It’s gut-check time for the New York Giants , who, after a mini bye, dive right into preparing for the most challenging part of their 2026 schedule, starting this week with a home date against the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2).
This nationally televised game is going to tell us a lot about the state of the Giants, starting with their resiliency, a characteristic that head coach John Harbaugh and his players have taken pride in showing through thick and thin.
It can probably be agreed that in the Thursday night loss to Washington, the Giants, from players down to coaches, did not have their best game and probably wanted a few things back.
But Harbaugh is not one to dwell on the past. The Giants head coach said he has the utmost confidence in his team, backed by their resilience in pulling off close wins.
“You’ve watched us play. People have watched us play. You know where we are. We’re going to do everything we can to win the game. Our guys are going to fight like crazy,” he said.
“They’re going to compete, and we’re capable of making plays. We can make plays on both sides of the ball. We’re chasing consistency, just like every single team in this league is.
“The so-called heavyweights, I’ve seen them play bad games too,” he continued. “This is a tough league. It’s pretty even. We’re in it just like everybody else. We’ll be fighting in there just like everybody else. And I know our guys; nobody’s going to outfight us. That’s for sure. Nobody is going to outcompete us without question.”
We’ll find out if he’s right starting Sunday, when the Giants host a heavyweight.
When we last left the Giants, the only player to miss the Week 10 contest against the Commanders was linebacker Malik Harrison (groin). Before the team took its mini bye, Harbaugh told reporters he expected to have Harrison back.
That doesn’t mean the Giants will have a completely clean injury report on Wednesday, as there are bound to be players with lingering issues, running back Cam Skattebo comes to mind, whose workloads might be managed.
Still, with the NFL season heading into the homestretch, the Giants are as healthy as can be unless something is lurking that isn’t yet known.
The Giants shook up their special teams return game, dropping receiver Charlie Jones and adding receiver Xavier Gipson from the Eagles’ practice squad. Gipson, who was with the Giants in training camp, will presumably take over kickoff and punt return duties, and the Giants hope he’ll be an upgrade.
His career numbers suggest that could be the case, as he has averaged 9.1 yards per punt return and 25.9 yards per kickoff return. However, he has also had some ball-security issues, recording six career fumbles on punt returns.
Harbaugh has already shown little tolerance for ball-security issues, so if Gipson wants his third stint with the Giants to last a while, ball security must be paramount.
The Giants haven’t had many players in for workouts in the last few weeks, and of those they have, none have been kickers.
That’s because Harbaugh still has confidence in undrafted rookie Dominic Zvada, who missed his lone field goal attempt (33 yards) last week and has six misses (all from the right hash) since Week 5.
Harbaugh has pointed to a problem with Zvada’s plant leg for his struggles. The question is whether the Giants can help him fix it, or whether the yips Zvada appears to be struggling with have become so embedded that things are beyond repair.
If the latter is the case, it’s fair to wonder how much longer the Giants will stick with the rookie.
After a stellar October in which he posted four straight games with 100-plus receiving yards, Malik Nabers has cooled off. In his last two games, he has caught 10 of 15 targets for 87 yards and no touchdowns. In fact, his last touchdown came in Week 5.
Nabers also has three drops this season and two fumbles, one of which he lost. Even more concerning, after averaging 3.83 first downs per game through his first six games, he is down to 2.3 over his last three.
Part of that obviously has to do with opponents erasing him from the game, but when opportunities do arise, Nabers has to be more consistent in making them.
He’ll have a challenge this week, as he’s likely to face Travis Hunter, who has been playing some solid ball. It will be interesting to see how the Giants plan to scheme Nabers open.

title: Wan’Dale Robinson’s Injury Could Cost Giants a 2027 4th Round Compensatory Pick
full_text:
Nov. 18 Update: Jim Wyatt of Titans.com, reported that Wan'Dale Robinson is out for the season .
The New York Giants ' path toward landing a fourth-round comp draft pick in 2027 has hit a snag, according to projections from Nick Korte of Over the Cap.
Korte projected that the Giants might be in line for an extra fourth-round pick as compensation for losing receiver Wan’Dale Robinson in free agency to the Tennessee Titans.
However, with news of Robinson landing on IR after suffering an ankle injury in the team’s Week 10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, that move, which will require Robinson to miss a minimum of four games, could be problematic for the Giants.
Wan'Dale Robinson going on IR could be problematic for the round of the Giants' expected 2027 compensatory pick. He's been barely hovering above the 4th/5th round bubble, and missing 4 games could make it difficult for him to stay above that cutoff. https://t.co/kszjlueNQn pic.twitter.com/KzBSNvruhL
Korte explained that Robinson has “barely been hovering above the fourth/fifth round bubble” as it stood before landing on IR. Now that he’s looking at missing at least four games, the question is whether Robinson will finish within range for the Giants to get a fourth-round comp pick for him.
The Giants currently have five draft picks locked in for 2027: their own first, second, third, and sixth-round picks, and a sixth-round pick owed by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the Daniel Falaale trade.
The Cleveland Browns own the Giants' fourth-round pick, which they received as part of the package New York gave up to move in the third round of the 2026 draft to select wide receiver Malachi Fields.
The Minnesota Vikings also own the Giants’ fifth-round pick, which the Giants gave up to acquire quarterback J.J. McCarthy in September.
Korte added that the Giants should still be in line to receive a fifth-round comp pick so long as Austin Schlottmann remains the Titans starting center.

title: Giants' 3 Toughest Remaining Opponents—and One Sneaky Trap Game
full_text:
The New York Giants (5-3-1) will only get red in the face if they dwell on their Week 10 home loss to the Washington Commanders. A surefire opportunity to take firm control of the NFC East instead became an unpleasant reminder that progress is not always linear.
Big Blue will have had 10 days to regroup by the time it plays its next game, and it must use that mini-break to sharpen its on-field execution and play-calling. The schedule is about to ramp up , so John Harbaugh had better have his team ready.
Three matchups stand out as ominous, and one could make fans combust if the Giants do not emerge victorious. The list kicks off with a huge challenge this Sunday.
The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) are, on paper, ahead of the Giants, and if their recent history with inferior squads is any indication, the home crowd at MetLife Stadium had better brace itself.
The Jags boast a +125 point differential, which is far and away the best mark in the NFL. Only two of their wins were by one possession. They scored 30 or more points in the other five, and their two losses were by a combined 10 points.
A 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans in London in Week 6 should give Giants fans some optimism, especially since New York beat that same team the following Sunday, but this is a daunting matchup .
Quarterback Trevor Lawrence operates an offense that ranks in the top five at 29.9 points per game, and the reloaded defense allows an AFC-best 16.0 points per game. The Jaguars are balanced, well-coached, and quite formidable on the road. And, oh yeah, kicker Cam Little has possibly the biggest leg in the league.
Harbaugh and his staff will really have to shine if they want to keep pace with this AFC title contender.
Two weeks after battling dangerous Jacksonville, the Giants will host the Super Bowl favorites. The San Francisco 49ers will push defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson to be more creative than ever.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan wields a wand over a dynamic offense that features MVP candidate Brock Purdy, former Offensive Player of the Year Christian McCaffrey, five-time All-Pro tight end George Kittle, and accomplished wide receivers Mike Evans (questionable) and Keenan Allen.
Outside linebacker Abdul Carter and the Giants’ defensive line must bring the pressure, otherwise Shanahan will work his magic at will. Fans may learn just how much this squad has progressed under Harbaugh when this one concludes.
The Detroit Lions may have the better record and the better offense, but for a young quarterback like J.J. McCarthy, who has already absorbed some big hits this season, a Dec. 13 meeting with the defensively ferocious Seattle Seahawks seems more intimidating.
The defending Super Bowl champions give up a mere 236.1 yards per game, nearly 37 yards fewer than the second-best mark. They are physical and savvy, allowing offenses little time and few opportunities to make something happen.
How Big Blue’s offensive line performs will likely dictate the outcome. J.J. McCarthy has shown what he can do when afforded the chance to scan the field. This may wind up being his toughest test of the year, especially with the unrelenting crowd at Lumen Field.
Defensively, New York will be challenged to stop Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But if its fairly stingy secondary can minimize the damage, the Giants could leave the Emerald City with a “W,” as playoff implications should loom large for both squads.
The Indianapolis Colts took a hammer to their foundation before the trade deadline and just snapped a five-game losing streak by beating a fellow rebuilding team in Miami. They face organizational uncertainty and have holes all over their roster.
So why should fans be worried? Simply put, the Giants have struggled to earn straightforward victories against weak competition. They needed game-sealing interceptions to hold off the last-place Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals, and they also lost at home to the New Orleans Saints.
There is also the Daniel Jones element . It would be the most Giants thing ever if the former No. 6 overall pick, who has now underachieved on two big contracts, were to torch his ex-squad.
The Colts still have star running back and former New York trade target Jonathan Taylor. Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen withdrew an offer for the former rushing champ before the deadline, so they might take some joy in embarrassing Indy on its home field.
The Giants cannot come into this game overconfident, however. They still face the Jaguars, 49ers, Seahawks, Cleveland Browns, and Detroit Lions before the end of 2026. In other words, this team does not have another bad loss to spare.

title: Giants Open Week 11 as Home Underdogs vs Jaguars
full_text:
Last Thursday, the New York Giants had a chance to enjoy something they probably won’t see for a while: being favored by the oddsmakers at home in a game they should have won.
Sadly, Big Blue squandered that opportunity multiple times in a gut-wrenching 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders, an outcome that, had it gone the other way, might have put an early end to the NFC East race and taken Washington out of the discussion entirely.
While the Giants remain in first place in the NFC East, things are about to get more difficult starting this Sunday against a 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars team that has entered the discussion as the team to beat in the AFC.
Not surprisingly, the Jaguars are 5.5-point favorites in that game, per FanDuel Sportsbook , with the total projected at 46.5 points.
What is surprising is that the spread isn’t bigger. Jacksonville leads the league with a point differential of +125. The Jaguars also have the best turnover differential (+9) and are playing some of their best ball as they continue to run away with the AFC South.
This season, Jacksonville has been lighting up opponents, averaging 29.9 points and nearly 360 yards of total offense per game, including six contests in which they’ve scored at least 31 points.
Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has more than enough weapons at his disposal. The Jaguars also run the football at the 12th-highest rate and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown rate, with 30 total touchdowns.
That alone sets up a huge problem for a Giants defense that ranks dead last in that department.
Defensively, the Jaguars have largely shut down their opponents. They’ve allowed only three teams to score more than 20 points and will look to use their strength in the trenches to derail the Giants’ hopes of controlling the matchup with a steady rushing game.
Meanwhile, head coach John Harbaugh’s Giants have a lot of work to do to restore confidence among the betting community after Thursday’s disappointing loss to Washington.
This week’s opening line marks the second-largest underdog role New York has carried into a game this season, behind the 10.5-point underdog spot in Houston.
It won’t be easy against this version of the Jaguars, who have been rejuvenated by the leadership of head coach Liam Coen and the belief that they could finally contend for the Super Bowl in February.
Harbaugh and company will need to show vast improvement in executing the details they missed in the loss to Washington, as they still have a great chance to win the NFC East if they can steal a few more wins in the second half of their schedule.
The challenge is that they’ve reached the toughest point of their journey, with upcoming games against powerhouses in Jacksonville, San Francisco, Seattle, and Detroit. They’ll need to grab a win from one of those four opponents to help their cause.
As quarterback J.J. McCarthy put it, getting that unforeseen win against the Jaguars will require very crisp football that, at times, New York has shown it can produce.

title: Giants TE Isaiah Likely Has Strong Start, but Wants the Wins
full_text:
New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely walked away from his team’s Week 10 loss to the Washington Commanders with mixed feelings.
In arguably his best game as a member of Big Blue, the 26-year-old caught nine passes for 127 yards and a 66-yard touchdown that seemed destined for “play of the game” honors.
But for Likely, who is having a monster year in his first with Big Blue, his individual accomplishments paled in comparison to the outcome of the game, to the point that he lamented what might have been for the team had the offense done its part against the Commanders.
“They’ve been doing a great job this year when they’re put in situations to ice the game,” Likely said about the defense. “But, as an offense, we need to look ourselves in the mirror and be able to do that ourselves.”
In nine games this season, Likely has done his part, catching 55 passes for 575 yards and seven touchdowns, the most by a Giants tight end in his first nine games with the team in the Super Bowl era. He is just the fifth Giant to catch at least six touchdown passes in his first eight games with the team.
At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Likely has already been a heavily targeted option in the passing game. His route-running and contested-catch ability have made him a favorite target for Giants quarterbacks Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston, and J.J. McCarthy.
In fact, Likely’s growing chemistry with McCarthy has been a source of pride for the Cambridge, MA, native.
For Likely and his Big Blue teammates, it’s all about flushing the last game and pouring their full attention into the next one, against a very tough Jacksonville Jaguars team that, at 7-2, not only sits atop the AFC South but also is tied for second (with six other teams) for the league’s second-best win-loss record.
Still, Likely and his teammates understand that the Giants must maintain their focus after such a heartbreaking loss.
At 5-3-1, New York still maintains its spot atop the NFC East. To continue as the division leader, it cannot afford to lose any of the confidence it has built over the past few weeks.

title: Giants Poach Special Teams Help from Two NFC Rosters
full_text:
The New York Giants have signed defensive back Tavierre Thomas off the Minnesota Vikings practice squad and receiver Xavier Gipson off the Philadelphia Eagles practice squad.
Thomas, 30, was originally signed as an undrafted free agent in 2018 out of Ferris State by the Arizona Cardinals, with whom he spent that summer in training camp.
The 5-foot-10, 212-pound Thomas, who is primarily a special teams player, has had stints with the Browns, Texans, Bucs, and Vikings.
He has appeared in 116 games with 22 starts and has 262 career tackles (163 solo), six tackles for loss, two interceptions (including one returned for a touchdown), six pass breakups, and one sack.
Last season, Thomas led the Vikings in special teams tackles with 19. It is anticipated that he will fill a punt gunner role with the Giants.
Gipson, who spent time with the Giants last season at two different times, was with the team this summer in training camp. Howeer, he was waived as part of the final roster cuts on August 30 and was signed by the Eagles on Sept. 11.
With Thomas and Gipson signed to the 53-man roster, the Giants released receiver Charlie Jones and defensive back Nikko Reed. Jones had been the Giants' return specialist, but he had his ups and downs in that role, prompting New York to seek an upgrade.
Gipson will presumably take over the return specialist duties for the Giants.
The Giants don’t practice until Tuesday, and the first injury report for Week 12 isn't due until Wednesday.

title: J.J. McCarthy: Giants Must Be ‘Crisp’ After Painful Loss to Commanders
full_text:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy was on the threshold of earning his seventh win as an NFL starting quarterback until he wasn’t.
In the fourth quarter of Big Blue’s Week 10 showdown with the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium, McCarthy engineered a 69-yard scoring drive in just three plays. The series ended with a 66-yard touchdown pass to tight end Isaiah Likely, giving the Giants a 21-17 lead with only 8:17 left.
Unfortunately, New York couldn't capitalize on its two interceptions of quarterback Jayden Daniels, leaving the door open for an eventual 24-21 comeback win for Washington in what was a major kick to the gut for the Giants.
While the loss has left a bitter taste in the mouths of the players, who have had an extra four days to stew on it, the team’s focus is on what the Giants do moving forward.
“For me, a takeaway is just do whatever you can to get a fast start, not hurt ourselves in whatever moment it is,” McCarthy said.
Despite their loss to the Commanders, the Giants are still firmly in control of first place in the NFC East — and they intend to keep it that way.
“We just gotta be so crisp, detailed, and execute on every single play like it’s the last play from snap one to the last snap," he said.
"We just got to do a better job of tightening things up, be consistently on the same page, all 11, and do whatever we can, find a way to get a win in those critical situations.”
The Giants will get that chance on Sunday against a red-hot Jacksonville Jaguars team that has been dominating the AFC South. So great is the interest in that game between two division leaders that it was flexed to the nationally televised slot, with kickoff set for 4:25 p.m. ET.
McCarthy, who certainly wasn’t the lone reason for the Giants’ loss to the Commanders, recognizes that he must be part of the solution moving forward, and that it starts with him correcting any mistakes he’s made that have hurt the team.
“Now it’s ‘What’s next?’ and ‘How can we prepare for Jacksonville?’” he said. “We just need to find a way to get that next win. That is really the main focus.”

title: 4 Unsung Giants Free Agents Who've Made Their Case to Stay in 2027
full_text:
The last thing the New York Giants front office brass are probably thinking about right now is which of their pending unrestricted free agents they will aggressively look to re-sign after this season.
Granted, the Giants have already extended one pending free agent on an expiring contract: cornerback Greg Newsome II, who signed a three-year extension coming out of the team’s bye week. But a case could be made for prioritizing re-signing several other Giants on expiring contracts, such as the players below.
Remember when head coach John Harbaugh, when asked about his inside linebackers, said that the team had three starters at the position? Two of them, Arvell Reese and Tremaine Edmunds, were actually starters, at least until a season-ending injury cut short Edmunds’ season.
The third starter, who has delivered in Edmunds’ absence, is Micah McFadden. The Giants’ 2022 fifth-round draft pick out of Indiana was a starter before Edmunds' injury, and when pressed into a bigger role, McFadden has responded.
Per PFF, McFadden has the highest season grades of his career in run defense (70.1) and pass rush (85.2).
In 202 total defensive snaps, McFadden already has six pressures. By comparison, he had 11 in 2024, his last year as a starter, when he played 668 defensive snaps.
McFadden has also cut down on missed tackles, posting just three so far after 41 in 2023 and 2024 as a starter.
In short, it’s been a nice comeback for McFadden, who missed most of last season with a foot injury that came when he was getting ready to enter a contract year.
Yes, Banks has had some issues lately with defensive pass interference flags, though at least one of those calls was “iffy.” But the fact remains that Banks has found new life under this coaching staff and in this defensive scheme.
Per PFF, he’s currently carrying his best grades overall (62.7) and in coverage (64.3).
But if you need more proof of how good Banks has actually been after beating out big-ticket Paulson Adebo for a starting job, consider that Banks has his second-best NFL coverage rating (85.2), behind only his rookie season (84.7).
He’s one pass breakup away from tying his career high of eight, set in 2024, and one interception away from matching his career best of two, set in his rookie season.
His attention to detail, scheme fit, and consistency have all contributed to Banks’ resurgence.
The Giants reportedly tried to extend Banks’ contract during the bye week but couldn't. But fear not, as the Giants can always cut Adebo’s high-priced contract in the offseason and apply the $14 million in cap savings toward the projected $23.119 million franchise tag for cornerbacks.
In case you missed it, Tyler Nubin, the Giants’ second-round draft pick in 2024, has quietly lost his starting job to Ar’Darius Washington, who has been as solid as they come in coverage.
Washington, who had a clutch interception in Thursday night’s loss to the Commanders, currently boasts a career-best 53.5 coverage rating and has allowed just 12 of 18 targets for 82 yards (6.8 yards per reception), with only 19 yards after the catch.
Part of Washington’s rise is undoubtedly tied to his prior connection in Baltimore to head coach John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, his position coach during the 2023 season with the Ravens.
But give credit where it’s due: Washington has progressed to the point where the Giants’ one-year contract gamble on him has not only paid off but also set up a promising situation at safety if the Giants can reach an extension with him.
Zaire Barnes doesn’t get his name called very often, but opponents sure know a lot about him. An inside linebacker by trade, Barnes has made his living on special teams and has been simply invaluable in that regard.
Currently, he is tied for second in the league in solo special teams tackles (8). Add his assisted tackles, and he has 14 altogether, which ties him for first (with Donovan McMillon of the Cleveland Browns) among special teams tacklers. Barnes also has a forced fumble.
In two years with Big Blue, Barnes has 27 special teams tackles. Add in the fact that it probably wouldn’t break the bank to extend him, and this becomes as much of a no-brainer as any.

title: It's Time for the Jets to Make a Demario Davis Decision They Can't Put Off Any Longer
full_text:
The New York Jets franchise did not learn from their prior CJ Mosley mistake.
After three dominant seasons with the franchise, Mosley's age began to creep up on him. New York, loyal to its veterans and locker room leaders, tried to find ways to get him on the field until he couldn't play anymore.
By the time Mosley played his last game with the franchise, the linebacker was 31 years old.
That makes it even more surprising that the Jets seemingly made the same mistake again - this time with veteran linebacker Demario Davis. The veteran linebacker signed a two-year deal with New York at 38 years old in the offseason. New York wasn't worried at all that his advanced age far exceeded Mosley, or that Father Time could hit him harder than they thought. They just needed quality leadership at the position.
But now, New York is suffering, and Davis is a key reason why . It leaves open further questions about what the team should do at linebacker beyond 2027 and for the rest of the season.
New York is running out of options for Davis. In last Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills, the aging linebacker was one of the worst players on the field, recording a 34.6 grade from Pro Football Focus. It was the lowest grade of any Jets full-time starter in the Week 10 defeat.
"We didn’t do a good enough job; that’s the area we certainly got to be better," Davis said. "Too many explosive plays got in the red zone and didn't get off the field."
It's not like last Sunday's performance can be chalked up to one bad game, either. Davis has been one of the worst linebackers this year in the NFL. PFF has graded his 2026 season at a 40.5 grade - 82nd out of 82 linebackers.
As a leader, Davis remains an important part of New York's defense. He is in charge of getting everyone set and communicating as long as possible. But actually executing plays on defense matters more than leadership - especially for a 2-8 team.
And the tape shows Davis is a step slower than he once was.
It's only going to get worse as well, moving forward. Players don't suddenly get better when they lose a step.
It's why New York must find a way to start thinking about replacing Davis on the field in some way. They may not have answers in their backup linebacker room, but for a team needing wins to save their coach's job, Davis might have to be the first player moved.

title: Regrading Jets’ Free-Agent Signings 10 Games Into the 2026 Season
full_text:
The Jets were active in the 2026 offseason, making 17 free-agent signings, 10 of which came from other teams. These signings were meant to bolster the roster, but the Jets are 2-8 after 10 weeks in 2026, leaving more questions than answers for general manager Darren Mougey.
It is clear what type of team the Jets are 10 weeks into the season. The question is, how did they get there?
With the season more than halfway over, it is a good time to look back at some of the Jets' offseason signings and give them a new grade now that we have a sample size.
Dane Belton was signed to a one-year, $4 million contract and has been worth the money. The safety hasn't been perfect, but has performed well. Belton has struggled at times in coverage, but he leads his position with a 91.0 Pro Football Focus run-defense grade . He also ranks first at the position for solo tackles, amassing 60 so far in 2026.
The 25-year-old has been one of New York's most consistent players on the field. The defense has struggled overall, but Belton has been a bright spot on that side of the ball. He's been a stalwart in the box, even if his coverage skills could use some work.
That said, Belton has been one of the best 2026 signings for New York.
Dylan Parham has been one of the best guards in the league after signing a two-year, $16 million contract with New York. The guard has put up an 82.3 overall grade according to PFF , sixth at the position. So, why is this signing only a B? He has not been able to stay on the field.
Parham missed four weeks after a knee injury knocked him out against Detroit. He injured that same knee in Week 10 against Buffalo and now looks like he'll miss more time. The former Raider has been great when he's on the field, but staying healthy has proven an issue for Parham this season. While he has easily been the best free-agent performer on the field, he just hasn't been on the field enough.
The Jets brought Demario Davis home for the twilight of his career to the tune of two years and $22 million on his contract. The issue is that Davis clearly looks to be nearing the end of his career in the league. The 37-year-old looks his age, ranking dead last at the linebacker position with a 40.0 PFF grade.
One of the main reasons Davis was brought back was to provide veteran leadership on defense. The issue is that he has been a liability on the field . He's clearly lost a step in coverage, and his 14 missed tackles this season aren't doing New York any favors. Davis will always be a fan favorite in New York, but it is evident his time in the league is coming to an end.
If an F- grade existed, that is what this free-agent signing would get.
The Jets signed corner Nahshon Wright to a one-year, $3.5 million contract in the offseason. Wright led his position in interceptions in 2025; in 2026, he has played two snaps. The Jets basically threw money away with this deal, as Wright hasn't played.
The corner was supposed to be a ball hawk who brought an interception threat to a team that has only amassed two in the past two seasons. Instead, he is a $3.5 million check sitting on the bench. New York didn't get value for Wright at the deadline , and it would take a miracle for him to re-sign come this offseason.
Whether he is just not good enough to get on the field or not, wasting money on Wright was the wrong move by the Jets.
The Jets' largest investment in free agency was Joseph Ossai. The edge rusher was signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in the offseason and has not lived up to those expectations. Ossai has played only four games this season and has yet to record a QB pressure, much less a sack.
The defensive end has 11 total tackles in 123 snaps, so there is some promise there. Ossai's biggest issue is that he hasn't been able to stay on the field, and when he does play, he is still lacking. New York will hope Ossai improves, as he is on the books for two more years after 2026.
The Jets didn't swing big in the 2026 offseason, but they did swing a lot. New York made plenty of signings, but few have panned out. It's clear to see the Jets missed on quite a few signings as the team looks to be headed toward another season at the bottom of the NFL.
There are some bright spots, but the overall group of free agents has been a disappointment for New York this year.

title: Frank Reich Is Officially on the Clock to Save His Jets Job With Bye Week Looming
full_text:
Stop me if you've heard this before: it was another humiliating loss for the Jets on Sunday, a 31-12 defeat to the Bills that dropped Gang Green's record to 2-8 on the season.
It was not as if they completely laid an egg in the game, either, after heading into the break down four and cutting the deficit to one on their opening drive of the second half. However, the lack of adjustments and conservative approach caught up with them and led to a much too familiar outcome for Jets fans.
To be fair, injuries have taken a toll on this team all season, and that continued in the injury-riddled loss to the Bills as quarterback Geno Smith (concussion, ankle), wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (right ankle) and guard Dylan Parham (knee) dealt with setbacks of their own.
That said, it still does not account for the poor job this coaching staff has done all season in terms of failing to consistently get their best players involved on a weekly basis. Sure, head coach Aaron Glenn will continue to face a lot of the blame, but offensive coordinator Frank Reich is just as guilty and at fault amid the five-game losing streak.
Yes, he deserves credit for getting WR1 Garrett Wilson more involved with team highs in receptions (seven), targets (14) and receiving yards (106) on Sunday, but there is still no denying that he is on the clock to save his job with two favorable matchups against the Chargers (1-8) and Dolphins (1-8) coming up before a Week 13 bye.
Although seven of New York's 10 games have been decided by one score, the inability to keep pace for the duration of a game has proved costly for multiple reasons. That was no different on Sunday, when the Jets were 3-of-13 on third down, 0-of-2 in the red zone and settled for field goals in goal-to-go territory instead of getting aggressive and going for six.
The Jets were at the nine-yard line facing a fourth-and-4 with 12 seconds remaining in the first half, but rather than taking a shot in a seven-point game against a team they were not expected to beat anyway, they took the easy route on the 27-yarder. Sure, Smith was hurt on the third-down play and that may have played a factor in the decision-making, but that was still a missed opportunity.
Then, after a 10-play, 61-yard drive that took almost five minutes off the clock to begin the second half, Gang Green kicked the 22-yard field goal on a 4th-and-goal at the four-yard line.
Although another field goal on the next drive answered a Bills touchdown and kept it a one-score game, Buffalo responded two plays later with another TD— a 45-yard pass from QB Josh Allen to WR DJ Moore (h/t NFL)—to make it a 24-12 game and take control.
ALLEN TO DJ MOORE FOR 6 BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hfrUwKQlws
From there, the Jets threw an interception, punted twice, fumbled and turned it over on downs in what turned out to be a blowout loss to the Bills . That lack of aggressiveness and failure to adapt to what is happening on the field is as much on Glenn as it is on the HC, but that still does not make up for the fact that Reich's offense has struggled to execute (particularly in the red zone) and get its best players involved .
While it is not always as common for teams to fire their HC during a bye week, coordinators tend to be dismissed when the product on the field is less than ideal. After all, the extra week off gives the front office additional time to look at some film and dive into the glaring issues without the immediate turnaround of another game the next week.
That is the position the Jets could find themselves in after a two-game road trip that begins with the Chargers on Sunday. Considering the Chargers (16 ppg) and Dolphins (16.4 ppg) are two of the three worst-scoring offenses in the league and have a combined 2-16 record, the next two weeks will be crucial for Reich to at least show that he is deserving of staying around through the end of the season.
The problems run just as deep for Glenn , but Reich should be feeling just as much urgency. You could argue that making a change midseason would not entirely fix the execution flaws that have plagued this roster through the first 10 weeks, but it would also minimize disruptions and give the new coordinator an extra week to get acclimated to a different responsibility.
There is also the Cade Klubnik conundrum as Smith faces some injury concerns , especially considering the former was late on some throws in his NFL debut and seemed hesitant with some of his decision-making in his first regular-season game.
At the same time, it is Reich's job to get this offense ready to play and to feed his best players the ball for the Jets to have any chance of getting back in the win column. With two winnable games before the Week 13 bye, Reich has two more opportunities to prove himself and keep his job in Gotham before some doubts about his future reach a boiling point.

title: Firing Aaron Glenn Should Happen ASAP as Jets’ Reasons for Change Keep Piling Up
full_text:
The Jets are heading down the barrow of another loss season .
At 2-8 with seven games remaining, the  Jets face the possibility of another losing season. More importantly, the organization must confront the possibility of making another head coaching change , as its current coaching regime isn't a long-term answer.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's seat is beginning to heat up as the team continues to struggle during his tenure. Despite arriving with expectations of turning the franchise around, Glenn has struggled to establish a winning culture in New York.
The Jets, who are fresh off a loss to the rival Bills, have struggled on both sides of the ball this season. The defense, which Glenn has identified as his superpower, has often failed to deliver. Meanwhile, the offense has continued to search for consistency.
To make matters worse, the team may be without Geno Smith , who is currently sidelined with an ankle injury. Smith has put together one of his better seasons so far through 10 games; he's thrown for 2,226 passing yards, 12 touchdowns, and three interceptions on a 67.1% completion rate.
Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) hopes to play Sunday vs. Chargers, per sources. This week’s progress will determine his status but he was ‘doing good’ as of Monday and will try to push through it. pic.twitter.com/R4aN79uyOA
Based on the Jets' performance this season, Glenn is on borrowed time. Rather than waiting until the offseason, the Jets should cut bait with Glenn before the season concludes.
New York isn't officially eliminated from postseason contention, but at this point, it would take a miracle for the Jets to have a chance to represent the AFC in the 2026 NFL playoffs.
Cutting ties with Glenn would give the Jets a new voice in the locker room through the end of the season and an opportunity to salvage what has been another disappointing campaign.
The Jets' current coaching staff has several potential candidates who could take over, and the organization may already have an interim option on its roster.
Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich has extensive head coaching experience, including stops with the Panthers and Colts. Elsewhere on offense, current quarterbacks coach Bill Musgrave gives the Jets another experienced offensive mind who could be considered for the interim position.
The Jets' defensive coordinator, Brian Duker, spent time with the Lions alongside Glenn during his tenure as their defensive coordinator from 2021-24. His familiarity with Glenn's defensive philosophy could make him another potential candidate to take over the team—especially now that Duker is calling Gang Green's defensive plays.
Aaron Glenn’s “superpower” for the #Jets lasted 10 weeks. Brian Duker calling plays for the team on Sunday is further a bad look for this current defensive staff.
At times this season, the Jets have looked like a team that has given up. Bringing in a new voice could help reinvigorate the locker room and give the team an opportunity to close out the 2026 NFL season on a stronger note.

title: Jets Face a Cade Klubnik Conundrum as Geno Smith Injury Creates QB Uncertainty
full_text:
From the moment the Jets completed the trade in March, they have stood by starting quarterback Geno Smith. The veteran signal-caller struggled in Las Vegas, but was seen as a perfect bridge quarterback for the 2026 team.
In many ways, he has been. Smith has completed 67% of his passes for 2,226 yards, along with 12 touchdowns and just three interceptions. He has not been New York's biggest problem throughout their 2-8 start.
For most of the year, Smith was on a trajectory to have one of the five greatest passing seasons by a Jets quarterback. That could be in jeopardy with his new injury.
And it opens up more questions about the team's quarterback room moving forward, especially when it comes to rookie QB Cade Klubnik.
Late in the second quarter of New York's 31-12 loss to the Bills , Smith received a big hit at the goal line and was quickly shuffled into concussion protocol. Later in the third quarter, the signal-caller suffered an ankle injury and did not return.
On Monday morning, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn provided a baseline answer for where they were in understanding his injury.
"(Geno) will get imaging today just to see exactly where we're at. So again, I will have more information on that later in the week," Glenn said. Less than 24 hours later, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that the veteran QB "hopes to play" and will attempt "to push through it" in Week 11.
New York is usually quiet when it comes to injuries and the availability of players, which creates a competitive advantage over its opponents. But the team is also worse without Smith on the field. In his place, the Jets could turn to Klubnik, as they did on Sunday.
Cade Klubnik's first NFL pass is a completion to Garrett Wilson! BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Cyxg8tuqzq
In relief, Klubnik completed 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards on Sunday while also throwing an interception. He added 26 rushing yards on scrambles, but was clearly late on throws and seemed too timid at times to pull the trigger.
In short, he looked like mid-round rookie quarterback who was getting on an NFL field for the first time in his career.
As the Jets move forward, though, their current standing opens the door for more of Klubnik beyond just being a backup. Even if the team doesn't want to think that way.
Speaking to reporters on Monday, Glenn made it clear: so long as Smith is healthy, he will be the quarterback for the team.
"Geno's our starter. That hasn't changed."
But the outlook of the organization clearly is better off having Klubnik play. New York isn't going anywhere this year. The Jets' record and draft standing have them on the outside looking in for a potential top pick in the 2027 draft and a chance at a top quarterback prospect.
The Jets even admitted that if Smith wasn't healthy enough, then they would be confident in their chances to win with Klubnik starting games.
"Very confident," Glenn said. "That's why he is on the team. If Geno can't go this week, Cade will be our starter, and we'll go from there."
But there are two reasons the team will continue to start Smith.
First, they are trying to give Glenn as much benefit of the doubt as they can. Any win that can prove he was the right head coaching hire is one they will gladly take. Smith gives the team the best chance to win.
Second, with a young group of players, New York needs a quarterback who can confidently move the ball downfield through the air. Klubnik's timing and anticipation are off as a rookie (which is still natural for a player of his standing) and will need time.
Jets throw an INT but get it back on a fumble on the return BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/f5vRx8b3m1
If the Jets were to start Klubnik, that would affect the development and film study of many of their young receivers .
So while it is best for the Jets to lose the remainder of their games for a top overall pick, the team's current standing and their belief in Glenn are why the team won't turn to Klubnik full time unless they have to.
New York still has plenty of decisions to make moving forward. As the team waits to see whether they can play Smith going into their road contest against the Chargers on Sunday, the Jets must soon decide on practice squad quarterback Will Levis.
The rival Patriots just lost Drake Maye to a reported broken ankle . Other teams around the league are also in need of quality quarterbacks moving forward.
If the Jets don't promote Levis to the active roster, another team like the Patriots may poach him away. That means they would lose out on a quality backup option should Klubnik get hurt at any point.
The Jets need to be proactive as a front office regarding their quarterback room, or else their outlook might get even worse.

title: Breaking Down Jets’ Injury Outlook to Begin Week 11 (Who’s Hurt & Who Could Return vs. Chargers)
full_text:
Because of the NFL's aggressive and physical nature, it’s nearly impossible for a team to finish a game without a player suffering an injury. While injuries are part of the game, some teams sustain more injuries than others, which ultimately affects how their season plays out.
The Jets are one of those teams.
New York has dealt with countless injuries on both sides of the ball, particularly on offense, where its full starting unit hadn’t played together since Week 1. That changed in Week 10, as all of the Jets’ original starters played against the Bills: for one snap.
Omar Cooper Jr. sustained an ankle injury on the first play and didn’t return to the game. Dylan Parham and Geno Smith also suffered injuries and were unable to return.
With Gang Green players continuing to go down, let’s take a look at the Jets' injuries heading into Week 11’s matchup with the Chargers.
Even though Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was listed as a limited participant on Friday, he was ruled out against the Bills with an illness. The former Louisville Cardinal has had an up-and-down season, recording 11 total tackles and a sack across eight games.
Despite this, New York continues to turn to him as the team’s starting nickelback ahead of second-round selection D’Angelo Ponds . In Brownlee’s absence, however, the Jets opted to use Malachi Moore as the fifth defensive back in sub-packages over Ponds.
If Brownlee is either a full or limited participant in the Jets' upcoming practices, we should expect him to play against the Chargers.
Injuries have derailed Kiko Mauigoa’s sophomore season. The former Florida State Seminole has dealt with a nagging quadriceps injury, which has forced him to miss seven of the team’s first 10 games.
Since re-injuring his quad in Week 6 against the Patriots, Mauigoa has been on injured reserve, but he is eligible to return for Week 11’s matchup with the Chargers. The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt reported Friday that Mauigoa was one of seven players on injured reserve who were working out off to the side of practice .
Lots of injured Jets working out off to the side to start practice: T’Vondre Sweat David Onyemata Marcelino McCrary-Ball Kiko Mauigoa Max Mitchell Tyler Baron Anez Cooper
This doesn’t mean Mauigoa will play next Sunday, but his appearance at practice indicates that he’s ramping up and getting closer to making a return.
Trevin Wallace was the only player who didn’t participate in any of the Jets’ practices last week and, as a result, was ruled out for Week 10’s matchup due to a groin injury. Although the injury has sidelined him for the past two weeks, it hasn’t had major consequences for New York’s special teams.
Even though Wallace hasn’t impressed in this role, recording just three total tackles and earning a 63.9 special teams grade , per Pro Football Focus ,  the team could use all the contributors it can get after allowing a 95-yard kickoff return for a touchdown to Dylan Laube two weeks ago.
If Wallace can be a full participant in any of the team’s practices this week, we should anticipate his return to the lineup next Sunday.
For the third time this season, Cooper has had his ankle rolled up on. The first time was against the Titans in Week 1, which landed him on injured reserve, and the second was in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
Although the severity of the injury is still unknown, head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that he was undergoing imaging today (h/t Dennis Waszak Jr.) If Cooper is a no-go, the Jets will rely on Isaiah Williams in the slot.
Aaron Glenn says QB Geno Smith (along with WR Omar Cooper Jr. and LG Dylan Parham) will have imaging today for their injuries. Glenn says Smith is the #Jets ' starter (not Cade Klubnik) if he's healthy. "If Geno can't go this week, Cade will be the starter."
Parham went down in the second quarter against Buffalo with a knee injury, the same one he injured in Week 3 against the Lions. Like Cooper and Smith, Parham underwent imaging today, but the severity of the injury is unknown, and his status for the team’s matchup against the Chargers remains uncertain.
If he can’t suit up, New York will task Jordan Meredith with starting at left guard.
Smith exited twice during the team’s loss to the Bills. The first time was for a concussion evaluation, after which he was cleared; the second time was for an ankle injury.
According to ESPN’s Ian Rapoport, Smith underwent testing today, which didn’t reveal anything major. While this suggests Smith shouldn’t miss extended time, it doesn’t indicate whether he’ll play in Week 11.
#Jets QB Geno Smith, who dealt with a variety of injuries on Sunday, underwent tests today that did not reveal anything major, sources say. Smith, whose ankle provided the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week. But so far, so good. pic.twitter.com/kJH0S7ZWg5
If Smith is available and practices during the week, we should expect the 14-year veteran to suit up. But if he doesn’t, New York will turn to rookie Cade Klubnik as its starter. Although Klubnik showed some flashes, he needs more time and reps before he can be a reliable starter.
The Jets have a lengthy list of players on the injured reserve.
Tyler Baron (knee), Anez Cooper (shoulder), Marcelino McCrary-Ball (ankle), Max Mitchell (head/concussion), David Onyemata (groin), and T’Vondre Sweat (ACL sprain) are all on the short-term injured reserve list and are eligible to return this season.
Of these six players, all but Cooper were seen working to the side at Friday's practice.
Meanwhile, Kingsley Jonathan (thigh bruise), Braiden McGregor (torn pectoral), Arian Smith (torn ACL), and Chip Traynaum (neck) are sidelined for the rest of the season.

title: Jets Rookie & Sophomore Power Rankings Week 11: What's Changed as Losing Streak Reaches 5 Games?
full_text:
Another week, another Jets loss. This time, New York fell to division rival Buffalo, 31-12, at MetLife Stadium.
Many of the same costly mistakes continue to persist, with the team struggling to score touchdowns in the red zone and failing to contain the run. With Gang Green falling to 2-8, they are on track to miss the playoffs for the 16th consecutive season, and head coach Aaron Glenn’s tenure in New York is all but over.
Until that time comes, fans will have to suffer through another second half of the season in which the Jets aren’t playing for anything. Despite this, some of the young players have inspired hope that 2027 could look different.
With that said, let’s take a look at where the rookies and sophomores rank heading into New York’s Week 11 matchup against the Chargers.
Note: Anez Cooper is currently excluded from the list, as he is on injured reserve.
We have a new addition to the rankings as VJ Payne made his NFL debut Sunday.
The former Kansas State Wildcat was placed on injured reserve after sustaining a bone bruise during training camp, which sidelined him for the first nine games. After being a full participant in practice for the last two weeks and after the Jets traded Andre Cisco to the Lions, Payne assumed his role on special teams, appearing in 14 snaps .
Although he didn’t play any defensive snaps, we should expect to see him receive an opportunity once New York is officially ruled out of the playoffs.
The Jets will need to upgrade several position groups this offseason, including the wide receiver room. Beyond Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper Jr., New York’s receivers have struggled to create consistent separation and haven’t provided much contribution this season.
This was shown against the Bills, as Wilson and Mitchell combined for 168 of the team’s 288 receiving yards, while Cooper went down on the first offensive play. One receiver who must show significant improvement to remain with the Jets is Arian Smith.
The former 2025 fourth-round selection has been extremely underwhelming, recording just seven receptions for 52 yards across 18 games. Although an ACL injury in Week 2 prematurely ended his season, Smith didn’t have a role in the offense, playing in just three offensive snaps.
With New York likely to reinforce the position in the offseason, Smith must make significant progress, or he’ll be elsewhere in 2027.
Kiko Mauigoa has had an injury-riddled year. The former 2025 fifth-round selection has appeared in just three games this season and is currently on injured reserve with a quadriceps injury.
Mauigoa’s absence hasn’t been a major loss for the Jets, as he’s exclusively played on special teams. But with Mauigoa eligible to return from injured reserve next week, he could get his first defensive reps against the Chargers.
With New York trending towards missing the playoffs and Demario Davis significantly regressing this season, the Jets must give Mauigoa an opportunity to show what he can do on defense.
With Cisco traded last week, Malachi Moore entered the matchup as the team’s backup safety behind Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick.
Despite his bump up the depth chart, no one expected Moore to play meaningful snaps, given that New York has primarily relied on Belton and Fitzpatrick. However, with Jarvis Brownlee Jr. inactive, the former 2025 fourth-round selection played a season-high 27 defensive snaps against Buffalo
Although Moore recorded three total tackles, he didn’t play particularly well in coverage, giving up a 45-yard touchdown to D.J. Moore and committing a controversial pass interference penalty on 2nd-and-11, which led to a touchdown four plays later.
With New York unlikely to make the playoffs, Moore should continue to see opportunities for the remainder of the season. But if he wants to maintain a rotational role under the new coaching staff, he’ll have to improve in coverage moving forward.
Geno Smith left Sunday’s game twice due to injuries, thrusting rookie Cade Klubnik into action. In his NFL debut, the former Clemson Tiger completed 11 of his 20 passes for 137 yards and one interception, and picked up 27 yards on the ground.
While Klubnik flashed on his first drive, leading New York to a 10-play, 61-yard drive that resulted in a field goal, he made some rookie mistakes. At times, he held onto the ball too long and missed on several check-down throws while looking deep.
These mistakes are expected from a rookie, so we can’t be too critical of Klubnik, especially since it's his first time getting reps. This won’t be the last time we see Klubnik this season.
With the Jets dropping to 2-8 and Glenn not providing an immediate update on Smith’s status, Klubnik could make his first career start against the Chargers.
We’ll know for certain once Smith’s availability becomes clearer through the week.
With Brownlee inactive, New York surprisingly opted to use Moore over D’Angelo Ponds.
The second-round pick played just seven defensive snaps against the Bills, yet Ponds made the most of his opportunity, recording a pass deflection that forced Buffalo to punt.
Limited action has been the theme of Ponds’s rookie season. The former Indian Hoosier has played just 94 defensive snaps across eight games, recording seven total tackles in this span.
Although Ponds has had growing pains at nickelback, New York must live with those mistakes and give him more reps in the coming weeks, given it’s all but officially eliminated from the playoffs.
There was hope that Kenyon Sadiq would build on last week’s performance and be involved in the game plan against the Bills. Unfortunately, that didn’t happen, as Sadiq finished with one reception for three yards.
The former Oregon Duck has experienced an up-and-down season. Through 10 games, Sadiq has registered 22 receptions on 30 targets for 238 yards and one touchdown. The majority of that production, however, came against the Lions and Chiefs, where he combined for 11 receptions, 154 yards, and a touchdown.
Sadiq has displayed high-end receiving potential with his explosiveness and athleticism, but offensive coordinator Frank Reich just hasn’t made an effort to utilize his skill set, as he’s been targeted less than three times in eight games.
This must change next week against the Chargers, as the Jets must find ways to get the young tight end more involved.
In his first three games since coming back from a thumb injury, Mason Taylor had become a trusted target of Smith, recording 12 receptions for 114 yards and two touchdowns. Despite this, Taylor hasn’t been nearly as impactful in the past three games, logging just eight receptions for 50 yards.
While the former LSU Tiger is partially to blame, as penalties and his lack of creating separation have played a part, the Jets’ offense just hasn’t been productive. The unit is averaging 19 points over the past three games and has struggled mightily to score in the red zone.
At 6'5", 255 lbs, Taylor is an ideal target in the red zone, but he just hasn’t been involved much in this area. While it hasn’t been a great season for Taylor, he’s shown potential to be a quality, all-around tight end.
It's National Tight Ends Day and Mason Taylor is joining the party MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F72SqDOTVz
Hopefully, he can close out the season on a high note and be more involved in the passing game.
With David Onyemata and T’Vondre Sweat sidelined, Darrell Jackson Jr. has been integral to the Jets’ interior line rotation. In each of the past five games, Jackson has played at least 30 defensive snaps, recording 19 total tackles, 10 stops, and four pressures.
While he’s shown flashes of a quality rotational player thanks to his size and tackling ability, it hasn’t translated into success for New York’s defense. The unit still struggles to contain the run, ranking 30th in the league in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3).

title: Aaron Glenn's Biggest Mistake vs. Bills (And What Jets Need to Change in Week 11)
full_text:
Despite making it competitive in the first half, the Jets once again failed to keep pace throughout Week 10 as they suffered a 31-12 loss to the Bills , dropping their fifth consecutive game as the season continues to unravel from them.
The Jets were even the healthiest they have been in a long time coming into the game and seemed ready to at least put up a compelling fight. That quickly proved to not be the case as rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. exited early after getting his right ankle rolled on and quarterback Geno Smith left the game twice after getting evaluated for a concussion and suffering an ankle injury after he returned.
While the special teams unit did its part and kicker Jason Sanders was a perfect 4-of-4 on his field goals, the same issues remained in the injury-riddled loss to the Bills . The Jets kept it close in the first half and only trailed 10-6 going into the break, but they were just 3-of-13 on third down, 0-of-2 in the red zone, committed seven penalties for 53 yards and allowed four sacks.
Aside from the two drives that ended in made field goals from Sanders in the second half, the Jets punted twice, threw an interception, committed a fumble and turned it over on downs. To make matters worse, the fumble took place as they were nearing the red zone, trailing 24-12.
The Bills immediately made them pay as running back James Cook broke free for a 74-yard touchdown run on the next play (h/t NFL).
74-YARD TD FOR JAMES COOK BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DFRLVP17FL
From head coach Aaron Glenn's lack of adjustments coming out of the locker room to his conservative nature as he continues to settle for field goals, the same problems continue to plague the Jets each week.
He has made it clear that play-calling is his "superpower," but Glenn has done nothing to back that notion up so far and even gave his play-calling to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, who had zero prior experience calling plays. That is just the latest bad look for a HC who is now 5-22 in Gotham and 0-9 against AFC East opponents.
That said, here's the biggest mistake that Glenn made on Sunday.
Coming into the game, it was going to be key for the defense to create pressure on Bills QB Josh Allen and keep him from using his mobility to make them pay. While they limited his production on the ground (five carries for five yards), he still had three total TDs (two rushing) and was only sacked once.
The Jets knew beforehand that Buffalo had the highest-scoring offense in the league (31.9 ppg) and a susceptible pass defense (241.9 ypg), so it was going to be important for them to be as aggressive as possible offensively to keep pace and limit the big plays defensively.
Not only were the Jets 0-of-2 in the red zone, but they got inside the 10-yard-line twice and even advanced the ball to the four-yard-line before settling for field goals both times. Instead of trying to tie the game at 10 before the half and going for the lead coming out of the break, the Jets played not to lose again and paid the price as the Bills converted their drives into TDs.
As a result, the Jets were playing from behind the entire game and it only seemed like a matter of time until the Bills pulled away. That is exactly what happened as Cook and the run game combined for 201 yards and 6.3 yards per carry to wear the defense down.
Glenn noted that "it's hard to win games when you operate that way," per Sports Illustrated's Nick Faria, when referring to the decision to opt for field goals.
It remains to be seen if Glenn takes back over the play-calling duties or not, but as poor as the second-half adjustments continue to be on that side, the lack of aggressiveness in short-yardage situations and heavy reliance on field goals is not going to cut it with a 2-8 record.
As the Jets prepare for a two-game road trip against the Chargers on Sunday and the Dolphins on Nov. 29, you would think that would be a favorable stretch for them against two of the bottom-dwelling teams in the league. Sure, the Dolphins beat them back in Week 7, but these should be two winnable games for Gang Green regardless if they play to their potential.
As a team that struggles with turnovers, protecting QB Justin Herbert and ranks last in scoring offense, the opportunity is in front of the Jets to capitalize on those vulnerabilities on Sunday. In addition to eliminating the self-inflicting penalties and getting more aggressive when points are available, Glenn needs to commit to a defensive play-caller and get his group to generate more pressure.
DC Brian Duker: "our group has really embraced our approach" pic.twitter.com/5ZA3HgfQia
Glenn and offensive coordinator Frank Reich need to make sure the best players are continuously being fed the ball, as well as getting off to quicker starts to set the tone from the opening kick. Additionally, the aggressiveness on both sides needs to be a priority, whether it be more disguises or pressure looks defensively or more explosiveness offensively.
Glenn continues to sink lower as his time remaining in Gotham runs thin, and if he cannot be more adaptable throughout the game and ramp up his aggressiveness, it is hard to see much changing.

title: Geno Smith Injury Makes Drafting a QB an Even Bigger Jets Priority in 2027
full_text:
On top of everything else that went wrong on Sunday, Geno Smith suffered an ankle injury after taking a hit to his lower body in the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills. The 36-year-old quarterback played only one drive in the second half, ceding the rest to rookie Cade Klubnik.
While Smith's injury may not end his season, questions remain.
Smith was a long shot to be anything more than a bridge quarterback. The Jets' record and Smith injury make that fact painfully obvious. With Smith's expiring contract and Klubnik behind him, New York will have to start worrying about what to do at the position.
With three first-round picks in the 2027 draft, the Jets must decide whether to use any of them on a QB.
Smith is not getting any younger. The QB is also only on a one-year, veteran minimum contract. Smith's injury is unfortunate if he misses time, but it might be a sign that the answer to the Jets' woes is still out there. When Klubnik was on the field, it was very clear what Smith has been lacking.
Smith is clearly one of the elder statesmen at the quarterback position. He is a Honda in a league full of Ferraris, serviceable but leagues away from other top QBs. Smith lacks escapability, as shown by his taking the third-most sacks in the league in 2026. That was even more evident once Klubnik took his place in Week 10.
Cade Klubnik's first NFL pass is a completion to Garrett Wilson! BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Cyxg8tuqzq
Klubnik brought movement into the pocket immediately. The rookie had 26 rushing yards against Buffalo. Smith has 54 rushing yards for the whole season. Mobility at quarterback is crucial in today's NFL, and Smith clearly lacks it. His injury proves that point further.
Whether or not Smith misses extended time, his inability to escape the pocket has been a bane to the Jets' offensive success.
At 36, Smith was never supposed to be the franchise quarterback. Despite his success throwing the football this season, his age has shown in his play. With his lack of mobility leading to an injury, it's evident the Jets must start thinking about which young buck is going to take his place in 2027.
The bad news is the Jets are in the NFL's cellar with a 2-8 record. The good news is that they currently hold two picks in the first six picks of the draft . This would give New York an opportunity to do something it hasn't since 2021: draft a QB in the first round.
With Smith's injury, depending how severe it might be, this may become an even higher priority.
Klubnik had flashes on the field, but he looked like what he was: a fourth-round pick. Between an interception, some accuracy issues, and holding the ball too long, Klubnik didn't look like the savior Gang Green has been waiting for. While he figures to get more time to stake his claim, Klubnik has a mountain to climb if he wants to change minds about drafting high at the position.
Smith's injury has shown that Klubnik isn't ready to take the helm of an NFL franchise just yet. The rookie showed talent, but the project seems longer than that of a top-five pick. Smith's injury could mean the Jets may have to invest come April if they are looking for a franchise savior.

title: Jets' Aaron Glenn Problems Run Much Deeper Than the Surface
full_text:
It was a mistake the moment Jets head coach Aaron Glenn uttered those words.
At the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine in Indianapolis, Glenn defended his decision to call plays for the defense this year. Glenn claimed play-calling was his "superpower" and was excited to pass along the success he found in Detroit to New York.
Perhaps that was the first indicator that things would not go well for the Jets this season.
Glenn's Jets are 2-8 following their dismal 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. It was also the first game Glenn seemed to give up play-calling to defensive coordinator Brian Duker—the same man the team was confident in believing they wouldn't need to turn to for those duties.
Aaron Glenn’s “superpower” for the #Jets lasted 10 weeks. Brian Duker calling plays for the team on Sunday is further a bad look for this current defensive staff.
There are many reasons why the Glenn era has failed. But his play-calling decisions and struggles to get the most out of his talented rookie class show that his 5-22 head coaching record is only the surface of his problems.
Glenn announced on Monday that Duker was the one who actually called plays. He also didn't commit to calling plays in the future for the remainder of the season.
"I gave Duker the lead when it comes to that, but again, I'm still a huge part of what we call," Glenn said. "There's been a collaboration throughout the whole season, to be honest with you. I had the lead the first game going up until this point, and this game, I wanted to give him the lead."
There are different ways to look at this decision from Glenn.
All these three options are more alarming than the next. And it also highlights the full failings of Glenn as a coach. The open bravado he first displayed to the media and fans is long gone. Instead, they have been replaced by a coach unable to answer questions his team has.
And it's only compounding the issues the team is dealing with.
The Jets simply don't know how to use the talent currently on their roster. That much was clear by the end of the first month of the regular season, and it's gotten worse since.
New York made four draft selections inside the first 50 overall picks. Each player has had an impressive play or game to show the team has quality things to build on with this young core.
There's just one problem—these small plays aren't being built up like they should.
In Sunday's loss, second-round cornerback D'Angelo Ponds received just seven defensive snaps compared to 28 for third safety Malachi Moore. Ponds was the third-highest-graded Jets defender by Pro Football Focus, compared to Moore, whose 28.6 grade was the lowest on the team.
" He's still not there yet , and I think he would tell you the same thing, but he's improving every week," Glenn said on Monday.
Turn your attention to the offensive side, and the confusion is even more so. 16th overall pick and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq caught one pass all game—a screen pass on the first play on offense. The play went for three yards and led to the injury of fellow first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr.
Why was Cooper—a player dealing with an ankle injury going into the game—blocking on a screen pass that can see players get rolled up on consistently? Why did the Jets only target Sadiq once on a screen?
These are questions the Jets haven't had answers to. Their most consistent defense, though, is that there "is only one ball to go around."
But do the San 49ers have trouble getting the ball to Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Mike Evans, Keenan Allen or their full collection of receivers? Of course not. Because their play-caller understands matchups and is able to scheme people open. New York's staff cannot.
And that is a direct reflection of how poor they have been under Glenn this season.
