title: 3 Reasons Why Eagles Have a Realistic Shot at Upsetting the Steelers in Week 11
full_text:
The Eagles will attempt to snap a seven-game losing streak when they host the Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field in Week 11. The two Pennsylvania squads haven't met head-to-head in the regular season since 2024, when Philadelphia triumphed 27-13 en route to winning Super Bowl LIX.
Pittsburgh boasts a 6-3 record and enters as a 4.5-point road favorite on FanDuel Sportsbook . Of course, that projection matters little once the players step on the field on Sunday afternoon .
Here are three reasons why the Eagles have a realistic shot at upsetting the visiting Steelers.
Running the football and protecting quarterback Aaron Rodgers has been the foundation of the Steelers' success this year. It's how they control the clock and avoid turnovers. Pittsburgh's offensive line has successfully carried out that strategy at home, but has faltered away from Acrisure Stadium.
Rodgers has been sacked just six times across four home victories. The veteran gunslinger has been sacked 20 times across five away games (2-3 record). Pittsburgh is also the only team in the NFL that has yet to score a rushing touchdown on the road. That's a big enough sample size to cause concern.
Boye Mafe gets the third sack of the game for the Bengals 🗣️ PITvsCIN on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pHk4cKIkEs
It's worth noting that Pittsburgh left guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury in Week 10 that is expected to sideline him beyond Week 11. This is a matchup that Philly's Moro Ojomo, Nolan Smith and Jonathan Greenard can exploit. A few timely sacks could be the difference in a low-scoring duel.
Injuries have played a crucial role in Philadelphia's struggles in the passing game this season. Pro Bowl wide receiver DeVonta Smith has only appeared in four of the Eagles' nine games as he deals with a hamstring injury. Dontayvion Wicks has missed the last three weeks with an ankle injury.
Both players are trending in the right direction ahead of Week 11, though. Their returns would provide a huge boost for quarterback Joe Milton. Smith is a crisp route-runner and has the body control to haul in contested catches. Wicks provides versatility and excels at tracking deep balls through the air.
My understanding is that the #Eagles expect DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks to return after the bye or shortly thereafter and are now in a position where they want to provide younger players more opportunities… https://t.co/epaEgIwSbj
The Steelers have surrendered at least 89 yards to an opposing receiver in each of their three losses. That includes when Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase tallied 231 yards on 11 receptions in Week 10. Relying on Milton's rocket of an arm to feed Smith and Wicks the ball could be the recipe for an upset victory.
The Steelers have lost 11 straight games in Philadelphia. It's a streak that dates all the way back to 1965. The past three clashes at Lincoln Financial Field haven't been close, either. The Eagles smoked the Steelers 27-13 in 2024, crushed them 35-13 in 2022, and destroyed them 34-6 in 2016.
It's clear that Philly's passionate fan base makes its presence felt whenever the Steelers come to town. Don't expect that to change on Sunday, despite the team's losing record. The Eagles have drawn in 349,395 fans through five home games (per ESPN ). That's the 10th-highest total in the NFL.
There's one more trend to point out. Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy is well known in Philly from his time leading the Packers and Cowboys. He sports a lackluster 4-5 head-coaching record at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles will take any edge they can get in hopes of ending their skid.

title: Sean Mannion Is Officially in the Hot Seat as Eagles Return to Action in Week 11
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ bye week is over. The self-scout is done. The excuses have a shelf life, and that shelf life expires for Sean Mannion on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Mannion’s first season as Eagles offensive coordinator has been a disaster. The numbers are ugly. The process has looked messy. The results have been even worse.
Head coach Nick Sirianni—and by extension, GM Howie Roseman and owner Jeffrey Lurie—has stuck by the unconventional hire through a seven-game losing streak and a 2-7 record overall. That said, any patience that was granted in September and October due to the attrition now has to be earned in the final eight games if Mannion wants any hope of a sequel.
Getting back starting receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks , and potentially running back Will Shipley, does not require a 180-degree transformation. It does require proof that Mannion can elevate players through adversity instead of simply managing their absences.
Smith and Wicks have been the clearest examples of Mannion's rocky start. When both receivers have been healthy, the offense has at least looked like it has a pulse. When they have not, the drop-off has been steep, and the supporting cast has not been maximized.
That is the difference between a coordinator who is scheme-centric and one who gets the most out of what is available on a given Sunday.
Smith remains elite when healthy and is the most reliable separator on the roster; Wicks has shown he can win with his route running. Reintegrating both should make the passing game less one-dimensional, even with the inexperienced Joe Milton at the controls.
If the same late-to-the-line, overloaded-at-the-snap issues that have plagued the unit persist even with those two back, you can rest assured the problem is not solely personnel.
Shipley’s potential return also adds another layer. He is not Saquon Barkley, but he is a legitimate complementary back who can handle a share of the load and contribute to the passing game.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
The Eagles have been thin at running back for large stretches of this season. Adding a functional piece behind Barkley should help. It also gives Mannion another chance to show he can build a more balanced attack rather than leaning on whatever is least injured against Pittsburgh.
The bye week gave the staff time to self-scout without the immediate pressure of a game plan. The Eagles also added old friend T.J. Paganetti , a run-game specialist, as a consultant on Monday. Those levers have to prove to be useful.
Any film sessions and schematic adjustments only matter if they show up in how the offense performs against the Steelers, an AFC playoff contender that hasn’t won in Philadelphia since 1965.
The Eagles don’t need Mannion to suddenly become the next Sean McVay. They do need him to demonstrate that his system can still function when key pieces are available, that the communication issues can be cleaned up, and that available players can be put in positions to succeed rather than simply asked to survive.
It’s esoteric and somewhat intangible, but that’s the bar for continued patience. Not a complete overhaul. Not a sudden jump into the top half of the league in scoring. Just clear evidence that the coordinator can raise the level of the players he has when they are actually on the field.
If that evidence does not appear soon, the conversation around the rest of the season will shift from “give Mannion time” to speculation about the next OC.
The bye was the intermission after a disastrous first act. Sunday is Mannion's first opportunity to prove that lessons were learned during the adversity.

title: Eagles Must Break the Chains Off These 3 Underused Players Coming out of Bye
full_text:
With a sixth consecutive playoff berth now just a distant dream, the back half of the 2026 NFL season should be all about development for the Eagles. If they're wise, they'll use their eight remaining games to give added on-field opportunity to some younger players to help them gain experience and confidence for the 2027 season and beyond.
With that in mind, here's a look at three underused Eagles who need to be unleashed from their shackles now that the bye week has passed.
Even though they held onto veteran tight end Dallas Goedert through the 2026 NFL trade deadline, the Eagles still need to unleash rookie Eli Stowers over the back half of the season to see exactly what they have in the young player after using a second-round pick to acquire him last April.
The fact that they drafted him in the second round demonstrates that the Eagles view Stowers very highly, but we haven't gotten to see much of him so far this season. He was sidelined for the first six weeks due to injury issues, and he's played sparingly since his return over the past three weeks. In total, he's tallied three receptions for 53 yards this season.
Coming out of the bye, the Birds need to break the chains off him.
By the time most people had turned the game off, Eli Stowers caught and ran this completely meaningless 34 yard pass to end the game. That ONE catch was enough to move him into 2nd place in receiving yards among Eagles TEs this season. He passed Mundt, who has played every… https://t.co/TCRQkY0u6w pic.twitter.com/bf5IwY4zFm
With Dallas Goedert heading to free agency, the Eagles will have to figure out how to properly address the tight end position over the offseason, and they won't be able to do that unless they have a better idea of what Stowers can bring to the field at this level. Getting him ample reps in relatively low-stakes games should be a priority for Philadelphia moving forward this season.
Edge rusher is a consistent area of need for Philadelphia, so they should see what they have in rookie Keyshawn James-Newby, whom they drafted in the seventh round in the draft in April.
The Eagles were prepared to trade linebacker Arnold Ebiketie at the deadline until the Bengals backed out of the deal . This shows that Ebiketie isn't in Philadelphia's plans beyond the current campaign, so some of his snaps should be reallocated to James-Newby, who has appeared in just two games so far this season. He flashed some potential during his limited time, though, including recording two pressures against the Panthers in Week 6.
The final eight games of the season will provide a perfect opportunity for the Eagles to increase his workload and see what kind of contributor he could be.
As the team's top pick from the 2026 draft, Makai Lemon has been receiving playing time all season. However, his role has expanded dramatically in recent weeks because the team's top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontavious Wicks, have been sidelined due to injury issues.
Even if those guys are back in the fold in the coming weeks , the Eagles should still continue to give Lemon a larger load.
Lemon has shown some real potential in recent weeks. During that time, he has shown an impressive ability to create separation and get open, and he's also displayed some good hands, despite a couple of drops. He's tallied at least six receptions and 55-plus yards in three straight games for Philadelphia, despite inconsistent quarterback play.
Makai Lemon has shown flashes On pace for 70 Rec 589 yds 2 TD For an offense that’s mightily struggled future is bright for the kid! #FlyEaglesFly pic.twitter.com/PElS4TiabE
Allowing Lemon to continue gaining experience and confidence should be the Eagles' goal over the back half of the season. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion should aim to feature him prominently moving forward.
Otherwise, he isn't doing his job right.

title: Breaking Down Eagles' Injury Report Coming Out of Their Bye (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return in Week 11)
full_text:
Injuries can quickly derail an NFL campaign. The Eagles have fallen victim to that notion in 2026, losing several starters during a disappointing seven-game losing streak . Returning to full health will be crucial to snapping the skid and being competitive in the second half of the season.
The Eagles' Week 10 bye provided extra rest for sidelined players ahead of a matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 11. The team's first injury report of the week will be released following Wednesday's practice.
For now, let's take a peek at those on the mend in the City of Brotherly Love.
The Eagles have been without wide receiver DeVonta Smith for five of their nine games, as he deals with a hamstring injury. Philadelphia has been careful in this situation for a reason. Hamstring issues can be especially tricky for pass-catchers who rely on acceleration and change of direction in routes.
The news surrounding Smith is trending in the right direction ahead of Week 11. The Eagles released wide receiver Hollywood Brown, suggesting the team is banking on Smith being back on the field soon. The 28-year-old has tallied 310 yards and two touchdowns on 26 receptions (41 targets).
Smith isn't the only wide receiver Eagles fans are anxiously awaiting to recover. Dontayvion Wicks sustained an ankle injury in the fourth quarter of Philadelphia's Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The hope is that four weeks of rest are enough to get the exciting offseason acquisition back in the lineup.
Pay attention to Smith and Wicks's status on Wednesday's injury report. Even limited participation would be a big step toward playing on Sunday afternoon. Their returns would be a notable boost for quarterback Joe Milton. He completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards in his Eagles debut in Week 9.
Linebacker Jihaad Campbell played 37 snaps against the Cowboys in Week 7 before he needed to be replaced due to hamstring and quad injuries. The Alabama product was then sidelined in Week 8 and Week 9. A return to practice, in any fashion, will be the first step to getting Campbell back on the field.
Campbell's absence has opened the door for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to play an every-down role at linebacker. He led the Eagles with 11 tackles (three tackles for loss) in Week 9's loss to the Giants. Keep an eye on how defensive coordinator Vic Fangio splits linebacker snaps once Campbell recovers.
Defensive back Michael Carter II suffered an abdominal strain in Week 5. The veteran returned to play in Week 8 but aggravated the injury in one snap. There hasn't been a concrete update on his status, other than the fact that he did not practice prior to being ruled out in Week 9. Expect clarity this week.
Carter allowed a 56.3 passer rating when targeted and just 5.5 yards per reception before going down (per PFF ). His return would be welcomed in a secondary that has been subpar as of late. Safety Andrew Mukuba is missing tackles, while cornerback Kenny Moore II is struggling in coverage .
Return specialist Britain Covey sustained a knee injury on Week 7's opening kickoff. He did not return to the game or practice before Philly's bye. Covey was not placed on injured reserve, though, so his activation should be near. Makai Lemon and Cooper DeJean will field kicks/punts in the meantime.
Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 17 and isn't expected to return this season. The three-time Pro Bowler suffered a calf injury in Week 4, which caused severe blood clots to form. Those clots moved to his lungs. Hurts is under contract with the Eagles through 2028.
Philadelphia has opened the 21-day practice window for running back Will Shipley. The third-year pro had logged 88 total yards and one touchdown on 25 touches before going down with a foot injury. Fellow running back Tank Bigsby does not yet have a timetable to heal from a core muscle issue.
Other members of the Eagles' IR list include WR Johnny Wilson (knee), S Andre' Sam (foot) and S Tucker Large (knee).

title: Kracz: 5 Things Eagles Fans Should Know as the Bye Week Ends
full_text:
The Week 10 action is officially over, so now is the perfect time to catch up with the Eagles as they come out of their bye week . Here are five things that every Philadelphia fan must know heading into Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season.
When we last saw quarterback Joe Milton, he was sacked seven times while completing just 53 percent of his 34 passes in a 19-11 home loss to the Giants. Not great, but he wasn’t ready after being here for just three weeks. He made plays with his legs, though, and led the team in rushing with 64 yards on nine carries.
Milton will likely get the start on Sunday against the Steelers. Still, Sirianni could always change his mind on Wednesday, as he did when he infamously said, "Tanner's our guy," then benched McKee for Milton just days before the Eagles hosted the Giants.
This is what Sirianni said about Milton after losing to New York:
Still, Milton's fate is tied to the whims of his head coach.
The QB was asked how he would spend the bye week. He said he would probably take two days off, then get back to learning the Eagles’ system.
“I just want to be better,” he said. “We want to be better as a team.”
The Eagles went three-and-out and punted three times to start the second half, allowing the Giants to take control.
It’s not the first time the offense has been so inept for long stretches in games this year. In fact, offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s unit has gone three-and-out on 43% of its offensive possessions, which is the highest rate of any team in the last three seasons and the highest rate for any Eagles team in the 21st century.
The Eagles filled two of the four openings on their 53-man roster, adding offensive lineman John Ojukwu and tight end Zach Ertz on Monday. Expect Ertz to make his march to the franchise record for most catches in an Eagles career. He needs eight more to break the mark of 589 set by Harold Carmichael from 1971-1983. In a lost season, at least it’s something.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
The flip side is what happens with developmental second-round pick Eli Stowers. The rookie tight end got just seven snaps against the Giants.
The hole in the NFC East didn’t get much deeper for them during their week off, with the first-place Giants losing and the Cowboys stumbling again in Week 10. Still, the hole was already plenty deep enough to entertain any thoughts about making a late push to the top.
At 2-7 and incapable of winning a game since Sept. 20, Philadelphia is four games behind New York (5-3-1) in the loss column and entrenched in last place in the division.
It was a stunning move to see general manager Howie Roseman move on from Jordan Davis , a defensive tackle that he just opened the vault for in the offseason, but the return of a first-round pick next year and a second in 2028 was too great to pass up.
As for Arnold Ebiketie, the Eagles thought they had a deal done with the Bengals to get a sixth-round pick next year, but Cincinnati messed up and had to back out . So, it might be a tad awkward for the outside linebacker when he shows up in the locker room.

title: T.J. Paganetti Reunion Could Shed Light on Eagles' Mindset as They Return From Bye
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — As they return from their bye week , the Eagles are bringing back T.J. Paganetti in a consulting role, a league source confirmed to Sports Illustrated .
The move mirrors previous outside voices the organization has brought in during the Nick Sirianni era, including Jim Bob Cooter in 2021 and Marcus Brady in 2022, not to mention Vic Fangio during the run-up to Super Bowl LVII.
Paganetti’s expertise is in offensive concepts—particularly the run game. Sirianni will speak on Wednesday and could offer more clarity on the role Paganetti will provide for the struggling 2-7 Eagles.
Although Paganetti’s institutional knowledge makes him a logical addition at a moment of clear offensive regression, the organization has used consultants in varying, sometimes unconventional ways.
For instance, Brady, a former offensive coordinator in Indianapolis and the current passing game coordinator in Baltimore, helped advise the defense in 2022 while Fangio offered up his defensive expertise to the offense before the Super Bowl that same season.
Paganetti held a variety of roles across his first stint with the Eagles from 2017 to 2024. He began as offensive quality control and assistant offensive line coach (2017-18) under Jeff Stoutland, then moved to assistant running backs coach (2019-20).
Under Sirianni, he first returned to quality control (2021-22) before being promoted to run game specialist/assistant tight ends coach in 2023 and run game specialist/assistant offensive line coach in 2024, where he again aided Stoutland. He was part of both Super Bowl championship staffs (LII and LIX) and left after the Super Bowl LIX win to become Kellen Moore’s run game coordinator with the New Orleans Saints.
Paganetti was later fired by the Saints earlier this month amid their own ground-game struggles earlier this season.
The timing is hard to ignore. The Eagles entered their bye week with all eyes on the offensive coaching staff and whether there would be any changes.
The organization went into the season intent on better marrying the running and passing games under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. That meant moving on from  Stoutland in favor of Chris Kuper (offensive line) and Ryan Mahaffey (run game coordinator/tight ends).
The shift has not produced the desired results . Philadelphia is currently mired in a seven-game skid, with the offense ranked near the bottom of the league and the line and run game a far cry from the record-setting 2024 unit that featured Paganetti in a specialized run-game role.
What’s somewhat strange—and perhaps telling—is the philosophical contrast between the two different ground game approaches.
Stoutland’s philosophy emphasized physical, vertical displacement, power-based downhill schemes, and a culture of technique, fundamentals and player development that turned the Eagles’ line into a sustained strength from the famed and marketed “Stoutland University.”
Mannion’s system, drawing more from zone-heavy influences, prioritizes lateral movement, wide-zone concepts, and better integration with the passing game. The personnel and teaching styles have not aligned cleanly this season, and the on-field product has reflected that disconnect.
Bringing back a Stoutland loyalist—even in a consultancy capacity—could be viewed as raising the white flag on the full transition.
At minimum, it reads as a concession that some of the old running-game principles that powered the Eagles’ previous sustained success need to be reintroduced.
Whether Paganetti can meaningfully influence scheme, technique, or messaging from a consultancy role is unlikely, but it remains to be seen. That said, the organization has at least signaled that the current run-game direction is not working as constructed.
With the season already largely lost and Jalen Hurts sidelined , the Eagles' focus seems to have shifted toward stabilization and identifying what elements of the one-time successful run-game identity are worth preserving.

title: McMullen: What Eagles’ Latest Flurry of Moves Could Mean Coming Out of the Bye Week
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles will get back to work this week after a bye in which they already let go of two reserves who didn’t fit into their 2027 plans when they waived wide receiver Hollywood Brown and offensive tackle Fred Johnson .
Add that to the recent trade of nose tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville, and the release of running back Jayden Blue and general manager Howie Roseman currently has four open 53-man roster spots to play with.
Roseman already filled two spots by elevating veteran tight end Zach Ertz and tackle John Ojukwu from the practice squad on Monday, and could have foreshadowed a third by staring the practice window of running back Will Shipley, who has been sidelined with a partial plantar fascia tear suffered in the London loss against the Jaguars.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
Blue was brought back to the practice squad Monday, as was linebacker Chance Campbell and tight end Hayden Rucci, an in-line blocking option which has been a problem.
All of the movement could just be the start of a continued significant churn that could mean opportunities for others, be it inside or outside the Jefferson Health Training Complex. In fact, Roseman, who has a history of trying to win outside the margins, could be opening up a larger in-season roster-building lever by scanning  the practice squads of other teams in order to find younger players with upside and a cost-effective short-term future.
Brown and Johnson weren’t playing meaningful roles this season, and neither was going to be part of the long-term picture moving forward.
Brown caught five passes for 63 yards. Johnson played 24 snaps. With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks expected back after the bye, and with younger options already getting looks on the offensive line, the Eagles made a practical decision.
The Eagles cleared the space, shed some salary, and seemingly accepted the reality of a 2-7 season that has long since slipped out of contention despite the realization that the rest of the woeful NFC East refuses to run away.
The trend could continue especially is the losing continues with veterans like Jonathan Jones, Elijah Moore, Kenny Moore, A.J. Epenesa and Arnold Ebiketie, who all fit the profile of aging or short-term players unlikely to be part of the 2027 core.
The Eagles already planned to move Ebiketie to Cincinnati for a 2027 sixth-round pick before the dysfunctional Bengals needed compensatory pick expert Nick Korte to explain how that deal would have cost them a third-rounder next April.
Obvious correction here: the Bengals gave up a regular 6th rounder--they did not gain one. The main point is of course about the 3rd round compensatory pick that this trade would cancel out. https://t.co/7Zjn5WK6NQ
Jones is 33 and has been limited by injury. Moore is 31 and was a midseason addition for depth while Epenesa has played sparingly behind a group of younger edge rushers. None of them projects as a building block for next year.
At 2-7, the Eagles should continue to be realistic about this season. Last Friday’s moves indicate that Roseman and the front office has already shown it is willing to make those calls so why not continue it?
At least, if there are viable options with potential that spans years instead of weeks.

title: 3-Round Eagles Midseason 2027 Mock Draft: Philly Casts a Wide Net to Address Several Needs
full_text:
As the Eagles come out of their Week 10 bye, it's hard not to think about the future. A 2-7 record upon their return has Philadelphia fans more focused on the possibilities that the 2027 NFL Draft could bring rather than the remaining regular-season schedule, especially after general manager Howie Roseman added some capital before last week's trade deadline .
According to Spotrac, the Eagles are on track to have nine picks in each of the next two drafts , giving Roseman & Co. plenty of opportunities to build for the future. The possibilities become even more exciting when accounting for the fact that Philadelphia will own two first-rounders in April thanks to the Jordan Davis trade with Jacksonville.
Eagles' current selections
That said, the midway of the 2026 season is the perfect time for a mock draft, so let's dive into what the first three rounds of the annual event could look like for the Eagles in April.
Rostering an elite offensive line played a key role in the Eagles' success over the last decade. The unit took a hit this season, with Lane Johnson retiring and Cam Jurgens traded to the Ravens—and that's without even mentioning that Landon Dickerson isn't getting any younger.
With that in mind, assuming they have the fifth overall pick, drafting Texas's Trevor Goosby is a no-brainer decision for the Eagles.
The Ohio State pass rush wasn’t great… but Trevor Goosby and Melvin Siani are also EXTREMELY good Just 2 pressures allowed combined between them against in Texas’s huge win over the Buckeyes pic.twitter.com/YlyiAgstFV
Standing 6'7" and weighing 312 lbs, Goosby is the type of behemoth blocker that can anchor Philadelphia's O-line for years to come. He's an athletic specimen who knows how to be in the right place at the right time, which is why he's allowed only three sacks across 1,571 offensive snaps , according to Pro Football Focus , since joining the Longhorns in 2023.
Goosby suffered a season-ending knee injury in October; however, he's expected to make a full recovery , per ESPN 's Pete Thamel.
Coming out of their bye week, the Eagles are tied for the fourth-fewest sacks (16) while owning the PFF's fifth-worst pass-rush grade (61.9).
In other words, drafting a promising pass rusher should be a priority early in the 2027 draft, which could lead Philadelphia to draft Alabama's Yhonzae Pierre. Since 2021, the Eagles have drafted four Crimson Tide products in the first three rounds, including linebacker Jihaad Campbell (31st overall in 2025).
After not drafting anyone from Alabama last year, resuming the trend of adding Pierre to defensive coordinator Vic Fangio's unit makes too much sense to ignore. The 22-year-old disruptor has improved with each passing season in the SEC, and the 2026 campaign isn't an exception, as he currently owns career-high PFF grades when it comes to :
Pierre isn't perfect, as he still occasionally misses tackles, but it's hard to ignore the 32 pressures (five sacks) he's racked up. He's also steadily improved in coverage, allowing only a 42.9% completion rate and an 11.3 passer rating on seven targets so far. It isn't a huge sample size, but it's notable after allowing 10-of-12 passes (83.3%) for 99 yards and a 101.0 passer rating last season.
Imagine if the Eagles can mold him into their next defensive great?
It's hard to say what the future will hold for Jalen Hurts. The Eagles lost their franchise QB for the season to blood clots last month, and while fans would love nothing more than to see Hurts make a full recovery, there's at least a possibility that he won't suit up for Philadelphia again . And if he does, he might not be the same player.
Whether he's under center in 2027 or not, the Eagles must prepare for a Hurts-less future eventually, which could lead them to draft UCLA's Nico Iamaleava on Day 2. On Saturday, I wrote about how Iamaleava could be a second-round target for Philadelphia , especially since he could become the same type of dual-threat fans are used to in Hurts.
Unlike Goosby, Iamaleava reportedly plans to return to UCLA after a season-ending injury, which was an ACL tear. We're at a point in modern medicine where that injury isn't as big an issue anymore, so it shouldn't deter the Eagles from ignoring what they could have with Iamaleava if his plans change.
There's a good chance that the Eagles' tight end room will have some vacancies to fill this offseason. As it stands, rookie Eli Stowers is the only TE Philadelphia has under contract for 2027, with Dallas Goedert, Grant Calcaterra, and Johnny Mundt all set to become unrestricted free agents in March.
Although the Eagles could re-sign any combination of them, it wouldn't hurt to add someone like Texas Tech TE Terrance Carter Jr. through the draft.
Carter is the kind of scoring machine most NFL coaches would love to inject into their offenses. He scored seven touchdowns on 76 catches across 25 games with Louisiana in 2023 and 2024 before transferring to Texas Tech the following season. That move proved to be the right call, as Carter has amassed 922 yards and 10 TDs on 82 catches since the start of 2025, meaning he's found pay dirt on 12.2% of his receptions.
Texas Tech’s offense is at its best when Terrance Carter Jr. is involved. One of the best TEs in the country after the catch. Carter has averaged 6.9 YAC per reception for his career pic.twitter.com/TKhkmIkvYK
He's known for his pass-catching, but Carter can contribute as a blocker, too. He's up to 65.2 run-block and 59.1 pass protection grades on PFF and has yet to surrender a sack throughout his five-year collegiate run.
Even if they return, Goedert and Calcaterra aren't getting any younger. It's time to invest in the future, and a TE room that's built around Carter and Stowers could help fuel the Eagles' offensive success for years to come.

title: Howie Roseman's Miami Visit Is Creating Eagles Buzz It Might Not Deserve
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Eagles general manager Howie Roseman’s Miami-Duke visit created the expected noise. The calendar, family context and the broader quarterback picture for the Eagles make it more routine than it looked.
The video clip went viral pretty quickly: Philadelphia’s general manager on the field before Miami hosted Duke, briefly greeting Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah.
"Bring him to Philly!" Philadelphia Eagles GM Howie Roseman a little pregame love for Canes QB Darian Mensah @WPLGLocal10 pic.twitter.com/QkhiiNuepN
For a team that has struggled , sits with Jalen Hurts sidelined for the season by blood clots and is projected to hold significant 2027 draft capital (including a potential top-five pick and another later in the round, any Roseman-QB interaction was going to generate some “bring him to Philly” reactions.
The timing amplified it, but the context points more to business as usual. The Eagles are on their bye week , the trade deadline has passed, and Roseman has more time than he typically has in mid-November.
More significantly, Roseman’s oldest son, Jake, attends Duke and works with the Blue Devils’ football program. That family visit is the far more likely reason why the Miami-Duke game made logistical sense during the bye.
Mensah himself was the starting QB at Duke in 2025 before transferring to Miami (a move that involved an NIL dispute that was later settled). Roseman was hardly the only NFL representative in the building for a high-profile ACC game—scouts from several other teams were present—but the personal tie to Duke and the time Roseman has with the Eagles off this week are the clearest reasons he was there in person.
None of that means Mensah falls outside the Eagles’ evaluation of quarterbacks when the position could top Roseman's wanted list next April. He is a productive quarterback who has put up elite numbers at Miami after earlier stops at Tulane and Duke. He will be on the board for teams that need a signal-caller in the first round. The same is true of other names that most personnel evaluators currently place ahead of Mensah.
Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker continues to draw the strongest “upside” comments. The former walk-on has the physical tools, production, and arm talent that keep him at or near the top of many 2027 quarterback rankings. Notre Dame’s C.J. Carr is viewed as the most advanced processor of the group, according to multiple personnel evaluators who spoke to Eagles On SI .
Carr is accurate, comfortable with pre-snap manipulation, and further along in the mental side of the position than most of his peers. Texas’s Arch Manning still carries the pedigree and the traits that made him a high-profile prospect, even as his tape this season has been more uneven than some of the others.
Roseman’s job is to uncover as much information as possible with all those possibilities.
A pregame conversation with Mensah, against the backdrop of a son at Duke, does not lock the Eagles into (or out of) any particular quarterback plan.
It is one hardly-significant data point in a process that will also include Mestemaker’s high-ceiling flashes, Carr’s processing, and Manning’s pedigree.
With Hurts’s recovery timeline unclear and the Eagles' roster in flux, that evaluation work on Mensah and others who participated in the Hurricanes-Blue Devils matchup is simply part of the job—no more dramatic, and no less necessary, despite the way it might have looked to the uninitiated on a bye-week Saturday in South Florida.

title: Fred Johnson's Release Underscores the Eagles' Personal Gong Show
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — For younger readers, "The Gong Show" was a somewhat iconic television game show from the 1970s in which often bizarre, eccentric and untrained amateur contestants performed on stage while a panel of three celebrity judges watched.
If a judge disliked an act, they would strike a massive brass gong with a wooden mallet to abruptly end the performance.
The always-interesting Fred Johnson recently introduced the percussion instrument into the Eagles' locker room to liven things up during what’s turned into a seven-game skid for an organization not used to losing.
Turns out Johnson’s gong had a shorter shelf life than A.J. Dillon’s infamous positivity bunny.
The big man eventually moved the gong into the offensive line room, but now both Johnson and his new toy will be filing a change of address form .
The last figurative clang of Johnson’s gong signaled the Eagles' waiving of a pair of veteran offensive players Friday: wide receiver Hollywood Brown and Johnson, the team’s proven swing tackle.
We have waived WR Marquise Brown and T Fred Johnson. pic.twitter.com/S4ieutMSfU
Neither player figured into the organization’s 2027 plans, so the decisions highlight the end of any realistic push for the 2026 postseason and a clear shift toward the continued evaluation of younger players who have an opportunity to be part of the solution moving forward.
The actual reasons for moving on are slightly different. With starting receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) set to return from injuries after the Eagles’ bye week, there wasn’t going to be much playing time for Brown.
An NFL source confirmed to Eagles On SI that Brown wanted to move on, and Philadelphia agreed after working out a non-injury settlement . In other words, Brown agreed to give back some of the $5 million he was guaranteed back in March for the opportunity to seek more playing time elsewhere, perhaps with a playoff contender.
Johnson, 29, is a little bit different. He has been a reliable swing tackle and backup for the Eagles in recent seasons and has garnered plenty of playing time since first joining the organization in late 2022.
Johnson contributed during the Super Bowl LIX-winning 2024 campaign (primarily filling in at left tackle for an injured Jordan Mailata) and logged a career-high 626 regular-season snaps in 2025 while starting nine games, mostly in relief of Lane Johnson.
After the Super Bowl season, Johnson left in free agency for an opportunity to compete for a starting job in Jacksonville. That didn’t work out, and the Eagles sent a seventh-round pick to the Jags to get him back just before the start of the 2025 season.
If it were a strict meritocracy, Johnson likely would have taken over at right tackle after Lane Johnson’s in-season retirement. Instead, the Eagles went with upside, inserting third-round rookie Markel Bell.
Fred Johnson appeared in seven games this season with only 24 offensive snaps, many of them as an extra tight end in a jumbo package.
The Eagles entered their bye week at 2-7 , last in the NFC East and mired in a seven-game skid. The team’s playoff odds have effectively evaporated, even in a weak NFL East.
In that context, cutting a veteran with no long-term roster value—and no trade value after the deadline—frees a spot on the 53-man roster while the evaluation of Bell continues.
These moves fit a broader pattern of roster pruning during the downtime of the bye. Earlier in the week, the Eagles also waived running back Jaydon Blue and traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis , opening multiple spots.
The organization can now promote or claim developmental players from practice squads. In-house, John Ojukwu, Kiran Amegadjie and Evan Neal could factor in as swing-tackle options behind Mailata and Bell.
For Johnson, the departure closes a productive chapter in Philadelphia. He took to Instagram after the news with a simple thank-you to the city , posting a photo from the Super Bowl celebration.
The Eagles return to action on Nov. 22 against the Steelers. By then, the roster will reflect a more explicit developmental priority—an acknowledgment that the corner on 2026 has been turned and the focus has shifted primarily to the future.
Essentially, the Eagles' 2026 season just got gonged.

title: Steelers' Cam Heyward Predicts Lamar Jackson's Future
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers still have not met their fiercest rival, the Baltimore Ravens, this season. The two foes will meet twice over the final four weeks of the regular season schedule.
No matter where the Steelers and Ravens are in the standings or where they sit in the playoff picture, their matchups are always a battle to the final second. That's what bitter rivalries create in the NFL. That rivalry will continue as long as the NFL and the two franchises exist. It survives and endures through the multitude of superstars involved. The latest is Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, whom the Steelers have had the displeasure of game-planning against for nearly a decade.
But according to Steelers defensive tackle and team leader Cam Heyward, the years of Pittsburgh dealing with Jackson might be coming to an end. On a recent episode of his Not Just Football podcast, Heyward made a bold claim about Jackson's future in the NFL.
"Let. me get a little petty and stir the pot," he teased. "I don't think he is [the Ravens' quarterback in 2027]. I think he wants to go to South Beach. Or, this is the dark horse one, he goes to Atlanta to play with Bijan. And then you got wide receivers around you."
Heyward is indeed stirring the pot with these comments. For starters, it's noteworthy that he named the Miami Dolphins and Atlanta Falcons as two organizations to watch. He's speculating, of course, but it feels bit more accurate coming from a player who goes up against him multiple times per season.
Secondly, it highlights the uncertainty in Baltimore. With a new head coach and staff, plus Jackson's contract running through 2027 with no extension in place, there is a very real chance that the Ravens and their star QB are heading for a divorce, something the Steelers would love to see.
Jackson has played the Steelers 10 times in the regular season and once in the postseason over his nine seasons in the NFL. In the regular season, the matchup has overwhelmingly favored the Steelers.
Pittsburgh holds a 7-3 record over Lamar in their head-to-head matchups. In those games, Jackson has performed like an average quarterback rather than the MVP player he normally is. The Steelers have limited him to 139 completions on 241 attempts for. 1,741 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.
But the Steelers would likely celebrate Jackson's departure from the AFC North because that means they might not have to meet him in the postseason. Unlike the regular-season battles, the Ravens hold the edge in the playoffs.
The Ravens defeated the Steelers during the 2024 Wild Card Weekend, the only time these two teams have met in the postseason since Jackson's arrival. Jackson completed 16 of 21 passing attempts for 175 yards and two touchdowns, plus 81 rushing yards on 15 carries.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: What Happened to Steelers' Alex Highsmith?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were handed an unexpected dose of reality during their 38-18 drubbing by the Cincinnati Bengals.
After storming out to a 6-2 record, the Steelers emerged from their bye week thoroughly outplayed by their AFC North rivals. Much of the loss can be written off to Cincinnati quarterback and MVP frontrunner Joe Burrow, who is at the top of his game right now. He dismantled the Steelers' defense, completing 35 of 44 passing attempts for four touchdowns and 409 yards.
The Steelers only sacked him once and forced zero turnovers. It was a disappointing outing for the defense, but it was especially so for the pass rush. While T.J. Watt battled against premier tackle Amarius Mims all night, Alex Highsmith faced significantly weaker resistance and was still unproductive.
For the seventh consecutive week, Highsmith was held to less than 1.0 sack in the contest. The output the Steelers are getting from their veteran leader is simply not enough, and in order to get back on track, Highsmith has to rediscover his game.
Through nine games, it's been an underachieving year for Highsmith. He's posted a total of 19 tackles, but only eight have been recorded individually, with the other 11 counted as assisted.
But tackles are only a piece of what Highsmith is judged on. The biggest piece is his ability to disrupt the quarterback, and he's well behind his usual pace. In nine games, he has just 3.5 sacks and five tackles for loss. His five tackles for loss rank 38th in the NFL amongst edge rushers with at least one snap, according to data from SumerSports. That figure is tied with Patrick Queen for second on the team, but that's exactly the problem.
Highsmith isn't getting home enough. The fact that he has the same number of sacks as the team's starting inside linebacker is concerning, but it's been disguised by the team's total sack numbers being at the top of the NFL.
One of the big reasons for Highsmith's decline in production this season is his average time to pressure. This refers to the amount of time it takes a defender, on average, to create a quarterback pressure. In years past, Highsmith has been one of the best. According to data from SumerSports, he averaged 2.40 seconds or less during the 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons.
Last year, that number rose slightly, as he averaged 2.56 seconds.
This season, he's taking even longer. Through the first nine games, it's taking him 2.62 seconds on average to create pressure on the quarterback.
Why that's a problem is that most quarterbacks are releasing the ball in about 2.5 to 2.6 seconds. Take Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. This season, he's averaging 2.59 seconds before he throws the ball.  Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence is averaging 2.61 seconds. Kansas City Chiefs superstar Patrick Mahomes takes an average of 2.56 seconds. Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love is averaging 2.45 seconds to throw in 2026.
What this demonstrates is the quickness and efficiency of some of the top offenses in the NFL. That's specifically a problem for Highsmith and the Steelers, who are counting on a four-man rush to get home and disrupt the quarterback.
Simple arithmetic is not on Highsmith's side right now.
Ever since the Steelers signed Nick Herbig to a new extension, the writing has been on the wall for Highsmith. One way or another, his time in Pittsburgh is closer to the end than the beginning.
The option most likely to happen is a trade. That's certainly a possibility in the offseason, as the Steelers will need to address their salary cap situation by moving on from at least one or two veteran players. Highsmith might not be having the most productive year of his career, but he's still 29 years old and one of the most complete EDGE rushers in football.
The more likely option, in my opinion, is that the Steelers let his contract play out and he walks away from the franchise following the 2027 campaign. According to contract data on Spotrac, Highsmith is entitled to a base salary of $15.5 million, plus a signing bonus, for next year. That adds up to a salary cap hit of $21.1 million, giving the Steelers three outside linebackers making over $20 million against the cap.
It's an expensive investment, but it remains the team's best position. And that's why I believe the Steelers will let this play out. Instead of taking a risk and moving on, the Steelers feel more likely to hold on to him and let him walk for nothing after 2027.
There's a lot of time until then, however. And the Steelers are trying to get back on track after being dominated by the Bengals. To get back on track, the Steelers need Highsmith to return to form and help snap the defense out of whatever funk Week 10 put them into.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Could Get Mason McCormick Back for Playoffs
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers avoided the worst-case scenario with offensive guard Mason McCormick, who left Week 10's game against the Cincinnati Bengals with an air cast on his right ankle.
McCormick suffered a pretty gruesome-looking ankle injury after running into quarterback Aaron Rodgers and left tackle Troy Fautanu on a play in the second half of the loss. He was carted off the field, with most of the staff and roster coming up to greet him as he was taken into the locker room.
Afterward, the belief was that whatever exactly happened wasn't good, and that McCormick was looking at a significant injury. Head coach Mike McCarthy said he hoped more news would be positive as the training staff continued to gather information, and according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the team avoided the worst-case scenario.
Rapoport reports that McCormick suffered a dislocated ankle on the play, and while it's going to keep him out for some time, there's a chance that he can return for the playoffs.
McCormick will also avoid surgery with the injury.
#Steelers G Mason McCormick, who was carted off in an air cast on Sunday, suffered a dislocated ankle that unbelievably did not feature a fracture, sources say. No surgery needed, as the ankle was popped back in place on the field. There is a chance he’s back for the playoffs. pic.twitter.com/OElot8md3v
That's great news for the Steelers, who will hope to get their star left guard back on the field for a postseason run. McCormick is the heart and soul of the offensive line, and everyone, including defensive players, made that known after the game.
"Seeing Mason go down was pretty tough," defensive tackle Cam Heyward said after the game. "He has been kicking a lot of tail all year long, and on an offensive line, he's going to stand out. So it's going to be up to the guys to step up."
"The amount of work and just the presence that he brings to his offense and to this O-line room, it's a big loss, man," Fautanu said. "He's not going anywhere, but obviously being out there on the field, I know his presence is still going to be felt."
The Steelers will lean on Spencer Anderson to be their starter moving forward. The versatile offensive lineman started the season at right guard but was replaced by Brock Hoffman. At the time, it was revealed that Anderson was dealing with a fracture in his leg but was not going to undergo surgery during the season.
Behind him, Ryan McCollum will now become the primary backup at both guard and center. Rookie Gennings Dunker is on Injured Reserve with an MCL sprain but could make his way back to the active roster soon to add needed depth along the interior.

title: Steelers May Be Worried About DeShon Elliott Injury
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers lost DeShon Elliott against the Cincinnati Bengals due to a pregame knee injury that ended his Week 10 before it got started.
Now, the team is doing their homework on defensive back help, signing A.J. Finley to their practice squad and working out Nazeeh Johnson and former Pitt star Jordan Whitehead two days after their Week 10 loss to the Bengals. While not adding someone to their active roster is a positive sign, spending so much time at the safety position might be an indicator that they're worried about Elliott's status moving forward.
And there are reasons to feel that way. Elliott suffered a season-ending knee injury in 2025 and after returning in training camp, the team made the decision that he was not ready to play come Week 1 of the regular season. He was placed on Injured Reserve and did not return to the lineup until Week 7 in Paris, France, against the New Orleans Saints.
He's played just two games this season, against the Saints and Cleveland Browns, and was limited to just 43 defensive snaps in those two weeks.
While the team has not yet revealed what happened to Elliott or what the injury is, there's reason for skepticism. With his knee having been injured in the past, if it's the same knee, the cause for concern is high. And while it doesn't mean Elliott is injury-prone, it may indicate that he needs more time than hoped for to fully heal and be able to play at a high level again.
Head coach Mike McCarthy has never been one to share too much about injuries. After the game, he offered very little about the situation, and did not expand on it during his Monday press conference.
"During his warmup, he had something that showed up, so we made him inactive," he said postgame.
If the Steelers are going to lose Elliott for an extended period of time, they'll likely make that announcement in the near future. For now, everyone can hope for the best. But Pittsburgh bringing in a handful of safeties to test out doesn't inspire the most confidence in the situation.
In the meantime, expect Robert Spears-Jennings and Jaquan Brisker to remain the starters for the Steelers. The seventh-round pick has become a very reliable piece of the defense and Brisker remains a player defensive coordinator Patrick Graham relies on in multiple situations.
As for Elliott, they'll hope he's good to go. And if not, they'll hope he can return again this season.

title: Steelers Add DB to Practice Squad After DeShon Elliott Injury
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are adding a safety to their practice squad following their 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10.
Ahead of their Week 11 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles, the Steelers announced that they've signed AJ Finley.
Pittsburgh hadn't previously made any additions to its practice squad, nor subtracted from it, since signing Marquez Valdes-Scantling on October 20.
Now, Finley joins the fray as the organization brings in additional depth in its secondary following a blowout defeat at the hands of its AFC North foes while DeShon Elliott deals with a knee injury that kept him out vs. Cincinnati.
A four-year player at Ole Miss from 2019 to 2022, during which he posted 243 tackles with eight interceptions and four fumble recoveries, Finley was not selected in the 2023 NFL Draft.
He proceeded to sign with the Los Angeles Chargers as an undrafted free agent and made their initial 53-man roster as a rookie.
Finley appeared in a total of 22 games for the Chargers through the 2024 campaign, posting 13 tackles and a forced fumble over that span.
He was later waived on November 25, 2024 and claimed by the Seattle Seahawks. Finley suited up for four contests with them to close out that season, logging a tackle along the way.
The 25-year-old did not play for Seattle in 2025 as it went on to win Super Bowl LX after suffering a knee injury that August.
Finley re-signed with the Seahawks this past offseason and later joined their practice squad after being let go at final roster cuts.
He did spend some time on Seattle's 53-man roster this year and played in three games while making a start, though he was waived on November 12 before finding his way to Pittsburgh.
Elliott's absence against the Bengals was evident, as Pittsburgh gave up 484 yards (406 of which were through the air) in that contest.
Cincinnati was able to do whatever it wanted against the Steelers' defense in the passing game as Joe Burrow and company were met with little resistance.
Now, with Elliott working through his injury after residing on the reserve/injured list until Week 7 this season while recovering from a season-ending knee/hamstring injury he sustained in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign, Finley becomes a potential option at safety for the team moving forward.
Pittsburgh also hosted former Kansas City Chiefs defensive back Nazeeh Johnson, who played in 29 contests for them from 2022 to 2025.
Johnson signed with the Tennessee Titans during the offseason but was suspended for the first six games of the year after breaking the NFL's performance-enhancing drug policy. Additionally, the 28-year-old underwent ankle surgery back in August and was released with an injury settlement.
The Steelers opted not to trade for a defensive back at the trade deadline this season, and that decision could end up haunting them. Now, they're doing whatever they can to help out their secondary on the fly.

title: Mike McCarthy's Message to Steelers After Bengals Disaster
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers were thoroughly trounced in their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. With a chance to make a statement, the Steelers were embarrassed by a better team.
In response, the Steelers can go one of two ways. The first is the dark side. They could give into the drubbing the Bengals handed them and let this season slip away.
Alternatively, they could flip the page on the loss and move on to their Week 11 opponent, the Philadelphia Eagles. That's the route head coach Mike McCarthy would prefer the team take. Speaking to the media during his weekly press conference, he offered some helpful advice for his team: let's move on.
"Most importantly is how we shift to Philadelphia," he said . "This needs to be one game, and it needs to stop there."
"Most importantly, learn from it," he continued. "You have the opportunity to learn and grow from every aspect of football when you just line up and practice, let alone in a game. There'll be things that happened last night that we'll be challenged again. So, let's get it on."
What McCarthy is proposing is exactly what the Steelers need to do. Week 10 went wrong in nearly every single capacity, but that doesn't have to define the rest of their season.
"This is part of the journey of a season," he said. "But it needs to be one game, and that'll be our approach as we prepare for Philadelphia."
The reason why this is so important is because good teams shake off their losses. No team, except for the undefeated 1972 Miami Dolphins, escapes an NFL season unblemished.
It's about how you respond to those losses that defines your season. Right now, McCarthy is doing his best to return his team to winning form.
One area the Steelers are trying to emphasize heading into Week 11 is their offense on the road. The team has had polar opposite results depending on whether they are the home or away team. That was once again in Week 10, as the Steelers were again outperformed on the road.
McCarthy singled out that issue as one they are focusing on.
"We need to win on the road. We need to play better on the road, especially on offense," he said. "Our gap between offensive performance on the road and at home is too wide."
Identifying the issue is one thing, but what about a solution? As McCarthy sees it , the ideal way forward is to prioritize the tiny details and fundamentals
"You have to keep emphasizing the little things," he explained. "That's what we'll focus on as we get ready for Philly."
Now, we'll sit back and see how the team responds in Week 11 against the Eagles.

title: Steelers Have a Systematic Problem
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' problems are systematic. Something they cannot change until ownership does. And ownership has no desire to run things differently, because somehow, they've convinced themselves that two words mean the same thing - and they don't.
"Competitive" and "contender" do not mean the same thing in the National Football League. One means you're the Pittsburgh Steelers, fighting for a winning record and a shot in the playoffs. The other means you're the Cincinnati Bengals, who are hoping their franchise quarterback can take them to the promise land with how well he's playing.
Art Rooney II refuses to "rebuild," and the Steelers aren't in need of a complete overhaul. What they need is patience. Something that Rooney refuses to display, and it 's causing the Steelers years of missed opportunity because of it.
Remember, as a child, your parents would tell you to practice patience? "Slow down," our moms and dads would say to us when we felt overwhelmed and like we needed to fix something immediately.
The Steelers are in desperate need of someone telling them to slow down.
Rooney seems to have this idea in his head that the Steelers can't go backward. He pushes that narrative to general manager Omar Khan, who then makes some of the worst decisions in the NFL.
It's a two-headed monster of poor decision-making, and it's unsolvable until one of them makes it stop.
DK Metcalf was a desperation trade and signing. Michael Pittman Jr. was as well. The revolving door at quarterback has become nauseating for Steelers fans, and Mike McCarthy is hinting that next year, instead of drafting someone and finally ending it, he's going to roll out Mason Rudolph to try and keep the team competitive.
But they won't be contenders.
The Steelers' problems start from the top down. And don't get it twisted, they won't always be evident. For the most part, Pittsburgh will win games, beat the teams they should and go on stretches where they look legit. But there will be plenty of reminders along the way.
Rooney is fighting the clock on retirement and it has to be hard to slow down when you understand there's not that much time left to go out in glory. But that's Khan's job to make sure the franchise is run the way a contending franchise is run, and he's simply not doing that.
The "Steelers Way" has lost its meaning and become something much worse than Rooney dreamt it would be. And maybe he's too blind to it to realize it's destroying any and all chances this team has at actually contending.
The system needs to change. Until it does, Pittsburgh won't be a real threat for a Super Bowl. And that starts with the two people making decisions.
Slow down. It'll do this organization years of good, and might find them their seventh Lombardi.

title: Steelers Working Out Former Chiefs CB
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are showing interest in a former Super Bowl champion. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, cornerback Nazeeh Johnson will be at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex for a workout as the team tries to find answers to a poor secondary in the second half of the season.
Johnson, 28, won two Super Bowls with the Kansas City Chiefs as a cornerback and special teamer. A seventh-round pick out of Marshall in the 2022 NFL Draft, Johnson has played in 29 games with six starts. Primarily a special teams option, Johnson has yet to record an interception and has just three career pass breakups while active.
He did not play in the 2023 season and has yet to play in the 2026 season.
Source: The #Steelers have former #Chiefs CB Nazeeh Johnson in for a workout today. Johnson had 66 tackles and one sack during his time in Kansas City, won two Super Bowls and was also a key special teamer. pic.twitter.com/MbN2SD6ofe
Johnson started his career as a safety and had his most productive year in 2024 when he recorded 66 tackles, three tackles for loss and a sack while starting six games.
Whether Johnson comes to Pittsburgh with expectations of playing defense or special teams, he's needed. The Steelers' secondary might be one of the worst in the league, and their abysmal performance against the Cincinnati Bengals put a spotlight on Asante Samuel Jr. simply not being enough to rely on him in big games.
On special teams, Danny Crossman continues to be under fire because of how poorly the group has performed. Both in kick and punt coverage, the group has given up big yards in almost every game this season, and are not making up for it in kick and punt return.
So, Johnson's addition will be welcomed no matter what.
Bringing in Johnson does not guarantee him a spot on the 53-man roster or even on the team in general. Pittsburgh will workout the veteran defensive back and then make a decision. At cornerback, they are pretty healthy, but safety may be another story.
DeShon Elliott went down with a knee injury pregame before kickoff in Cincinnati and was unable to play. He just returned from Injured Reserve after missing the start of the season with a knee injury that ended his season in 2025 as well.
It's unknown how severe the injury is at this time.
So, Pittsburgh could be looking at Johnson as a safety who they can stash on their active roster or practice squad, who brings reliable special teams play and versatility in the secondary. Two boxes they need checked before Week 11.

title: Mike McCarthy May Have Hinted at Steelers 2027 QB Plan
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers don't have the answer for who will be the starting quarterback next season or in the future.
Aaron Rodgers is retiring at the end of this season with the Steelers, his 22nd in the NFL, and at age 43, ending what will be a Hall of Fame career.
The Steelers have many options they can go with for 2027, but Chris Collinsworth spoke with head coach Mike McCarthy before the 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium in Week 10, and he gave praise to backup Mason Rudolph.
“He even brought up the idea that, ‘Hey, everybody just assumes we’re gonna take a quarterback with Aaron retiring. We’ve got pretty good quarterbacks in here,’ Collinsworth said.
"As if, I don’t know about that. Do I want one of these young quarterbacks, or do I wanna take one of these guys that we’ve had a full year to develop here and let them play? If it falls to them in the right way, they probably would. If not, I think they just roll out Mason Rudolph. They’ve been impressed.”
The Steelers have the highest-paid defense in the NFL this season and are projected to have the second-highest next year.
Pittsburgh is relying on their defense to win them games, which they've done through most of 2026, giving them a 6-3 record.
Rudolph is a veteran who has experience playing for the Steelers and in the NFL, with 19 starts in 35 games played, with 4,927 passing yards and 30 touchdowns in his nine seasons as a professional.
The Steelers have gone to Rudolph before, as he went 5-3 in eight starts and 10 games played when Ben Roethlisberger was injured in the 2019 season.
Rudolph also won three straight games to end the 2023 season, after Kenny Pickett was injured, and helped the Steelers clinch an AFC Wild Card spot.
He isn't the best quarterback available, but he's under contract for 2027 and has starting experience, which gives him an edge over many other candidates.
The Steelers would most likely rather go with a veteran than a rookie, which they did with Russell Wilson in 2024 and Rodgers these last two seasons.
The Steelers have two younger quarterbacks who they could play over Rudolph, if they feel like they can add more and help them win in 2027.
This includes Drew Allar , whom the Steelers selected in the third round in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Penn State, and Will Howard, whom they drafted in the sixth round in 2025 out of Ohio State.
Both quarterbacks have yet to play in the NFL, but have excelled in college and could be the Steelers' answer next season.
The Steelers could also look at players in the 2027 NFL Draft , despite the quarterback class not living up to expectations.
Where Pittsburgh finishes the season and where they pick in the first round will play a big role in how they approach adding a new quarterback, if they do so.
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers Have QB Problem Aaron Rodgers Can't Solve
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers possess a laundry list of problems, many of which were revealed during a 38-18 butt-whooping at the hands of the Cincinnati Bengals.
On both sides of the ball, the Steelers were "decisively beaten," head coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. The defense was unable to "settle down," according to inside linebacker Patrick Queen, and that shakiness allowed Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to move the ball at will and score 38 points.
On offense, it was a silent day for the team's top weapon and running back, Jaylen Warren. Left guard Mason McCormick sustained an ankle injury that appears to be serious and possibly long-term. Wide receiver DK Metcalf ended his five-game touchdown drought, but he once again failed to be a difference-maker on the outside.
All that included, and the list of issues the Steelers must address is overwhelming. Unfortunately, that list is not complete unless it includes quarterback Aaron Rodgers. After beginning the year playing like a solid game-managing quarterback, the soon-to-be 43-year-old QB's play on the field doesn't align with the winning football he and the Steelers claim to be pursuing.
Aaron Rodgers is an undisputed, first-ballot Hall of Fame candidate when the time comes.
Even the greatest in league history eventually lose it, and the decline of Rodgers has been ignored for far too long. The version the Steelers brought to Pittsburgh was obviously not Rodgers in his prime, but this season appears to be a very clear regression for the four-time NFL MVP.
This regression is most evident on throws beyond 10 yards. Rodgers will go down as one of the best pure passers in NFL history, capable of locating a pass with pinpoint accuracy.
That description is not anywhere close to applicable to the current version of Rodgers. He's completed less than 60% of his passing attempts five times in nine starts, and on the season he has a 60.8% completion percentage. The numbers just get worse the farther downfield Rodgers attempts to throw the ball.
Rodgers has attempted 52 passes between 10 and 19 yards. He's completed 24 of those attempts for a 46.2% completion percentage. That ranks 42nd among all quarterbacks with at least one dropback in 2026, according to SumerSports .
For passes 20 yards or greater, it's even worse. He's attempted 44 passes of 20 yards or more, but he's only completed nine passes. His 20.5% completion percentage ranks 43rd in the NFL among all quarterbacks with at least one dropback this season.
Despite that, the Steelers remain overreliant on Rodgers having the ball in his hands. He's attempted 30 passes or more seven times in nine contests. He and Metcalf continue to create nothing on offense, but the offense won't stop trying to cram a square peg into a round hole.
Right now, Rodgers is on pace to have one of the worst statistical seasons of his NFL career. Sure, he doesn't care about individual statistics, he only cares about ending his final year on the right note.
But it will be very, very hard to end Rodgers' Hall of Fame career on the right note, the way he has been and continues to play.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 3 Risers and Fallers Heading Into Seahawks' Week 11 Bye-Week
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) have some momentum coming out of the 21-13 Week 10 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Seattle has won two consecutive games for the first time since Week 1 and 2 of this season. The offense is finally playing with some consistency and the defense has addressed some of its biggest problems early. Now the team looks to develop more as a team during the bye week.
​At the halfway point of the season, there are changes happening to the Seahawks’ roster . Some players are seeing great changes while others are losing their role or status on the team. A player’s traction on the team can temporarily affect their status or, possibly, affect their future.
​Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is already the best player on the Seahawks and the best receiver in the league. JSN, however, is proving that he should be easily the favorite for his second offensive player of the year award. He should also be considered for the league MVP award as he is on pace to break Calvin Johnson’s single-season receiving yards record . There hasn’t been a player more reliable than JSN this season and this season shows he is the standard of how to be a franchise wide receiver.
​For several weeks, there were Seahawks fans and media outlets were ready for the Seahawks to move one from veteran edge rusher Dante Fowler Jr. In the last two games, however, Fowler has been a more reliable defender off the edge. Fowler accounted for three total tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and a quarterback hit. The Seahawks didn’t trade for an edge during the NFL Trade Deadline, but they have an emergence in Fowler.
​Veteran running back Zach Charbonnert was only six yards away from accounting for his third 100-yard rushing. He rushed for 94 yards on 20 carries for an average of 4.7 yards per carry. Originally, Price was projected to be the No. 1 running back, but the coaching staff seem to want Price to learn under Charbonnet. The coaching staff also values Charbonnet’s veteran leadership , which should be a big boost for his next contract.
​This season has been difficult for the Seahawks’ offensive line, which has regressed as a unit. The player who has arguably regressed the most is right tackle, Abraham Lucas . While he has been a solid run-blocker, he has been a below-average pass-protector. Lucas has allowed six sacks, four hits and 26 pressures this season. Lucas left the game versus the Raiders with an ankle sprain. Head coach Mike Macdonald doesn’t have a timeline set for Lucas to return .
​Just a few weeks ago, there were opportunities for second-year wide receiver Tory Horton to see an increased role and reps after the minor knee injury to Rashid Shaheed, who returned in the game versus Las Vegas. Horton didn’t take advantage of the opportunity to get more playing time. In the game against the Raiders, Horton only had 10 offensive snaps and three special team snaps against the Raiders while not seeing a target.
​Rookie defensive tackle Deven Eastern saw his opportunity by being added to the 53-man active roster after the injuries to veteran defensive tackles Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili . He was added to the roster mostly for depth and as an emergency defensive tackle. After being on the roster for two games, he was waived and signed back to the practice squad.

title: 2 Bye Week Goals for Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are 6-4 as they approach their upcoming Week 11 bye.
The Seahawks are in the mix for a playoff run in the NFC , but to achieve their goals, they need to make the most of their bye week. Here's a look at the two main goals the team should have over the next couple of days.
The Seahawks are incredibly grateful to have Jaxon Smith-Njigba on offense. The reigning offensive player of the year is looking to rack up another trophy, as he is on pace to break the NFL record for most receiving yards in a single season.
With JSN on a record-breaking pace, no other receiver on the offense has more than 300 yards, including Rashid Shaheed, who signed a 3-year, $51 million contract over the offseason. The Seahawks need to find ways to get other players on the offense involved to give them more versatility and optionality.
The fact that the offense is so one-sided toward Smith-Njigba is not good for what the future holds for the team. A predictable offense is harder to win with later in the season, so the team needs to figure out how to make other players more dangerous to other teams. That opens things up for Smith-Njigba because teams will skew their game plans toward stopping him and do whatever it takes to make sure he is blanketed.
JSN has broken all of those tests this season, but eventually someone is going to figure it out. If the Seahawks can showcase a threat elsewhere, it will only make things easier for the unit.
The Seahawks have struggled to stay healthy this season, but even with those struggles, they have maintained a winning record. Getting players like Sam Darnold and Leonard Williams back to full health, along with trade acquisition Quenton Nelson, will likely determine how far the Seahawks go this season.
One of the strengths the Seahawks had last year, which helped them win the Super Bowl, was that a lot of their top players were healthy going into the final weeks of the season. As the team heads toward Thanksgiving, they need to figure out a way to heal so they can put their best 53-man roster on the field on Sundays.
Given how talented and top-heavy the NFC is, this could ultimately be the difference between who advances to the playoffs and who is sent home earlier than they should be.
