title: Making the Case for Sam Darnold and Drew Lock as Seahawks Starter
full_text:
This 2026 NFL Season has been confusing for the Seattle Seahawks (6-4) and the 12. May signs show the Seahawks may have taken a few bad steps back from their Super Bowl-winning form. The offense may be finally establishing itself after the 21-13 road win at the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. There might still be some questions at quarterback that need to be answered.
On Monday, head coach Mike Macdonald already issued a statement that Darnold will be the starting quarterback moving forward, if he is healthy. The biggest factor is whether he is healthy, as he has missed the last two games with a quad and broken ribs injury. There are several reasons why Darnold should start the rest of the season, but there are key reasons why Lock should start.
​The Seahawks have already decided that Darnold is the best fit for the offense long-term. He needs a lot of things around him to be right or nearly perfect. He needs the offensive line healthy, an established running game, competent play calling and a reliable pass-catcher. Darnold has only had one of those all season with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Ngiba . Once he has them, he can outperform expectations, as evident in the NFC Title game.
​With Price and Charbonnet back, offensive coordinator Brian Fleury getting more comfortable with the offense and the offensive line returning healthy, Darnold has what he needs to push the limits for an explosive offense. Darnold possesses the consistency and big-play vision to get the offense rolling. His downside is his turnovers , which have been an issue due to the limited offense and his injuries. Darnold has more upside due to his experience and familiarity with the team.​
Lock is an average starter on other teams that don’t possess the tools for a top-ten offense. When he does, with a team with great experience and the league’s best receiver in JSN, Lock can be inserted into a productive offense and up to the standards of a playoff-caliber quarterback, but only with the Seahawks.
​Through nearly four games for Seattle, filling in for the injured Darnold, Lock has completed 73.1% of his passes for 837 yards, seven touchdowns, no interceptions, a QBR of 85.8 and the league’s second-highest quarterback rating of 125.6. He has been one of the most productive quarterbacks in the games he has started. Lock, however, has started against some of the worst defenses in the league: the Arizona Cardinals (twice) and the Raiders.
​For Lock to be the starter for the rest of the season , he would be the much healthier option and he would need to show he can play against great defenses. The Seahawks will face the San Francisco 49ers (8-1) in Week 12 after their upcoming bye week. San Francisco possesses the fifth-ranked total defense and the 12th-ranked scoring defense in the league. This would be a good test for Lock with this Seahawks offense if Darnold can’t play due to injury.

title: 3 Reasons Why the Seahawks Are Sticking With Sam Darnold
full_text:
I’ve been fairly open in recent times about my preference for the Seattle Seahawks sticking with Drew Lock at quarterback. Yesterday, Mike Macdonald came out and stated in no uncertain terms that Sam Darnold will be getting his job back when health allows. Not my preference, but I can still seek to understand it. So here are three reasons why Sam is the guy.
This first one is nice and simple. The Seahawks won the super bowl about nine months ago, and they did it with Sam Darnold at quarterback. For most of the people in this organization right now, it’s the one and only super bowl they’ve won. I can certainly understand why the team would feel obligated to let Sam play while there’s any hint of ambiguity on who to play.
Lock has mostly played weak defenses this season, while Darnold’s struggles have largely come at the hands of stronger units. He’s also been without his top running backs for most of his games. That’s enough to open the door, and given what Sam did last season, maybe it’s just a matter of respect. He’s earned himself a few more rolls of the dice.
This is probably the ‘best’ reason I can come up with. Maybe the Seahawks believe that Drew Lock has a ceiling lower than winning a championship. Maybe there’s a higher floor with Drew, and maybe there’s more stability to be a playoff team, but when you’re playing a team like the 49ers, Bears, or Vikings, he’s just not going to be able to do enough to get the win.
Darnold, while he’s fully capable of playing some truly awful football, has accessed that ceiling quite a bit here. The ceiling that allowed him to be an MVP candidate in the first half of the season , or out-duel Matthew Stafford to win the NFC. Maybe the assumption concerning Lock is wrong, but if the goal is to win it all, then you play the player who can accomplish that.
This is the one that feels a little more cynical to me. But even still, on some level, I get it. The Seattle Seahawks are a few months away from making a massive decision on Sam Darnold’s future . The decision they make will have a giant effect on the team for the next several seasons. They have to get it right. And right now, they’re not working with a lot of data.
Darnold has missed several games this year, has played through injuries in some of the games he’s played, and has been without several key teammates. Maybe they feel like they have to give Darnold these last seven starts to make sure they know exactly what it is before they make a decision. Even if it costs them a chance to defend their title this year.

title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Is Embroiled in the Greatest OPOTY Race of All-Time
full_text:
In a season full of battles and arguments between members of the fanbase of the Seattle Seahawks, one man is uniting all sides. Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s game is beyond any debate or discussion . But is that uniquely dominant season going to be enough to win Offensive Player of the Year? Normally, yes, but this year is far from normal.
Chances are you already know all about JSN’s incredible season to this point. He’s currently in possession of the NFL’s receiving triple crown, leading the league in receptions (79), yards (1,207), and touchdowns (10). He’s on pace to break the single-season receiving yards record by nearly 100 yards, and his 134 reception and 17 touchdown tracks would be top 10 all-time.
He’s also tops in receptions of 20 or more yards (19), yards after catch (422), and receiving first downs (57). His 82-yard touchdown in week 2 is currently the longest catch in the league for 2026. And he’s doing it in an offense lacking any other credible threats, a run game, high-level quarterback play , or capable offensive coordinator. He might be the best ever.
This is the primary competition right now. While JSN is tracking to have maybe the best WR season ever, Gibbs is making a play to have the greatest RB season ever. He’s the first one to crack 1,000 rushing yards on the year, and is also sitting on 41 catches for 384 yards. Throw in a league-leading 13 touchdowns, and you can see why this is going to be difficult.
His pace, since he’s only played nine games, is 452 touches (4th all-time), 2,613 scrimmage yards (1st by over 100 yards), and 23 touchdowns (8th). If Gibbs can hold these lines, on a great offense with other viable options (Amon-Ra St. Brown is on pace for over 1,400 yards, Jameson Williams for nearly 1,000), it might be better than JSN’s pace.
OPOTY has become the ‘non-QB MVP award’ in recent years, more or less, but it hasn’t always been. As recently as 2018, a quarterback (Patrick Mahomes) won MVP and OPOTY. Matt Ryan, Cam Newton, Peyton Manning, and Tom Brady have done it too. Adrian Peterson, not a quarterback, also managed to win both. So it can most certainly happen.
If it happens this time, it’s Burrow who can pull it off. Joe Shiesty leads the NFL in completion percentage (74.7%), yards per game (310.6), touchdowns (27), and QB rating (117.7) among QBs who have played the whole season. His paces are 5,279 yards (4th all-time) and 51 touchdowns (2nd) are MVP and OPOTY caliber. His QB rating would be 6th in NFL history.
Right now, the odds are in Gibbs’s favor, sitting at +100 compared to JSN’s +125. But that’s not at all definitive. Burrow is essentially off the board, +8000, perhaps indicative of the belief that he won’t win it if he wins MVP, where he’s -115 right now. I’m not sure I agree with that, but assuming the award really is earmarked for non-QBs now, it’s a two-man race. (Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook )
Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER .
And it really might be the best two-man race of all-time. In two months, we really might be looking at the best wide receiver season ever against the best running back season ever. Obviously, the extra game JSN and Gibbs get to play will be part of the conversation. But I don’t think it’ll be the dominant story when the numbers are this incredible.
The Seahawks play some weaker defenses the rest of the way, like Dallas, Philadelphia, and Carolina. But they also have some tougher draws, like two games against the Rams and one against San Francisco. Gibbs only has one easy mark the rest of the way in the Tennessee Titans. Most of his remaining matchups are against top 10 defenses.
However, it’s much easier for JSN to have a slow day than Gibbs right now, simply because Gibbs is a running back. Far less likely he has a game where the ball doesn’t find him, between his complete domination of the rushing attack in Detroit and the receiving production he adds. JSN can occasionally get caught in a low-volume day. So, sadly, right now, advantage Gibbs.

title: Tory Horton May Have Earned Larger Seahawks Role After Raiders Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks dominated on defense and were outstanding on offense, especially in the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 10 victory . Still, it was a special teams play that might have sealed the deal going into the bye week.
With just 2:04 left to go in the game , the Raiders kicked off to the Seahawks after knocking down a field goal to make it a one-score game. The Seahawks knew that a touchback would result in an additional time stoppage, so they wanted to avoid this at all costs. That prompted wide receiver Tory Horton to make arguably the biggest special teams play of the season.
The effort by the Seahawks special teams to prevent the touchback and keep the clock running 👏 SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YF6eTRh4gs
"It kind of bounced off my hands and I kind of just like drifted out of bounds," Horton said via the team's website.
"So, kind of just pointed at Sheed (Rashid Shaheed) to pick the ball up and return it. Just wanted to just keep the ball in play. I wish I caught it with one hand, but that's a pretty hard catch to do with the ball and go inflight like that. So I was still happy that Shaheed recognized the ball was in play and picked it up after I told them and just happy that we got it under 2 minutes."
Going into the contest, Horton wasn't even supposed to be in that position to begin with. However, circumstances changed throughout the game, and that forced Horton into that situation.
"It was a tremendous play," head coach Mike Macdonald added after the game.
"Tory's actually trying to catch that ball, albeit with one hand. Just an incredible play. With George Holani going down, we had to take JD (Jadarian Price) off of kickoff returns, so those are guys that haven't necessarily practiced (kick return) a bunch in a while, especially with this game plan. So to be able to step in and be able to execute some of those critical situations is some great stuff by them, great job by our coaches, and it really helped us close the game out."
Knowing that Horton wasn't even supposed to be in that position but made a play on the fly in a crucial situation that normally doesn't pop up is exactly how the Seahawks want to identify themselves. They have a next-man-up mentality that places importance on all 70 players on the main roster and practice squad, giving them moments to shine like this.
This identity helped carry the Seahawks to the Super Bowl last season, and it is what has them on pace to go all the way once again. It's going to take more plays like this after the bye, but this is a sign that the Seahawks are getting ready to make a run.
The Seahawks will return after the bye week to take on the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:25 p.m. PT inside Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

title: NFL Playoff Picture: Where Are Seahawks Going Into Bye Week?
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are still in the win column after beating the Las Vegas Raiders 21-13 in their Week 10 matchup.
The victory allows them to keep pace in a crowded NFC playoff race that has five teams that are above .500 fighting for three spots. Here's a look at the NFC playoff picture following Week 10.
1. San Francisco 49ers (8-1) — NFC West Leader 2. Detroit Lions (7-2) — NFC North Leader 3. New York Giants (5-3-1) — NFC East Leader 4. Carolina Panthers (4-5) — NFC South Leader 5. Minnesota Vikings (7-2) — Wild Card 1 6. Chicago Bears (7-2) — Wild Card 2 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4) — Wild Card 3 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-6) 11. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) 13. New Orleans Saints (3-6) 14. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 15. Arizona Cardinals (3-7) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7)
The entire NFC North sits above .500, and all four are in the playoff picture. The Minnesota Vikings' win pushes the Green Bay Packers into a tie with Seattle and the Los Angeles Rams, who beat the Arizona Cardinals by multiple scores.
The NFC North is likely going to beat up on each other to the point where at least one team will not be in the playoff picture by season's end. The Vikings are 3-1 in the division, while the Packers are 1-3. The Detroit Lions are 2-0, while the Bears are 0-2. There are plenty of games left between now and the end of the season, and that could make a massive difference in the grand scheme of things.
If one of the NFC North teams falls by the wayside, it opens up a spot for the Seahawks or Rams, who are both 6-4 and fighting for likely one wild card spot. The two teams won't meet until Week 16 of the season, which could be an early start for the playoffs. That means the Seahawks only have four games between now and then to enhance their positioning and get ready for when the games truly start to count.

title: Mike Macdonald Just Ended the Seahawks QB Controversy
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are going into the bye week after a pair of big wins from backup quarterback Drew Lock.
Lock is 3-0 as the Seahawks starter this season, which is the same amount of wins Darnold has as the team's starter. This includes Darnold's start in Week 1 against the New England Patriots when he was substituted out of the game due to a glute injury for Lock.
Darnold's struggles and Lock's success could lead many to believe a quarterback change is on the horizon. However, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald shut down the possibility of switching things up when the team returns to the field in Week 12.
"Yeah, I'd say we're really optimistic that he's going to be able to get a full week's worth of work and be able to play against San Fran," Macdonald said of Darnold via Seattle Sports 710 AM.
Mike Macdonald on @SeattleSports on if they think Darnold will be able to practice next week... "Yeah, I'd say we're really optimistic that he's going to be able to get a full week's worth of work and be able to play against San Fran."
Darnold has struggled with interceptions this season, throwing nine in seven games with the team. That has been the primary issue the Seahawks have dealt with in games where Darnold is under center. However, the Seahawks believe he still provides them with the best chance of winning moving forward.
So far this season, Lock has thrown 93 passes without an interception. He has seven touchdowns as well, including two against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10. However, Lock did fumble the ball twice, which could part of the reason they aren't making a change.
The Seahawks should be basing this decision on what has happened this season rather than what happened last year. Darnold was brilliant last season, and winning a Super Bowl shouldn't go unnoticed. However, he has not performed at the same level this season as he did in 2025. Lock has been strong in his absence, which does warrant some consideration for a change.
The Seahawks have to hope that McDonald and the coaching staff are making this decision for the right reasons. It isn't about what has happened in the past, but rather about who puts the team in the best position to win in the future. Lock has shown that he can lead the team to a win more often than Darnold.
While that shouldn't be the only reason behind the decision, it should be under consideration as the team prepares for the home stretch.

title: Seahawks Run Game vs. Raiders Proves Not Trading for Jonathan Taylor Was Smart
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are feeling pretty good about themselves after a 21-13 victory against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 inside Allegiant Stadium.
In the win, the Seahawks had their best game on the ground to date. It has been an inconsistent issue throughout the season, but it all came together against the Raiders . It proves that their decision not to trade for Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor was the right one.
In the win against the Raiders, Zach Charbonnet led the backfield with 20 carries for 94 yards. Meanwhile, rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price ran the ball nine times for 36 yards and a touchdown, proving that there was a solid one-two punch in the running back room.
"We were hoping to take another step in the run game today [and] I thought we did," head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame via the team's website.
Price spoke about how the committee approach the team is taking is infectious and how each of them is making each other better.
"We've been doing a pretty good job," Price said via the team's website. "Watching Charbs (Zach Charbonnet) go out there and make guys miss, break tackles and stuff like that, it makes you want to go out there and do the same. I like where our offense is heading."
The trade deadline last week sent the league into a frenzy as multiple blockbuster deals were consummated. Taylor was one of the big names discussed as the Colts went into a fire sale, which included a deal with the Seahawks for offensive lineman Quenton Nelson . Ultimately, the Seahawks chose not to trade for Taylor, or any available running back for that matter.
Taylor stuck with the Colts and ran the ball 16 times for 83 yards in a 24-22 win against the Miami Dolphins.
While a Taylor trade would have made sense by improving one of Seattle's weak spots, the team ultimately concluded that the lack of run-game production had to do with injuries to Price and Charbonnet. Earlier in the season, it took them a few weeks to get some momentum, but now that they have both been active for the past three games, the Seahawks have an established plan moving forward.

title: Hanich Panic Meter: Seahawks' JSN Could Break Single Season Record
full_text:
In just two years, Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba became a No. 1 pass-catcher. Just one year late last season, JSN became a superstar and became the league’s offensive player of the year. He might finish up his fourth season with one of the most legendary achievements.
​ JSN, once again, played like the elite player he is and became the Seahawks’ offense to help Seattle win 21-13 at the Las Vegas Raiders. He caught eight receptions for 171 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Raiders. Just like he was last season, JSN is on pace to break Calvin Johnson’s single-season record of 1,964 yards set in 2012. There is a great chance he may accomplish it in 16 games as opposed to 17 games.
​Through 10 games this season, JSN has caught 79 receptions for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns. He is only 758 yards away from breaking Johnson’s record. For JSN to break the record, he would have to average 108.3 yards in each of the remaining seven games. To break the record in the same 16-game timeframe as Johnson, JSN would have to average 126.4 yards in each of the remaining six games,
​He has accounted for at least 100 yards in eight of the ten games this season. It doesn’t matter if it’s Sam Darnold or Drew Lock throwing him the ball; he finds a way to open. He has 721 receiving yards from Darnold and 486 in nearly four games from Lock. He is easily a solid path to be named offensive player of the year for a second consecutive season and, possibly, league MVP if the award were quarterback-focused.
​JSN was on pace to break Johnson’s all-time receiving record last season. Through 11 games last season, JSN caught 80 receptions for 1,313 yards and seven touchdowns. This meant he only had 652 more yards in the remaining six games to break the record. It was at that point, there was some offensive fatigue and the running game had to be re-established. JSN would only account for 480 yards during the final games to finish with 1,793 yards.
​Last season, it seemed like it was a surprise that JSN was so elite at creating enough separation and making big plays after the catch with his speed and elusiveness. This season, despite being mentioned as one of the top receivers in the league, he is still getting open so much. He has a great feel with either Darnold or Lock throwing him the ball . It seems like no matter how many times the opposing defenses game plan around him, JSN still finds ways to get open.

title: Exclusive: How 49ers TE George Kittle's Positive Mindset Helped Him Through Achilles Rehab
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle's biggest strength is his infectious energy and unwavering drive to strive for excellence in everything he does.
It's no surprise that this mindset has helped him become the franchise's all-time leader in touchdowns among tight ends.
However, the highs of Kittle's career were met with a significant setback during the offseason, as his life changed drastically after he suffered a torn Achilles in the NFC Wild Card game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Yet despite the adversity of his biggest injury setback so far, Kittle recalled that his unwavering positive energy kept him going throughout the offseason, always keeping Week 1 in sight.
"Yes, my life definitely changed," admitted Kittle to 49ers on SI's Henry Cheal.
"My off-seasons have been pretty consistent for the last ten years. I had another surgery after the 2023 season, but that was fairly straightforward and the rehabilitation process didn't take too long.
"This time, my goal throughout the entire process was simply to get back out there for Week 1.
"When I spoke to my surgeon, even before the surgery, he told me, 'Hey, you have a chance.' And I said, 'That's all I need. Just tell me I have a chance.'
"You don't really have to do much to motivate me. I'm a pretty motivated person every single day when I wake up. I love life, I play football for a living, and I don't have a lot to complain about. I'm pretty excited to get up every single day.
"I think that mindset was one of the things that allowed me to get back because every day of rehabilitation was enjoyable for me. Yes, it was meticulous and incredibly boring at times, but overall, I thoroughly enjoyed it.
"I will say that my off-season didn't change as much as I thought it was going to. With an Achilles injury, you don't necessarily need someone working on you every single day.
"For example, if you have a knee injury, you might need people stretching your knee and working on your legs every day. With my injury, I was able to do a lot of the first eight weeks of rehabilitation by myself.
"That meant I could still go on holiday with my wife and enjoy myself, which I thought was important for my mental health. You don't want to spend every single day in the same building doing the same thing over and over again. I think that would have driven me mad!
"Overall, I think having a very, very positive mindset can take you a long way."
Kittle subsequently made his return to the field for the season opener in Melbourne in Week 1. Since then, he has recorded 557 receiving yards and five touchdowns, performing as though the Achilles injury had never happened .
Sometimes, motivation can be found in the lowest moments, and Kittle made sure to use that adversity as fuel.

title: 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk Opens Up on How Much Longer He Wants to Play in the NFL
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers face an intriguing decision this offseason regarding veteran fullback Kyle Juszczyk .
The 2026 season, like fellow teammate George Kittle, marks a decade with the 49ers after both joined in 2017.
Juszczyk is 35 right now, and after hitting free agency momentarily in March 2025, he signed a two-year contract, which means he will become an unrestricted free agent heading into 2027.
The noticeable achievement of playing for San Francisco can't be ignored. A decade with one team deserves all the praise. That said, considering that half of the regular-season games have been played, there's been no talk or speculation about an extension.
When asked by NBC Sports Bay Area about setting a goal on how much longer he wants to play in the NFL, Juszczyk shared: "I don't. It's so hard to put a number on it.
"I was having this conversation with Fred Warner the other day. It's easy to say you've got a few more years left. What's difficult is when you're looking at that final year.
"I've been saying I've got a few more years for a long time. That's what I told Fred because he said he couldn't imagine what it would be like playing for 15 years.
"I told him that he might say that now, but it's easy to say you've got a few more years when you're not looking at the final one. When you're thinking, 'This is my last year,' it's not easy to pull the trigger and say you're done.
"That's kind of where I feel like I am right now. I'm just going to keep saying I've got a few more years because I can't say this is my last season. I don't want to say next year will be my last year, either. It's easier to keep pushing that decision down the line a little bit."
Regardless of how long he's around for, whether Juszczyk stays or goes will be a major talking point in the offseason. What will his valuation be? What will the 49ers decide to do? He also recently said he's a "fullback when it comes to contract negotiations" while calling himself a tight end.
There are arguments to be made on both sides, but it remains a fascinating situation for the 49ers to think about. Juszczyk's experience, versatility and importance within the locker room will all factor into the decision, making his future one to watch closely as the offseason approaches.

title: Why Kyle Shanahan Sees Christian McCaffrey as a 'Perfect Mentor' for 49ers' Kaelon Black
full_text:
If one aspect of the San Francisco 49ers deserves praise this year, it's their running back coaching .
Christian McCaffrey's reduced workload has played a massive part in that. The 49ers kept their word throughout the offseason, and rookie Kaelon Black is already proving to be a valuable addition in easing the burden, albeit only some of the time .
The two running backs are producing at an identical rate, averaging 4.5 yards per carry. McCaffrey has naturally (and unsurprisingly) had more opportunities, accumulating 519 rushing yards from 115 carries, while Black has managed 356 yards on 79 attempts.
Black has now spent half a season learning from McCaffrey. There are few better running backs in the league to learn from. McCaffrey is not only an excellent runner but also a reliable receiver who offers plenty in the passing game. His 1,000-1,000 yard season says enough.
With injuries to offensive weapons becoming a frequent occurrence in 2025 and this season, McCaffrey's importance to the 49ers has only increased. He led the team in both rushing and receiving last season and currently ranks second in receiving behind George Kittle.
“I think Christian’s the perfect mentor just because even if he doesn’t say anything, just how Christian works every second. Christian’s the most detailed, focused, obsessive player I’ve ever been around," shared head coach Kyle Shanahan on Monday .
"Just watch how he blocks when Deebo’s [Samuel Sr.] running back and he’s playing receiver and just the technique and the effort he goes through on every single play.
"Just the way Christian plays football is the best example or mentor to anybody who’s on our team or anybody who wants to watch how a football player goes about his business. I also think Christian really respects Kaelon.
"I remember Christian telling me right when he got here how much of a pro that guy seemed like and seemed like he was made of the right stuff.
"It’s because K.B., similar to Christian, he works at everything. He’s very hard on himself. He’s very tough and approaches each day to get better. As talents and as people, I think they pair together very well.”
This could prove particularly valuable for San Francisco in the long run. McCaffrey won't be able to maintain his current level forever, but Black showing similar traits gives the 49ers another reason to be encouraged about their future at running back.
Black has made a notable impact in several games, but his performance against the Dallas Cowboys saw a big step in his development.

title: Why 49ers LT Trent Williams Could Play in the NFL in His 40s
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams has teased retirement at the end of 2027, but has now stated he could play for even longer.
Back in April, Williams signed a two-year contract extension, meaning he will be 39 upon expiration.
He's previously said he's open to playing until he's 40 , but he's also hinted that the contract he signed could be his last due to understandable family reasons. Nobody knows what he'll ultimately decide, of course, but his recent interview could suggest that he's considering playing well into his 40s.
“I’m a huge competitor. This game has changed my life in so many ways and I just can’t find a reason to let it go," Williams shared on Bay Area Radio Station KNBR .
"I know the accolades and everything is fine, me being 38 years old is fine, but I still have a passion to play this game. I think I’ve been supremely blessed to be able to have the ability and the mindset to take me deep into my career to where I still want more.
"It’s an obsession of mine. Football is one of the things I dream about. I wake up thinking about it. I go to sleep thinking about it.
"If I still have the ability to put what I think is good productive play on film, it’ll be hard for me to look at my teammates in the face and hang my cleats up. As long as I feel that god gives me the grace to get out there and be the player I know I can be, I’m gonna be lacing them up.”
Realistically, Williams has all the leverage if he continues to produce at a high level. He's still one of the best players in the league at his position.
Whether that means continuing with the 49ers or elsewhere, nobody truly knows. What's certain is that San Francisco needs him right now. He's ranked second among tackles in the league by PFF with a 90.1 overall grade, second in pass-blocking grade with an 87.8, and fifth in overall grade with an 84.9.
Stats like these, especially when considering Williams' age, show that at 38, he continues to prove he's a once-in-a-generation player whose impact cannot be overstated.
No matter what happens, his importance to San Francisco remains undeniable, and replacing a player of his caliber would be an enormous challenge for the organization when the time of his departure arrives.

title: Kyle Shanahan Explains 49ers Tough Nate Hobbs Decision
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers did not activate cornerback Nate Hobbs from the IR despite returning to practice for a second week. Head coach Kyle Shanahan made it clear that the decision was purely roster-related. They thought that Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir were healthy enough to get through the game. On top of that, they liked Ephesians Prysock as their backup over Hobbs.
"Because we thought those two gave us the best chance to win," said Shanahan on why he did not decide to activate Hobbs.
When asked if the team would activate Hobbs this week, Shanahan made it clear that it would have nothing to do with his ability or health. It would be more of a decision about roster numbers.
"I'm not sure,” said Shanahan on Monday after the game. “It's Monday, so we've got to see how it goes. You've always got to cut someone to activate someone too, so we've got to see how everyone is. But he's looked good these last two weeks. I know he's chomping at the bit to get back out there and won't hesitate to do it if that makes sense for our 53."
The 49ers have until November 25th to activate Hobbs. So, they can let him sit for one more week, but they would have to quickly make a move before Week 12 to activate him and release a player from their roster.
San Francisco is thin on the defensive line and at cornerback. However, both Nate Hobbs and C.J. West are expected to return to the lineup soon. The team could release Khalil Kareem as one of the corresponding moves. However, the other move that they would make is tough .
If San Francisco likes Prysock over Hobbs, and Siran Neal is their best special teams asset, there is no defined role for Hobbs on the roster. They would add him to the roster and make him a healthy scratch in his first game back.
Still, they have to activate him. They are not the team to let a healthy player be lost for the season because of too much depth. Green and Lenoir are still working through injuries, and Prysock is still unknown. It helps that they trust Prysock right now and do not have to force Hobbs onto the roster.
However, the move is going to have to come soon. We will see who gets released.

title: 49ers Coach Opens Up on Nick Bosa's Struggles
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are still waiting to get the Nick Bosa that was expected before the season in 2026. After Bosa had multiple offside penalties overshadowing a couple of pressures in his second game back from injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked what he saw from Bosa so far .
Shanahan noted that there are some plays that it looks like the All-Pro rusher is back to his old ways. However, he also made it clear that there is still some rust to be shaken off from the 29-year-old who missed Weeks 3-8.
"I see Nick working his way back,” admitted Shanahan. “I think that he has a number of plays that look just like Nick, and I think he's had a few plays that don't.  I think Nick's ready to go, and I think he's definitely affecting the quarterback and doing some good things out there.”
Shanahan added that Bosa has missed a lot of time. He was recovering from an ACL injury this past offseason. He played for two weeks and injured his calf. In total, he has played seven games in the past year and a half. So, the 49ers head coach expects him to take some time before he is fully himself.
“Nick's going to get better the more he gets back with us,” admitted Shanahan. “He's taken a lot of time off with his injury. He had a lot of time off before that, going into Australia with his injury over the summer and everything like that, or from last year, so he hasn't gotten to play a lot of football.”
However, Shanahan made it clear that he is not worried about Bosa, and expects him to record his first sack of the season any week now.
“I still see a guy out there who's a top pass rusher, who does a lot of good things,” added Shanahan. “He's got to handle the majority of the chips, which doesn't give him as many opportunities on the edge. But I'm not worried about Nick. Nick's going to get better each week, and he'll eventually get there."
Bosa has seven pressures since returning to the lineup, according to PFF. The team has now only played two games with Mykel Williams healthy alongside Bosa. We will see if the duo can flash more in the 49ers' Week 11 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

title: 49ers Aren’t Hitting the Panic Button on Their Underwhelming Pass Rush
full_text:
The main reason the San Francisco 49ers allowed the Dallas Cowboys to make it a close game in the end was because of their defense, specifically their pass rush .
It was underwhelming against the Cowboys. They failed to make it difficult for Dak Prescott. He was only sacked once, and that sack was because he ran out of bounds with Dre Greenlaw in pursuit.
Prescott was pressured only 16 times on 54 dropbacks. The 49ers’ pass rush has been underwhelming in the last two games despite Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner returning. But this game, especially, was eyebrow-raising.
Bosa, Buckner, Osa Odighizuwa- someone, anyone- should’ve made at least one play with the Cowboys needing to pass often in the fourth quarter. Yet no one stepped up. Despite that, the 49ers aren’t hitting the panic button.
“Obviously, we didn't get any sacks, but I thought we affected the quarterback,” Kyle Shanahan said on Monday via conference call with reporters. “I thought we hit him. I thought we wore down as the game went. I wouldn't have said it was a bad pass rush game by any means if I never watched the fourth quarter.
“But, by the time we got to the fourth quarter, I thought we had a chance, it was 38-19 with like nine-and-a-half minutes to go, and I thought we had a number of chances to get them off the field. Everyone had their moments in that, but then I thought we really died out and the pass rush disappeared. I thought all 11 did, but mainly our D-Line.”
Translation: The 49ers’ pass rush was adequate until they couldn’t maintain the fast pace of the game by the fourth quarter. They were all running on an empty gas tank.
That can’t be helped, especially when the Cowboys are moving fast. The 49ers couldn’t rotate and keep their best players off the field if they wanted to. But Shanahan isn’t excusing his pass rushers. He knows they need to be better if they want to go far this year.
“We’ve got to be able to finish better. We’ve got to clean some stuff up. I thought there were some times that we did rush them real well and Dak [Prescott] did a good job getting rid of it. Sometimes they had some chippers that we need to rush better on because we didn't get there at all. But, for the whole part of the game we’ve definitely got to do better.”

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Isn’t Worried About Nick Bosa — Yet
full_text:
It hasn’t been the most encouraging performances from Nick Bosa in the San Francisco 49ers ’ last two games.
He’s lacking the significant impact that we’re accustomed to seeing from him, which can be attributed to rust. Bosa missed five games due to a calf injury, undoing all the momentum he was building up for himself.
He still hasn’t notched a sack this season and has only recorded 12 pressures. It gets to a point where you have to wonder if Bosa is rusty or if he’s lost a step . If you asked Kyle Shanahan what he’s seeing from Bosa, he’d say that he isn’t worried about him — yet.
“I see Nick working his way back. I think that he has a number of plays that look just like Nick and I think he's had a few plays that doesn't,” Shanahan said. “I think Nick's ready to go and I think he's definitely affecting the quarterback and doing some good things out there.
“But, Nick's going to get better the more he gets back with us. He's taken a lot of time off with his injury. He had a lot of time off before that, going into Australia with his injury over the summer and everything like that, or from last year, so he hasn't gotten to play a lot of football.”
Translation: Bosa is performing well despite all of the setbacks in the last four months, but the 49ers will need him to find his groove soon. They could’ve used high-level Bosa in the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys.
That is a moment where he’d take over in the past. But he, along with the other defensive linemen, failed to rise to the occasion. Given what Shanahan said, it’s only a matter of time before Bosa can return to his elite form. He’s still encouraged by what he sees from Bosa.
“I still see a guy out there who's a top pass rusher, who does a lot of good things,” said Shanahan. “He's got to handle the majority of the chips, which doesn't give him as many opportunities on the edge. But, I'm not worried about Nick. Nick's going to get better each week and he’ll eventually get there.”
It’s good that Shanahan is giving Bosa some grace with all the time he’s missed. But only so many more games can pass by without Bosa being significantly impactful before the 49ers start to truly worry.
If he can’t make his mark at least a couple of times before the regular season ends, they will feel extreme worry internally. For now, they’ll hold out hope he hits his stride in the next several games.

title: 3 Overreactions to 49ers' Stressful Win Against Cowboys
full_text:
It was a game that was much tougher to win than expected, but the San Francisco 49ers got the job done against the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40.
However, because the game was a stressful win, there are few overreactions to unpack. Here are my three overreactions from the 49ers' Week 10 win against the Cowboys.
Dak Prescott lit up the 49ers, and how couldn't he? There was no pass rush to bother him throughout the game. Prescott was extremely comfortable on nearly every dropback. He was only pressured 16 times, for a 29.6% pressure rate.
A defensive front with Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner, and Osa Odighizuwa, that is pitiful. They need to be a lot better than that if they want to avoid giving up 40 points in a game. But this has happened for the second straight game.
The 49ers' pass rush wasn't a significant factor against the Las Vegas Raiders either. For a team with Super Bowl aspirations, this must improve. They will not win the Super Bowl without an effective pass rush. This is a concern until proven otherwise.
If Brock Purdy hadn't put on his superhero cape , the 49ers would've lost to the Cowboys. He was amazing in this game and strengthened his MVP case.
However, the fact that the 49ers needed him to play at such a level for them to beat the Cowboys, who are no better than average, is concerning.
Is this what the 49ers need to win games? Does Purdy have to perform at an incredible level every game? Given their ineffective pass rush, it may be true, but it's unfair unless others pick up the slack.
The only bright side to that is it would exponentially help his MVP case since Purdy will be the driving force of the 49ers' success while overcoming other weak areas.
Is the 49ers' offensive line declining after their hot start to the season? They just made the Cowboys' defensive front look like a top-five unit. Purdy was sacked five times and pressured 12 times on 35 dropbacks.
It's the highest pressure rate (34.3%) he's faced since Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks. It's one thing to have a difficult time against Seattle, but the Cowboys? It was a concerning performance by the 49ers' offensive line.
Maybe it was just one game slide, with the Cowboys extra motivated. But the offensive line could be leaking oil, and it's not going to get better next week against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense.

title: 9 Winners and Losers From 49ers' Week 10 Win Over Cowboys
full_text:
Defeating the Dallas Cowboys was way more stressful than it needed to be for the San Francisco 49ers . It went down to the wire before they sealed the deal in a 46-40 win.
Several 49ers stood out positively in this game as winners, while a few others were negatives. Let's take a look at the winners and losers from the 49ers' Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
Someone hand Brock Purdy a top hat and a wand because he looked like a magician against the Cowboys. The 49ers needed him to be, or they would've lost.
Purdy strengthened his MVP case with his immaculate performance, completing 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards (career-high), three touchdowns, and no turnovers. He did all of that despite a bunch of pressure in his face throughout the game.
Another elite 49ers performer was Christian McCaffrey. He tallied three touchdowns and 223 scrimmage yards. But his most impressive work was his two touchdown catches and runs that made history.
McCaffrey caught a 74-yard and a 66-yard touchdown pass, becoming the first running back in NFL history to have multiple receiving touchdowns of at least 65 yards in a game. Have yourself a day, McCaffrey.
Running 20 routes and catching five passes for 61 yards probably isn't what the 49ers had in mind for Keenan Allen in this game. But that's exactly what he did, and they needed it.
Allen's contributions helped sustain drives and kept the passing game flowing. The 49ers needed a wide receiver who could separate with Mike Evans out. Allen has answered that need.
What a breakout game for rookie Kaelon Black. He's a tough running back to bring down, as shown by his 25-yard touchdown run. This kind of performance has been brewing since Week 7.
His numbers may not be that impressive (11 rushes for 53 yards), but his impact is as clear as day. He's been a solid addition to the 49ers' offense.
He only reeled in two catches for 49 yards, but make no mistake. Watkins is a winner from this game. It's another example of how he's becoming a key offensive player. Whenever he gets his chances, he makes the most of them. He continues to be rewarded.
It was an extremely rough game for Deommodore Lenoir. The Cowboys made a point of picking on him in coverage. Lenoir was targeted 16 times, allowing 10 catches for 134 yards and three touchdowns.
George Pickens outclassed him. I'm sure playing with compromised health hindered Lenoir, so he gets credit for toughing it out. Still, he was demolished. It was by far the worst game of his NFL career.
One of the touchdowns Lenoir allowed could've been avoided had Marques Sigle not abandoned his zone. The 49ers were in quarters coverage, so Sigle had a deep quarter zone.
Yet for some reason, he charged downhill within seconds of the ball being snapped. It seems he bit on the play action, which was foolish. He left Lenoir on the island with Pickens, who scored where Sigle should've been in his zone.
It felt like on almost every pass attempt, Connor Cobly was being driven back. He was having a difficult time holding his own. The entire offensive line wasn't playing up to par, which is why Purdy was sacked five times. But Colby's struggles stood out the most, as usual.
The 49ers' pass rush was their most pitiful performance in this game. They were ineffective for the second consecutive game. Except this time, they were downright nonexistent. Dak Prescott was pressured only 16 times on his 54 dropbacks.
A pass rush led by Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner, and Osa Odighizuwa must be better. It needs to be better. That's enough talent to make an impact. They don't need to pop off for five sacks or more a game, but it can't be as poor as it was in this game.

title: What We Saw From Baker Mayfield at Buccaneers Practice and What it Means
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 3-6 and still treading water as they look to make the playoffs. They're a game out of the division lead, but every game is crucial from here on out — and they have what may be their toughest game of the year on Sunday.
The Bucs are set to play the Detroit Lions on the road in Week 11. The Lions are 7-2 and boast one of the best offenses in football, and the Bucs will have to keep up on both sides of the ball to pull off the upset and get the win.
Their best shot at doing that would be with their starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield. But Mayfield is dealing with an ankle injury he picked up against the Chicago Bears, and his status for Week 11 heading into this week has been up in the air.
Here's the latest report on Mayfield's status, combined with what we saw from him at One Buccaneer Place on Wednesday:
ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday morning that Mayfield is a "long shot" to play against the Lions, but that he's more likely than not to play against the Carolina Panthers in Week 12's divisional game.
"From my understanding, the Bucs know Mayfield is probably a long shot for this week but also know Mayfield will push to get ready and play, so they aren't ruling out the possibility," Fowler wrote . "There's more optimism about next week's matchup with Carolina, a crucial divisional game."
Wednesday's practice seemed to corroborate that. Mayfield did appear at toward the end of practice, but he was a non-participant. He did not appear to be in a walking boot, however, which is a good sign for the long-term status of his injury as the Bucs head into a crucial set of games.
First practice back from the bye — Antoine Winfield Jr. and Baker Mayfield didn’t practice, but Yaya Diaby IS practicing.
If it were to lean one way, it doesn't seem like Mayfield will play. The Buccaneers have already moved quarterback availability to Thursday as opposed to the usual Wednesday, and if Mayfield didn't practice at all on Wednesday, he's unlikely to rally and start against the Lions on Sunday.
Should Mayfield be unable to play, the Bucs would turn to Jalon Daniels, who has already started three games for the team. In his three starts, Daniels is 1-2 with three touchdowns and five interceptions. Mayfield himself is 2-4 as a starter in Tampa Bay this year, throwing three touchdowns and four interceptions.
The Bucs will face the Lions at Ford Field in Detroit at 1 p.m. It will be a tough task, but from here on out, every game is crucial for this Bucs squad.

title: The Craziest Buccaneers Stats Through the First Half of the Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had a season of ups and downs (mostly downs). They're 3-6 and have the worst passing offense in football, but they're just a game out of the NFC South, have an elite defense and boast an impressive running game.
The Bucs are, in many ways, a statistical enigma — it's hard to tell whether they are much better than their record or right where they're supposed to be. We've collected a few stats that make the Bucs a bizarre football team throughout their first nine games of the season.
The Buccaneers have the best rushing offense in the NFL (163.9 rushing yards per game) and the very worst passing offense in the NFL (141.9 net passing yards per game). They also have more rushing yards than passing yards at this stage of the year — not great.
The Bucs have to find ways to throw the football if they want to win games. They can really lean on the run game (and have in all of their wins), but the passing game has failed them in more ways than one.
Bucs kicker Chase McLaughlin has yet to miss a kick in any capacity. He's a pristine 22-for-22 on field goal attempts and he's 18-for-18 on extra point attempts. He's also Tampa Bay's leading scorer, currently accounting for 84 points.
We don't mean to jinx him, but McLaughlin could be on his way to a historic season. Three NFL kickers in history — Gary Anderson, Jeff Wilkins and Mike Vanderjagt — have had a perfect kicking season during the regular season.
Only Vanderjagt has had a perfect season through the regular season and the playoffs. The Bucs would have to make it to the playoffs for McLaughlin to test out that record, too.
The Buccaneers are 3-6 and one of the worst teams in the NFL by record (and most of the others are also in the NFC South). Despite that record, though, the team has a positive point differential of +24 points. That's the 11th-best number in the NFL.
Every team ahead of Tampa Bay has won six or more games. The Bucs have lost every single one of their games by one score, and two of those losses were by three points.
Tampa Bay has had a blowout against the Panthers to help increase that number, and holding the Atlanta Falcons to zero points the week after helped their differential, too. But two things seem to be for certain — the Buccaneers find themselves in close games a lot, and they have a lot of trouble actually winning them.
The Bucs have been doing this for the past few years now, but they seem to play better on the road than they do at home.
The Bucs are 2-2 on the road this year, but they're just 1-4 when playing at Raymond James Stadium. Their average points scored across those splits is also fairly interesting — they average 16.8 points per game on the road and 29.5 on the road.
The team's win over the Panthers is a bit of an outlier, by either way, the Bucs seem more comfortable on the road. Thankfully, they'll be heading to Detroit to play the Lions next Sunday at 1 p.m.

title: Chris Godwin is Costing the Buccaneers $85,000 Per Yard Right Now
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers passing attack has been their weakness this season.
The Bucs currently own the NFL's worst passing game in the league, having not even thrown for over 1,500 yards at the midway point of the season and not a single wide receiver eclipsing the 300-yard mark.
It hasn't been pretty, and for one wideout in particular, it's starting to look even worse thanks to how much money he is making.
Former Pro Bowl wide receiver Chris Godwin signed a contract extension with the Bucs before the start of the 2025 season for three years, worth $66 million. The $22 million per year was enough to keep him in Tampa Bay rather than seeing him walk to a team like the New England Patriots.
But now, just a year and a half into that deal, it's looking like a massive overpay.
Godwin has never looked quite right after dislocating his ankle in 2024, and his stats mirror that sentiment.
Last season, Godwin had the lowest receiving yardage total of his career with just 360 yards. He also only saw action in nine games as he dealt with rehab and injuries, and he only found the end zone twice.
Now, Godwin, who has already seen as much action as he did all of 2025, is set to have yet another down season. Godwin has only mustered 29 catches for 259 yards and no touchdowns.
That means that he is currently earning nearly $85,000 per yard in annual cash compensation. That is not a great return on your value or investment. If you account for his actual salary cap hit, that number gets higher at $130,050 per yard.
It's highly unlikely that a magic wand is waved and the Bucs' passing game improves enough for Godwin's contract to be worth it. That means the Bucs' front office should be looking at alternatives this offseason.
Godwin's team option, $20.7 million, is in 2027. However, the Bucs do have a potential out once the 2026 season concludes if they decide to cut bait with the aging wideout.
If Tampa Bay decides to cut Godwin outright before June 1, they would not only save the $22 million he is owed in salary, but they would also save approximately $13.7 million in cap space with his dead money coming way down.
There are always options on the table, however. Godwin and the Bucs could decide to meet for him to take a massive pay cut to stay with the team until his contract runs out — see Jamel Dean just last year — before he hits free agency.
They also could come together on a trade that could net them draft capital this offseason, but this scenario seems highly unlikely as they should have traded him beforehand if they were to go that route.

title: Why Wide Receiver is the Buccaneers' Biggest Need
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have plenty of areas to look at fixing this offseason when the regular season wraps up.
The Bucs are 3-6 at the moment, and if that gets worse, head coach may be an area the Bucs try to improve on after five years of Todd Bowles. The team could also serve to shore up its interior offensive line, and tight end will definitely be a point of consideration.
There's one area that may be the most crucial for Tampa Bay, though. And unfortunately for the Bucs, they've spent a lot of draft capital investing in that position very, very recently.
There are a lot of problems with Tampa Bay's offense. Bucs' offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is having some trouble scheming up the passing game, and quarterback Baker Mayfield is having some trouble executing that already-poor scheme.
Those are all parts of it. But the Bucs need wide receivers desperately because, right now, the lack of talent in that room is a big reason why the passing game has faltered the way it has.
Wideout Jalen McMillan is injured and has been since Week 2 of the NFL season. In his absence, the Bucs have rolled with three main wideouts — Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Tez Johnson. Neither of those receivers have over 300 yards at the moment, with Egbuka leading the pack at just 278.
Godwin is on a three-year, $22 million deal, and his age has shown itself over the past two seasons. Johnson has been good in spurts, but he doesn't have the skill set to be a main target in Tampa Bay, and he isn't big enough to be a viable threat between the hashes that the Bucs desperately need at the moment.
Finally, there are the two players the team drafted over the last two years. Egbuka was supposed to be a future WR1 for this team when he was drafted in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, but he hasn't looked the part at all from the back half of last season through this one. He lacks physicality at the catch point, struggles with getting separation and has been battling injury frequently this year.
The Bucs also drafted wideout Ted Hurst in the third round of this year's NFL Draft, and while it's very early, he hasn't made much of an impact this year. He's dropped two passes that could have been touchdowns, and his drop problem was bad enough against the Chicago Bears that he got benched early in the game.
The Bucs are 3-6 right now. It's unknown exactly where they are going to pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but they should definitely be looking for help at wideout. They need a receiver who can open up the middle of the field for them and be able to get separation through either their speed or their route-running acumen — the Bucs have neither on the squad right now.
Tampa Bay plays the Detroit Lions at 1 p.m. on the road Sunday.

title: What the Buccaneers Signing Cooper Rush Really Means
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers added to their quarterback room on Monday, signing quarterback Cooper Rush to their practice squad. The move would have been very strange just a few days ago, but new information puts the move into perspective.
Rush comes to the Buccaneers after a new report about starting quarterback Baker Mayfield. Mayfield is reportedly dealing with an injured leg and ankle, and his status against the Detroit Lions is uncertain.
Rush's signing might reveal more about that uncertainty, though, and it may not be good for the Bucs.
Rush signing with the Bucs at all makes it more unlikely than not that Mayfield plays against the Lions.
The Bucs would need an emergency third quarterback on the practice squad should Mayfield be out, and Rush would serve that role. He has no prior experience with any Bucs coaches, but he is a veteran who has started two games in the NFC South so far this season.
The Bucs would probably have turned to quarterback Brett Rypien for this, but Rypien signed with the Raiders' practice squad before they pursued Rush.
Additionally, Tampa Bay's previous practice squad quarterback, Easton Stick, was elevated to the 53-man roster on Monday after hitting the limit for three elevations, which he accrued while backup Jalon Daniels filled in for Mayfield when Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3.
Rush's signing — and Stick's elevation — seem to mean that the Bucs are seriously worried Mayfield will not play in Week 11 against the Detroit Lions, if they aren't absolutely certain of it by now. Should that be the case, Daniels would serve as QB1, Stick would back him up as QB2 and Rush would only enter the game in an emergency as the team's emergency QB3, which all teams are allowed to have on game day.
The Bucs will face off against the Lions in Detroit at 1 p.m. on Sunday. Rush's arrival seems to indicate that Daniels, an undrafted free agent rookie, will take the helm of the offense once again.

title: One Buccaneers Rookie Is Making a Lot of People Look Wrong
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers drafted linebacker Josiah Trotter early in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft with the expectation that he would contribute to a unit that had declined drastically over the years.
Like any rookie entering the league, there were plenty of red flags around him. His coverage, particularly in space when matched up with running backs and tight ends, was horrendous, and his passion for the game would sometimes cause over-aggressiveness, which would then lead to missed tackles.
While he still has his moments, Trotter has quickly taken himself from a rotational linebacker in Todd Bowles' defensive scheme to a three-down starter, shutting up those who doubted him or thought he was drafted too early.
Trotter has played extremely well for a rookie alongside Alex Anzalone, and he has been a key piece in the defensive turnaround this season.
Trotter's biggest strength has been the ability to fill gaps in the running lanes, and he is tied for 17th overall in the NFL in total tackles with 76. He is fifth among all rookie linebackers in tackles, trailing Anthony Hill Jr. (82), Arvell Reese (81), Jacob Rodriguez (80), and Sonny Styles (80) — all of whom have a game or two in hand on Trotter.
Trotter also has three passes defended, three tackles for loss, one quarterback hit, one sack and an interception that he took back for a touchdown — the only rookie defender in the league with a pick-six this season.
His run defense grade of 72.9, per Pro Football Focus, nets him as the 19th best out of 80 qualifying linebackers, only trailing Jaishawn Barham and Rodriguez amongst rookie linebacker run-stop rates.
Trotter has also been excellent when rushing the passer, grading out 22nd among 80 qualifying at his position (70.5). Bowles has found something in Trotter's instincts for seeing the ball and getting the ball, which has also led to him generating multiple pressures.
While Trotter has silenced his critics with improvement in his run defense, pass rushing, and tackling efficiency — just a 6.2% missed tackle rate on the year — he still has tons of room for improvement when it comes to coverage.
Even though Trotter has improved this area of his game since his time in college with Missouri, there is plenty of room to get better. His 53.8 coverage grade places him 54th out of the 80 qualifying linebackers, allowing 18 completions on 27 targets for 146 yards (5.4 yards per target) and a 74 passer rating against him.
Trotter has an extremely bright future ahead of him, but if he wants to throw his name in the hat as one of the best pure linebackers in the game, he must brush up on his ability to cover in the passing game while continuing to be a ball hawk against the run and when rushing the QB.

title: Bucs Sign Veteran QB After Concerning Baker Mayfield Injury News
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered the offseason this year with a quarterback room of Baker Mayfield, Jalon Daniels, Connor Bazelak and Jake Browning. Since then, things have changed significantly.
Both Bazelak and Browning were cut at the beginning of the season. That made way for Easton Stick to join the Buccaneers' practice squad, and when Mayfield dislocated his thumb and was out for three weeks, Brett Rypien also joined the team while Daniels started and Stick was elevated to the active roster, and he was then released on Oct. 27.
Now, though, Mayfield appears to have picked up another injury. Because of that, the Buccaneers are bringing on yet another quarterback to the practice squad, and he's already started football games in the NFC South this season.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday that former Atlanta Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush was signing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad.
Rush has started two games this season for the Falcons. He threw for 229 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions with a total QBR of 4.3 across both of those games — naturally, with a statline like that, he was released by the Falcons on Oct. 19.
He comes to Tampa Bay after Rypien's departure and during a time where Mayfield is dealing with another injury. He picked up a leg injury against the Chicago Bears, and he's reportedly been in and out of a walking boot during the bye week.
This move would indicate that the team is genuinely preparing for Mayfield to be out. The Bucs have Stick and Rush at their disposal if Jalon Daniels were to start against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
Stick has already been elevated from the practice squad three times since Mayfield was injured the first time. Were the Bucs to elevate him a fourth time, they would have to sign him to the active roster, so it would be interesting to see how they approach who backs up Daniels between Rush and Stick.
The Bucs play the Lions at 1 p.m. on Sunday in Detroit. Who will be their starting quarterback, and who will be that starting quarterback's backup, remains to be seen.

title: Buccaneers' Week 12 Game Just Became Even More Important
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got to rest and recuperate during their bye week, but now, they have to get back to work and try to win the NFC South.
The NFC South race is quite close. And while the Bucs won't play a division game right off the bye — they have to contend with the Detroit Lions first — they'll play a division game the week after in Week 12 that could now be the most important game of their entire season.
The Bucs started the bye week half a game back of the Carolina Panthers, and after this week's Sunday slate, the Panthers are still Tampa Bay's main roadblock.
The Carolina Panthers beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 on Sunday, moving to 4-5. As a result, the Panthers and the Bucs have now played the same amount of games, so Tampa Bay is one game back of the Panthers for the division.
The Bucs beat the Panthers once already in Week 7 in dominant fashion, winning 43-13 in Charlotte. That could give them the upper hand in any tiebreaker scenarios to come, but Tampa Bay will want to win both games against Carolina to be absolutely sure — and they have the chance to do that in two weeks.
The Bucs play the Panthers in Week 12 on Monday Night Football, and that could very well be for the division lead. The Bucs have to play the Lions first, though, and the Panthers will play the Baltimore Ravens at home in Week 11.
If the Bucs win and the Panthers lose in Week 11, they'd have the same record heading into that matchup. If the Bucs win and the Panthers win in Week 11, the Bucs would be one game back with the chance of evening their records and securing a tiebreaker, and if the Bucs lose and the Panthers win in Week 11, the Bucs would be two games back and would desperately need to beat Carolina.
No matter how it's stacked up, this Week 12 game is crucial. But before that, the Bucs will head to Detroit to play the Lions at 1 p.m. next Sunday.

title: Buccaneers Just Got a Huge Break Ahead of Lions Matchup
full_text:
Following the events that unfolded this weekend, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers sit just one game behind the NFC South-leading New Orleans Saints for the top spot in the division.
There is plenty still to fight for if you are the Bucs, and they will have a tough test against the NFC North leaders, the Detroit Lions, on deck in Week 11.
It will be a challenge for Tampa Bay, but they will fortunately be coming off their bye week when they face Detroit, who will be coming back from an international game in Germany.
The Bucs have likely caught another break heading into the matchup, as Lions' star pass rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, suffered a serious knee injury in their win over the New England Patriots.
Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL early in the first quarter against the Patriots after celebrating a sack on Drake Maye.
Just brutal… pic.twitter.com/W6OOuamVBQ
He will miss the remainder of the 2026 season.
The injury marks Hutchinson's second serious injury of his career. He suffered a tibia and fibula fracture in his leg during the 2024 season. It's a super unfortunate circumstance for one of the best edge rushers in the league, but it will make life easier for the Bucs' offensive line.
In Hutchinson's stead, the Lions will likely rotate the likes of rookie Derrick Moore and veteran DJ Wonnum.
The Bucs have leaned on the ground game all season, and likely will continue to do so as Baker Mayfield and Zac Robinson try to figure out how to fix the passing game. However, that might have to wait, as it was reported that the Bucs are also dealing with a significant injury problem of their own after Mayfield suffered a lower-leg injury against the Chicago Bears.
If Mayfield is unable to go against the Lions, the Bucs will turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels once again.
Missing two stars in an important NFC matchup is never ideal, but for Tampa Bay, the absence of Hutchinson should give them a bit more confidence in coming away with a victory as they hunt down the Carolina Panthers in the division.

title: Something Is Seriously Off With One Buccaneers Star This Season
full_text:
Tristan Wirfs might be the best player on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Throughout his career, Wirfs has earned multiple All-Pro and Pro Bowl selections, as well as a Super Bowl ring in his rookie season. He has established himself as one of the best offensive linemen in football and is well on his way to a Hall of Fame career with the Bucs.
So why in the world is he struggling with penalties this 2026 season?
So far, Wirfs has five false start penalties this year, which is tied for the third most in the NFL. According to Greg Auman of Fox Sports, Wirfs has 16 such penalties in his previous six seasons combined. So why is Wirfs dealing with so many mental lapses this season?
Tristan Wirfs is tied for third-most false starts in the league with five. He had 16 total in six seasons before this year. Has already matched his career high for a season. https://t.co/WMEswGRpiD
Well, the first reason could be Zac Robinson. With a new offense comes new challenges, and we've seen the Bucs this year struggle with many different things offensively, especially in terms of communication. It always feels like the Bucs are late snapping the ball and getting the play off offensively. It would not be a surprise at all if the miscommunication falls into offensive line issues as well.
It may also be prudent to take a look at the center and quarterback situations. The Bucs have had two different starting quarterbacks this season with Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels, which can lead to so many differences in how the offense is run — from a Robinson standpoint and to how Mayfield and Daniels like things done on offense.
Finally, take a look at Graham Barton and how he's done this year. Yes, he's improved with regard to blocking, but one has to wonder how his communication with the offensive line has been, given the false-start issues. Is Barton struggling with offensive line adjustments before the snap? Is it Mayfield and Daniels, or is it Robinson and the coaching staff? These are some of the biggest questions that are on Bucs fans' minds right now.
While Wirfs has been playing fantastic ball this season, we will have to wait and see if these false-start issues continue. It could be a symptom of a much larger problem that has been plaguing the Bucs' offense throughout this season.

title: Cam Ward’s Week 11 Outlook Skyrockets as Cowboys Make Major Defensive Coaching Change
full_text:
I think it's fair to say that Titans fans are feeling good about Cam Ward entering Week 11. The general outlook has changed from questioning Ward's status as the franchise QB to comfortably assuming he'll be there by the end of this year or beginning of next season.
The Dallas Cowboys provided Ward with a favorable matchup this week already, but the team deciding to make a serious personnel shift right before Tennessee travels to Arlington has taken the hype around Ward's growth to the next level.
Per Ian Rapoport, the Cowboys are handing over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant Mike Pettine. DC Christian Parker will remain on the staff, but has been relieved of calling the plays due to a stretch of defense that head coach Brian Schottenheimer called "unacceptable."
#Cowboys senior assistant coach Mike Pettine will now take over as play-caller, so do for the first time since he was with the #Packers in 2021. Action from coach Brian Schottenheimer after a stretch of defense he called “unacceptable.” pic.twitter.com/RDXeOPMZ2G
Pettine produced some elite defenses in his early days with the New York Jets, but he hasn't called plays on that side of the ball for a reason. His last stint in such a position came with the Green Bay Packers from 2018-2021, where a defensive breakdown in the NFC title game led to the Packers choosing not to renew his deal.
Five years removed from that effort, Pettine is facing a flaming Titans offense. Dallas is looking for a refresh with the move, but now looks like the worst time.
The Cowboys just allowed 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss. FOX Sports has their defense ranked dead last in the league (just above the Titans) allowing nearly 400 total yards per game.
It makes sense why Dallas would want to try something new, and on paper, who better to do so against than the 1-8 Titans? The issue is, the Titans' record doesn't tell the full story of a team that has improved in large part due to consistent QB play.
Not only that, but Pettine isn't a hidden defensive mastermind or anything, even if his experience bodes well for Dallas. Think back to when Brian Callahan handed over offensive play-calling duties to Bo Hardegree last season for the Titans. He made the move just before Tennessee let him go.
This feels more akin to that - a desperate, deep-staff change - than something that's going to completely right the ship for the Cowboys. Entering Week 11, Titans fans should see this as a promising turn of events for Ward's climb rather than something that could put a stop to it.
Look out for a big game from Ward this coming Sunday against, hopefully, a Cowboys defense that hasn't figured out their league-worst problems in a matter of seven days.

title: Titans' WR Room in for a Major Shakeup in Week 11... and That's a Good Thing
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans' injury report in Week 10 was a major factor in the team failing to mount a winning effort over the Jacksonville Jaguars; that, and the Jags were 6-2 with a runaway lead in the AFC South. Some teams are just further along.
It was already bad enough, but things got a little worse in that regard for Tennessee. The most notable news on the injury front came in the form of WR Wan'Dale Robinson being sent to IR with an ankle injury. He'll miss at least four weeks of football for Tennessee.
Robinson hasn't been great in his first year with the Titans, but he's a vet-leaning pillar in an otherwise young unit. Although, upon a closer look, that becomes the exciting part about Robinson missing time from Week 11 on.
The Titans are 1-8. They've got two first-round picks and a second-rounder ready to bolster this rebuild. Cam Ward has almost convinced Tennessee that he's the long-term guy for the job under center. What better time is there to see what your young guys have?
Not only will Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike get to continue in their recently-expanded roles, but rookie WR1 Carnell Tate is also tracking to return from his two-week absence.
Throw practice-squad regular and fan-favorite Xavier Restrepo into the mix, and you've got a pass-catching room comprised almost entirely of young and developing playmakers. Calvin Ridley is the lone exception, but his snap count in Week 10 doesn't inspire confidence in his involvement.
It also works out that multiple guys in that rotation are trying to prove something, to some extent, about their role in Nashville. Ayomanor came into this season behind Ridley, and has since been climbing in the rotation. Effectively the WR1 when Tate was gone, Ayomanor will look to keep pace even in his return.
Dike has seen a recent uptick in pass-catching snaps, breaking his Pro-Bowl mold as a returner. He's got seven receptions over the past two games, including a touchdown. Dike wasn't in the WR rotation really at all to begin this year, and now has a window to continue to cement himself within it.
Finally, Restrepo was just promoted to the active roster to fill in for Robinson. This is a guy who has come close so many times, including making the initial 53-man cut this season before being promptly released. The next four weeks should pose multiple opportunities for him to leave a lasting mark.
To top it all off, Ward and the Titans' offense have a favorable matchup with a middling Dallas Cowboys defense. Look for a lot of movement through the air, and potentially some movement in Tennessee's WR room too.
